review_text: Sugarfish lives up to the hype! I ate there the 2nd night it is open, and waited over 4.5 hours- better than the 5 hour quote time! Once seated everything was great- the service was wonderful and you can taste the difference in the high quality fish they serve.

The HYPE is real! Came to Friday's Grand Opening and was met with a 2 hour wait. There was no way in hell I was waiting 2 hours to each lunch. So I put my name on the list just for the hell of it. I sat down to answer a couple emails and the host approaches the 2 people waiting to eat lunch who were waiting for over an hour and he says to us a table for 3 just opened up would you 3 mind sitting together. We all looked at each other and said why not let's do this. So we sat together and had a memorable first meal at Sugarfish. It was awesome to share this opening with people that had all just met at the grand opening with a love for premo sushi. The place is gonna kill it btw. So we all ordered the Nozawa menu. I had some changes since I don't eat shellfish and they were very accommodating. Started with organic edamame, then tuna sashimi in a ponzu sauce with scallions. It was so fresh and so delicious. Then came the sushi... albacore, tuna, salmon, yellowtail, snapper and sea bass. All amazing. Then came the toro and salmon Hand rolls to finish off the meal. It was an amazing meal. I didn't want it to end. It was great to meet the people I had lunch with as well as the master himself, chef Kazonori Nozawa. I will be back for more.

Do not walk to put your name on the 5hr wait list. RUN. The best meal we have had since dining at Sugarfish in downtown LA in 2013. It's so so so good and impossible to describe. Did not want it to end and can't wait to go back.
Well worth the wait! Just as delicious as in LA but even better in NYC! Super friendly staff and amazingly fresh, perfect sushi! Wow can't wait to go back!!!!

We arrived about 30 minutes before they opened and were seated in the first group. The meal took about an hour and a half. We all ordered the Trust Me menus - some of us went with the standard and others, like myself, ordered the largest version. The food was very good. The fish quality was very good and the rice was warm and loose. I prefer the rice to be slightly vinegared like Yasuda and Nakazawa, however this restaurant clearly isn't in that class. The service was still a bit spotty but that's to be expected with a new restaurant. Everyone was incredibly nice and the staff quickly corrected any mistakes. Overall I think this is the best option for omakase style sushi in this price point. Light years ahead of Haru and others. I will definitely return.

Got quoted 3 hours wait time, but instead it became a 5 hour nightmare. We went back when we didn't get a text, and was told they were backed up and said the wait would take another 30 minutes. It ended up being 2 hours more than the quoted time. I can't blame the staff though, they were nice; and it wasn't totally their fault. They just need to be more aggressive with the self righteous New York diners that linger after finishing their meal as if there's no one else waiting to sit. The food didn't live up to the hype. The rice was over powered with vinegar, I don't mind vinegar but it was just overpowering you can't taste anything else but vinegar. I also expected the rice to be on loose, but it just broke apart. Since we were the last few to be seated for the night, I'm guessing quality just went down hill. Hoping to give them a chance again after the hype dies. Until then, just a friendly PSA to all NYC diners: gtfo in a timely manner.

yum! tried to come on Saturday but by 6 pm they had stopped accepting names. The people at the door are extremely gracious when they say no, and it is opening weekend. Came back on Sunday and put our name down and were quoted 3 hours, but we were texted within 1.5 hours and were seated 5-10 minutes of arriving to the restaurant. The restaurant is in a great location, so go to a nearby bar and have some drinks! 
There is no bar for you to wait at at the restaurant.
Anyway we sat and shared a trust me and then ordered some extra pieces (salmon, yellow fin sashimi, toro and salmon rolls). All the sushi was fresh, delicious and so so well thought out.
They give you some wasabi, ginger and soy when you order but they will not really provide any more, which is fine. Some pieces of fish will come with soy or sauce already on it so they will recommend not adding any.  I had the stag leap which was delicious and my boyfriend had the Sapporo. Tip is included and the meal is very reasonably priced.

4 for the food; 3.5 for the service. I stopped by for lunch and wait time was long but shorter than originally estimated. They take your number down and text you when you're close to top of the list to return to the restaurant. I was seated in the back bar type area. Food was good, on par with what I remember having at the Sugarfish location in Beverly Hills. Fish was fresh and delicious. Pacing of the meal was a bit off so there was quite some wait time between sections and service was generally frustrating. I had to repeat my request for water, then part of my order was forgotten (the waiter was asking me the end of the meal questions and I point out I was still waiting on an item) and when it was ready; it was served to the guests next to me. So I had to wait for it to be re-made because once they set a plate down for a guest they can't take it back. I'm fine with the policy but I was getting tired of the mistakes and waiting. Will give them a few weeks to get the kinks out and hopefully things will be smoother next time.

After moving to NYC and leaving my beloved favorite sushi spot behind, you have no idea how excited I was to see Sugarfish in NYC.

Highlights: Consistency. It tastes exactly as fresh as it did in Los Angeles, and the quality is incomparable to most sushi at other price points.

Unfortunately, there are no reservations- so there will be a long wait for quite some time in the future months.

The only think you will find close is Domo Domo in Greenwich Village. But in my opinion, Sugarfish is far superior with both quality and service.

From LA to NY, no longer do I need to travel far for outstanding melt in your mouth sushi for cheap. Get the Omakase- it's so worth it. Tips already included. Similar layout as the locations in LA and spectacular service as usual. Got to beat the rush at 5:30 and the line was down the block at 6

Really excellent sushi; omikase style at a lower price point than some of the other big name places in Manhattan. 

Their "Trust Me" entree comes in three sizes, making it a flexible choice for all appetites, and I prefer their selection of fish over some others. I was particularly happy to get a toro roll included in my meal without having to add it. 

The rice is fantastic. It's warm and loose and the contrast to the fish really steps this up a notch from standard sushi joints. It's not traditional vinegary rice, but I like it better that way. They also don't automatically dot every nigiri with wasabi. I know it's not traditional, but maybe I'm just a progressive sushi eater. 

That rice. So good. 

The fish itself seems a step below the top tier places, evidenced primarily by texture and tenderness. Still very good. 

As for service, the place is jam packed because it's new and if we hadn't gotten there a half hour before it opened, we would have been waiting for HOURS. This popularity makes it a bit hard on the staff, and there were a few logistical errors in serving our party of 6. Everything was very cordially fixed, and they even gave us a roll on the house because it was a mistake. Everyone is very nice there. 

Overall, I dig this place more than something like Sushi Yasuda, which is more of an "experience," but not as cost effective for what isn't necessarily that big a step up in terms of enjoying the actual food. Sugarfish is good. 

But then again, I still love my salmon avocado maki from the joint down the street in Brooklyn, so what do I know?

As good as in LA, warm, but efficient service and the Trust Me as always was perfection. For the quality and value, there is no better.  Got a seat at the sushi bar with no wait at 5pm, the hype won't die and it shouldn't.  Go at off times, eat often.  Welcome to town Sugarfish.

I've only ever had very quick stop-ins at Sugarfish in LA, so this was my first real experience with it. We went at 11:30am on Sunday (a half hour before it opened), and got seated right at 12, but by the time we left it was a 3+ hour wait. 

I went all in -- I got the Nozawa Trust Me, which is their biggest omakase option, and costs $45. I really liked everything I got with it, with the yellowtail and sea bass being particular highlights. The only thing that held me back somewhat is the obvious comparison to Sushi Yasuda, where you can get almost as much food with their $44 entree option, and the sushi is essentially perfect. Sugarfish has some cheaper options, but I don't think I'd be excited to pony up for the Nozawa Trust Me again when I can make that trade off and go to Yasuda.

Should also note -- they still seem to be working out a lot of issues here. The servers were all extremely nice and apologetic when things were going haywire (and I ended up getting an extra hand roll by mistake!), but it happened a number of times. I don't put a lot of weight on service anyway, but for those that do, be aware that this might be an issue.

Excellent experience.  Walked in at 12:15, restaurant was packed but they were able to sit us at the bar immediately. Service team was courteous, efficient, knowledgeable and FAST!  Food was terrific, I went with the "trust me", my friend ordered off the menu. I will absolutely be going back.

I've tried this place when I visited LA two years ago and honestly, it wasn't that memorable. But when I found out that they have recently opened up a location here in NYC, I decided to give it a try again. And I'm SO glad I did. I was just in Tokyo and even waiting on line for two and a half hours at the infamous fish market was not as good as Sugarfish, and I am quite a picky eater. When we arrived there around 12:30pm on a Wednesday afternoon, it was already packed with a number of people waiting, and we were told the wait was 45 minutes to an hour for two people but they took my phone number down and said they would contact us when our table was close to being ready. We walked around the neighborhood but ten minutes later we already received a text that our table was almost ready! I ordered the Nozawa Trust Me and it was so worth it. My favorite was the blue crab hand roll, hands down. But I enjoyed everything else as well. The rice just melts in your mouth but they have distinct flavors that might not be to everyone's liking. I was tempted to order more but I decided to save the deliciousness for another time. Since they just opened, I do agree with another reviewer that they're still sorting out a few kinks here and there, but otherwise, the service was on point. There's also no tipping allowed. I don't know if I would have waited the three to five hours others have, but I'm just glad I had a flexible enough job that I can enjoy new popular restaurants during the weekdays. I'm already drooling over the next time I'm coming here.

I've made plans to go to Sugarfish the second my friend send me the article regarding the opening its first outpost in NYC.  I love sushi and who can turn down an omakase meal for only $51. The only other place I can think of in NYC with a similar price point is Sushi on Jones, which has a time limit and a pretty rustic accommodation. Anyway, we decided to try our luck by getting to Sugarfish on a Wed at 5:30, the wait was an hour, which was not too bad. We decided to kill some time at the wine bar across the street.  

The restaurant texted us exactly one hour later, by then, there was a long line outside of the restaurant. We were seated promptly and we immediately decided to order "the Nozawa trust me" set, which contained the most items out of the three omakase meals. 

I was really blown away by the quality of the fish. I think my favorite was the scallop (which was the daily special) and the hirame sushi. I loved how the fish was perfectly portioned and could practically melt in my mouth. I really enjoyed the warm rice, however some of the rice had too much vinegar, making them inedible. I had to pick out the rice because they were ruining the sashimi for me. Given the fact that there were twelve sushi and two rolls, I didn't mind skipping some of the rice. 

My least favorite dishes (aside from the vinegary rice) were the blue crab hand roll and the tuna sashimi. The crab was over dressed and tasted like a plain crab salad you can get at any Japanese market. Meanwhile the tuna sashimi was under seasoned and the quality appeared to be poorer vis-a-vis the rest of the sushi. 

As most reviewers pointed out, the service was extremely efficient, but spotty. They were quick to bring out each course, but neglect to take away the old ones. I had to track down a server to take away our empty plates as our table was jammed with plates. It was also weird that they would bring out a plate for one person at the time, instead of bring out all of our plates. 

Lastly, the space was beautiful, well decorated and perfectly lit. The tables were fairly close to each other, which is expected given the popularity of the place. There is a small upstairs lounge that provided a good space for people to wait for their tables. However I don't think people knew about it as it sat quite empty for the first half of our meal. Overall, there are definitely a few kinks that needed to be worked out, but I believe that it is the best value omakase in the city.

This place definitely lives up to the hype. The menu selection is simple, so if you're looking for exotic sushi, this isn't the place for you. If you're looking for the most fresh fish and rice, it's a must try.

They don't take reservations, and the wait can be long so show up early.

Tip is included, which is great! Overall, the pricing is very reasonable. A dinner for two including a bottle of wine came to a total of $120.

Went there on opening day, got there 10 mins before it opened and there was already a line. Once the restaurant opened, we were promptly seated to our tables. The food in itself was extremely fresh and good. For only $45 you could get the largest omakase meal which included edamame as an appetizer, several different types of nigiri sushis, handrolls and their sushi special (which was toro for that day). Best part is that tip is included!

Overall, this place lives up to the hype. Would most definitely recommend and come back.

I finally had the chance to check out Sugarfish after multiple attempts!  I tried going a few times and I was quoted 4-5 hour waits.  I decided to come before they opened one day and that was a smart choice.  I recommend everyone do the same and come before they open.  Also, please take their wait quote times with a grain of salt.  There is really no way to tell how long it will take before a table opens up for you and you have to understand that if you are quoted around a 4 hour wait, it could very well go into 5 or 5.5 hours.  Yes, this sucks, but you have to look at it with in their perspective.  

The servers here were generally very friendly, but there were some servers that brought out the food that need some additional training.  This is the reason for me taking away a star.  The sushi is recommended to be eaten right when it comes out and not let it sit.  The handrolls are recommended to be eaten right away while the seaweed is still crispy.  I am a slow eater and the servers brought out plate after plate of my dishes from my omakase.  My table started to get cluttered and the worst part was, they would bring out dishes, but not take away the empty plates!?!  I don't understand that logic.  The servers need additional training and should be mindful of their guests.  If they see us still eating, don't plop down another plate, especially if the restaurant's motto is to encourage guests to eat the sushi fresh once the dish comes out.  I did not appreciate feeling rushed.  The servers also don't do a good job in explaining which pieces are which and just plop the plate down.  The server would explain it to one person at the table, but not the rest when ours came.  If the server is going to only explain it once per table, than bring everything out at once.  This definitely needs some fixing.

I ordered the Nozawa Trust Me.  Everything was delicious and the fish was really fresh.  I won't go into detail for each dish since I'm sure others will.  The portion size was perfect  and I appreciated them using quality fish.  The only negative was the vinegary rice.  I felt the vinegar to rice ratio was off and all I could taste was the vinegar.  The vinegar was overpowering and I couldn't taste the fish.  I ended up eating the fish separately and then eating the rice separately so I could taste the fish.  I don't know if this was done on purpose, but this is the only negative.  It's not that it tasted bad, but this is the first time where I'm eating such vinegary rice.  The rice is also packed loose and not the typical packed nigiri kind that you're used to.  I especially appreciated the fresh wasabi.  It didn't look like something out of a tube.  I can't get over how well priced the omakase is.  I also can't get over the fresh and great quality fish.  I would probably eat here everyday if I could, but alas, the lines and me not being in the area often will prevent me from doing so.  

Bottomline - my meal was delicious.  The food was great and I will be back.  It is definitely the best omakase in NYC that is decently priced.  This place puts Sushi on Jones to shame.  The prices here are the same and you get value for your dollar.  I hope the restaurant will succeed and expand since I foresee the hype (which is real) and wait times not slowing down at all.

Sugarfish is sweet and great but let me start with what is not.  

It is NOT a top sushi place.  It is a fun place for good quality standard sushi.  But it is not a top quality place like Zo or Yasuda.   Not by a mile. 

It is NOT well lit.  That is an understatement. It is dark like almost impossible to see dark.  Turn up the lights !!

What it is , is a great place to get a high quality but standard sushi meal.  Rice Temperature is warm which is great.  The yellowtail was super tender and the toro handroll was excellent.  The price is super reasonable (1/4 of zo and 1/2 Yasuda ) so great bet for the money. 

We had someone put our name down and all in it would have been a wait of nearly 4 hours. Hopefully that dies down and normalcy settles in.

Every time I visit my sister in Los Angeles, we make a point to dine at at SUGARFISH. It's the best sushi I've ever tasted and is consistently excellent. The warm rice is magical perfection. I'm glad they've opened up an East Coast operation at last. Was the two hour wait worth it? Yes. Go eat here. Trust me.

Probably would get on a wait list of 5 months to eat here. The most incredible sushi I have ever had. 

The service is almost as perfect as their food. Thanks Kyu and Daniel for making this a 5 star experience!
Perfect fish, kind waitstaff helped me with my stroller. Trust me light was the perfect amount of food for lunch, $23 including tax and tip. Can't wait to go back.

The business claimed their listing, which states that they take reservations, despite write-ups and 6-hour waits suggesting otherwise. 

LA-originated Sugarfish recently expanded across the country to NYC to excellent results. They're in a well-decorated space in a prime location across from Gramercy Tavern. THE NOZAWA TRUST ME ($45.00) is a superb omakase deal, with perhaps the best fish quality / value combo in NYC (almost certainly when you consider that it's no tipping/service included).

Organic Edamame
Tuna Sashimi
Albacore Sushi (2-pc)
Salmon Sushi (2-pc)
Yellowtail Sushi (2-pc)
Snapper Sushi* (1-pc)
Hirame Sushi (1-pc)
Toro Hand Roll
Blue Crab Hand Roll
"Daily Special" (2-pc)

Service was already firing on all cylinders -- there was a generous portion of edamame greeting us when we sat down, refilling our iced matchas quickly and constantly being attentive but not intrusive. The only awkward part of our experience was a server's reply when we asked where they source their fish from: "All over!", they replied, then walked away.

This was a 5-star experience knocked down to 4 stars in hopes that the review isn't taken down for a 7th time.

Definitely meets the hype, mostly given the great value for quality sushi. We had high expectations since we had been to Sugarfish in LA in the past, and the feel seemed pretty much identical to our experience there. My wife and I both opted for the Nozawa Trust Me ($51 incl. tip) and we're both perfectly full on the way out and very happy with the overall quality. That said, we're not sushi snobs so I don't know how it compares to some of the other big name / high end sushi restaurants around the city. 

Went at 5:15pm on a Friday, put name down for a party of 2 and was quoted a 3-3.5 hour wait time. Got the text to come back at around 7:25pm, so after only a little over 2 hours.

The hype is real!  Never been to the LA locations but everyone raves about them and I can see why.  The food was very delicious and service was fast!  We got the Nozawa Trust Me set which includes the most food of the 3 sets.  The albacore definitely stands out, which is why we ordered some more!  For $45 for the set, which includes the "hospitality charge" its a good deal for some high quality sushi.

I think this place has been massively overhyped, after eating here I am surprised there are lines. I had the trust me lite. The sushi quality is so-so, its nothing to be excited about eating. The rice is warm which adds a nice component to the taste but the rice itself is too hard to be enjoyable. The sauces are also too salty. The toro roll was decent but fell apart as I ate it. If I was somewhere in the suburbs outside NY this is the kind of meal I would expect.

Love. This. Place. Went in Los Angeles for the first time and got hooked. Now I can get my fix on the East Coast too. The combination of the warm rice and cold fish is melt-in-your-mouth sexy. This is also the place where I learned to love the hand roll. Trust me!
I've been to SugarFish in Cali once beofreo and fell in love. Recently visit the highly anticipated opening of the one in NYC. IT WAS IDENTICAL. FESH SOFT AND TO DIE FOR. GOING BACK WEEKLY.

This is an amazing sushi experience! We had arrived at the restaurant a half hour before opening and highly recommend doing that if you do not want to wait for hours in line. We got in right away when it opened. Ordered the trust me combo for lunch  and everything was phenomenal. Fish is so fresh! Greatest sushi I have ever had. Would give it ten stars!

I was able to try this place out with no wait on the Saturday of Thanksgiving weekend.   Despite all of the rave reviews on Yelp, I must say this was perhaps one of the most overly hyped places that yelp has misguided me on to this day.  

I won't say that I'm a know-it-all when it comes to sushi, but I would consider myself somewhat knowledgeable when it comes to it.  Here's a list of things that just didn't sit well with me - even for the $50 price point:

1. Factory style sushi.  Ever been to sushi buffets?  That's what the sushi seemed like because by the time you got your food, you can see subtle hints it wasn't made to order.  
2. Dishes were coming out onto our table before we even finished our previous course.  This does not happen typically in "omakase".   
3. They use a crap-ton of rice vinegar/soy sauce on the sushi.  So much sauce that the rice soaks it all up and the nigiri just falls apart when you try to pick it up.  This is a sushi no-no.   
4. Fish definitely wasn't that fresh.  They had substituted for sea bass today.  The sea bass definitely tasted fishy.  Could be because of the the holiday weekend...but that shouldn't be an excuse.
5. The rice.  People may say it's the fish that makes the sushi, but it's really the rice.  I'm not a fan of their rice.

Here are the good:
1. Service was very attentive.  
(sadly that's really it)

If you take your sushi seriously, I would highly recommend not to come here.  If in particular, you care about authentic sushi, this place is simply a no go.  Instead of spending your 4-6 hours waiting for this place and want to spend $50 elsewhere on sushi, go hit up Sushi on Jones, 

PS, I got back home with a stomach ache after trying to drink the sugarfish cool-aid.

Amazing - came here on a Saturday for lunch - of course you have to wait online

Got the Trust Me - trust me it was awesome, see pictures - everything melted in your mouth, my favorite salmon sushi and blue crab hand roll

Ordered uni sushi - creamy, out of this world goodness

Definitely will be back

Simply outstanding and worth the value. We had no wait when getting there at 3 on a Saturday for 2, which was great news considering we were ready for a 3 hour wait. Our server, an Asian (Korean?) guy with glasses, was super nice and did a great job explaining the menu and the values of the restaurant. We got the nozawa trust me and boy was every item a surprise. Ok other than the edamame, that was pretty normal. 
All the fish was super fresh, which is hard to say for this side of the country. They basically had an assortment of all the fish I could want. I have to say they slightly over-sauced some of the rice, and the sushi fell apart REALLY easily, but forgivable for the quality. The hand rolls were amazing, I left the table when they brought my roll and they brought me a new one when I came back to make sure it's still fresh and the seaweed still crispy. They definitely didn't skimp on the fish/crab for these at all. Great new experience with set menus without going to Japan

Unbelievebly GREAT !!!,must come & experience your self, wil not disappointing. A lot better than the next door.Truly japanese QUALITY sushi.Perfect place to encounter experience sushi master chef from japan.Definetely no doubt ,i will bring all my friend .

The best sushi I've ever had, fresh and excellent staff. I've visited the downtown LA location and it's highly recommended. Go with the Trust Me menu item if you have never been there before. So yummy!

4.75

I unfortunately have not been able to try the California locations, so I was very happy when this opened up.  

I waited two hours to sit down.. such a long wait.  But hey, it was worth it!  I knew there would be a long wait since this establishment recently opened.  Got there at around 5pm on a Wednesday and sat down by 7pm.  They at least have a texting system in place that will message you when your table is almost ready and they give a 15 minute window to return.  There is also an area upstairs that is a nice waiting area (in addition to the very small area at the entrance of the restaurant) that is good to have a chat and relax while waiting.

Upon sitting, I looked over the menu, which had a great choice of sushi, sashimi, and etc. Many items caught my eye, so I decided to go for their most expensive set, the Nozawa Trust me!  You save a few dollars getting it as all ($51 compared to around $65+ if you get everything separately).  

My order of the Nozawa Trust Me consists of the following: (all sushi comes in two pieces), Edamame, Tuna Sashimi, sushi that included of Albacore, Salmon, Yellowtail, Snapper, Sea Bass, and Scallop, hand rolls that consisted of Toro and Blue Crab.  As a note, they did not have Hirame (which is normally on their Trust Me menu), so they had substituted it for Snapper and the special that night was Scallop.

Of course the star of the show was the sushi.  Many of the pieces I had felt like the fish melted in my mouth.  I honestly could taste the freshness in these pieces of sushi and sashimi here.  My favorite ones included the Tuna Sashimi, Salmon, Albacore, and the Toro hand roll.  As a note for the hand rolls, it is best to eat them once they are delivered to you, as this allows you to best experience the combination of the warm seaweed paper and rice with the fish.  So DON'T LET IT SIT TOO LONG!

Anyways, service here was excellent and I would definitely come back again (hopefully the wait will not be as long.. but I have heard people quoted longer wait times).  

NOTE: Prices here already take tipping into consideration, so there is no need to provide an additional tip upon paying your bill.

Went here Thankgiving eve and we were seated almost immediately.  My friend and I ordered the Nozawa Trust Me, it was AMAZING!  The freshiest Sushi I've ever had.  You will not find trendy exotic rolls or sushi here, but the quality that is served to your party will leave you very happy!  Must go and take lots of friends and family!  Enjoy!


2nd Review

Just as fantastic as the first time!

As much as I'd like to give this place more stars, I felt some things were off. We had the Nozawa omakase sushi lunch. For $45 you get a decent amount of food. The fish was not anything spectacular just your run of the mill cuts of tuna, yellowtail, salmon, Hirame and snapper sushi along with two handrolls. The cuts were average quality fish. The rice was on the mushy side not in line with the best japanese restaurants in NYC. The two handrolls were ok. Onto the service. As I have ranted about in the past, my experience is always affected when the staff is not japanese. They just miss the markings quite often. As with most omakase meals, the ebb and flow is important. If you are not sitting at the sushi bar, your waiter/waitress would have to bring the plates over. However when one waiter brings you your plate and another waiter brings your friends plate a minute later it ruins the ebb and flow of things. This was the case for every plate they brought over. It's not like the plates were that big. So basically you are stuck waiting for your friends plate of food to be brought (usually a minute or so) before got can both eat. That's kinda annoying. I would understand if this was a large party, but we were only two people and the restaurant wasn't packed as we were there closer to 2pm. Something to think about!

Tip included in their prices - no need for additional tips!

A great value and experience for the money spent. 

Wait - Can't comment, I went before it opened (30 minutes before) and by the time we were about to enter the line probably tripled. 

Service - Super nice and friendly staff. I sat at the bar area and they explained everything really nicely and wasn't rude. The staff was attentive (refilled my water, explained my different sushi when served, etc). 

Food - I chose the Nozawa Trust Me option. Their lunch time $45 sushi set. The daily special when I went was Scallops (which was delish btw! I liked it more than some of the other sushi). 

The food is prepared for you to eat so its fresh but not made in front of you so I can't really call it omakase. I have to say, their fish and sauce is good! The fish was nicely prepared and felt like it was melting in my  mouth. The rice was a bit too seasoned for me though, and occasionally I would feel that it was too salty/sour vinegary taste to it. I hope they will quality control it because I like how nice the place is. It's rather efficient and the meal portion was nice. Can't say I'll wake up early to wait before they open again tho. Might try dinner next!

Loyalty - They have a card where you fill out your email, and after you receive the confirm email you can activate it so that if you visit twice and eat there before your birthday you can receive a meal on them. Must fill the card only once per visit.

Arrived at 4PM the day before Thanksgiving and we were quoted a wait time of about 2.5 hours. Holy moly! Who even eats at 4PM (Linner)!? I guess everyone had the same idea and thought that there would be less people. The hostess said that they were busy the entire day due to the holiday but the wait is usually not this long on a weekday around this time. There is a small waiting area on the main floor and additional room to wait upstairs. The bathroom is located upstairs as well. Most people leave after providing their name and number.

At 6PM, we received a text to go back to the restaurant and wait for our table. We overheard the hostess quoting wait times of 4 hours or more. By the time we were seated, they were no longer accepting any more diners. 

The lighting was perfect when we started our meal and in the middle it became much darker. What is up with that?

Yes, this place is amazing because the largest omakase option (Nazowa Trust Me) is only $51 (tip included) and the fish is fresh. However, the Nazowa Trust Me might still not be enough for some. 

My favorite out of everything was surprisingly the salmon. It was topped with some sesame seeds that really enhanced the flavor and texture of the fish. The blue crab hand roll was a little too fishy for my taste. And at the end of the meal, we actually received another order of tuna sashimi by accident (no complaints)!

One thing that I really disliked (and others have mentioned in their reviews as well) is the sushi rice...way too much vinegar! The soy sauce was too salty as well. I wonder if they offer low sodium soy sauce.

They give you a larger than expected portion of edamame. I was disappointed that they ran out of Uni (Santa Barbara) to order and Hirame. The daily special was scallop, but I've had better at Katsuya South Beach. We also had 2 orders of toro and it melted in my mouth, as expected.

Service was fairly fast and very friendly! I would definitely come back but would not wait over 1 hour.

Although the quality of fish is INCREDIBLY good (one of the best I've ever had), the Sugarfish does not adapt to the client. They only offer 3 options of sashimi, while they offer many, many more fishes only as sushi, which as a seafood lover who suffers from digestive issues and doesn't eat rice with fish, was very frustrating, and inconvenient. 

The server informed me that they were out of 20% of the fish options they offered even for sushi (I was forced to pay for sushi to only eat the fish), and that two types of fish were low in stock so I would only be able to have them if I ordered a multiple dish combo. 

I would have loved this restaurant and returned if they adapted to the New York public better. We like to order salads at sushi restaurants, enjoy torched varieties of seafood, and definitely sashimi options for the fish and seafood they offer. I love crab, lobster, hamachi, sea bass, and should be able to have them without having to pay for sashimi and waste rice.

Food was good! The rice was warm which was unexpected but the quality of the fish was great. We got the "Trust Me" and the Nozawa "Trust me". Even though you might have to shell out about 30/40 pre tip/tax for it. Its definitely a place to enjoy good service and great ambiance.

I've been to Sugarfish in LA and always loved it, and so I jumped on the hype bandwagon when I heard they were opening their first New York location.  However, I was somewhat skeptical if they could recreate the same amazing experience and how it would hold up with the NY sushi landscape.  

Even though my expectations were high, they were exceeded!  After trying to go once at 5PM and being quoted a 5-hour wait, I went back a second time at 4:30 to wait in line for a reservation.  Once I put my name in, they have an easy system of texting you to let you know when the table will be ready.  They were exactly right on the time estimate, and I ended up being seated at 6:30.  Although it was still mobbed outside and in the entryway, once we sat at our table it was a completely calm and enjoyable experience.  The staff couldn't have been nicer, and we were not rushed whatsoever during the meal.  The employees definitely don't let the stress of the popularity impact the experience.  The fish was amazing, with the warm rice always being a highlight.  Everyone dining was very happy to be there, and I can't wait to brave the lines and go back!

One of the best sushi experiences I've had in NYC, hands down. I'd put this up there with DomoDomo, which has been my top sushi experience in this city.

Be aware that the line here is insane. You will go there and likely get quoted several hours for a wait. They will call you when your table is ready, then your whole party has to arrive within 15 minutes or they will give up your table (crazy). You then may wait up to a half hour in their waiting area for your table. Like I said, fantastic sushi, but this policy is the reason why I had to dock a star. If you're given a 4 hour wait, do you really think your whole party is going to stick around close enough to the restaurant to arrive within 15 minutes of their call? If it was exactly 4 hours and you could predict the call timing, this would be fine - but in my experience, they have called ~1 hour early and you're nowhere near the restaurant. My friend tried to go 4 separate times before getting in with me finally. Word to the wise: put your name down at an off time (maybe 4:30pm on a weekday) when it's about a 45 minute wait, so you can easily stick around. Wish they did reservations here instead!

Aside from that craziness: the food is fantastic. The sushi is pieces like they actually do in Japan, so don't go looking for your Americanized rolls here. They serve you a few pieces at a time, and the rice is warm like it is supposed to be, so you're supposed to eat them quickly while the rice is still warm. They have multiple set menus, or you can order your own pieces. I highly recommend getting either "The Nozawa" ($42) or the "Trust Me" ($32) set menu. These are very similar and will leave you with a great assortment for a very reasonable price (no tipping allowed), keeping you full. I'm not usually an albacore fan, but we all agreed that the albacore was the best piece we had, so make sure to get that!

For dinner, the ambience was dark and trendy, which was surprising to me because I had thought the yelp photos made the restaurant look a little brighter. I enjoyed the dark/trendiness afterall.

My friend and I the $51 omakase. I thought it was incredible value for the price. Flavorful pieces. Definitely a fantastic deal.

I do have to be picky for a moment here, I found each sushi piece to have a little too much rice, and found the rice to be a little too sticky and vinegary for sushi rice. 

All in all, I will likely come back.

Horrible experience! We ordered the "Trust me" omakasa and it was nothing special! The scallops were very fishy and so disappointing. Service was ok at best. They need a little more training since they just opened up. They have "to go menu" item was they were not able to take a "go to" order. Very odd! I would not return to this joint. Take your money somewhere else!

Hello 800th review, hello mediocre sushi. So, the famous chain from LA has finally landed in New York and I was pretty excited to give them a try. Before I went, I already assumed it would be a four star review due to their overwhelming popularity in the West Coast, I was mistaken. I think if I was new to sushi or a novice, I would be able to overlook some of the flaws, and would probably enjoy it. But if you know anything about legit sushi, you would probably think it was just OK. I eat a lot of sushi and the sushi here really bothered me, nigiri is the balance of seafood and rice, their rice completely ruined the sushi. It's so weird, I am so used to having rice ruin the sushi by it being underseasoned, but Sugarfish managed to do the complete opposite and overseasoned the hell out of it, it kinda felt like a lime punched me in the mouth. For me, it was a 3.5, but I rounded down since I ordered Santa Barbara Uni and there was so much vinegar that I barely tasted any Uni at all, all I tasted was the vinegar and rice. Congrats Sugarfish for fucking up Santa Barbara Uni. I am obsessed with Uni and anyone who eats sushi should be too, but I legit hated the Uni here. Overall, I really left thinking it wasn't bad per se, but I definitely left feeling disappointed. 

Also, the restaurant itself is unusually dark, I get that it was trying to go trendy but it felt out of place for a Japanese restaurant. The other thing that annoyed the shit out of me, was the pace of the dinner, I felt like all the food was flying out of the kitchen. They served the edamame from the Omakase, then came the sashimi and then the first plate of sushi came shortly after. Dude, like wtf, there is no room on the god damn table! The entire meal felt rushed and plates kept coming out back to back. I guess it was a bonus for them that tip was already included in the price...

The food: 

The Nozoawa Trust me: 
Organic Edamame
Tuna Sashimi
Albacore Sushi (2-pc)
Salmon Sushi (2-pc)
Snapper Sushi (2-pc)
Yellowtail Sushi (2-pc)
Sea Bass Sushi (2-pc)
Toro Hand Roll
Blue Crab Hand Roll
Daily Special which was Large Scallop Sushi (2-pc)

Tuna Sashimi- The flavor on this was nice, it had a nice acidic pop but the tuna was a little weird for me. I never had tuna so light tasting and light textured before. https://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=Er4SwPn3fnmBgUCqQoJl3Q&userid=Y_iTTjKvV5hLy-880SZzlA

Albacore Sushi- The fish was preseasoned and was was surprisingly mild, but then I get smacked with the tang from the rice. https://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=2ypeoBEFGW_d-zFnIxE7xQ&userid=Y_iTTjKvV5hLy-880SZzlA

Snapper Sushi- Any kind of white fish will be more mild in flavor and this was no different but the texture on the fish was nice.

Salmon Sushi- I think salmon is automatically good and the one here was, I also liked the sesame seed addition.

Yellowtail Sushi- I liked the yellowtail, it wasn't as silky and sexy as other yellowtails but the flavor was good. But the rice was too aggressive. https://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=vLQr1_B2VmH-LdQWsZ_VLQ&userid=Y_iTTjKvV5hLy-880SZzlA

Sea Bass Sushi- I thought it was weird but they added jalapeno to the sea bass, I wasn't crazy about it.

Large Scallop- This had the jalapeno as well and it's kind of a shame, why would you mask a perfectly fresh scallop???

Toro Hand Roll- The seaweed was great since it was nice and crunchy but the toro was barely noticeable.

Blue Crab Hand Roll- The seaweed on this was great as well and it shocked me how much I enjoyed the crab roll, I wasn't expecting to like it at all but I did. https://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=dr2-fasv1y-B7wfL7MWO6w&userid=Y_iTTjKvV5hLy-880SZzlA

Santa Barbara Uni a la Carte- I ordered this at the end and it pissed off me off. Uni is amazing, but shit rice ruined amazing Uni. https://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=NrNhbzTP80-pVj1zd7pE5w&userid=Y_iTTjKvV5hLy-880SZzlA

Is the sushi good? Yes. Is it worth the hype? Depends on how long you waited to get in. Somehow Sugarfish has brilliantly marketed Omakase as the "trust me." The value is indeed great but not worth a long wait. There are plenty of gems in NYC serving the same delicious fish. The price is right, but I left hungry.

Trust me to trust the Nozawa Trust Me tasting menu plus an order of uni (sea urchin) and an order of unagi (eel). Fresh seafood with sushi rice that you'll actually notice quality preparation of the rice - each roll was executed perfect and is tasty.

Called 5 times before driving there from Queens. I was told they closed their waitlist and an abnoxious "sorry" when asked why they didn't answer their phone. Another person continued to explain they choose not to answer the phone because it's too busy. Clearly their 1 min to answer the phone is  more valuable than my 30 min to travel back and forth with nothing to show for it. 

Extremely rude and unthoughtful! If you're too busy to answer the phone you should add a voice message conveying the waitlist has been closed for the night. You don't accept reservations as it is and now on top of expecting your customers to wait for a seat which they may not even get, you blatantly tell me you CHOOSE not to answer your phone. 


A business is nothing without it's customers.
Never returning.

Anticipating a long wait, we attempted to get there 15 minutes early on Sunday for lunch. Fortunate for us, even though we were late, we got seated promptly at noon despite there being a line about 10 people deep.

The server quickly went over the menu and the three of us got the $45 set, knowing we would be full half way in (yolo). Everything about the restaurant was quick, quick, quick and gave it a "fast food" vibe. In about 45 minutes, we were done with our meal. Nothing stood out but the saltiness of the soy sauce in the pieces. It overpowered the tuna and the scallops, which was the daily special. Also, the rice was too loosely packed and would fall apart after picking it up. A few of the pieces were fishy, mainly the yellowtail. 

I will give it to sugarfish that each piece was tender and almost melt in your mouth that almost made the meal.

Arrived here on a Friday exactly at 11:30 & snagged two seats at the bar without having to wait. My husband & I ordered the 'Trust Me' but were accidentally given 'The Nozawa.' I have never had sushi like the sushi I had here--it was absolutely incredible. The only down side was that the nozawa was A LOT of food and I ate until I thought I would explode, but it was so good I didn't care. 

The service was excellent as was the management. It was by far one of the best meals I've had in New York and I can't wait to go back.

The wait is horrendous - up to 4 hours. The first time we tried to eat here, we put our names down around 5:45pm and the lady told us it would be able a 3 hour wait but our table wasn't ready until about 9:30pm. Luckily, we didn't end up waiting that day since we were way too hungry for that - thank goodness! The second time we went, we weren't super hungry so we figured we could afford a 3 hour wait. We went around the same time again 5:45pm over Thanksgiving weekend and got seated around 8:30pm. We had the Nozawa Trust Me and it was great. The fish variety were definitely a bit bland and not as exotic as you would get at a true bar seated omakase but I thought everything was super fresh and tasty (I always love a good hint of yuzu pairing). I would definitely come back given that for the price, I thought it was very much a quality meal for a solid omakase. Not sure if I'd ever want to wait that long for a meal again though.

Had higher expectations for this place after all the raving reviews and how great it is in LA. I wanted to wait a few weeks before trying this new sushi spot since a couple reviews stated the wait for many hours. The three of us arrived just when it opened at noon on Sunday. There was a line out the door, so best to come about 15-20 minutes before opening to secure a seat. The placed filled up so quickly. 

After we were seated, we received menus right away. It's a pretty straight forward menu with al la carte items and three omakase style options. We opted for the "Nozawa", might as well go all out. The organic edamame came out first and it was pretty bland. Maybe I'm used to warm edamame and this was more cold/room temperature. The waiters seemed quite vigilant because right after we finished they swooped in to take away the empty plate. They do provide you with wasabi and ginger, and it was nice that they refiled the ginger without us asking. Although the slices of fish were huge and melt in yo mouth, the rice and soy sauce the chef used was way too overpowering. When I picked up a few pieces with the chopstick, the rice crumbled and fell out. The daily special of scallops was extremely fishy tasting. I wish they masked that taste, but a few of the other pieces were fishy too. The toro and blue crab hand roll were okay, nothing very special. You just had to eat it right away or else the seaweed wont' be crispy anymore. 

The meal was very fast, as we were done with the whole omakase in less than an hour. The service was on point and they did come by more than once to refill our waters and check up on us. However, maybe the experience would be different if seated at the bar? The quality of the fish was good but the soy sauce really overpowered the meal. 

Also, it's a no tipping restaurant so the whole meal was $45 + tax. They also have it to go and it's only one dollar more!

After dying internally every time I saw photos of Sugarfish LA on Instagram, I was given new life when I was told that they opened a NYC location.

I wasn't expecting to be blown away because there are so many other as notable and renowned sushi spots here as well, but I still was. 

I came at 5:45 PM on a Tuesday night, at which time there was no wait for complete parties. 15 minutes later, the wait time jumped to 30-40 minutes, but they have a waiting area upstairs, where I saw others sipping on drinks. The whole place is dimly lit and very chic. 

Service was accommodating and smooth the whole night. The hosts were happy, cool, and collecting in the chaos of guests and incomplete parties clamoring for a table at the start of the dinner rush. The host came upstairs to grab us when it was my party's turn to be seated, easing my anxiety of being missed. 

I highly recommend getting the Trust Me. It was just enough food to be happily stuffed. The second round (tuna sashimi) literally stopped the conversation in the middle of a sentence because of how incredibly soft and buttery it was. Still, the night I went, they replaced the Toro Handroll with a Salmon Handroll (but they had a special of Toro?). Salmon is my favorite though, so I wasn't too disappointed-- and I've never had such a crisp hand roll before. 

My only other qualm was that they brought out the rounds a little quicker than I'd have liked, but I am a relatively slow eater, and they did note that they'll try to slow the rounds down.

At any rate, Sugarfish has an unique taste and presentation that I think is worth going out of your way for. I know I'm definitely coming back, especially for the birthday special.

This restaurant gives me hope in humanity. I had heard great things about the LA restaurant, but never really understood why it was so famous until it opened in NYC. I went for the first time a week ago on a thursday, and to my surprise there was a 5 hour wait. Normally, this would make me mad, but not after I ate that god damn fish. 

You have to get the "trust me". It is a 6 course barrage of amazing sushi, hand rolls, edamame, and tartar. I dont know what those chefs in there are doing, but every time I bit into a piece of sushi, I got upset. It made me upset for a few reasons. Firstly, each bite meant I was nearing the end of my buffet. Next, what the hell was I doing my whole life??! This place is literally cheaper than every other lame high end asian place in NYC ( See: Nobu, Buddakan), and 10x better. I started kissing my rolls and taking selfies with them so I could savor the memories. Every day I think about this place. Sometimes I stay awake at night looking at the selfies of me and the albacore tuna roll and just thinking to myself. I have been evicted from my apartment because I spend all of my money here, and I just quit my job. Regrets? none.

All the hype and authenticity from LA, Sugarfish is incredibly affordable and serving up some simple, fresh sushi. Expect long waits...the lunch line starts way ahead of opening time with an average of an hour to an hour and a half wait; for dinner, come around 3pm and hopefully the wait will be 5 hours and not already filled for the day. 

Definitely get one of the Trust Me's to get a good tasting of their tuna sashimi, sushi assortments, and handrolls. Surprisingly, I was actually very full at the end of the meal after a Trust Me set with an extra piece of Santa Barbara uni sushi. Some pieces were a bit too sour, possibly too much yuzu which masked some of the natural flavors. The rice more than makes up for this - each grain is perfectly warm and intact like the way it should be.

The service is decent and with tips being already included it's really a great steal for the quality. Would love to come back and make lunch here a monthly recurrence!

I can see why people are talking about this place but honestly, I don't think that it is worth the hype. Considering it's price, I must admit that you definitely get a good value for the quality of the fish. By no means is it top-notch quality fish but it is good enough. However with that said, the rice had too much vinegar mixed into it and the rice was too sticky, which caused it to fall apart very easily. I want to give them the benefit of the doubt that it was just a bad batch but I guess I'll never know. My friend and I each ordered the Nozawa Trust Me and two orders of the sweet shrimp. The daily special for the day was large scallops, which were very good, a little sweet and fresh. We also wanted to get an order of the Uni sushi but to our disappointment, they already ran out of it.

We came in on a Sunday afternoon at 2:20PM and were quoted an hour wait even at such an odd time. As luck would have it, they were actually able to squeeze us into a table right away. All of the staff members were very friendly and accommodating besides this one waitress who just dropped off the sushi, mumbled something and ran away without even making eye contact.  Luckily, she only brought us one item and wasn't our main server.  I really liked the ambiance of the restaurant but I just wish that the meal didn't feel so rushed.

Delicious, fresh fish at a very affordable price. I had the nozawa trust me. 

One big mistake: the rice, it had too much vinegar and it was served WARM throughout the meal. The rice even fell apart when my friend picked it up with his chopsticks! Some pieces were extra salty due to the sauce (ponzu or soy) they put on it. On some pieces I took the rice out entirely just so I can truly appreciate the fish. I was looking forward to the Toro but I was disappointed. It was chopped up and had very little flavor.

I enjoyed the Scallops and salmon pieces.. Without the rice of course!

Luckily, we did not have to wait for a table but it is definitely not worth an hour or two wait!!!
Excellent sushi. 1.5 hour wait so be prepared to do something else in the area while you wait. Super excited to finally have a Sugarfish in NYC!

The freshest, most delicious sushi is at Sugarfish!

My husband and I both had the "Trust Me". We also split sweet shrimp and a  toro fatty tuna roll. At first, we thought we were going to be starving after our meal but little by little our bellies happily filled up.

Don't come here for rolls, just do straight up fish. They know exactly how to sauce them (if needed).

I visit LA very often and I've eaten at Sugarfish many times. I saw that New York just opened one and I wanted to check it out. The quality of food was good and what I expected, but I ordered Trust Me and a few other sushis on the side. They're supposed to give you a new dish every 5 minutes or less. I had to wait 15-20 minutes for each one to come out. The server barely checked up on us. They charged me for the sushi I ordered on the side which never came out. Overall, poor customer service and not worth the wait. Won't be coming back.
loveeee this place. amazing lunch sushi. gratuity is included so beware.
Ordered scallop, sweet shrimp, and salmon sushi, uni sushi, toro hand roll at lunch time. Quality was excellent, but little pricy and very little food. Overall I loved it.

So glad that they o-fish-ally opened in NYC! This was my go to spot for sushi in LA. I used to only eat rolls drenched in sauce and then I had sugarfish. This is your gateway sushi. Bring all your non-sushi eaters here. I guarantee you they will never go back to the AYCE sushi after eating here- or at least they will understand the diff bw AYCE sushi and real sushi.

I always get the trust me. Do NOT get the trust me lite. It's a waste of money. The lunch menu is much better valued than the dinner menu--same things, just more expensive at dinner. Lunch ends at 330. 

There wasn't a wait when i went, but i hear it's averaging around 45min - 1hr . Def worth a try if you've never been.

3 years ago I stumbled upon this unassuming sushi restaurant while traveling for business in LA. The experience was life changing.  Perfectly seasoned sushi rice, served slightly warm with amazingly fresh, melt-in-your mouth fish.  I dreamt about this place for the last 3 years, hoping that someday they would venture east to delight the palettes of my native NY.  So glad you heard my calling. Welcome to the greatest city on earth Sugarfish now all my friends will understand my obsession.  
#trustme #dontwalkrun

I really wanted to like this place but it really fell short of expectations. I was super excited to try this after hearing raving reviews about their Downtown LA location. For anyone who had omakase before, it would be a disappointment. The fish pieces are fresh which is why it is still a 3 Stars review...BUT the overly vinegar rice was unbearable. The pace was also really fast for they are serving 6 pieces of sushi per plate at a time. I would kindly ask your server to slow it down. No tipping restaurant. 

I went for the Nozoawa Trust me dinner menu which comes with Edamame, Tuna Sashimi, 10 pieces of nigiri sushi, Scallop Sushi (Daily Special of the Night) Toro Handroll, Blue Crab Handroll. Quite honestly, most of the sushi pieces taste about the same with the overly vinegar rice. To sum things up, the only ones I liked was Salmon, Scallop, and the Blue Crab Roll. 

With so much potential, I really expected more from this place. If you do wish to come here, I would anticipate a wait but there is a waiting area upstairs where you can sit. I do like the texting system that gives you notification of when your table is ready. I would not come in the evening, it is sooo dark in there. Be careful with the steps. 

Less vinegar, please!

I'm a fan. It was my 4th attempt at getting in. The first three tries came back with a 3-4 hr wait. This time I got in at an off dinner time and bam, entry! My wife thought it tasted like a regular restaurant in Japan which is on par with Japan-style. I thought it was milky, soft, smooth and fresh. Impressed and nobu-style quality. And best of all, it's the cheapest price you can find at such quality. We went for the omakase and paid just over $100 for 2 people with sake! Definitely one to add to your list.

Amazing service and food 
We went for lunch and ordered the largest set to share with two people 
They made a slight mistake by giving us food which belonged to another table but were super chill about it, apologized and didn't charge us 
Sushi was amazing and melted in your mouth instantly 
Definitely will come back again 
I stumbled upon it as there was a line outside starting at 11am!

Unreal. I highly recommend you come here. It's really inexpensive for such a high quality. I recommend the trust me....and trust me on that recommendation. The highlight was surprisingly the salmon. It was BEYOND fresh and the sesame seeds were a perfect touch. 

We came at 2pm on a Tuesday and waited about an hour for our table. They text you when your table is ready and there's a 15 minute grace period so the move is to put your name down and walk around the neighborhood.

Excellent service and delicious warm seasoned sushi with fresh fish - not adding much to what everyone else said

This place opened last month and the waits are long.  I was trolling review for recent wait times...

Came here on a Monday at 1:15 for party of 3 and waited 1 hour.

Came here tonight for a party of 2 - Wednesday night at 5:45 and it took 10 min to get in the door and to counter to put my name in.  Then I was given a estimated wait time of 3-3.5 hours.  Sure enough I was seated at 9:10.  Waiter told me that previous nights on Friday and Saturdays,  there was a 6 hour wait-insane.  I told the waitstaff that I needed to leave by a certain time and my order was impeccably timed where I was able to enjoy and get out in 40 min to catch a show.  Service here can be quick but it depends on how long patrons hang around.

The good thing is that they have a texting system and will text you when your table is ready within 15 min.  You need to text back to confirm and don't end up actively waiting,  but plan your dining time accordingly.

Once inside - excellent service and food. Gratuity is also included in the menu prices making it a good deal.

Also when you get your check,  there is a postcard inside where you can fill in your name and if you come twice,  you get a free meal on birthday...read the fine prints - was rushing out...

Not worth it. Not worth the wait. Not worth the money. Definite pass. SO LAME.  Don't believe the hype. They're so ridiculous and they don't realize they're not the only sushi place in New York City. No gluten free soy sauce

Went to Sugarfish on a Thursday before the holidays at about 1:30pm. My friend lives down the road, so she cleverly put her name on the waitlist, I hopped on the train, hung out with her for a bit and an hour and a half later we had a seat at the bar. 

We both ordered the Nozawa Trust Me set, which included 10 pieces of sushi, two hand rolls, tuna sashimi and edamame to start. Very good value for $45 including tip. The fish pieces were fresh and generously cut and the rice was slightly warm.

My only gripe (and it was a big enough one to knock off two stars) was that the rice was overly vinegared, which meant that it overpowered the fish completely. Some of the sushi pieces came with a Ponzu sauce, which was a double hit of mouth-puckering acid. Everything else was spot on, so this was a disappointment.

Service was efficient, but friendly and the food came out at a good pace. Ambiance was buzzing but not overly loud and the lighting was tastefully dark but not too dark.

Willing to give Sugarfish another try in case the vinegar issue was a case of opening jitters. So close to perfection!

Seriously THE BEST Sushi Restaurant in New York! 

The service there is amazing and everyone there is super attentive and nice. They also give great recommendations and are always available if you have any questions.

Amazing Quality, Amazing Service, Amazing Atmosphere. I'll definitely be back! 

Only setback is the wait for a table. We were told it would take 2-2.5hrs, but thankfully, it only took about 1-hour. They also have a digital list which will send you a text to notify you when you're closer to the top of list before messaging you again when your table is ready. This is great because it gives you time to go back to the restaurant instead of sitting and waiting for 1-2hrs (or more) for a table.

After wanting to try Sugarfish in LA and waiting until it opened in NYC, I was really excited to check out their sushi. I luckily didn't have to wait very long to get a seat since I went for weekday lunch but was so disappointed by the quality of food that I will definitely not be a repeat a customer. 

Process: Got there at 11am for a 11:30am opening on a Tuesday and was first in line. There really wasn't a line until about 11:20am and even then there were only about 10 people so if you're able to swing by for lunch on a weekday it's really easy to get in. 

Food: We got the Nozawa Trust Me ($45 at lunch including hospitality). Edamame was cooked perfectly and super fresh but let's be honest, I'm here for the sushi. The tuna sashimi was nothing special with a ponzu dressing. I'm not a huge fan of these preparations as it washes out the flavor of the fish. The fish was definitely good quality but nothing to rave about and the selection is pretty boring for the price point and not the usual omakase level. The most disappointing thing about the sushi was the lack of artistry. They clearly make their money from volume and they've perfected the process. It felt like factory sushi where the rice is over seasoned, way too hot and shaped using a mold versus hands. I can easily make sushi at home but I usually pay to eat out because of the skills involved in making a perfect nigiri. This is not it. If you actually appreciate the artistry of sushi chefs and love fish other than salmon, tuna, and yellowtail, stay away from Sugarfish. 

Price: $45pp for the Nozawa Trust me at lunch. I know this is supposed to be their biggest selling point but I've definitely had better sushi at this price point (especially at lunch); you just have to know where to go and stay away from the overhyped spots on the boring best of lists by Eater, Thrillist, etc. 

Service: Really weird system where each person at a table has their own waiter bringing out food. Timing isn't always perfectly synced up so it's a bit awkward since you don't want sushi sitting around for long waiting for your party to get their food. Staff were friendly but pacing of the meal was way too quick.

Pretty good value, but by far NOT the best sushi in NYC and not worth waiting for.  Fish selection pretty generic; size of fish a bit larger than average, flavor and freshness of fish also pretty average.  Rice is warm and more vinegary than usual, which I liked (I love the taste of sushi rice, but rice flavor was a bit strong relative to the fish).  My favorite item was the crab handroll, which was the only thing that was a little bit different than most other places.

Only OK.  Not worth the wait and is better in LA

The good:
-The sweet shrimp and large scallops had a nice yuzu and shiso sauce brushed on it that was interesting
-The uni was fresh and had a very delicate and soft texture
-What and yummy rice
-Blue crab hand roll was fantastic
-Friendly, fast service

The bad:
-Some pieces didn't taste very fresh
-Sesame on top just doesn't do it for me. It overwhelms the taste of the fish
-The long wait

After several times of trying to get in, I finally got there on time to be put on the wait list.
Definitely worth the wait!
The service was super attentive if at times a bit to attentive and the inclination to rush the customer. The venue had a chilled out ambience and the sushi itself was outstanding! Having tried some other high end sushi places in the city, I was impressed at the quality of the sushi and the value for money.
One of my new favorite places in NYC (helps that I live a stones throw away). Only downside is that if you don't have your name on the list by 6pm latest, you're not getting in.
Look forward to going back (if I can hack the wait).

The sushi is very good and the prices are excellent but it is hell getting into the restaurant. The first time I attempted to eat here, I came at 4pm on a Saturday and was quoted 2-2.5 hours. I didn't want to eat until later than that, so they suggested I go to a store and come back in half an hour. I did that and at 4:30 the estimated wait time was up to 4-4.5 hours. Fine. Went home, got a drink with friends. No text. Went to the restaurant at 9:30 (5 hours later and past the window they gave me). They apologized for running behind but said they were unable to give me an updated estimate. Ended up eating elsewhere and didn't get the text until 10:15. Extremely frustrating and it probably would have worked out just right if I put my name down when I first got there at 4.

Came back a few weeks later on a Friday and there estimations seem to be reliable, but it's just not worth it. I prefer being able to make a reservation even if it's hard to get.

Only go there if you don't care what time you end up eating and have zero plans the whole day. You only have 10 minutes once they text you!

I've been dying to try this place since I saw their locations in LA a few months ago (but never had a chance to dine there) so happy to hear they opened up in NYC! Got my friend to put our names down for a table at 5pm. It was approx a 3 hour wait so we only got seated at 8pm. My friends and I ordered the Trust Me - which is approx 10 pieces of sushi for $39 pp. I really liked the seabass and blue crab the best. Overall, the sushi is probably the best I have had in the city. My only complaint is that they bring out the dishes so close to one another and don't pace it out, so it feels pretty rushed. Also, tip is included in the menu price which is one less thing you have to worry about! I'd definitely come back for takeout once they start offering it. :)

I heard this is famous sushi chain which came from West coast. After my first trial here, I get why this place is famous. I personally believe that the most important part of sushi is rice underneath, not the fish. And the rice from this sushi place is probably better any sushi I had in Japan. (went to Tokyo three times, Osaka/Kyoto/Hokkaido once) However, it might not be fair to compare to list of sushi that I had in Japan because I was a student = no money = just looking for cheap sushi place back then. Now I have a job here and with this much of quality sushi? Yes for sure I will be visiting this place many times in future whenever I want to have good quality sushi. (assuming that their quality level doesn't change over time) But be careful with the waiting line. It can be like HELL or you won't be able to grab a table at all.

[Updated on 2017.07.29]
I visited this place for the second time couple months ago and the second visit was pretty much right before the restaurant was about to close. And sushi quality was far worse than when I visited here for the first time. My first visit was pretty much right after the restaurant just opened. Considering sushi deals with raw seafood, it is not nonsense that sushi quality really depends on timing when you actually visit the place. So just have that in your mind.

Absolutely amazing! Hands down the best sushi I have ever had!!

I sat at the bar, so my experience was amplified by the extremely friendly bartender.  The service was some of the best I have experienced. The food quality is amazing and cooked to pure perfection!

The food was stellar, but as others have said, this place is a massive asspain to get a table in.   They don't accept reservations and are terrible at estimating.   This place is the stereotypical NYC abusive restaurant- habitually disrespectful of patrons' time.   If you like being convinced a restaurant is exclusive and delicious because it abuses you with multi-hour waits, you'll love this place.   A lot of NYers are into that, but it's not my thing.  I'd rather just make a reservation and come back later.   

If you do get in, order the omakase, like you probably should at every sushi restaurant.   The food is excellent and some of the best fish I've had in ages.   Atmosphere is very "contemporary American restaurant", but meals are pretty standard Japanese fare.

The food is good. Nothing especially amazing and it seems everyone loves the price point, but I would rather pay more for a real omakase experience rather than sitting at a table and having food churned out super quickly. I felt rushed the whole time and one server even made a comment that she would tell the kitchen to slow down the dishes since she saw that we were not eating as quick as the dishes came out. The restaurant is also very dark so it was difficult to see the food. There also wasn't any wasabi in the nigiri so don't forget to do it yourself.

Living in LA, I've been to many a sugar fish out here so it was pretty cool to see one in NY. Unfortunately this one didn't quite live up to what I'm used too (I get it, it's harder to get fresh fish like in LA) but here's my experience

- Fish quality. I mean I don't expect fresh but some of the sushi had a strange after taste imo. Don't know if fish in NY waters are different if not but it was odd.

- a little pricier than LA.

- the wait sucks. It's new and NY is crowded but waiting to get in was not fun.

- the place is cramped.

Of course I'll always trust chef nozawa and his sushi but I think I'll stick with sugar fish in LA and eat sushi elsewhere when I'm in NY.

I was using both hands to eat so obvi I was servicing the food and myself. Had to use both knees at one point. I personally don't enjoy a sugary fish, especially when it results in peeing sitting down. Thanks.

Accommodating and helpful staff, chic decor, and excellent fish. Definitely recommend the Trust Me menu. Highlights we're albacore, salmon sushi, and tuna hand roll. Definitely recommend making a reservation.
Just as good as the one in LA! Everyone was so friendly and attentive. Definitely worth the wait. Will be back.

The food was by far THE best I have ever had. It was so delicious and fresh.  The service was excellent. I highly recommend sugarfish. There will be a wait, but the food and service is definitely worth the wait.
SUGARFISH is by far the BEST SUSHI on the planet.  The service at this location is superb and the food is outstanding.  I recommend this to everyone.

Awesome! Just as good as the Sugarfish that I love so much in Beverly Hills, California. Super, fresh and delicious sushi for a reasonable price. Service was a bit in the weeds so hopefully they add some floor staff. Like the bar in the back for solo dining. Terrific lunch spot, I will be back.

Omasake at a very reasonable price. We had the "trust me" and ordered the sweet shrimp and uni a la carte. Everything on the "trust me" was delicious and the rice on the sushi was perfectly seasoned. The uni was buttery and sweet. However, my sister and I did not like the sweet shrimp at all and the waiter came over and asked us if everything was alright because he noticed that we were both cringing. He offered to take the dish off of our check and notify the kitchen. Service was great.

This place doesn't take reservation and it's a long wait even on a weeknight. For a table of 2 on a Wednesday night, we waited about 2 hrs for a table but it's worth the wait. The fish was fresh and the sushi was serve at the perfect temperature.  The omakase was only $39, can't beat that for this quality of sushi and hand rows! The $39 also includes the tips, it's a not tips restaurant. I'm impressed with the food and the service. I will certainly be back soon!

I really wanted to love this place, but it was a HUGE disappointment. We came in on Saturday at 4pm and guy who was accepting reservations told us that approximate wait time was 1 to 2 hours. We put our names on the list and went to hang out nearby. Two hours later we dropped by Sugarfish to check on status of our reservation. Same guy told us that we still need to wait around 2 hours!???? Why the heck did you tell us that wait time was 2 instead of 4 hours at the first place??!!! Starving to death we went to another Japanese place nearby and gave up our reservation. If you wanna eat at Sugarfish you'd better wake up at 9 am and put your name on the list. Horrible reservation system and total lack of respect for customers. Never again!

Came at around 4 pm on a Sunday and waited about an hour, so not too bad. My two friends and I did the Trust Me lite, and it was definitely enough food. Everything was pretty good, but the pacing was annoying at times (they'd bring dishes while we were still finishing others). The red snapper was absolute perfection, and I really enjoyed the tuna poke, too. Overall I'd recommend it.

Went for lunch and ordered a la carte. The manager did not bother to write down the order, as a result random pieces of sushi we did not order arrived on our table. She was generally apologetic and offered pieces that we did not order on the house, however the experience was very confusing. Fish was fresh in general. Will go back again as their price is very reasonable.

Nice new addition to the NYC sushi scene, which has lots of bad, cheap sushi and lots of incredible, ultra-pricey sushi but little in between.

The "Trust Me" ($33 at lunch, service included) was a parade of clean, fresh bites and hand rolls. Only complaint would be that the flavors were a bit monotonous -- you're not getting any remotely adventurous pieces of seafood here.

Overall a fine spot, with the caveat that we arrived early for lunch and were seated right away - no way I'd wait an hour for the experience.
Service was good and fast during mid weekday. All the fish was fresh, especially the Uni was amazing sweet and fresh. One down side about the rice : too much vinegar and fo not stick.

Ordered the "trust me"

Fish was good (not spectacular, not amazing, just good) You can get the same quality at decent Japanese restaurants, not those fast food ones. Some reviews complaining about sour rice. I think it was just the pieces that came with sauce on the sushi already. It was the sauce that was sour, not the rice. Didn't bother me.

-Unsuccessfully tried to get in twice: 4:30 and 5PM on a Tuesday/Friday, there was no wait. I had expected a long wait (planned on putting name on list) so party was incomplete. Came back 30 min later with full party and the wait was up to 4 hours. LOL---I did not wait. 
-3rd time I successfully got in with minimal wait by lining up maybe 15 min before store opened for lunch. Line got pretty long by the time store was opening. 
-restaurant feels very corporate, try calling them, you can't get a person on the line
-staff was very attentive

I don't think this place lived up to the hype, please don't wait over an hour for this unless you were already in the neighborhood.

Sweet, fresh fish from the newest sushi hot spot in town isn't always what it seems. 

Ever since Sugarfish opened up, I knew my best chance of getting a seat was right before the lunch rush. I was luckily in charge of organizing a team lunch and per the recommendation of the hosts from the previous night when I stopped by, I was able to snag a table for four by arriving around 11:15 to wait on line for the first seating at 11:30.

We had the choice of the bar or a table and we opted for the bar for the experience. Don't be fooled though, the bar is literally just a bar. The sushi is made in the kitchen and there isn't really a view. All we saw were water glasses and POS systems. We all went for the Nozawa Trust Me, which gave us a little bit of everything. Edamame promptly came out and we were on our way.

Tuna sashimi was a great starter. The yuzu ponzu was a nice pairing with the thinly sliced tuna, although I thought a few slices were a bit too thin and lost that meatiness you typically get with thick slices of sashimi. Next came the albacore tuna and salmon. The salmon was soo tender and tasty. The fattiness was unlike anything else I've eaten, and I appreciated the extra seasoned sushi rice. It wasn't too sticky, too heavy, or too bland. It had a great balance of vinegar and substance. The albacore was also a tasty fish to nibble on.

The next plate had a hit and a few misses. The yellowtail was so tender and soft, it was definitely the best yellowtail I've ever had. The scallops weren't a home run, but I appreciated the daily special's natural sweetness and how that was allowed to shine on the plate. There was a strange peppery aftertaste that I couldn't figure out if it was intentional or just my imagination.The sea bass and snapper, however, were both pretty disappointing. Both were very fibrous and hard to eat. The flavor also wasn't memorable and I wanted to quickly move on to the other pieces.

The final two courses were the hand rolls, which I theoretically would've loved. However, again, they both failed to meet my expectations.
