The seaweed used was so heavy in flavor that it covered up the profiles of the both fishes. The toro had basically no flavor and the mushy substance didn't chalk up to an enjoyable chew. The blue crab was very fresh, but 3/5 of my bites were filled with shells, making it very very hard to enjoy.

The service was pretty decent throughout, although only one person actually knew what each fish was. When they were served, the woman sped through the names so quickly that even when I asked her to repeat them, I only heard half of them. Alex at the bar was much more accommodating and patient in describing the food.

Yes, $45 for a lunch omakase isn't crazy, but it's almost to the level of a power lunch. If I had to shell out for this myself, I would've been very very disappointed. Now that I know, I won't be recommending to my friend's to wait on line and to let the hype die down if they still really want to try Sugarfish. I would recommend either saving up for the next level omakase if you're looking for an extra special and tasty sushi experience.

Casual, affordable and SUPER DUPER delicious sushi restaurant in NYC. One of my favs, for sure! 

FINALLY GOT TO TRY SUGARFISH and I can thoroughly impressed with my experience! 

Came here on a snowy Saturday night, hoping people really arent going to trek out there to try some bomb sushi. Oh boy, I was wrong. We put our names down around 5:30pm, was quoted about 2-2.5hr wait. Dinosaur and I decided to stick around and grab some drinks nearby while we waited.

After 2 hours, we were seated at the counter right next to the kitchen! Our server, Alex, was super sweet and gave us his favorites and recommendations. We got 2 Trust Me and a Lobster and Toro split cut roll. 

Favs of the night:
*Salmon sushi: the sesame seeds takes the dish onto a whole new level of goodness. Super fresh sushi that literally melts in your mouth. 

*Toro handroll: Dino and I both agree that the nori is what makes the handrolls special - crispy, warm and doesn't stick to the roof of your mouth. What's the secret Sugarfish! Dino and I visited Kazunori, their sister restaurant in LA, and their handrolls were SO GEWD!! Sugarfish's was the pretty much the same.

Trust me is DEFINITELY enough food for one human, maybe not a Dinosaur. I had to surrender a couple pieces to Dino because I was way too full and he was still a bit hungry. 

Expect a wait, but that's a good sign to a good sushi restaurant. Ample waiting area upstairs as well. There are really good weekend happy hour places nearby so those few hours will fly by! My favs are The Cellar and Punch.

Arrived around 5pm on a Friday and ended up being a 3 hour+ wait for a table for 4. 

That said the experience and food definitely lived up to the hype. Can't believe the quality of the food for the cost. At a time when omakase options are running at least $150, for $40 you get the same quantity and quality- just comes attached to a ridiculous wait. 

Will be back but prob when the lines die down a bit.

Good quality fish for the price. However, don't expect to have your mind blown away or anything.

I came with the bf on a weekday at around 3pm. They quoted us a 2-3 hour wait, but texted us after 1 hour that the table was ready. We got the Nozawa ($51) and the Trust Me ($39). Out of the fish that came out, everything was fresh and good quality. However, the rice was a little too vinegary and sweet, and too warm for how sushi rice is supposed to come out (One of the handrolls almost burnt my boyfriend's mouth it was so hot). The only outstanding sushi pieces were the Albacore Tuna. Everything else was enjoyable, but nothing special.

We also ordered some uni sushi ($15 for 2 pieces) off the menu. They told me it was Santa Barbara uni and fresh, and it was the best decision we made. I'm a huge uni fan, so I was excited. It did not disappoint and the uni was melt in your mouth good. Definitely get the uni.

Overall, there are actually other pretty affordable places that beat sugarfish in NYC in my opinion. However, not a bad meal for the price (tip is also included). If I come back, I will be ordering albacore sushi, uni sushi, and maybe some other things off their menu instead of the trust me or nozawa. The wait is crazy though and we went at an off-peak time on a weekday too.

sooooooooooo good!!! 

besides having to wait online for 30 minutes to then put yourself on a list that could be an additional 1-3 hours... if you can dedicate the time, do it. the food is amazing.

Sushi was amazing and incredibly fresh. Most notable differentiating factor that sets this sushi place apart from competition is the warm rice. The flavors marinates better to taste, allowing for a happy marriage of fresh fish and warm rice. Every piece of fish was incredibly fresh and prepped with immense effort. We ordered the table d'hôte, went with the "Trust me", a bit more expensive than the one other option, but completely worth it. 

Tip: Waiter will tell you, but the sushi that already comes with sauce on it, do NOT dip in other sauce or soy sauce! Will ruin the experience of how that particular piece of sushi was meant to taste. :)

The "Trust Me", consisted of: (everything was amazing, but my favorite ones are basically all the ones with sauce). 
1. Organic edamame 
2. Tuna sashimi
3. Albacore sushi 
4. Salmon sushi
5. Yellowtail sushi
6. Hirami sushi
7. Toro hand roll
8. Blue crab hand roll

I tried Kazunori, the famous handroll restaurant in LA, and I was hooked. When I found out sugarfish (same owners), was opening in the Flatiron District- I was beyond happy. Not sure if the lines have become shorter, but my first time I went, it was a three hour wait and the next time, the line was so long that they cut the waiting  list even though we arrived at 6pm. So arrive early, put your name down, and plan on waiting... but the wait is DEFINITELY worth it. Never have I had sushi so buttery that it melts on your mouth.

Was so sad when leaving Los Angeles because I wouldn't have Sugarfish as often, but to my surprise they opened here, and I could not be happier. They are so consistently good at every location.

Yes, there is usually a long wait, no they do not take reservations. I always find it quite amusing when people get angry about long waits... if a place is good... this will happen.. its expected. I also find complaints about them not taking reservations amusing, because 1. if they did, these same people would be mad that they could never get one, and 2. Sugarfish has a pretty quick turn around due to the style of service and menu,  and they are always packed.... I wouldn't take reservations either. #rantover

Everything is melt in your mouth fresh. I go with the trust me/nozawa everytime, and I have not been disappointed. 

Sometimes the dishes come out too fast, ( usually this is not a problem for me because its so good I usually eat it before my plate hits the table) but all you have to do is ask them to slow it down a bit and they oblige. Everything is meant to be eaten right away to truly taste the flavors and warm rice, not to sit in front of you while you tell your "really important" story ;)  

If you accept that this is a unique type of restaurant, and get over having to wait for delicious sushi, then you will probably become addicted,  which will suck... because then I'll have to wait longer... #worthit

Terrific sashimi, great menu - we each did the Nozawa Trust Me with an added order of uni, plus a few bottles of the house sake.

The good: delicious and fresh sashimi and hand rolls at a very reasonable price. 

The odd: Well-meaning details, like pre- and post-dinner soaps (pre- unscented to not disrupt your meal, post- scented, when I guess it no longer matters) - both were the same awful pink, scented hand soap you get at every restaurant. I don't care, but then don't have different pre- and post-meal soap dispensers.

The bad: Rushed and somewhat disjointed service. Two to three hour wait for a 40 minute meal. 

Verdict: go if you can get in despite the wait, and don't mind feeling rushed after said wait. Go for the quality and price, just don't expect to feel like you ate at Daniel. I'd return, if for nothing else but the salmon sashimi and blue crab hand roll.

I came here on a Monday at 11:15 (mind you, they open at 11:30) and was already the 10th person on line. By the time it was 11:30, the line was down the block. I'd definitely recommend coming early as you have to wait for the entire first seating to finish eating before you get seated! They only seat full parties. I can't imagine what weekdays look like here.

Quality: 5/5. I love love love that they serve sushi here over warm rice. Reminds me of Sushi Yasuda in that regard. The quality of the fish was great and was allowed to shine through (not like Sushi of Gari where it's a lot more adornments). They don't have cool stuff like seared/torched fish probably because they're pumping these out like water. But for $33 for the trust me menu (included edamame, tuna sashimi app, 6 pieces of sushi and 2 hand rolls), it's a great deal - which explains why the line is so long. I'd definitely come back here again but I had a great experience given I waited 15 min. I'm sure if I were waiting for an hour my experience would be different.

Service: 5/5. We were a party of three and the dishes all came out within 30 seconds of each other. Plates were cleared quickly and we got free refill of hot green tea (aka they put more hot water in it, but still nice). The servers were very friendly and genuine despite not being able to get tips here! Service was extremely fast and we were not kept waiting long between courses (we all had the trust me menu which was perfect for lunch).

Ambiance: 5/5. Looked modern and clean, chairs were comfy. Table spacing was perfect.

My friends who live on the West Coast are always blathering about how much better sushi (and Mexican food, and weather) is out there. I can forgive their regional bias because in my benevolence, I'm tolerant of people that are obviously inferior to New Yorkers in every way imaginable.*

And I've had sushi out there. It's largely the same as it is here. 

So when a few of my co-workers that used to live in California (and wisely moved to NYC) were hyped up on Sugarfish coming east, I tempered my expectations. I patiently waited with them before we sat down to our first lunch here.

And then I was blown away, because Sugarfish is truly on another level. In all seriousness, this is some of the better sushi I've had in my life, and that is no exaggeration. It is buttery, melt-in-your-mouth perfection, and it doesn't cost me over $100 for lunch. These are things that don't often coincide in the sushi world. This is the elusive, magical Manhattan sushi that lives in the middle (absurdly high quality, without the corresponding absurd prices).

The most popular choices on the menu are various forms of Trust Me, and you should trust them. They care about their food, and your enjoyment of it. 

They make pointed suggestions as to how and when to eat each course.
They insist you eat the hand rolls while the nori is still crisp. 
They made me like hand rolls (unheard of). 
They said nothing as I shoveled tuna sashimi into my face, uncontrollably.
They served us albacore (sustainability!), and it was fantastic.
They have two different hand soaps in the bathroom, unscented for before your meal, and scented for after. FOR PETE'S SAKE.

So to my West Coast friends who insist that your sushi is better...is this what you were talking about? If Sugarfish was the only sushi joint in California, I might believe you. Even though I don't like being wrong.

We actually had more than a few service issues (the host needs some training on how not to ruin everything, our server stole my water glass and gave back one that was probably tainted by one of my dirty companions, and said dirty companion kept having to wait while the rest of us were given our deliciousness several minutes before him**)...and of course there's the wait which they could handle better (NoWait exists now everyone)...but I can't justify docking them a star, despite all that. The sushi is just too good. 

I guess the bright side of being wrong is that I never have to go to LA again, because Sugarfish is here now. 
_____________

*What is this hypocrisy you speak of?
**This was kind of funny, but only because it was him.

Melt in your mouth sushi, without flying to Japan. There will always be a wait, but it's worth it! My crew waited about 1hr, but I've heard of 4+ hr waits on busy night. My favorite piece was the albacore. The staff is very attentive. Eat the pieces as soon as they come out from the kitchen!

So I've been to the one in LA and fell in love! When I found out there was one in NY I had to give it a try. Wait time I heard could be hours but I guess we got pretty luck the host said it was a 15-30 minute wait for a party of two, within 5 minutes we got seated. Service was amazing no complaints at all. Food I'd give a 3.5 out of 5, we both had The Nozawa which was good but I feel like the one in LA was better. Some of the fish had a really fishy taste but other then that it wasn't bad

OMG.  I had never been to SugarFish before, but love sushi.  It's sort of a passion.

My friend had been to a location in LA, and I was eager to check it out.

We got to the restaurant on a Monday morning at 11:44am (it opens at 11:30am) and all the tables were taken, and there was a line around the block to put in your name.  This is what we expected, so no worries.  It's a day-long commitment to getting a table.

By 12:08pm we had put our name in, and were told it was about 1 hour to 1 hour 30 minutes wait.  We wandered around the neighborhood and were texted to return to the table after 1 hour 30 minutes, then re-checked in and waited for our table.

At 1:45pm we were at a table, tummies rumbling and minds preparing to be blown away.

We both ordered the Nozawa and it was transformational.  We started with the edamame, which was a nice, palate cleansing starter.  We then received the tuna tartare which was beautifully presented in a flower-shape and in a lovely, light ponzu.

We then moved on to the sushi.  I've never had albacore and salmon that literally melt in my mouth.  The real distinction was the rice - it was warm and seasoned so perfectly to compliment the fish, but maintain its own soft, textured, vinegar essence.

We then had the scallop (daily special), snapper, yellowtail, tuna and hirame.  All the fish was delicious, but the stand outs were the albacore, salmon and scallop.

The meal ended with a tuna hand roll then a blue crab hand roll. Both were exceptional, and the blue crab really stood out with its briny, creaminess.

We then ordered one more order of albacore and salmon because they were *that* good.

To give you an idea of how transformational this meal was, I literally closed my eyes every time I ate a piece of sushi and just relished in the moment.  Life.  Changing.

I will definitely be back, when I have time to wait for a couple of hours.  Definitely worth it for the price, the service, and the quality of the food that is clearly hand crafted, with every minute detail poured over to give you the best experience.  

It's an experience for the soul.

there's nothing negative to say about this place. i did the chef sushi tasting, i believe that is the only way to do it. the food is beyond delicious, literally the best sushi of my life. i will be back on any occasion i can get in.

I came the first month they opened when it was crazy to get a table.. but I hear since then its not too bad. They DONT take reservations--- &  you can't get passed the automated machine when you wanna call to see if they're still taking walk ins for the day. Meh.

I hopped on the train & took the chance anyway. I showed up at 8:45pm on a Thursday Night (thinking I'd have less of a wait because its after the dinner rush) and the hosts said they stopped taking new walk ins at 6:30pm... they were booked the rest of the night! I begged.... "PLEASE I came an hour from queens, and I'm just a party of one!"

The host was polite & with a huge smile said "wait its just you? Let me see, we actually have a single seat at the bar!"  Boy, I was SO happy!

I ordered the NOZAWA TRUST ME. It includes an edamame app, 2 handrolls & 13 individual pieces.... for $51 dollars (tip was included already) that wasn't bad AT ALL for fresh dinner ....& I was def satisfied. 

I LOVED the taste of the blue crab handroll! I wanted to order another one but the waiter suggested I try something new since it was my first time. He suggested the lobster handroll....and it was GLORIOUS. No regrets.

I was on a roll (literally), I decided to order a sake bottle for myself-- not sure what possessed me to do that but I was so happy hahaha & it was the perfect ending to my dinner. 

****The rice of the sushi is a little on the vinegary side which some people hate (but I personally like).*

Definitely in my top 5 for omakase in NYC because of the price. If you go for lunch, the Nozawa Trust Me is $45 (including tip). People said sugarfish is just okay, but for $51 and whats included in it.... its definitely a bang for your buck for some fresh bomb tasting sushi!

I don't know how to rate this place. Most reviews are relative. Some places are just not worth the pay but I wouldn't go back to this place even if someone paid me unless it was just to drink.

Wanted to see what the fuss was about because of its popularity in California. Had the Nozawa trust me menu and the very dry sake.

Sake added the star. I understand most fish is flash frozen to a degree but when it's a place with a three hour wait, you shouldn't have to taste the fish still defrosting in your mouth. The special scallop nigiri was beyond fishy - I could not get the taste out of my mouth. Toro and crab handroll - didn't finish.

If you actually enjoy fresh fish and not just a trendy spot. Go elsewhere.

The one in LA is definitely better. The fish was great and the service was great. But the ambiance is lacking--you're basically eating in an underdecorated room with no flair or anything special. 

It's definitely a good idea to do one of the omikase choices...it's TONS of food

I'm going to hate myself for giving out this little secret, but coming on Sundays for lunch is amazing. My wife and I had no preconceptions about getting into the city early enough to wait in line for the first seating, and were even prepped with backups in case the wait was too long. But Sunday seems to be the day that just... works. I've been told that if you show up by ~11:45AM, you'll be able to make it in for the first seating. YMMV. For us, since we showed up right around noon, we missed out and had to wait, but the text system employed by Sugarfish gives you a much longer leash than other restaurants. In the 45 min we had to roam around, we walked through Eataly, took some snaps of the Flatiron Building, joking debated eating at Shake Shack, and people watched at Madison Sq Park for a couple minutes. For those who just want to sit and wait, there's a seating area upstairs where you can chill out as well.

Our server Sophia was super friendly and awesome. There aren't a ridiculous amount of options here, even self-noted by the waitstaff, but what they do have, they do it good. Real good. I'm super happy that Sugarfish exists as an option to occupy the sweet spot of casual but really friggin' awesome sushi. I not made of money. I can't have omakase every day. But, can I spare $65 for a treat every couple of months? Yeah. Definitely.

BTW if there are ever scallops or sweet shrimp on the menu... get it.
Really great value in consideration of high prices for quality sushi elsewhere in the city. Speedy service and a cool atmosphere.

Small, unpretentious, chain from LA that serves a limited menu of high quality sushi at affordable (by sushi standards, anyway) prices. There is a bit of a wait, although coming for first seating or at an off time is probably your best bet at a shorter one.

You can choose from three fixed menu's. I recommend getting the Nozawa Trust Me with the most offerings. It was enough food for me, although I think my husband would have been hungry if we didn't also order a couple of pieces a la carte.

On the day we went, the Nozawa Trust Me featured edamame, albacore(2), salmon(2), yellowtail belly(2), sea bass(1), snapper(1), daily special scallops(2), a toro hand roll, and a blue crab hand roll. Everything was fresh and flavorful, if not slightly over sauced. If you like shoyu, ponzu, and vinegar, which I do in varying amounts, then I think this flavor profile will really work for your palate.

The two a la carte items - albacore belly and the sweet shrimp (ebi) were really delicious as well.

Tipping is already included, which I really liked.
Service was very good and their table system is on point.

This is going to change things around here.

My friend and I went into the restaurant at around 2:00 on a Saturday. The wait was 2.5 hours. Luckily, they take your phone number and text you when you're table is ready. This allowed us to go around the city and wait for our reservation. We both ordered the "trust me." The sushi was served warm and was so delicious. The only down side was I found a bone in my salmon, I immediately told the waitress and she brought me a new plate and apologized. I would go again simply for the hand rolls which are to die for. The atmosphere is nice, small and casual.

I have to prepare you beforehand, be prepared to wait we had an 1.5 hour wait to be seated for a table of three. I went into the evening thinking I am never coming back here in my natural life. I was proven wrong, I will definitely be back. The reason the food just everything was out of this world amazing, you should realize the wait will happen, and accept and dedicate the time because your taste buds will be thanking you for the rest of the night.   The Tuna Sashaimi with the sauce and the scallions...I cannot say enough, it simply melts in your mouth so delicious.  We also had a toro fatty tuna roll and the "Trust Me".  You can trust this yelper, everything we had that night was beyond scrumptious it was a dining experience for the ages.   The sauces that come with the fish are to die for.  This place...yes you are going to be waiting on a line, but the prices are worth the tasty experience and the wait is also worth it.   Give this place a try one night, you will so not regret it.  One last thing the staff were also very courteous and friendly tried to make the wait in lines as painless as possible. Again, this place is worth the waiting in line.

Not great, not terrible.

Don't get the fascination with this place, I guess since it's new, and I'm sure, given the competition around, it will all calm down very soon.

Last time had Lobster Roll and Blue Crab roll.

Both ground up, I guess lobster and crab, with whatever else is added to create more volume.

Staff was nice, but messed up order, which is odd too for a place where people wait on a line to eat.

Wait for 1 to 2 hours or more, be rushed to your table, order quickly, get your edamame cold, then have the waiter slaps plates after plates of fish with warm rice,lot of rice, more rice. This is the Olive Garden of sushi. If you love sushi, don't waste your time. You are being rushed, served a rushed sushi! Not worth even considering going there!
It's just ok. If you never had sushi then maybe go... otherwise I wouldn't go. Seems like sushi here are geared towards sushi newbies.... go to places like sushi yasuda or oya for great sushi.

The sushi and sashimi here were just ok. The Trust Me menu came with very basic selections such as tuna, salmon, scallop, red snapper, albacore, yellowtail, crab meat handroll, and a tuna handroll. The sea urchin was decent. This is by no means anywhere near the top quality sushi (ichimura, shuko, etc) that NYC has to offer. I'd put this one in the medium quality category. It's definitely not worth the 2 to 3 hour wait. People are just coming here for the scene, not the food. This is by far the most overhyped restaurant I've been to in NYC.

We heard great reviews about this restaurant and been wanting to try this place. We arrived at the restaurant at 12p on Saturday and saw there wasnt much of a wait time since no one was there in the front. However, we asked the hostess how long was the wait and he said about 45 minutes. We put our name and number down.  After 30 minutes, we received a text that our table will be ready soon and we waited additional 20 minutes.  After getting seated, we ordered the "Trust Me" for lunch. The tuna sashimi was decent but it had a lot of the citrus flavor mixed in. As for the other sashimi, it was also decent but not all that fresh. The experience was not memorable and we had better sushi at other sushi restaurants.

Sugarfish, a very popular sushi restaurant in LA, has finally landed in NYC! Sugarfish, opened by chef Kazunori Nozawa, prides itself on delivering the classic omakase experience without the traditional omakase price point. Sugarfish also features Chef Nozawa's signature warm sushi rice, which is a new experience for those of us who are used to the more traditional sushi rice preparations.

In classic NYC-style, the wait times for Sugarfish have been insane. On any given day, for lunch and for dinner, the wait times can go up to 2.5 hours. I came in with a party of 3 on a random Tuesday afternoon and we were quoted a 1.5 hour wait. It was more or less about that time - but there is a waiting area upstairs where the restrooms are that they don't really advertise.

Once seated, our waiter came over to explain their menu. They're known for their three omakase menus: the Trust Me ($33), the Trust Me Lite ($23), and the Nozawa Trust Me ($45). Each menu has some of the same basic items, but the two more expensive menus feature a little more extra as the price point goes up. We opted for 2 Trust Me's - to keep it simple. The "Daily Special" was Large Scallops, which we ended up ordering on the side to try.

First up was the Organic Edamame, which was served chilled. I actually like chilled edamame since it's not as mushy as warm edamame. This was a nice opening to our meal! Next up was the Tuna Sashimi, which came pre-marinated. I really enjoyed the dish - the sashimi was fresh and the marinate was tangy and sweet at the same time.

The first two pieces of sushi to arrive was the Albacore and Salmon. The Albacore came pre-sauced, so we were advised not to dip it in sauce sauce. The Albacore practically melted in our mouths - it was so soft and moist. The Salmon, however, was my favorite piece. It's perhaps because I've always been partial to salmon, but boy was it fresh and delicious!

Our last two pieces of sushi to arrive was the Yellowtail and, since they ran out of Hirame that day, the Sea Bass. The Yellowtail was very tasty - but the highlight of the plate was the Sea Bass. I've never had Sea Bass sushi before so this was a real treat. It came pre-sauced with a spicy, tangy sauce that really helped highlight the freshness and clean-taste of the fish.

Our first hand roll to arrive was the Toro Hand Roll. They recommend that all hand rolls be eaten as soon as they arrive since the warm rice will cause the seaweed to wilt. Definitely be sure to eat it as soon as it arrives because crisp seaweed really adds to the mouth-feel of the roll. The toro was tender and melts in your mouth.

I thoroughly enjoyed the previous hand roll but was completely blown away by the Blue Crab Hand Roll! The blue crab was moist, fresh, and had just a hint of saltiness. This is definitely my favorite hand roll of the two.

We finished our meal with our added order of Large Scallop ($7.00). The scallop was super sweet and very fresh - something that's a common theme at Sugarfish. If you're a fan of scallops, definitely get yourself an order!

Service was attentive and sufficient. Due to the fact that all items are served as they are made, sometimes we all didn't have a particular dish at the same time. This wasn't a huge issue as they're meant to be eaten as soon as they're placed onto the table, but it was a tad awkward to be at a different pace as my other dining partners.

I really liked that gratuity is included in the price of the meal - just like restaurants in Japan! All in all, Sugarfish serves up some really delicious and quality sushi. It's not the best sushi I've had (in NYC and in Japan), but for the price point, it really cannot be beat.

High quality sushi that comes in standardized combo.

Recommended by a friend as it is really popular in LA so came with friends to try to NYC shop. Came at 11:45 AM while the shop opens at noon. Already a lot of people waiting so if you want to beat the lunch rush at weekends, COME EARLY. Otherwise, 1 hour of wait is normal. The place isn't small though so it must be that it is super popular.

Here you could order a la carte but most people choose from one of the three combos - trust me lite ($23), trust me ($33) and Nozawa trust me ($43). I did just Trust Me as I was told it was already enough for one person and it turned out true. 

The good thing about the combo is that it is served course by course rather than at the same time on a big plate. According to the server, they want to make sure once the sushi is made, it is immediately delivered to the customer to make sure it is fresh. I love this attitude.

The wasabi they provided looked very fresh - unlike the one you can find in the cheap restaurant or supermarket (which is very sticky and too green with additives), this one was actually more powdery and less green - it was from the actual wasabi plant and was grounded fresh. It was also less spicy. From the wasabi, you can know the quality of sushi.

Sushi course by course:

- Organic edamame: surprisingly extremely GOOD! You would think this as regular edamame but this is not. The salt is in the water where it was cooked and the beans inside themselves are better breeds than the normal ones.

- Tuna sashimi: the fish was fresh but the sauce was mediocre. Just soy sauce and some scallion.

- Albacore sushi: the sauce was good - there was some garlic in it. 

- Salmon sushi: AMAZING! Besides the fresh fish, the temperature of sushi rice was just right - lukewarm, which helped the taste of rice and fish blend together

- Yellowtail and Hirame sushi: good but nothing too special.

- Toro (fatty tuna) roll: it didn't taste as good as real fatty tuna in one piece - the toro in the roll was minced and it was not as fragrant as the one chunk fatty tuna I had in Japan. Unimpressive

- Crab roll: a lot of crab inside and delicious!

If you are still hungry, you can order sushi a la carte but I felt it was enough for me, who usually have pretty big appetite.

Hot green tea is recommended as drink, which doesn't interfere too much with the fresh fish taste and helps you digest and clear off the taste in your mouth for the next course.

Great experience -- scallop, Santa Barbara uni, and their marinated albacore tuna were definite standouts. 

I've been to the Sugarfish in Santa Monica, and the taste & service is very consistent. Obviously get there early as there are huge waits.

LOVE this place. I was a regular at Sugarfish in LA - Marina Del Rey, DT and Brentwood. I was just saying a few months ago how NYC is just missing a Sugarfish... and voila! 

I visited the NYC location today for the first time, and the fish and service were excellent as usual. BUT, the rice was not as warm and as 'melt in your mouth'-ish as LA. My friend agreed and she and I lived in LA together ;) We may have gone on an off time, and hopefully next time we go it'll be back to 'normal' and we won't have to chew as much as we did (that is the beauty of Sugarfish -- to have everything just melt in your mouth). 

Anyway, it is absolutely delicious regardless and one of the best sushi experiences of all time. Crossing fingers the next time we go, the rice is warmer! 

TIP: Go mid-day BEFORE 5:30 p.m. It gets packed quickly!

We finally were able to go this place after trying to put our names down the list 4 times previously. We were told the list was closed for the night, or the line of people that were trying to get on the list was way too long. Fortunately we live in the neighborhood, so it was easy to stop by before or after gym a few days in a row, until we succeeded to finally be on their list.
They texted us 15' before so we walked again from home there, I don't know how ppl that live other places can actually wait or get there in time. 
We were asked if we are ok with sitting at the bar, which I usually love because I imagined a raw bar setup. Little did we know that that bar is around the waiters cleaning area, and it actually feels that you are around the trash area. The Trust Me Menu started disappointingly with some cold and plane edamame, that did not even have plain salt on them. Since we were staying at that station, we noticed the edamame were on plates already and covered in plastic wrap in advance, maybe like in an airplane, but even in airplanes, they actually warm them up and put some spice on them before serving. The rest of the sushi pieces from the omakase-like menu were actually very good and they were more than enough for us. But New York has a lot of other very good sushi places that spare you from that list drama that is waisting a lot of time, and also other places serve warm edamame seasoned with hot delish spices.

Fresh and filling omakase for $43 or less?! Doesn't get sweeter than Sugarfish!

Originally a chain from LA, Sugarfish has finally made it's way to the "feast" coast. You can choose from three sets or go a la carte or do a combination of both. We decided to go big or go home with the Nozawa trust me set ($43) although cheaper alternatives Trust me lite ($23) and Trust me ($33) were available. The Nozawa Trust me differs from the Trust me set by offering the "special" and an additional set of sushi. 

The fish was delightfully fresh and was so soft it melted and became one with my tongue. My favorite was the hamachi and salmon. There were also some unique nigiri- like sea bass, which is something I have never had raw. The set also comes with hand rolls, and I found the blue crab to be scrumptious. My complaint is that I found some of the nigiri to be over-seasoned, almost sopping, and the rice sadly just fell apart many a times from the fish when I was trying to enjoy my meal. 

Consensus: Wouldn't wait 2-3 hours for it, but for a 30 min wait (1pm lunch on a weekday) and for the price it is well worth it! It's no Sushi Nakazawa but a girl's got to get her sushi fix! 10/10 would come again for some more Sugarfish!

I've been to the LA location of Sugarfish so I was excited to have it arrive in NYC.  Beware of the long wait though.  If you come before 6pm, the wait is about an hour so be sure to hang out nearby and wait for the text.  If you come after 7pm, I wouldn't bother waiting since you will have a 3-4 hour wait.  The place is very small since it's just one floor.  The second floor is just a waiting area and the bathrooms.  The sushi was excellent - delicious, beautifully presented, and decently priced.  The prices include gratuity so it's really not bad.  I would recommend getting the Nozawa Trust Me to share with someone.  It's a good variety of fish and a filling meal.

So glad they decided to come to NYC! As a jealous New Yorker I was weary of how good the sushi actually was. Once you take that first bite of sushi, everything else in life becomes irrelevant. The best sushi money can by. Even the white rice has so much flavor. Rice is always served warm, sushi is super fresh and the specials are an omakase in itself. A steal. If you come twice you get a free dinner on your birthday ! Don't forget to sign up

Really good and really reasonably priced, but not better than sushi yasuda and not worth a 4 hour wait - my wait was only 30 min but I also went by myself.  The sushi is great/fresh but what separates them apart from the rest is the rice - it's loosely packed, served warm and heavily vinegar-ed.  Glad I tried this once but probably will just go to Yasuda in the future.

Excited that I got to try out this hot new sushi spot from LA. Having heard about the lines and waits, my friend and I arrived at the terribly unfashionable hour of 4:30pm, to find that the dining room was bustling and nearly full, but there was no wait to be seated for our party of two!

We ordered drinks and each got the Trust Me. Sushi was served warm, fish was very fresh and delicious, although I found the rice a little chewier and softer than what I'm used to so it fell apart more readily than I expected. However, the flavors were so on point that I never used the soy sauce once. I thought that the Trust Me was the perfect amount of food, although I could see my husband going for the Nozawa, which includes an extra piece of sushi and a cooked dish. 

Overall, the pacing was a little quick but this place is packed and I guess they want to serve as many as possible - they did offer to slow the pace of dishes coming out when they saw our plates starting to back up after the third course. 

Ambiance is dark and you are close to other tables so it is not a very intimate experience, but more of an energetic city vibe. My friend and I had a great time - I would definitely come back again if there was little to no wait - as for waiting 2+ hours, that seems to be hype and I don't know that it would be worth waiting all night for this sushi - this is Manhattan after all and there are plenty of great sushi places.

I came on a Friday night around 530, and it took at least 15 min to just put my name on the list so that i could wait another hour before i could get a table. Which is fine, i stopped by paragon to check out some snowboarding gear and before i even realized, my table was ready. My bf and I each got the Nozawa trust me, and we added on a order of the uni and the sweet shrimp. (things that i definitely wanted to try along with the scallops after reading the reviews and looking at the picture). Luckily for me the scallops were the daily special that night. I was definitely a fan of everything on the menu except the sweet shrimp. I never had shrimp like that and although i love uni and pretty much all seafood Ive come by...there was definitely an odd slimey texture to the shrimp. Service was good, although even if your partner has ordered the exact same thing...you may get your order first and finish before they even get theirs....i understand that they want it to be EXTREMELY fresh and for the seaweed not to go soggy but it kinda sucks for the other person. I would definitely come again, but i cant say i would want to wait an hour or more again to get a table.
AMAZING sushi, and a great dining experience.  The wait time is tough but the sushi was outstanding, and I enjoyed the service.

Trust mE! Best fish I've ever had- and all the servers are so friendly and energetic and made for a wonderful dining experience. 
Tried the "trust me" menu option and every piece of fish was incredible- it was also my first time eating sashimi so I know my experience is limited but the bar was officially set very high! sO GOOD!

No joke the fish is like butter. It melts/vanishes in your mouth instantly!!! The rice the fish is serve over is soo warm. It is scrumptious. 

I actually like that they don't take reservations because otherwise, it would probably be impossible to book a table. The service is great, and the price is extremely reasonable for what you get (tip is also included). 

This place is very traditional so don't expect to order a miso soup and green salad as an appetizer. They also don't have avocado, and I wish they did, but I get that they want to keep the experience as traditional as possible. Also, there's no dessert. There is strictly amazing sushi and only amazing sushi.

Don't know what the hype is all about. The warm vinegar rice was hard to eat. Mushy and strong vinegary rice killed the taste of the fish so was not sure if the fish was fresh or not. Does not justify the 2 plus hour wait time. Rather get sushi from trader Joe's.
Excellent service and incredibly fresh sushi! The "trust me" menu is always the perfect amount of food and served at the perfect pace! My favorite spot!

I loved when I had SUGARFISH in LA and I was so glad it opened in NYC. I went with two of my high school friends and one arrived early and put our name down because there was an estimated 2 hour wait. Yikes. I got there closer to the time we agreed on having dinner and we ended up waiting another hour, even though they said earlier that our table was almost ready. The waiting and teasing of "your table is almost ready....just kidding wait another 45min" was not a pleasant experience. Especially considering when I went in LA there was a 0 minute wait, I was a little "meh".

However, the fish is still literally like butter. Like, if you're 100 years old with dentures, this would be perfect for you. Or I guess anyone for that matter... Anyways I still really like the fish and the crab hand roll but I gotta say similar to LA, the rice is still lacking. It's too pliable and falls apart regardless if I use my fingers or my chopsticks. It just hinders the entire experience of sushi if you're struggling trying to eat something in one bite when it just falls apart on your plate.

Other than that, my other complaint is that it's way too dark for a sushi restaurant. I don't know if I'm biased because in LA the restaurant was bright and airy and I could actually see the color of the fish I'm eating...but I probably should be able to see the color of the fish (obv exaggerating...but only by a little...).

Idk, I started writing my review with 4 stars but after writing the last few paragraphs bumped it down to 3. o.o

We come all the time.  We showed up at 6pm tonight and were told a 3 hour wait. It has now been 4 hours and we have not gotten a text and you cannot call them.  We expected to eat dinner at 9pm but now our night is ruined and won't be eating until 11pm.  Food is decent but the horrible way they treat customers in the neighborhood will ensure that they don't stick around

OMG AMAZING. The best sushi I have ever had. It melts in your mouth, the fish is so fresh. The rice and warm and amazing. The flavors of the sauces are incredible. The service was quick and the prices are great. Only con - 5.5 hour wait on a Saturday night when we got there at 5:30 we sat at 10:30 -- be prepared to wait! They have a text system though so you can wander elsewhere until you are called !!
Just as delicious as LA. The salmon hand roll is incredible. It's worth the wait and lives up to all the hype.

After reading countless Yelp reviews about the long waits for this LA based establishment, I decided to come here for first sitting on a Sunday morning for lunch. The restaurant opened at 12, so my friend and I decided to meet at 11:45AM to beat the rush. I was late but thank goodness she's always on time. I arrived right before noon and she was #10 in line and the line had already went down the block!!

We were able to make it into the first seating (phew) without any problems. Both her and I decided to order the Nozawa menu. This is a no tipping restaurant so the price listed is basically what you'll be paying + tax. 

Although I do agree with many reviews saying that the rice was vinegar-y, I didn't mind it too much. I also did quite enjoy the warmish rice that was served as well. The sushi pieces really did melt in your mouth and the scallop that day was amazing. For NYC, I think it's a very well priced place to enjoy some quality sushi.

I've been to Sugarfish twice already.
The first time I went, I went for lunch on a Tuesday with 2 other people around 12:45, and the wait for 3 people was 1.5hrs. It wasn't too bad since it's right by a lot of shops on 5th ave, so killing time isn't too hard.
They also have a waiting area if you don't feel like walking around.
The second time I went, I went at around 3:30pm with 1 other person, and expected to wait around the same amount as the first time. I went to put my name down and the guy said we actually got very lucky because someone cancelled, which meant we were able to get seats right away! Another party of 2 came in right after us and they told them 1.5 hr wait. 
So for the wait time.. it really depends when you come, but I wouldn't suggest after 7pm because they can stop taking down names if it's too full.

As for the food.. I want to give it 4 stars because it's really good sushi, but I've had better sushi at Yasuda. The fish itself is very fresh and melts like butter, but the rice was a bit too sticky for my taste. Nonetheless, I would definitely come back here to eat some good quality sushi for only 30 something bucks!

Also - lighting is a bit too dark for my taste.
Didn't know if I was getting full or sleepy towards the end of my omakase...

I'm a diehard sushi fan, and honestly this place is really overrated. Yes it's decent sushi and affordable, but if you are an experienced sushi eater, don't waste your time. We went in at 1pm on a Monday and they told us it was 2.5 hour wait. When we finally got seated, the service was horrible( of course it was expected since they had that no tip policy). The menu was disappointing, not a lot of options. And worst of all, a lot of stuff wasn't even available. And when we finally got the sushi, it tasted mediocre. I admit I'm a little bit of a sushi snob, but this place prides themselves for having excellent rice, and their rice was so bland. It was too sticky, and had a bad after taste. I honestly don't think they are using the right rice for that matter, and we're putting a little too much in the sushi as well. The fish quality was decent but not as dramatic as some other reviews quote: melts in their mouth. Anyways overall not a pleasant dining experience and would not visit again.

This place is great for the price you're paying. The sushi is fresh and tasty. My favorite piece was the salmon with sesame on top of it. The sesame seeds​ added a nice flavor and crunch to it. The blue crab hand roll was great as well. I took away one star because the rice was too vinegary for me. Maybe the chef who did that batch of rice had shaky hands today.

Came here with my wife for her birthday since she loves sushi!  we came at 5 PM and there was already a 3.5-4 hour wait, we almost couldn't believe it, but we were adamant to try this place so we put our names down and went to a bar to get some small dishes so we didn't starve waiting for a table here.  After 4 hours we finally get seating and eagerly anticipating our food.  Once it comes and we start eating, we are kinda let down, the rice packed a lot of flavor, but the fish itself didn't have much flavor unfortunately and the fish should be the star, not the rice. So while the meal was good, in the end it just wasn't worth the 4 hour wait.

So delicious, so amazing and so happy it's now in NYC. The quality is on par with the LA locations and it's just the best fish ever. It melts in your mouth and the rice is out of control! 
The wait is long and you have to be smart about the time you arrive to place your name (ex. 5pm on a weekday possibly no wait, by 6/630pm 2-3 hour wait) but they do text you when your table is almost ready which is nice. 
Friendly staff, quick service and good prices. Do it!!

Great sushi! there was a wait and alot of people in line. plan ahead for a little wait. sushi was delicious! very fresh. Rice was a bit filling and they put more vinegar than other sushi spots in the rice. I am not a big fan of vinegar.

Awesome place! Especially for the price point.

Came here for dinner - the wait wasn't too long.  They told us 30 mins but within 5 mins, we were seated.

We were originally going to get the Nozawa Trust me but then realized that the since the daily special was the large scallop and that was basically the only addition for $11 as opposed to a la carte for $7...we opted for the regular Trust Me menu and got bay scallop hand roll and the albacore belly sushi as well.

Everything was freaking phenomenal!  My favorites were definitely the regular albacore sushi and the bay scallop hand roll.  The albacore literally melted in my mouth and the bay scallop was so flavorful and fresh.  My "least" favorite would probably be the yellow tail mainly because I'm not such a huge fan of it in the first place.

We were also pleasantly surprised when they accidentally gave us the daily special with additional sea bass and yellow tail sushi - I guess someone ordered the Nozawa Trust me but since they gave it to us instead...it was on the house.  The scallop was freaking delicious!!

Everything was incredibly fresh, great texture, and very flavorful.  I would definitely go back once they start doing the To Go boxes because I can already envision myself basking in the sun at the park nearby with a box of sushi.  Yum!

This place is insanely popular. We came to put our names on the list at 6 pm (admittedly on a Friday) they took us in at 10:45 pm. Not even kidding. If you like good food enough to wait for 5 hours, sure. If not, go on a weekday for lunch.

Amazing service and fresh sushi! Met up with a friend and waited for an hour .  Prompt service . We ordered the nomaza omakase since it was our first time at a sugarfish restaurant .  

My favorites were the tuna and the scallops ! Delish !!

The ambiance is nice but that's about all you get. I'm a serious sushi snob and I was super excited to try this place, but it really fell short for me! The wait was LONG (5 hrs!) but sometimes the wait is worth it, so that didn't even bother me, especially after all the hype. 

I ordered the Nozawa omakase.... The quality of the fish was good, but the rice is awful. For one. They use wayyy too much for each nigiri piece and the sauce is just so vinegary it ruins every bite! I think the quality of the fish and the taste and portion of the sushi rice is equally important for nigiri. And man, the rice just ruined the entire experience. There was a few times (oddly) where the sauce would taste like a jalapeño soy sauce mixture. It wasn't good at all. I don't even think there was a favorite piece for me. They also bring the food out so incredibly fast that you are over stuffing yourself to keep up. Most top notch sushi places really understand timing when eating omakase. It just felt too rushed. 

The pros- it is super affordable and no tip for the bill! But, if you haven't tried it yet, I would wait until it becomes less popular to give it a shot. The wait is surely not worth what you're getting if you know your sushi. I've had takeout that has been better. I'm pretty baffled at the high reviews!

We literally waited 4.5 hours for 2 ppl, as quoted, on a Friday night. Sounds crazy and I don't usually do stuff like that, but just figured we'd hang out around the area while waiting. Also thought it wouldn't literally be 4.5 hours, but it was accurate. The hostess could have been friendlier and it was just a weird experience with her where I felt she was surprised we actually came back after 4.5 hrs. Besides her, the waiters were all really friendly. We had the Trust Me and were stuffed. Good price for what you get, but not worth the wait.

The food was fantastic. We each ordered the Nowaza and were very satisfied by the end of the experience. The only negative was a five hour wait (which was expected). Alex was an incredible server. We were seated at 10:30pm, but he was still very enthusiastic and friendly. He made us feel like we were his first table of the night. Great experience.

The wait was well worth it. I got there at 6:00 pm on a Saturday evening with a wait of 4.5 hours!! I was so curious to see what the hype was about that I actually waited the four and half hours. I had 75 parties in front of me . The service was very quick and everything was served as made. We ordered the Trust Me menu and it was just perfect. The fish was so tasty and the rice was warm and full of flavor. The server made sure you ate the sushi as you were served. Along with the trust me menu we had the Nigori sake which complemented the dish so perfectly. I wasn't overly full and my taste buds were so satisfied. I will come back and wait again because it was so good! Thank god it was worth the wait .

Yes, we knew it would be a 3+ hour wait.  No biggie since I live in the area and they text and give you 15 mins to get over there. But be prepared to wait.

I got the Nozawa Omakase and girlfriend got the Trust Me Lite.  Nozawa was a lot of food, and Trust Me Lite was probably 6 items (edamame, 4 pieces, toro handroll).

Fish quality was good, all the pieces were tasty.  Highlights were Albacore Tuna, Salmon, Yellowtail, Scallop, and Blue Crab Roll. Only detriment was rice, which was a bit soft and too much of it.  Rice was coming apart when you picked it up, and especially when dipped in soy.

Service was good, food came in pieces but fairly quickly.  TIp included in price, and price was pretty good relative to quality.

Overall a good experience, as long as you can manage the wait. I've certainly had better sushi, but this was nice for the price.

After a 3+ hour wait on a Sunday night, the sushi on the Trust Me menu was very tasty, but we definitely felt a bit rushed and the overall atmosphere was rather factory-like.  Also, the waitstaff was very nice and polite, but it seems there are a few kinks for them to work out-- they brought me a dish that was actually for the neighboring table and even though that table was able to get the waitstaff's attention and have the right dish brought to him, they didn't seem to notice that I was sitting there, not eating, for 10 minutes, while I tried to get someone's attention.  Also, our waitress gave us a different explanation for the same pieces of sushi than she gave the neighboring table! And they were supposed to bring the edamame out first, but accidentally brought it second, after the tuna.  I would definitely go back based on the sushi and price point, but don't go expecting a calm, serene omakase experience that you might get elsewhere.

I was really excited to try this place and came for my birthday. Rushed to Sugarfish straight after work at 5pm and there was no wait but by 5.20pm there was a line out the door just to put down names. 

Pros: Service was excellent (despite no tipping policy). Kudos to the staff for being really professional and nice. Felt a little rushed at times, but I don't know if that's a function of the kitchen or the staff. Prices were excellent. $51 for the Nozawa (which we ordered) was really good for the amount of food. Drink options were reasonably priced.

Cons: Well, the food. The fish was fresh, but I couldn't really taste it because most of the flavor was drowned by either the ubiquitous ponzu-scallion sauce, or the overly vinegary/salty rice. The tuna sashimi appetizer was disappointing - the fish had no real flavor. 

I guess you can say that you get what you pay for, but what's really disappointing was the fact that the experience could be so much better if they just went a little less heavy handed on the ponzu and the vinegar.

I lucked on the day I wanted to try this place for lunch. Knowing that the wait has been crazy. I arrived at 1115 am on a rainy weekday. I was second in line - I attribute that to the crappy weather. I was stoked to get in for the 11:30 lunch start. 

Sat at the bar which is just full of staff and not a sushi chef. The chefs are in the back frantically churning out food. 

It's the not the most serene atmosphere compared to other higher end sushi places. Staff are busy running around but very good with talking to customers about how this place works and just overall service. This place doesn't require tip as it's already embedded in all the prices. So you just pay what you eat after tax. This was my first experience at a place that does that and service was great. 

There are three set menus and I chose the most popular one which is the "medium size" of the tastings. It's called the "trust me" $33: Organic Edamame, Tuna Sashimi, 2 pc tuna sushi, 2 pc salmon sushi, 1 pc yellowtail, 1 pc sea bass, 1 Toro Hand Roll, and 1 Blue Crab Hand Roll. This is likely enough for a lunch but I opted to add on a 2 pc albacore belly sushi ($7.25). 

The edamame was salty and strangely addictive. Tuna sashimi was refreshing and lightly seasoned. All the nigiri here are lightly dressed with soy sauce in the kitchen so the server does mention that you should refrain from adding further soy sauce or wasabi. The one thing different about the nigiri here is that the rice is slightly warm and the rice vinegar seasoning the rice is a notch or two higher than most places. I didn't think I would like that but strangely it worked. I can see how some would hate it. The fish is of very good quality and melts in your mouth along with the rice. The flavours all worked and I didn't use any wasabi or soy sauce the entire time. All the fish were delicious. But my surprise of the day was how much I loved the hand rolls. They were the perfect size unlike those absurd cone shaped hand rolls we've all had. The seaweed was so crispy - you could taste the seaweed flavour and you didn't have to fight the normal chewiness. The staff do tell you that the hand rolls should eaten immediately upon being served as the rice is still warm and seaweed still crispy. It's true - waiting a bit longer does lead to the eventual chewiness. The toro hand roll was a fave as I could eat those all day. 

I left paying $43 and I was so full. Service was great and good exceeded my expectations. I would go back but I wouldn't wait for hours. 

Next month the new hand roll only version of this place will open up near this location. I will look forward to that on my next NYC trip!

The food at Sugarfish is delicious - fresh, simple, melts in your mouth! However, the best thing about our dinner at Sugarfish was our incredible waiter, Daniel. He was so knowledgable about everything on the menu and so warm and welcoming! He was hands down the best waiter I've had at any restaurant! It was clear that he wanted to make our experience the best it could be - it was as if he was hosting us in his home. He checked in with us to make sure we were happy, asked how things were, rearranged our food after it was served to make our table look more presentable, etc. He allowed us time to browse the menu and was attentive but never imposing. Would definitely come back to Sugarfish and hope to have Daniel as our waiter again!

Crazy wait but so, so worth it. We put our name on the list around 6pm and were seated around 10:30. Nearly everyone else in the restaurant was a bit drunk by this point. Being more on the sober side, it was funny to watch others--several people fell/stumbled down the stairs while we were waiting to be seated. No problems though and an excellent meal. They accidentally brought be an extra hand roll and it ended up being on the house. I'm not complaining. Will be back.

Love the warm rice!  I hope Sugarfish starts the trend for warm rice with sushi.  It really makes a big difference, and you feel like you are having a hot meal even though you are having sushi.  I don't know why they don't serve miso soup though.  The sushi is really fresh, especially the salmon with sesame seeds.  Love the handrolls too.

Trust me... Get the 'Nozawa Trust Me'! You will not be disappointed. 

The fish was amazing and the wasabi had a real kick. I ordered the Trust Me (middle size) thinking that the Nozawa was too much food but I was wrong! 

Also, the staff was friendly and attentive, which makes every experience better. Note: this is a no tipping restaurant.

Famous for his own style of sushi, chef Nozawa has created the "trust-me" style of sushi, which was operated in Studio city since 1985. Worked with his partner Jerry Greenberg, Nozawa has established Sugarfish, which brought him so much fame.

At sugarfish, what I have discovered was the skill of "aging" fish. While many fish was brought from Japan, Europe or the west coast raw and fresh, it is certainly not to take it for granted that fish by itself, without any work, is the best way to consume. By testing out his own soy sauce and ponzu sauce, Nozawa has come up with a list of high quality, well flavored sushi/sashimi options. 

In his "trust-me" style of sushi, I sampled aged tuna sashimi, sea bass, and albacore, which proved to be my favorites. With enough chewiness and a light touch of spiciness, the sea bass has completely caught up my attention. Another point that I found myself quite enjoyed was the contradiction between the cold toro and the warm vinegar rice - at the time they met up in my mouth, it was definitely an interesting experience.

Sugarfish was well priced and probably is the best place to get affordable high quality sushi. However price tag itself stands for something too, and please don't compare it with those Michelin rated sushi places where Blue fin tuna was transported from Tsukiji market. Just as Nozawa himself has once stated - stay true to what you believe, the rest will take care of itself.

Quite simply...sushi heaven. 
I had Chef Morimoto serve me dinner in Mumbai and this was better

Best sushi I've ever ate. None of that Americanized junk either basic simple sushi fish & rice and that's all they need. Can get super busy for dinner time. "Trust me" plates are amazing I went in here never eating scallop sushi before I was weirded out by it at first now it's my favorite kind of sushi definitely recommend.

I missed the opportunity to go here when I was in L.A., so I was thrilled to hear this restaurant was opening in NYC. My sister had warned me it would be a long wait, and that there was a chance we wouldn't get in. I simply said, why don't we make reservations?! Silly me, for some reason this restaurant doesn't take any. To their credit though, even though there's a ridiculously long wait, they text you when your table is about to be ready rather than make you wait there in the restaurant. So we strolled around the flatiron area shopping and getting a drink, luckily the time passed. We were told at 2pm it would be a 3 hour wait (Lol, so much for lunch!) - but got the text around 4:30. Fyi, the line starts to form even before the restaurant opens...wow! Another FYI, the lunch menu is slightly cheaper than dinner menu for the "Trust me" orders (but if you want lunch here you better get here early!). 

The restaurant is dimly lit, and I guess I understand the long wait because (not only is the food delicious) but the restaurant seemed pretty small. I was recommended to order the"Trust me" so I went for it, even though I'm usually not that adventurous when it comes to fish. But every dish melted in my mouth, and you can really tell the fish is as fresh as it gets. My "trust me" order involved edamame, sashimis/sushi (tuna, yellowtail, salmon), and a roll (toro). They space out each dish to stretch out your meal and also let you anticipate the next roll. My favorite part about the dishes was they don't recommend dipping the rolls in soy sauce because each roll comes with a unique sauce that MAKES the taste of the roll. My goodness, those sauces. 

I was surprised that for $39+ the "Trust Me" didn't fill me up as much as I wanted - I expected to feel like I needed to be rolled out of the restaurant! I recommend ordering an extra roll to share with the table or upgrading to the "Norwaza" (few extra pieces than Trust Me) if you have a big appetite like me! I DEFINITELY recommend ordering one of the 3 "Trust Me" set menus since it makes for such a unique experience, and because if you come here that's just what you do. End of story.

How dare they get 4 stars! Best sushi in the states. The only possible complaint is the wait but thats because of the limited space they're working with and also they get a lot of customers. Everyone is friendly.

I was extremely excited to experience the hype that was SUGARFISH. Many friends who traveled to LA, ventured to try this renowned spot and I couldn't believe they were opening one in NY. This place does not take reservations, but the great thing is that you can put your name down and they'll text you when a table is about ready.  Two and a half hour wait on a weekend during dinner time (we arrived at maybe 5:30pm, put our names down for a party of two, and seated at about 8pm) and I was very underwhelmed. 

I just had a wonderful omakase experience in San Francisco the week before (Akiko's, a local favorite on Bush St.), and I just don't think this place could ever compare. We ordered a Nozawa Trust Me and Trust Me + Sake. The entire experience is quite quick, with the staff (very friendly), serving each dish very consistently after one another (8-10 dishes). Servings consist of the typical salmon, tuna, albacore, yellowtail etc. They recommend eating most pieces while fresh especially the hand rolls (blue crab, and toro). There was definitely an urgency from the staff for the hand rolls where they made it a point to encourage us (more than once) to consume the rolls rapidly, which I understand is a staple, pretty much written-on-the-menu suggestion (not rule). 

While I liked the rolls (blue crab was delish) and the meal itself proved to be more filling than anticipated - I found little enjoyment in the flavor of the pieces that were served. I had an overwhelming flavor of vinegar from the rice that completely overpowered what should have been the star - the fish. I was literally just consuming vinegar rice for the most part and that type of acidity didn't sit well with me. Additionally, the sake that was recommended, didn't match well with what we ordered. It was good, but totally didn't complement the fish in any way. Overall, I felt the food was lacking in quality and while the price doesn't break your wallet (~$40-50), I don't think it's worth the buck nor time spent waiting. You can definitely find better quality sushi elsewhere!

I've been a loyal devotee of the LA sugarfish for a long time now so I was excited when they finally opened one here. ITS AMAZING OF COURSE. I dunno how they do it but the food is delicious, great service, and SO affordable. Pass on the seriously $$$$$ Sushi Yasuda and go here. Get one of the Trust Me menus. God I'm drooling just thinking about the soft fish, warm rice..... *foodgasm*
3 hour wait is a joke. Food is very good but not worth that kind of wait. I only order pickup and eat it at my house.

I was there March 10, 2017 at approximately 2pm and there was a female at the front acting as the hostess.  She told me that I had to wait 1 hour for a party of 2.   She was real mean to me for no reason.  Then I knew 2 people that I bumped into going in and were told they had to wait 30 minutes.   It looks like she was prejudice of Hispanic women.  It's sad that they have to act that way.  Avoid this place !!!   They are not nice

Overall: it might be cool to wait in LA for four hours for decent sushi, but it is absolutely maddening to do so in NYC. GET RESERVATIONS. 

Atmosphere: very small, somewhat cramped and nothing wildly special. 

Food: If I feel badly rating this restaurant poorly it is because it actually turns out pretty delicious and fresh sushi. I am one of the few people who love when the chef chooses your dishes for you, and Sugarfish does precisely that. My friend and I went for the most expensive "trust me", which really isn't expensive at all, by NYC omakase standards. The tuna tartare, salmon, yellowtail and tuna pieces stood out by far. The fish pieces were quite generous, but two pieces of each was a bit much. 

The two hand rolls were also delicious and somewhat different from what you typically receive in an omakase. Two were probably overkill, though, as we were completely stuffed by the time the second one came around. If restaurants were rated on food alone, I'd give this a solid 4.2. 

Service: this is a huge part of why this restaurant leaves a proverbial bad taste in my mouth. They were off by an hour on their estimate of how long it would be before we'd get a table. That's a big deal when you've already waited 3 hours. Additionally, when we made our way back to the restaurant (If you're not back within 15 minutes from the time they text you, they give your table away), we waited an additional 30 minutes. 

More frustratingly, when we sat down, our sushi was rushed out to us to the point where we couldn't keep up with the speed of the kitchen. Two waiters had to ask the kitchen to slow down because we weren't flying though our meal. From the time we sat down to the time we got up, we were there about 45 minutes. 

Staff is friendly but really doesn't care about the inconveniences of their establishment.
Love love sugarfish. Same quality as the LA stores, but really long wait. Fast service when you sit down and definitely go with their trust me menu. Can't wait for NY to start doing take out as well!

I crave sugarfish. that's how good. Ive had 2 really good experiences out of 3 in the past month in terms of the wait. 

What works for me: 4PM Saturday walkin. I get a 1.5 - 2 hour wait estimate. I go shopping in union square - wait came out to about an hour and 15 mins both times - score. 

Bad experience - Saturday at 1:15PM - quoted 1 to 1.5 hour wait. Did not go shopping because I brought my dad out on a cold day and he wasn't about going back out in the cold. Wait ended up about an hour and 45 min when we sat down. I'm just saying, every minute past the estimate gets exponentially frustrating. 

To be fair - I don't have an answer on how to handle the long wait system which can range drastically if because drop out of line. 

But bottom line - sushi is on point and worth it. just worth it. there's enough reviews about the food - just leaving more of a tip on how to get a table.

...it's just sushi (decent sushi though) ... but still just sushi.   i think most people go to sugarfish for the price.  it's not hard to get good sushi(omakase), but harder with that price.  
that being said, you either have to wait or you pay extra hence the loooooong wait for sugarfish during regular meal time. 
if you do omakase(trust me) and you have more than 4ppl at the table it will be a bit weird as they will come one plate at a time ¯\_(ツ)_/¯   and you can't (well not suppose to) wait for the others, especially the handrolls. 

it's all personal preference as to which fish tastes better,  but i just want to say the eel (kabayaki) is prob kanto style, so very tender... personally i prefer the kansai style which is chewier but it's just me being rustic.

My friend took me to this place once, and now I can't stop going back. 
The quality of the sushi is amazing. The service is good. 
The bad part about this is that you can't make reservation or even put your name down and have them call you when the table is ready. There is always a wait and if you don't wait there you will not get a table. I work next door to the place, so after finish work I have to go and wait another 30 40 min for the table. I just wish there was a easier way. I am still giving them 5 starts because, the review of the place should not be affect by the rules of the establishment.

I really can't think of a reason not to give this place 5 stars, except for maybe the wait. 

Both times I've tried to come on a Sunday night. The first time I got there at 6:30 and was quoted a 3.5 hour to 4 hour wait. I knew I wasn't going to actually come back but left my name because I was curious how long it would actually take. They ended up texting me at 9, so it was closer to a 2.5-3 hour wait.  This past time, we went to put our name at 4:40 and were quoted a 2 hour wait. Living within walking distance makes this a pretty easy option as we go put our name down, go home and then leave right after they text us to go back to check in again.  They ended up texting us at 6:00 this past time, so it ended up being closer to an hour and a half wait. I asked them out of curiosity how long the wait was at 6 and they said 3.5 to 4 hours, so it sounds like you have to put your name down around 5 at the latest if you want to eat before 9 (at least on a Sunday).

The service was great, our server was attentive, pleasant, and very cheerful which is always welcomed.

We looked up some reviews ahead of time and noticed that they don't have gluten free soy sauce, but they can make the sushi gluten free, so my boyfriend just brought his own Tamari.

We both ordered the "Trust Me", and then shared an extra order of salmon sushi, and also each got an extra hand roll at the end, since we weren't completely full, though we were particularly hungry, so on a normal day it may have been enough.

We also shared a bottle of Nigori Sake, which is unfiltered and delicious with a hint of sweetness.

Now onto the items that stood out to me:
Edamame - served cold, which I prefer, and it was tasty and a nice portion.
Tuna Sashimi - the sauce was amazing and the tuna was very fresh.
Salmon sushi with sesame on top was perfect.
Yellowtail sushi -  very good as well.
Sea bass stood out because it had a spicy flavor and had a unique flavor.
My favorite items though were the hand rolls, specifically the toro one. It is served with the seaweed crispy and hot, which I haven't seen elsewhere and it was delicious.
I love the rice here, the flavor is amazing and the warmth from the rice with the coldness of the fish go perfectly together.

Overall for $60 with the "trust me" + Sake + an extra sushi order and 2 hand rolls, the price and quality of food can't be beat (tip is included). I'm very excited this is in the neighborhood and look forward to coming back often.

I have to admit, I jumped off the Sugarfish Hype Train as soon as I tasted their food. What's wrong with it? I'll break it down for ya:

1. The fish all tasted like they had muscular atrophy. I know I shouldn't compare it to fancier joints but the flesh here just taste mushier than normal, no matter which fish I got. You sure you guys got the hookup for top notch fish suppliers? Seems....fishy to me. 

2. SOUR AS HELL. The chefs all have a super heavy hand when saucing their sushi, and the black sauce mixture has a crapton of vinegar that rendered some pieces inedible, think sour patch kids without the kids. If I pick up a piece of nigiri and there's still sauce on my plate, then it's oversauced. Oversaucing also contributes to point 4, which you will read about in a bit.  

3. Scale. I found two scales in my mouth while eating the snapper. What the heck? Isn't it sushi basics 101 to get rid of the scale? I mean I would understand it if you suck at cutting pieces of fish and they all end up looking janky, but it's unacceptable when there's scale on the fucking thing when I'm paying $40 for a meal. I'd gladly choke on the scale if it was a $4 street food in south east asia. 

4. Rice that fell apart. I've been using chopsticks since I weened off my mother's milk. If I pick up a piece of your nigiri and there's a 50% chance that it falls apart before it lands in my mouth, that shit is on YOU. I don't care if your restaurant is a special snowflake in the industry for using warm rice, KEEP IT TIGHT, AIGHT? 

The core equation for Nigiri is Shari + Neta, and you managed to screw up both, congrats. Next time I'll just go to my neighborhood Chinese Takeout joint for sushi instead of dropping bills at this poor excuse of a joint.

Peace. 

PS: The blue crab hand roll was nice.
Quality fish at reasonable prices. Tastes AMAZING. The wait is a bit long and they do not take reservation, but its worth it. The albacore and blue crab were my favorites.

It's a 3.5 but I'll put 4 for the pleasant service. 
We came on a Friday around 4pm. Our wait was 30-45mins which is understandable. Customer service before we were even sat down was very welcoming. 

First timers so of course we ordered the Nozawa Trust Me. Dinner hours so price is $51. THEY ACCEPT CARDS, NO TIPS - INCLUDED IN PRICING!

Edamame was a little over salted for my taste but I still finished it. 
Tuna Sashimi with ponzu sauce. Very good, I can see why it's one of the top favs. 
A set of 2's came next - Albacore, Salmon and Snapper. Albacore was BOMB. Gotta say it's my favorite from the whole set of Nozawa. Salmon was good. Snapper was mediocre. 
Next set of 2's - Yellowtail, Sea Bass and Large Scallop ( daily special ). I love yellowtail and this did not disappoint. The sea bass and scallops were masked by the over sauced rice. Though you can feel the scallops were extremely smooth on the tongue. 
Toro Hand Roll was exceptional. Server also mentioned that we should eat the hand rolls as soon as possible. Probably because the seaweed is so crispy and it wouldn't be the same if it went soggy. 
Blue Crab Hand Roll reminded me of those Blue Crab Spread you can get from Costco but warmed up and less salty. 


Overall it was something to experience.
Would I come again? I wouldn't say no but it's also not a very big yes. 
Service was nice. It wasn't too slow or too fast. Place was full so customers should be understanding if service isn't as snappy as you would like.

My friend has been telling me about Sugarfish out in LA for a while now so I was excited to hear one was opening up in NYC. I didn't have high expectations since the price was so affordable. We went with the full The Nozawa Trust Me menu and also added two types of sushi pieces. The fish was either flavorless or fishy in the not fresh way. The rice was the worst offender, it was over seasoned with vinegar, very soft and wet, and there's plenty of it. The service was really odd. I understand that everything is meant to be eaten a la minute so the waiter would come with a plate with two pieces on it for me, then come back a minute later with my husband's place. Then he would come back with another plate before I've even finished my sushi, then a minute later with my husband's next plate. Now the table is filled with plates.The waiter comes again with my next round, takes the two plates I already have, then a minute later my husband's next round. I felt like he was in such a rush to give us the plates asap and go back for my husband's that he was throwing the plate at me. I felt so rushed it was like eating at a buffet except I didn't have to get the food myself. Plates were piling up so fast I started stacking them. I'm a person who likes to eat fast but this was ridiculous! I don't get why there is such a long wait for this place. It's not worth the cheap affordable price. I would rate it a tiny step better than Chinese take out sushi. But factoring in the wait, price, and weird service I would rather eat the latter. 

P.S. The tuna mush in the tuna hand roll taste like the tunafish you would get in a school lunch sandwich, maybe worse because I happen to love tunafish sandwiches.

5/1/17 I think 2 stars was too generous. I am changing it to 1.

Came here on a weekday night a while back with a friend and still had to wait the 2 hours. I was a bit worried since they do close at 10 PM and we arrived around 8 PM but the hostess said they will seat us even after they close which was great to hear. My friend and I just went off to a wine bar closeby to kill some time but I finally got a text when the table was ready.
