We got the Nozawa ($51 which includes Organic Edamame, Tuna Sashimi, 2 pieces of: Albacore Sushi, Salmon Sushi, Snapper Sushi, Yellowtail Sushi, Sea Bass Sushi, Toro Hand Roll, Blue Crab Hand Roll and "Daily Special")

I thought the salmon with sesame was a really good touch. Sea bass hit me by surprise, it had a bit of a spicy kick to it. The amaebi was on the spicier side with a hint of yuzu and unfortunately, the 2 pieces of amaebi didn't consistently taste the same - one piece had sweeter rice and the other piece was saltier, perhaps they didn't mix their sushi rice evenly enough. The Albacore tuna was really good with yuzu and ginger flavors - literally melts in your mouth. 

On top of the Nozawa dinner option, we ordered an additional Albacore Belly Sushi and the Uni which I have to say, was really the highlight of my night. My friend and I did enjoy our dinner here. I think its a good baseline of what sushi should really taste like which I appreciate - anyone that thinks AYCE sushi is good sushi, you really have to reevaluate your life and come to Sugarfish to really start expanding the palette for real sushi. Since I've already been to a few Omakase spots already, Sugarfish is not mind-blowing for me - I've had much more tender pieces of fish and at a warmer temperature at other spots which really makes a huge difference. I agree the price is good, but I rather pay a little more for that mind blowing, every piece melts in your mouth experience and not have to wait forever to get a seat. However, I am glad to have tried it, I definitely would come back but it just did not meet my expectations since it was already so hyped up from everyone.

I do have to say, the service here is really great. The staff members and our bartender were very attentive. The timing of when we received our food was well executed. Oh and FYI, tipping is already included in the price which is great!

I REALLY wanted to like this place, but unfortunately, as some other reviewers stated, the food just did not live up to its hype I would have given one star, as that is how bad the food was, especially when compared to its price, however, I have added an extra star for the service. 

There were just so many inconsistencies with the rice. Some of the rice that came out was steaming hot, while another piece was close to room temperature. On one plate, one piece would contain rice that was heavily seasoned, and the piece tasted like there was no seasoning whatsoever. All the pieces of fish that came pre-sauced were so salty and sour, it was hard to eat. Not only that, there was so much sauce that the rice completely fell apart on multiple locations. Not only was the rice inconsistent, the fish also came out in a variety of temperatures. Albacore was cold and salmon was warm. I am not sure about other people, but I'm pretty sure that sushi rice should not be so hot that the piece of raw fish is warm by the time it arrives to the customer.   Not only that, I knew that this meal would not be good when the second course, tuna sashimi, did not taste like tuna. Instead it was hard to distinguish what fish was served going on taste alone. I also ordered a side of Uni that had an ammonia like after taste, which explained what I smelled when I first walked into the restaurant.

I sat right next to the window, so I spent a good amount of time watching the kitchen. I noticed that what everyone was eating was mass produced sushi. By offering 3 entree dishes, the kitchen was able to send out 5 plates of the same dish, and have them sitting in the window for the server to takes each plate to a separate table. I also noticed a black spherical device that was rotating next to the 10 rice cookers they had. I asked a server what it was, and my assumptions as to why the rice was inconsistent was proven correct. That ball was used to mix the rice. Yes. Even the rice is not mixed by hand. I can only imagine how the fish arrives to the restaurant. Maybe it is precut? Maybe it is cut to order? Who knows. I'm just saying that with 7-8 cooks in the kitchen, if you can't have at least one person mixing rice, what other shortcuts were taken to serve people at a faster pace. 

The only real praise I can give is to the owner. He is a genius for coming up with this concept. He basically has people paying a premium for what tasted like mediocre conveyor belt sushi. He also has the perfect market who believe that this sushi is so amazing for such a great price. However, if I wanted to pay $50 for a sushi lunch, I know plenty of other places that would have given me well made nigiri. Maybe if Westerners stopped obsessing over sauce filled rolls, and instead actually ate real sushi, they would know that what they were eating could be bought for $20 a few blocks away at a place like Maguro or Tenzan in Midtown. 

In other words, crappy food, great service, and a genius owner.

This review is more of a 3.5 star --but given the wait time, I'm going to round down. I waited about 1.5 hrs on a Friday afternoon (2-3PM) a month or so after it opened.

The quality of the fish was good but like other reviewers have mentioned, the sauce overpowers the taste of the fish and the rice falls apart. Honestly, if I'm going to pay over $50 for omakase, have the rice stick together for god's sake; it's messy and it makes your food look cheap. 

To sum it up, I would give it another try given the quality of the fish to $$ but would not wait another 1.5 hrs.

The. Hype. Is. Real.

I'm glad expanding the franchise has not diluted the quality and taste of SUGARFISH. It is every bit as delicious as the LA locations (and trendy). My friend and I got super lucky on Saturday when we went for dinner. We planned to put our name in and then go shopping in the area until our names were called (no reservations here!), but a table just got cancelled for 2 as we walked in. We immediately snatched them.

We didn't go for the Trust Me because we wanted to share and sample a larger selection of dishes. My favorites were the blue crab (surprising because I don't tend to like crab), large scallops, and the albacore. The toro was probably the biggest letdown comparatively; it was good but not perfection like the other fish had been. Honestly for the price, I would eat everything twice over.

Delicious freshness at a reasonable price - what's not to love?

The sushi is ok and long wait. I have to compare to the Sugarfish in Los Angeles.  The one in New York is different as far as quality of the fish and rice, the ones in Los Angeles are better. The rice seem to be too mushy and sticky. The fish is not as soft and flavorful. I wish they have more consistency compared to Los Angeles.  Of course you wouldn't have notice if you never had sushi at the other Sugarfish.

Finally, the famous LA restaurant has made its way into NYC.  There has been a lot of buzz around this restaurant and its awesome fish.  I heard the lines can be crazy and the wait can be hours long.  I'm just not the type of person to wait that long for food, no matter how good it is.  So I decided that if I made it there before it opens, there will be a good chance I'll make the first seating.  I got there on a holiday around 11:10, I was 3rd in line as my friend dropped me off to look for parking.  At about 11:20, the line quadrupled.

The restaurant is quite unique, there are two floors, one floor with tables and upstairs with bathrooms and a waiting area.  Knowing NYC real estate is expensive, I don't know why they didn't put tables upstairs.    

They have a menu with a decent selection with 3 "Trust Me" options in which the restaurant selects certain sushi to be part of the Trust Me option.  Do I trust them? Hmmm...I've decided to trust them and it was a good choice.  For those indecisive people who don't know what to order because it all looks so good, the "Trust Me" option is great.   

I got the $45 Nozawa trust me

Organic edamame
Tuna sashimi (2 piece)
Albacore sushi (2 piece)
Salmon sushi (2 piece)
Yellowtail sushi (2 Piece)
Snapper sushi (1 piece)
Sea bass sushi (1 piece)
Toro hand roll
Blue crab hand roll
Daily special (2 piece - it was scallops)

The sushi was very fresh and it literally melted in my mouth, so tasty.  The rice had a bit too much vinegar for my taste buds.  This place is a simple sushi place, no avocado or any of the special stuff you usually see at typical sushi restaurants.    

Service was good as they checked up on us various times and they bring out the sushi a little bit at a time and it came out quite fast.  Once you are done, they are ready to bring out your next dish.  

Suggested to get here early if you don't want to wait hours.

I had been craving the Sugarfish sushi experience since I moved from California back to the East Coast.  When I found out there is a Sugarfish in the Flatiron District I couldn't wait to try it.

A friend was in town for business so I met her for a few days and we enjoyed the same delicious sushi in an East Coast setting that we've come to know and enjoy in California.

The quality, presentation, flavor, and freshness was similar to the West Coast restaurants and that was reassuring.  We weren't sure what to expect but everything was delicious and it felt like we were in LA, except of course it was much much colder. 

The tax and hospitality are included as they are in the other locations, so our check was $ 55.53 each (we both got the Nozawa which was probably too much food as we left feeling stuffed to the gills).  Usually I choose the "Trust Me" but I think I was so excited to experience the Nozawa sushi cuisine that I went overboard.

Can't wait to go back another time.  We waited upstairs for a table.  It was a weeknight around 8 pm and of course there's always a wait, no reservations.

I arrived 15 minutes before opening on a Saturday and got first seating. Ordered the Trust Me and added an additional hand roll. It was just enough for a light lunch...for me.  Great service.  The waiter explained all dishes.  Fish was very fresh. Melted in your mouth. No soy sauce necessary.  Tax and tip already included in the menu price.

The fish is absolutely delicious.
I do appreciate that they tell you "we recommend that you eat it now as soon as it comes out of the kitchen"
The contrast of warm rice w super fresh cold fish is sooooo good
And the handrolls are excellent too
Crispy and yes! Eat it As soon as it comes out of the kitchen is the trick. Eat it right there and then. yUM.
Last week went to sugarfish in LA after the whole wait debacle in NYC.  No wait at all!!! The food is pretty good,  very simple and nothing overly special, but not worth the wait for sure!

Yay finally made it! You would think that waiting months after it opened would help with the waiting time, but it definitely didn't. I marched over here Friday after work around 5:30 (it was pouring rain), and it was still a 2 hour wait. Me and my friend were both so shocked, but we both had zero plans that night so we decided to wait. It was pretty nice because they had a huge seating area upstairs so we just did some work while we waited to pass time. It would've been nice if they had a bar up there, but maybe it's good that they didn't so we could sit in quiet. 

Once we got seated, we both ordered the Nozawa Trust Me - if we waited for two hours, might as well go all out, right? My favorite was probably the yellowtail and toro hand roll, omg. They didn't have uni which was a bummer, but hopefully I'll be back LOL.

The quality was great, and the service was even better. Definitely worth the wait, but I hope I never have to wait 2 hours ever again.

Whoaaa, this place set the bar for sushi in my opinion. I've had a lot of fish over the years, my go to for sashimi was Takahachi...until now. The first time I tried to go to Sugarfish was when it first opened (mistake). Every time I checked, I couldn't even get my name on the waiting list. I live right around the corner so I figured I'd just wait until the hype died down a bit. Months later, I completely forgot about wanting to try it until today. 
I came in on a Monday at 2:30pm alone and got seated immediately at the counter. I ordered the Trust Me ($33) and everything was honestly incredible. I've never had fish melt in my mouth. On top of the set omakase, I ordered the sweet shrimp and another blue crab hand roll. The sweet shrimp was actually my least favorite (kind of bland), but I had to order another crab hand roll. The one that came with the set was devoured within 2 seconds so I figured I needed another to savor it.
The service was also great, everyone was very friendly and advised how to eat the pieces as they came out.
Definitely check it out but try to go during the afternoon. Whenever I walk by at night I can tell it's still super crowded inside. Regardless, try to get a seat here. The food is really great.

Tips: 
-Try to refrain from using soy sauce. They already advise against it, but I tried it on one piece out of curiosity and couldn't even taste the fish. It's too overpowering and the fish itself is so good it shouldn't be muted. 
-Eat the pieces as they come out, especially the hand rolls or the seaweed gets soggy.
-No tip necessary (it's included)!
-If you're super hungry, get The Nozawa. I came in quite hungry and the Trust Me didn't fill me up completely (even with two extra separate orders).

Least authentic sushi place I've ever been to.
The sushi is not omakase as many people believe it to be. It is a set menu.
Nothing about the food is cheap. You can get a lot better and actually fresh fish for the price.

The appetizer which consisted of frozen tuna with ponzu sauce was nothing special. The tuna was still defrosting and I could literally taste the plastic packaging.
The cuts for each nigiri were not professional and haphazard. Sadly the best nigiri was the albacore which is the lowest quality tuna you can get. You will never see any sushi place serve this because it is usually reserved for canned tuna.

If you are Japanese or actually have experience eating different sushi, you will be greatly disappointed. I went before The NY Times review came out but the review says it all. Besides the ambiance the place is mediocre. All hype.

I was finally able to try Sugarfish after wait a bit for it to open. You will definitely need to try and clear your schedule a bit if you arrive at six. We got there a little after six and there was a line just to put your name down. We waited like twenty to thirty mins to put our name down and waited another two hours for them to tell us our table was ready. Its a pretty long wait but it was totally worth it. 

We all got the Nozawa Trust Me. Each course is served as quickly as possible when its ready, so sometimes one person got their food while the others waited. It turned out a lot better because everyone got to taste the sushi at its freshest. The rice was still warm and chewy. The fish was all really good quality too. I think my favorites were the handrolls however. The combination of having the warm sushi rice, toro or crab meat and the crispy seaweed was absolutely amazing.

Overall the dinner was excellent and I would love to totally go back. The price definitely beats other places I been to with the same or better quality. It is a pretty small restaurant so it is a little cramp inside.
Fantastic bang for your buck. Great service-great great great!

So I gave them a try yesterday....without realizing what I was in for regarding the wait. How dare I stumble across this unsuspecting place expecting to have my crabmeat and yellowtail rolls with a side of edamame within 10 minutes. NOT! More like 45 minutes. The secret is apparently out and I was late to the party. Not only was there nearly an hour wait to be seated, but 30-45 min for a takeout order. I don't know if I'll ever get to dine in here. However, they do offer you the convenience of ordering through the Chow Now App. I highly recommend it, as it will come in handy, if your time is valuable. 
As for my food, the blue crab was tasty and the yellowtail was quite fresh. I found the edamame to be a bit salty. All in all, I was satisfied with my selections. Now that I know the ropes, I'll be ordering through the app for pickup or ordering from DoorDash for delivery. Definitely worth a try!

I want to really give this place 3.45 points due to the extreme wait time if you're not there at a certain time.  Food is excellent for the price.  You would not expect more and they delivered. The wait staff and host is very nice and well trained. I arrived at 4:50pm waited about 10 min to put my name down. Table for 2 was a 45min-1hr wait which is acceptable compare to the 2-3hrs. Finally sat down at 5:45. Wasn't bad at all.  Anyway,  the food was simple but yet fulfilling. Ordered the nakazawa because honestly,  didn't think we'll come back again due to the wait.  The only issue was the rice from the sushi wasn't cooled enough toward the end of our course. All the fish was fresh.  The daily special was scallops and that was yummy. Best of all,  no tipping!

Small pieces of fish that were completely over sauced and over flavored to the point that it was dripping onto the plate, and at one point all I could taste was lemon. Why. Rice under the fish was falling apart - not an anomaly literally almost every single piece fell apart. No respectful omakase should have that happen especially one that boasts a 3 hour+ wait. Hand rolls had too much rice but the seaweed was crispy. Wasabi had the texture of being microwaved. Soft poop. Worst omakase I've ever had go somewhere else tbh.

This place lives up to the hype!! 

Came at 11:40am on a Sunday and got seated immediately when they opened at noon. I opted for the Trust Me, which was $33 for lunch. I didn't think that I would be full at the end but I definitely was. 

Each piece of sushi was mouthwateringly good and unlike any other sushi I've had in the past. The rice is actually kind of creamy in texture and infused with flavor. I loved the sesame and salmon combo, and the albacore with ponzu was amazing (good thing there was 2 pieces!) 

Our server was also friendly and described each piece and suggestions on how to eat it (with or without sauce). She also told us about Sugarfish's new hand roll bar KazuNori, which I'm now excited to check out!

Every sushi lover should try this place for its wonderfully fresh fish, complex flavors, and beautifully simple atmosphere.

I don't really get it. Well I guess of do, since it's an LA craze and therefore a "cool thing to do".

Got the Nozawa Trust Me (the larger omakase/prix fixe). The fish texture and freshness was definitely memorable due to its melt-in-your-mouth quality, almost as if it weren't fish. But the rice on each piece of nigiri was drenched in vinegar, warm and mushy. If you realllllly love vinegar this place might be for you, but I like my sushi rice to add solidity to each piece. Not leave a moist caked-up feeling in my mouth with each bite.

Finally, by the end of the meal... I was like, "this is it?" Don't think I can consider SUGARFISH an affordable sushi place at the quantity they serve it at.

Please, I beg of you, someone tell me why every single sushi restaurant doesn't serve their rice warm. It is the number one thing I don't understand in this universe, and I am one to contemplate the relative nature of space-time.

Sugarfish has 3 menus - Lunch, Dinner, and Take Out. They are all fairly similar, so I won't delve into the differences between each. Let's discuss dinner for now.

You can order a la carte (a hand roll is about $6), or get one of their mini omakase options:

- Trust Me Lite ($27)
- Trust Me ($39)
- The Nozawa ($51)

If you're a light eater, the Trust Me Lite might do, but if you're even mildly hungry, I'd recommend the Trust Me. Your meal will come in a bunch of small courses so that you can enjoy each bite exactly the way the chefs intend you to. It's almost blasphemous to put soy sauce or wasabi on your sushi beyond whatever the pieces come with.

As I mentioned above, all of the sushi has warm rice. Once you try this, you will seriously wonder why you've never had it before. It makes so much sense - the contrast between warm and cold dances in your mouth as the fresh fish delights your palette.

One thing I MUST note. This didn't detract from my rating, but you better expect to wait...maybe 2 to 2.5 hours. If you have a friend (or enemy) who lives in the area and can put your name down, I'd suggest calling them. We went to Society Bar nearby and enjoyed a few beers and games of pool. There are a few other places to hang or shop in the area which I recommend you scope out ahead of time.

Even in spite of the wait, if you like sushi you need to try this place.

I came here today with a friend because we had this in LA and when we heard that they opened one in NYC, we knew we had to try it.  However, when they first opened, the wait time was too insane.  So we decided to come 30 minutes before opening (11:30am) so that we don't have to wait as long.  We were not the only one with this idea.  We created a short line waiting for opening.  They let us in at exactly 11:30am so they were very punctual.  They seated us quickly and the room filled up quick.  

There are 3 omakase options:
1: Trust me 
2: Trust me lite 
3: The Nozawa Trust me 

We ordered the Nozawa Trust me to share which was enough food for the two of us because we did the same in LA.  The Nozawa has tuna sashimi, edamame, albacore sushi (2pcs), salmon sushi (2pcs), yellowtail (2pcs), snapper (1pc), hirame sushi (1pc), toro hand roll, blue crab hand roll, and daily special (2pcs).  We had the big scallop as our daily specials.  

The fish were fresh and delicious.  I saw a lot of people have complained about the heavy vinegar and the rice being warm.  However, that is their style of how they prepare their rice even in LA.  I have to admit this had a little more vinegar than I remember.  The chef has each piece sauced and seasoned already so no additional sauce is needed.  As with the warm rice, I think it's a creative combo with the sushi because it just melts in your mouth with the sushi.  This is different from most sushi places because the rice is usually cold.  The one complaint I did have about the rice is that some of the sushi rice did not stick together, so they were falling apart.  

I would definitely come back again.  The quality of the sushi for the price you are paying is definitely worth it!

Don't Go. There are a million wonderful, similarly priced places in the city that are worth your time and will treat you MUCH better.

I've been to Sugarfish in LA a few times. Its always been OK, never exceptional - really nothing yo go out of  your way for or what on 2 hour lines to eat. 

They opened the NYC off shoot and I figured I would give it a try. I checked the website: No Reservations, Walk in only, first come first served. Fine I figured once I'd give it a try.

I made the 30 minute commute and when I arrived the wait list was closed, no one else could dine for the night (it was around 8:30PM). I spoke with the manger, very friendly but basically her offer was to add us to the waitlist and if there was fish left we could eat 3 or so hours later. 

My main issue here is that they won't answer the phone, they don't communicate this on the website, its basically roulette with your time and your evening plans. That's what they think of you as a customer. 

That's not OK. 

As I said, there are a million other equal or better options - I suggest you go to them. You aren't missing anything, expect that crappy feeling of seeing your evening plans screwed or waiting for hours for a meal that in the end won't be very special.

There is nothing sweet about this place.

Our wait for lunch on Good Friday was relatively short. I got on line at 11:15am and they promptly opened the door at 11:30am, where about 30 people got seated in the first wave. The entire meal takes about 50 mins from start to finish so make sure you time it well to minimize your wait.

Hubby and I went with the Nozawa Trust Me. I wasn't super hungry so was debating between that and Trust Me but went with Nozawa since it comes with 4 more pieces and it was our first (and now the only) time so why not!

Service was decent especially since gratuity was included already.  

Edamame was a bit too salty, not as good as the frozen edamame from trader joe's.  Quality of the sushi was subpar, taste was pretty bland.  Where is the nature sweetest of the fish? The pieces with yuza sauce were too saucy, and thus I couldn't even taste the fish itself.

The only notable item was the blue crab hand roll. Nori was toasted so you can taste the seaweed as it melts in your mouth.  But you can easily get the hand roll from KozuNori.

We overheard the couple next table asking for uni sushi. They were told the season is over so they don't carry uni now.  Really?? I just had uni at Sushi on Jones 5 days ago.

If you are looking for a REAL sushi experience, go to Tanoshi.  Alternatively, sushi on jones is similarly priced but the quality is much much better (comes with uni and wagyu).

FINALLY had the opportunity to try Sugarfish two weeks ago. I went with a friend that had already been so she went around 6pm on a Wednesday night and we were sitting down at 7pm. We were lucky as the wait is normally at least 2 hours. The restaurant has a great ambiance. It's very dark and on the smaller side, but they have a cute lounge on the second floor where you can wait/have a drink before you sit down. 

When it comes to sushi I'm normally not adventurous. I usually only eat Tuna, but I decided to be open minded as Sugarfish is known for their omakase/boxes. I went with the "Trust Me" as my friend at first tried the "Trust Me Lite" and said it wasn't enough food. Best decision to order one of the prefix box options. This way I was able to try most of the sushi Sugarfish has to offer. The quality was amazing and everything tasted so fresh. I also ordered two pieces of scallop sushi on the side, which were excellent! 

Next time I come back I may not order the box, but now know what I liked best. Highly recommend trying this out for your first time! Also, I need to mention that I'm allergic to shrimp and the waiter was extremely accommodating and made sure my sushi was prepared separately. Loved my experience overall and can't wait to go back soon!
Great sushi. Clean and simple flavors. The chef clearly wants to showcase the freshness of the fish. Fav was halibut and the crab hand roll
This place is amazing The sushi is prepared well and each piece of sushi I had from the trust me option melted in my mouth! I enjoyed the fish on the warm loose rice. Definitely coming back!

One of the best sushi places I've been to!! So delicious, so fresh, hits the right spot. Here is the bet part -- the price point is so reasonable, it's UNREAL. There is a little bit of a wait but it's worth every penny!

100% does not deserve the hype or the long wait lines. It's a decent deal for the amount of food and quality, but their signature dishes have way too much signature sauce that overpowers the fish. It's suppose to compliment the fish, not make the fish and rice a medium for ponzu and soy sauce. Don't get me wrong, other pieces that didn't have the signature sauce, were great and I'd recommend those pieces only (ask the waiter which pieces are already seasoned).

Everything we (New Yorkers) thought we knew about the hierarchy of sushi has changed. The mold has been broken, the glass ceiling has been shattered, and the standards are redefined. 

Sugarfish, welcome to New York City. Enjoy your stay as much as we have enjoyed having you so far, as evidenced by our willingness to wait over 5 hours for one of your tables.

Prior to the opening of Sugarfish, if we wanted lower priced high end sushi we were stuck with Tanoshi, Sushi Dojo, and the laughably under portioned Sushi on Jones. (I might also throw Domodomo in that list, but they do a little bit more than just nigiri.)

Sushi in NYC has always been a prime example of the phrase "you get what you pay for." However, Sugarfish and a few other new contenders (Uogashi, Kanoyama, and Katsuei to name a few) have begun to blur the lines dividing top end and mid tier sushi.

While the sushi here will never match the quality of NYC's big boys like Nakazawa, Kura, Akami, and etc. Sugarfish's quality to price ratio is unrivaled. The value here is a really really big deal, and the sushi is actually really freakin fantastic.

Go with the Nozawa Trust Me. At 45 dollars for lunch it's a steal. The course plays out as follows:

Edamame
Tuna Sashimi
Albacore Nigiri
Salmon Nigiri
Yellowtail Nigiri
Snapper Nigiri
Hirame Nigiri
Toro Hand Roll
Blue Crab Hand Roll
Special Nigiri

The seafood was all fresh and well prepared. Some pieces came with ponzu, scallions, or soy. Every garnished worked well and in harmony of with the fish.

The rice was a particular favorite of mine, and shockingly the target of a lot of criticism from my fellow users. I love the way the  loosely packed rice crumbles and dissipates in the mouth. It has bold vinegar flavors and come out a little warmer that what you would get at a true omakase. However I believe it is a genius preparation on their part. This creates a buffer for the travel time between chef to table so it can best replicate the sushi bar omakase temperature. I think it works very well.

Outside of the Trust Me specials I also recommend their specialty pieces a la carte. Specifically the Scallops, Unagi, and Albacore Belly.

Service was great, our waiter was attentive, he did a great job describing the menu and offering suggestions. Waters were refilled promptly and the staff that put the food on our table explained to us what each piece was.

My (beautiful, amazing) friend stopped by at 4:40 on Sunday afternoon and we were seated about 30 minutes later. We both ordered Sapporos but mine didn't come for some reason... made contact with the waitress a few minutes later and she exclaimed "your drink!" before I even asked. $7 a pint ain't a bad deal for Gramercy...

I did by-the-piece because I didn't care about a decent chunk of the Trust Me's but those are definitely the best deals here. Even so, 2 pieces for $6? Sign me up.

Salmon, snapper, and sea bass: each pair of nigiri had perfect texture and flavor. Rice was good too. Appreciated the citrus-y sauce on the snapper. Unfortunately they were out of fluke, which is my favorite.

I also got a toro handroll to try, which came out lightning fast (like within 2 minutes)... and then strangely my friend only received 1 of her 2 handrolls. And then they tried to give me a toro handroll again. We figured out pretty quickly what had happened and they encouraged me to eat the extra handroll and said they would cover it. Her missing roll came a few minutes later. A+ customer service.

The quality you get for the price is absurdly good for New York. The space is sexy. What are you waiting for (other than the wait?).

I finally had the chance to try sugarfish today and the experience was phenomenal. My friend and I came right before the 6pm rush and got seated within 15 minutes since we didn't mind sitting by the counter. 

Our server Kat, recommended The Nozawa trust me omakase to get the whole sugarfish experience. They start you off with edamame, which is already prep in advance so it's cold. (In case you expect a warm bowl of edamame) This gives you that extra bouncy crunch when you bite on it.

Then the Toro sashimi comes next, it has a tangy sauce bathe with green onions which gives your palate kick in the mouth right before your sushi pieces rolls in...

We had the following in order:
Albacore Sushi 
Salmon Sushi
Snapper Sushi
Yellowtail Sushi
Seabass Sushi
*Daily Speical - two big scallops sushi*
Toro hand roll
Blue crab hand roll

Each slice of fish was cut into a perfect bite size piece that was laid on a warm bed of rice. You can literally taste every grain of rice as you bite into the sushi. My favorite was the salmon, yellow tail and the scallops. Each bite of the sushi instantly melts into your mouth, it was A-mazing.

There were a couple of sushi pieces that is already glazed with the tangy sauce so you don't need soy sauce. I prefer eating my sushi without the tangy sauce so I can actually get the taste of the fish in my mouth.

Thus, My overall experience with sugarfish is a 4/5, the staff was attentive, the ambiance is cozy and the wait wasn't long.

Tip: Arrive earlier to beat the crowd if you have a larger group, and eat a piece of ginger after each sushi to cleanse your palate for the next sushi :)

The staff was pleasant and hospitable. They've nailed that part of the dining experience. What we didn't enjoy was getting served in increments. That translated into some of us having no food in front of us for extended periods of time while others ate. We even had to remind our server about forgotten items that never arrived at the table. She promptly got them served to us, however. 
The food is sufficient. We selected a variety of sushi and rolls and they were just fine. Nothing special. In fact, I was surprised at the lack of flavor. I'm talking lack of natural flavor that you'd expect from quality, fresh sushi. Much of it was bland. Maybe because of the hype and the long wait to get a table, we went in expecting to be blown away. The reality was that it was more of a fuss than was warranted.

First time visiting and trying this experience. A friend of line had been craving it all week so I went with her. 

We arrived at 5PM and waited about 10 minutes before getting to the counter. We were told a table for two would be available shortly at the bar. It was only a 15 minute wait. We sat in the corner in front of the sink, lol. Not too bad to be honest. According to google 5PM is prime time for them so my friend and I got lucky! 
  
The servers name was Kat. During our meal another customer found that her glass was cracked. She had already finished half her drink before noticing. Kat rushed to grab the glass and bring it to the back. She was quick to solve the issue. 

Below are some notes of my experience:

Salmon - very fresh. Sesame adds a nice texture 

Large scalops - tangy and spicy. 

Toro hand roll - so flavorful. Sad when I finished it. Warm and savory.

Meal ended awkwardly as we were not made aware that our daily special was already included during our meal. 

I believe we should also include a description of the bathroom because it's part of the experience, no? 

soap label are a nice touch. Spacious. Smelled of urine that hadn't been cleaned all day. Located on second floor accessed via front of restaurant. 

Overall, if visit again. I felt very satisfied and not sluggishly full. Good first experience!

Forgot to add that the green tea comes out of packets :( I was hoping it was matcha powder.

Everything was delicious and the service was awesome. 
Got the sample set price meal for lunch and it was PLENTY of food!
Delicious!

YES YESS AND YESSS

Sugarfish is a godsend from LA. I wasn't expecting much, but fish quality is SUPREME. Rice is warmer than other places. Some days rice is too vinegary and nigirizushi will fall apart, if you notice this and don't like that, ask them early on to ease off the vinegar in your pieces. 

If you're asking yourself, I'm not that hungry so maybe go the lite option? then I ask you, why are you even here?! Get either the -Trust Me $39 (crowd fav) or -Nowaza Trust Me $51 (includes daily specials - SO WORTH IT). You won't regret it. Lunch is cheaper (trust me lunch $33 vs dinner $39). 

TRUST ME
-Some pieces are pre-sauced, like the albacore with a soy sauce and the sea bass with a ponzu sauce. They weren't bad but I like the pure fish [unsauced]. 
-Albacore tuna was one of the most delicious cuts I've ever had. So soft, really just melts away. No fishiness, just clean and delicious. Definitely a standout piece and probably a reorder
-Salmon is the only one where I find it to be a tad slimy
-Handrolls: I preferred toro but I appreciated the bright brine of the blue crab, creamy too. Hand rolls here are very unique as toasted nori, warm rice and cold fish create temperature magic on your palette, a warm-cool delight.
-Uni (a la carte): Finally. I have been waiting to try Santa Barabra Uni and this was it. I've had so many bad pieces of uni before this, but THIS WAS GOOD - the zenith of uni. Unbelievably creamy, no metallic aftertaste, top of the line sea urchin.This uni was pristine and just divine. Great finish to my meal. 

FREE BIRTHDAY MEAL
You get a free* Trust me Combo on your birthday. How? The first time you eat here, fill out the card at the end. You'll get an email asking to confirm your account. If you eat there another time BEFORE your birthday, you will get a coupon 1 week before your next birthday. Make sure you check-in with them via another card on your 2nd visit. *Must go twice between birthdays (fill out cards BOTH times). Why was that so long? Because. they explain it TERRIBLY on their website. You're welcome. Please don't compliment 'Thank you'. Just take me out! haha, no seriously, you owe me a trust me bc I just got you a free one.. Gift cards accepted too. message me for address. No seriously. You owe me a Trust me! I know where you yelp!

Considering the quality, prices here are wayy CHEAPER relative to Nakazawa, Shuko, Yasuda, Masa, O Ya and all the other NYC sushi omakase giants

Please Sugarfish. add more NYC locations. This one gets ridiculously packed! If you're even debating on lunch (cheaper), make sure you come by 11:30 or you're gonna wait. God was on my side as I strolled in around 12:15 and there was ONE seat opening up at the counter! God Bless (prayer hands emoji). Stories of hour-long waits are true, don't be those people! Also, your whole group must be present before seated. A standout meal overall and really a fantastic mission at Sugarfish. Their integrity really translates into their food. Thank you Sugarfish!

I'm from LA and am a bonafide SugarFish junkie so finding out that one opened in NY was like finding out Santa is real. I was really frickin excited. The wait can be extreme and I'm not good at waiting for food so today was my first experience. I came solo at 5:30p on a Friday and was sat immediately in the back at the bar. I went with my usual: Trust Me but sub scallops for salmon and cut rolls instead of hand. I was not disappointed!!!! It holds up. The fish is just as fresh and every bite melted in my mouth. Special notes: You don't tip here, as is customary in Japan and real Japanese establishments. Also, the waiters are very knowledgeable and helpful with substitutions so definitely ask questions. Daniel is especially wonderful. 
Run, don't walk, but please don't take my seat!!!!!

The food is Sugarfish which is all over LA which is always good and tastes the same and you know what you're getting if you're familiar with Sugarfish. The fish melts in your mouth, the rice is warm, your mouth and belly will be delighted...

We waited about 3 hours for a seat on a Thursday evening after putting our name in at 7 PM. Okay, fine. To add insult to injury the staff at the front isn't the most pleasant to deal with, but maybe that's a NY thing, I don't know. One of the staff walked by me in such a crazy rush that my iphone was knocked out of my hand, landed face down on the floor and I ended up with a cracked screen. Hayely, the "general manager" came to apologize because "sometimes these things happen" and it just "gets so crazy". Alright, sure.

I was with a colleague who wanted to try the food though I don't suggest waiting 3 hours to eat here, or putting up with the condescending way they like to speak to you. A number of people walked out in a fit of rage saying things like, "they didn't even look at me!". It is what it is but NY is full of good food, full of good sushi and full of better service from the minute you step in the door.

If you're ever in LA, go to one of the MANY Sugarfish locations there instead.

Super yummy fresh fish.
The seaweed is winning ticket here, fresh and crispy! Hand rolls to die for.

Sugar fish is amazing! Went for lunch - arrived a little after noon on a rainy day and there was no wait for a table. Got the "Trust Me" and all of the food was delicious and timely. The service is impeccable - everyone is extremely friendly and helpful.  I loved my experience and definitely will be back! So glad Sugarfish is in NY!

A very pleasant experience. Got in in a reasonable time for lunch during the week. Had the Trust Me (chef's menu) and felt a couple of the varieties were pretty indistinguishable. The fish was otherwise tasty and very nice in terms of temperature, size, etc. Found the rice fell apart to easily--whether picking up with chopsticks or fingers. Worth eating, but not celebrating.

So after drooling over my friends' IG and FB pictures of this place, I knew I had to make a date with her & her hubby while my bf and I were visiting NY. Sugarfish doesn't take reservations, but figured hey if we're first the wait won't be that bad. Unfortunately, other people had this thought and I was running late. So we had to wait about an hour, but with all the cute shops in Flat Iron, it wasn't a big deal.

We received our text that our table was ready and headed back to the restaurant. We still had to wait a bit longer, but that just gave us an opportunity to order a beer from the bar. Once we were seated, the waiter explained the menu and how it works as it was me and my bf first time. We all had The Nozawa Trust Me and I couldn't have been more delighted. Every single thing they brought out was amazing!

We started with the organic edamame which was good. Then moved on to the tuna sashimi which melted in my mouth. Next came the albacore and salmon... salmon, the butter of the sea I tell you! Next up was the snapper, yellowtail and daily special (scallop). The snapper was great, the yellowtail was hella good and the scallop was good, but I would've gladly traded it away for more yellowtail. The toro and blue crab hand rolls were also very good. I liked how the nori didn't get soggy and limp.

I'm glad I was able to have my first Sugarfish dining experience with some NY friends and hopefully I can plan a trip to the original in LA soon. Domo aritgato!

Great omakase and it is a must! The sushi rice is a touch more vinegary and warmer than most restaurants, but I didn't mind at all. The service was great - attentive and informative, not pushy, and did not rush us out despite the wait.

We went with the Nozawa Trust Me set. I was a bit full at the end, almost uncomfortable. But everything was so delicious! My favorites were the yellowtail, the snapper (melt. in. your. mouth.), and the blue crab roll. I would not hesitate to come back for another round!

Finally made it over to this popular LA sushi chain. The hype is still a real thing as we were told we had to wait for 2.5-3 hours for our table of 3 on a Thursday night at 730. it ended up being about a 2 hour wait but with their awesome app we waited around the corner and could see what number we were in line. They do a great job of telling you what this place is and what it isn't. It's not a high end fine dining sushi experience, however, the ambience is great and they did a awesome job with designing the space. The service is impeccable (with prices as low as theirs for good quality seafood they need to have a fast turn around/high volume). I had the $51 tasting menu and it was great! If you aren't too hungry I would get one of the lesser options or order a la carte. Setting your expectations to what the establishment is offering and telling you, you won't be disappointed!
This is easily the best sushi in Manhattan. Fresh, smooth and perfectly prepared. Highly recommend.

As an LA native, I'm no stranger to sugarfish and frequent the Calabasas one often. The NYC one has exactly the same menu as the others, and felt as if I were back on the west coast. Of course, they have the same policies for waiting until the whole party is there and whatnot, but the same great service as well. I usually go for the trust me, both for lunch and dinner, and find it to be a good amount of food. If scallops aren't included, I typically order a side of those too. Don't come here expecting to order crazy sushi rolls and whatnot (they don't have them), the set menu is the way to go. 

My favorites are the albacore (melts in your mouth), tuna sashimi, and the halibut.
Food is incredibly dank and fresh. Slightly expensive given it is not very filling but still outstanding. Crowd is pretty douchey, LA-y otherwise would've given 5 stars.

Sugarfish has AMAZING sushi. (The fish is extremely fresh and extremely delicious.) I would highly recommend going for one of the three omakase (or "Trust Me") options if you want to try a good variety of sushi.

The restaurant does not take reservations and does not seat people until the full party is present. The tip is also calculated straight into the price of the food, so you don't have to worry about that when you pay.

Given the quality of the sushi, Sugarfish is probably one of the best deals in town. I got the Nozawa set and was loved every piece. Usually there are parts of omakases that I feel like I could skip if I went back, and this really wasn't the case here, I was legit satisfied by every piece of fish I ate. The service was great, the servers were super knowledgeable about both the fish and sake, and it helps that they were also super nice.

If you want americanized rolls, this place is 100% not for you, but if you want a really solid traditional sushi meal for a good price, this is a great place to be.

Underwhelming and overpriced. Not worth the hype or the wait. 

Went for lunch and had one of the set omakaze style menus. The decor is modern, chic, and clean. Unfortunately we sat at the bar / counter - not really a bar since it is actually the service counter for the staff. We got to watch them fill up glasses of water, serve the premade (and not properly kept) edamame plates, and watch the kitchen staff through the back window. Our waitress was lovely although she definitely served people who arrived after us their food before us. 

Fish was very fresh, although given that the restaurant / kitchen looked like more of a fast casual kitchen than a traditional sushi kitchen, the time between ordering and serving was quite long. Edamame was premade, our waitress forgot the wasabi and ginger, the tuna sashimi wasn't anything to write home about, the other rolls included in the "trust me" were also tasty but not worth the inflated price / small servings. We also had some cut rolls: scallops, lobster, and yellowtail. The scallops were mediocre and didn't have much taste, the lobster was basically a lobster salad and definitely not worth the price. 

But hey, service is included and you don't have to tip?

I think sugarfish is really around a 3.5. I'd heard mixed reviews about it, but still found it to be better than what I was expecting.

I finally managed to get a table around 4 PM on a Sunday after stopping by a few times during the week and being told ridiculous wait times. I ordered a la carte and had the bay scallops and tuna sushi, along with salmon and blue crab hand rolls.

I absolutely loved the sushi rice! It had the perfect consistency and I really liked the vinegar taste. The wasabi and ginger were also extremely fresh. I ended up feeling like the fish was actually a weak point - the quality is relatively good for the price, but not as good as I would have liked. In the hand rolls it almost felt like the fish was overpowered by the rice and seaweed. I also disliked that the scallops were completely coated in mayo.

Overall, sugarfish is definitely a bit pricey for the quality and portion size, but I liked the other (aside from the fish) ingredients enough that I would go back if the wait time dies down.

So stop reading this right now and GO. That's all I'm saying. The best sushi I've ever had. Period (and I've had my share). No words could properly describe the experience other than saying that you just have to go. Order the chef's tasting and be prepared to be blown away. Went for lunch and it was actually quite reasonable price-wise as well.

After hearing about this amazing LA chain, I waited months for the hype to die down a bit. We came here on a rainy Sunday afternoon and scored a table for two right away! 

We got the Trust me Nozawa for $45 for our omakase lunch, and it was well worth it. You really get the bang for your buck. Oh, and the tip and tax are included in the price. Even better! 

The service was great, food came out quickly, and the meal was surprisingly filling. I also really enjoyed the green tea here. 

My favorite dish was actually the salmon. They put sesame seeds on top which complemented the fish perfectly. It really melted in my mouth. Other standouts were the large scallops and yellowtail. 

For some of the fish, they doused them in sauce which I thought was a bit over the top. My only complaint is to not have the sauce overpowering the flavors. It worked for the scallops but not for the others. The rice was SO good. 

Overall, a no frills omakase spot with great value. Can't wait to be back!

My favorite sushi in LA is now gracing NY with its presence. Luckily I happened to be in NY for my birthday and could not pass on the opportunity to claim my birthday Trust Me meal. I came after the lunch rush and was promptly seated at the bar. The vibe is lively and service is always the best. Special shout out to AM Jeff for making me feel special on my birthday. My favorite specials are albacore belly, uni and salmon sashimi. Sushi was very fresh and salmon melted in my mouth per usual. I subbed out blue crab hand roll for bay scallops and there is nothing better than biting into the crispy nori and savoring the warm rice. Lobster roll is a must as well. Can't wait for SugarFish to take over NY!

Let's start with the wait. We waited a solid 2 hours, but we ended up walking around and getting a drink nearby so that wasn't a huge deal because we were aware there was going to be a long wait. They texted us when a table was available and give you 10 or so minutes to get back to be seated.

Because it is so busy, I didn't find the waiters/waitresses to be too friendly but more so just trying to get things out as quickly as possible. This place had been hyped up for a while so I was excited to try the sushi. It was quite different than what I usually order but it was a nice surprise.

We both got the Trust Me and it was definitely enough for dinner. My favorite was the blue crab roll - definitely order that! Wish I had more than one. All the sushi was very fresh and nice and light. I know some people say that it was overpriced, but to be honest this was about right for the amount of food and having tip included.

I would go back, if I had a lot of time to spare but I'm definitely not running back. I would give this a 3.5/5
Delicious sushi, now one of my favorite places in the city. The wait is worth it. The manager and the server were wonderful. :)

Everything was so amazing from the service to the food that melts in your mouth. Went to put my name in at 6:30 knowing about the long wait on a Saturday got seated around 8:45. Worked out perfectly for us!

This is a new type of sushi for New Yorker's.  What do I mean by this?  Well it isn't expensive high end sushi that you need reservations and to get dressed up for, but it ain't the typical bland sushi that you can get at any walk in Japanese restaurant either.   

It's somewhere in the middle.  You can get high quality tasting fresh fish for a cost of only $45 (including tax & tip).  I read all the reviews before I considered going and was actually not going to try it because there was so many mixed reviews.  But I happened to be in the neighborhood and wanted some good quality sushi.

First the wait, waited about 1.5hrs on a weekday for lunch.  So we had a very late lunch but that's ok because we walked around to Flying Tiger and Trader Joe's.  We got the Trust me for $45 and if you count, you get 13 pieces of sushi.  It wast just enough to fill us up and not feel overly full.  Although I kinda wish they'd have dessert.

Yes the sushi comes out pretty quickly, it's because they're a "fast casual" place.  You want service fast, you want a shorter wait, am I right? 

The fish was perfectly done, the rice was perfectly done, service was fast and reliable. No complaints here, except that they ran out of the Uni.  I hope they open another location so this one can get some relief, they turn the tables so quickly I'm not surprised they don't run out of ingredients.

Service was friendly they have a waiting area upstairs as well, equipped with bathrooms. Anyways, we ordered the nozawa trust me it comes in the order listed and they serve it as soon as it's made. Which uh I kind of expect from most restaurants but sure. All the fish were fresh and good. Two exceptional ones were the tuna and the snapper. The only drawback was, as other reviewers pointed out, the vinegar or whatever was really strong. What's worse is they put it in the rice so when you go to pick up the nigiri, it falls apart. They only put the vinegar with a few pieces so it wasn't that big of a fault. But I'd recommend them to just lightly coat the fish/seafood with the vinegar instead...the flavor will be there and hopefully not too strong and the rice won't fall apart 

Overall a good sushi joint. Kind of pricey though and it didn't fill me or my gf up so not good in that sense. Otherwise a nice sushi place with room to improve. Service was good decor was clean

Trendy, Trendy, and Trendy. Sugarfish is overall a solid place to grab a bite to eat, but the quality of the food is a tad bit overhyped. The Trust Me is good, but I am not a huge fan of the handrolls. My date had the Trust me Lite and she thought it was good (the rice being the best part). However, she did not feel like the food was worth the price.

I ordered a trust me light, loved every damn bite. This could be the best sushi I've ever had. My party of 2 sat at the downstairs bar on a Wednesday night at about 6:30p on 6/14/17. Service was solid, the manager was chipper and kind, the server was a nice kid with glasses. Beer was cool.

I would give this five full stars-- maybe even six if it were possible-- if it weren't for the absolutely ridiculous line. 
I'll start with the good, though, because it was an amazing meal. I got the Trust Me and Trust Me lite boxes. The sushi was the freshest fish I have ever tasted. Each plate of food they brought out was better than the last. The rice was actually sweet, but in a really good way, a way I could never have imagined. Each flavor was totally unique. Not even just to the restaurant, but no two dishes tasted mildly the same. I was happily surprised by everything served. I usually leave sushi restaurants starving, but after Sugarfish I was perfectly full. The service was good and the place is cute inside-- I would recommend turning a few lights on as it is not trendy to be THAT dark.  

Now for the bad. I walked up to the restaurant and there was already a line out the door. Once I got to the hostess to be seated, I was told it would be an hour and a half to a two-hour wait. I had planned my entire night around this meal, so, naturally, I waited. I walked around Gramercy area for a while which was fine. Almost two hours later, I was texted to go back to the restaurant. Once I got back, I still had to wait for the table to be cleaned. Someone that had just walked in was told that they would have to wait 4 hours to eat. It was already 8pm. Ridiculous! I don't care how trendy, hip or cool your restaurant is. It is downright rude to tell someone that the wait is that long. And, it does not make it seem cooler! Take reservations, add more tables! It's insane. 
Was it worth an hour wait? Definitely. Two hours? Still, yes. Three? Probably not. Four? Absolutely not. Nothing is worth that unless it is sushi made out of 24k gold that is never ending!

All in all, I had a great meal. I am happy I was not the person with the four-hour wait. The food was great. I would love to go again, but as a normal person with a real life schedule, it is a bit hard to wait around like that.

I totally recommend this place if you are a huge fan of raw fish. Everything is raw here except for the rice haha big fan of freshness! We got here around 7pm and didn't get seated until 9:15pm. Be prepare for a long wait !! Tips are also included in the bill.

Summary:
A "new" restaurant brought to you from La-La Land of LA that promises a "different kind of sushi dining experience" that falls flat and far short of expectations.  The chefs promise only traditional sushi of the highest quality however, barely improve upon supermarket sushi.  The 2-4 hour wait is definitely not worth the wait or hype.  Skip this place.

Food:
I can't say anything bad about the quality of the actual fish.  All of it was very fresh.  But that's to be expected of anything above gas-station-sushi.  What does Chef Jiro, Chef Nakazawa, and other famous sushi masters say the secret to good sushi is?  The rice!  Sugarfish massively fails on this simple, yet key metric by which to judge sushi.  The rice barely stuck together, was almost runny and honestly way too vinegar'y.  What the hell?  #EpicFail

Service:
The last time I checked, it's the 21st century, 2017 to be precise.  There are such services as OpenTable, Resy, and even Yelp for god's sake!  Why the hell don't you have a reservation system in this day and age?  Absolutely unacceptable.  

While we promptly received our food, the care and attention of the majority of Japanese restaurants simply was not there.  No instantaneous water refills?  Come on!

Atmosphere:
Ah, I see what they were going for here... "Intimate"  Yet another #EpicFail

Instead of being dimly lit, the place is barely lit at all!  It is quite a cavernous venue but increase the lumens if only by 10%.  I could barely see my date let alone the terrible sushi rice!

Decent sushi place.  Reasonable pricing for sushi.  However, I have been to better sushi places in nyc.  If you are looking for an affordable sushi, then nozawa can be a good choice, but if you are willing to pay $10 more, i know several places that serve better sushi than nozawa.  I was not impressed by the food here.

This review is for takeout! I ordered takeout with my sister and her hubby and Sugarfish did not disappoint! We got the "To-Go Trust Me" ($40) which included edamame, tuna sashimi, 2 pieces of albacore tuna, snapper, salmon, and yellowtail, 4 pieces tuna sushi, and 4 pieces of crab sushi. We also ordered extra rolls (8 pieces each) of scallop, tuna, and salmon, and 4 pieces of eel sushi. The takeout experience was great- you order and pay on the website and they immediately send you an email with your receipt and an email with the estimated time for pickup. The sushi was fresh and perfectly cut. The eel was my absolute favorite and I loved that it came in a cute lunch box with directions on sauce pairings. I thought it was very reasonable in price (came out to $33 each for 3 people) and definitely worth every penny! If you want to dine in you should make reservations or call ahead to see the wait time as it has been super packed since opening!

The thing to do here is apparently their omakase, or chef's choice menu. But here it's a bit of a cheat, because it's a preset menu that basically doesn't change, other than maybe seasonally. When I think omakase, I think of the chef deciding in the moment, or at least each day, what they want to serve. This is a preprinted, online, menu, that's invariable other than, if you get the biggest of the three selections, one daily special.

The place is a bit frantic, and on a rainy Tuesday afternoon was filled to the gills with people. I was actually surprised that I got in at a table rather than the sushi bar. So was my waitress, who pointed out several times over the course of the meal how lucky I was to have a table. Especially one by myself. Leaving one seat open with no one in it who was eating. Thanks, ever so.

The sushi, all good. Very fresh. They have lots of rules. Is this a new thing, rules for eating sushi? The menu tells you (with my commentary): Rice should be warm and loosely packed so it melts in your mouth (I found it odd - too warm, and so loosely packed that most of it fell apart when trying to pick it up); Each plate is served as soon as it is prepared, so don't wait to eat it (and if you do, your waitress will remind you that it's waiting); Handrolls should be eaten right away while the seaweed is crisp (if it's properly toasted, it should stay crisp for more than just a couple of minutes); Dishes that are sauced, except sweet shrimp, should not be dipped in soy sauce (I didn't get sweet shrimp, and hey, I'll decide if I want to dip it in soy - the four guys next to me had made sludgy bowls of soy and wasabi and were dipping everything in it - at least they didn't get admonished for it); We decline requests for extra sauce, salt, or additional rice (the first two are just inhospitable, the last - who orders extra rice for their sushi?)

Overall, good, but nothing special or out of the ordinary. There are far better places to have sushi in NYC. Good experience but not one I'd go out of my way to repeat.

Served over warm rice, the fish is noticeably fresher tasting than your average sushi spot. Service is attentive and seemingly available at the right time without being annoying or overbearing. Wouldn't say this is a place for experimentation (haven't ordered outside the "trust me" menus), but would recommend sugarfish for a fresh, delicious meal in a casual, accessible setting. No res policy means you can prepare to wait, but the host will take down your number if it's for longer than 15 minutes.

This place is like industrialized sushi place, which lacks a personal touch and the quality is just average. I appreciate their internal decoration and no tip commitment but the taste of the food is just ok.

I have been a fan of Sugarfish since I lived in Los Angeles. I think all New York foodies were excited when this came into town. I have been there twice since it has opened. Both times I arrived and waited on line for over an hour. It is always worth it and the food is delicious! I give this 5 stars because I believe when value, quality, service, and ambiance are taken into consideration, this place has it all.

The New York Sugarfish is amazing. If you're new to the sugarfish restaurant you have to realize it's an experience, the putting your name down and waiting is part of the brand identity and making you get excited about eating the sushi. The sushi has ponzu sauce inside the rice and the rice is very very soft so it melts in your mouth. All the fish is fresh and each piece is so soft and delicious it can be addicting. Sugarfish is definetely a great and much needed addition to Nyc sushi scene because of its authenticity and great cozy feeling of its interior. It's truly the best and worth any wait time that is given

The sushi was amazing and prices were amazing. You can't get a better sushi meal for the price. I'd say that my dinner there was as good as some of the best sushi restaurants in the city but way cheaper. Really enjoyed it. Only negative is they rush you to order and the food comes out very quickly so you are in and out of there fast. But if you're hungry that's good I guess
For a super trendy place, the staff was very courteous and patient. Some of the dishes were good, and some were amazing.
Fresh fish, attentive service and a calming environment. Accepts no gratuity! I shall return

Came here due to their one Michelin star rating and I have to say I am pleasantly surprised by the sushi here.

I do enjoy the fact that it is not your typical stuffy Michelin restaurant, the staff is that is very easy-going and the service staff are very down to earth. Their menu simple, the tasting selections and offerings are simple into the point.

We had their most comprehensive tasting and every fish was the amazing. The rice was one of the best sushi rice I have tasted as it's flavoring was perfectly sweet and vinegary well the rice self was big and plump, and the texture was just taking enough so that stuff together for the sushi pieces but came apart in your mouth very easily.

For drinks we ordered the iced green tea, which was great and refreshing it a perfect complement to the sushi. Price point was spot on, if not on the more economical side. I can now see why there was a wait for lunch even at 2 o'clock in the afternoon!

The only downside is that it never seem to have to need which is one of my favorite sushi pieces.

Very good sushi, the omakaze (sic) isn't really a changing menu so not totally true experience. That being said, all the fish was well prepared and the rice not too tightly packed. The price is excellent for the quality that is received. When I finished my tasting menu I asked if there was anything else she recommend I try not on the tasting menu. She recommended the Unagi or the bay scallops. I listened to her suggestion and she did not steer me wrong. Be aware long waits are possible here.

Simply amazing. My boyfriend and I were starving looking for food at 10pm on a Tuesday and we thought why not check out the line at Sugarfish. We were seated immediately at the bar where we ordered the sampler platter an an extra maki roll of tuna. The portions are great so you don't leave feeling too stuffed but you feel like you are satisfied. I can't tell you the amount of sushi restaurants I've been to where I order a hundred things on the menu and then feel so disgusted by the end that I want to throw down the money and run. 

The fish here is of a much better quality than anything I've eaten in New York. We typically go to NOBU for this type of fare and let me just say, we will likely not be returning. The price is so reasonable and the fish is so much better that it's hard to justify going back (sorry NOBU).

Will be back.

This was the best sushi experience I have ever had. The quality of the fish was superb and the service was awesome. The warm sushi rice, how can I even begin to describe the quality of the rice! Orgasmic, delicious, and perfectly flavored to compliment the fish. This experience is definitely worth the wait and the prices are amazing for the meal you get at Sugarfish.

Ok, actually the sushi at this place is fantastic. Fish so fresh it melts in your mouth. Rice so flavorful it changes what you think sushi can taste like. I never eat scallops because shellfish that isn't fresh does me wrong, but today, I ate scallop nigiri for the first time in 10 YEARS. The service is minimalist, not really part of the experience, but with food this delicious, who cares! My gf and I both indulged in the larger portion Trust Me menu. It was all so good, but too be honest, it was a little more food than I would have preferred for lunch. Next time, I'll get the regular.

Sugarfish is a bit of a novel idea here in NYC. It's neither a run-of-the-mill sushi restaurant nor a high-end $200 Omakase. They serve good-quality sushi in an Omakase style, but about half the courses of a standard Omakase and a much more manageable price-point

We ordered the Nozawa trust me, which is their most comprehensive Omakase and includes 9 courses (10 if you count the edamame), and costs $45 per person. The quality of the fish was very fresh for the price point, and the presentation was persistent with most quality sushi restaurants. They also included Toro, Scallops and blue crab in their courses, so they didn't skimp on the expensive cuts of seafood either. 

The problem, I believe, comes when they attempt to bring all of these elements together to form the actual pieces of sushi and nigiri they serve. The whole was not greater than the sum of it's parts, and there was always one thing or another off about each piece of sushi we received.

For reference, an experienced sushi chef serving omakase would season the rice with a small amount of vinegar, insert a dab of wasabi, press it under a slice of fish, and brush the top with soy if necessary. This usually comes together perfectly as each piece would have varying amounts of wasabi/soy/rice depending on the type of fish.

Each piece we received at Sugarfish however, had too much or too little of one of these elements. Several pieces had so much soy that a lot of it would leak out into the plate it was served on, and everything else in the nigiri would be overpowered by the flavor of the soy sauce. A few other pieces just had far too much wasabi to the point it got uncomfortable. Two more pieces clearly had too much vinegar in their rice, and the bed of rice would fall out from under the fish before we could even get it to our mouth.

Now don't get me wrong, the sushi was not BAD, in fact it was pretty good. It was just the craftsmanship did not stand as a proper Omakase, especially when you are paying nearly $50 per person. If it wasn't for the quality and freshness of the fish, it would be comparable to going to a cheaper sushi restaurant where the patron can smother however much soy sauce or wasabi as they want on their sushi. 

I'm disappointed, but I also see a lot of potential in this restaurant. If I had to guess, I would say their issues stem from lack of experience. They have fantastic service, they have a beautiful space, and their ingredients are fresh and high quality, so the foundation is there. I'm looking forward to coming back again when they've hopefully gained a bit more experience crafting sushi.

The hype is not real. 

Tried to come here for dinner and was told there was a 2 hour wait so we ended up leaving. Came back for lunch a week later because the menu is basically the same but a little cheaper. 

Service was okay, we had to ask for them to refill our waters . At least they were smiling? 

My sister and I got the Nozawa trust me which consisted of a total of 10 pieces of sushi, 2 handrolls, edamame, and tuna sashimi. We were very full afterwards but we didn't pay to be full. We paid for good sushi, which it was not. 

First off, everything was fresh (two stars). That's it. There was too much rice with the sushi, and it also kept falling apart. What kind of sushi just falls apart when you pick it up?! Even ones I buy from the grocery stores don't do that. The sauce that was on some of the sushi was too vinegary. That's all I tasted for half the meal. When I tried to cleanse my palette with ginger I just tasted vinegar. HOW?! We just paid to eat vinegary rice. 

After leaving the restaurant I started feeling sick. About 30 minutes later, my sister felt the same way. 

Conclusion: fresh fish, too much rice and vinegar. Would not return.

Good sushi. I ordered in from here and got the trust me lite. I think the real experience for Sugar Fish is to eat there. However, I went at 715pm and there was a 2 hour wait...I'm not sure what the best time to go is to avoid this nuisance of a wait time. I wouldn't recommend ordering in unless you're willing to splurge on sushi. D'agostino, the super market, has equally as good of sushi. I'm hoping the hype is real when you eat at the restaurant. I will say though that the presentation in the box is spectacular and adorable. I think the next time I come here will be for a 2pm late lunch to get a few pieces of sushi in my tummy.

I get it, you get a hot restaurant that is the talk of the town, that's awesome and congrats on your extended wait times, with no possibility of reservations. That's not my issue.  My issue is with your pretentious staff whom are fresh out of college yet think they run New York because the work here.  Holy hell what a terrible experience.  Talked down too, chastised, ultimately, wanted to eat and get out of there fast. Get over yourself.  On top of that, really didn't think this sushi was that special. Would much rather find one of the 1000x options in the city with comparable sushi, but offer an accommodating staff.  Will not be going back, so many other restaurants that are popular and exciting in this great city that have so much more to offer.  Was really looking forward to coming here and it was a complete and utter let down.  Take some time to hire some competent staff and maybe I'll give it a go in a few years.

Wow. Almost at a loss for words! Had lunch today at  Sugarfish. First of all, I was so happy that there was no wait at 12 o'clock on a weekday. We were seated right away. All of the staff members were incredibly friendly. The menu is easy to grasp because there are three omakase options and only a few a la carte items. 

Two of us shared the Nozawa-Trust Me, which included an assortment of sushi, as well as edamame and sashimi (meant for one person technically but can be shared by two, as well). In addition we ordered two pieces of eel sushi and two pieces of sweet shrimp sushi off the a la carte menu. 

Everything was incredible - each bite contained the freshest fish that melted in your mouth. Most memorable was the albacore and also the daily special sushi which was scallop. We couldn't decide on our favorite because it was all so wonderful. The rice is served slightly warm and at times fell apart because of how soft it was. Very delicious. Most of the sushi was so flavorful you hardly needed soy sauce. 

Anyway, Sugarfish absolutely lived up to the hype I've been hearing. Lunch for 2 came to $77 including alcohol and tax (tip is also included in their prices). Will be raving to everyone I know about this restaurant!!

Everyone in LA is obsessed with Sugarfish, so I thanked the heavens above when one finally opened in NYC - and walking distance from my office, even better! Timing is of the essence at this location. They don't take reservations, and if you go during prime lunch or dinner hours you will definitely have to wait quite a while. Lucky for me, I'm a big fan of early bird eating so I like to go for lunch right when it opens at 11:30 or for a super early dinner (like before 6). 

By and large, most people get one of their set meals, the Trust Me ($33), the Trust Me Lite ($23), or the Nozawa ($45). Depending on how hungry I am that day I alternate between the Trust Me and Trust Me Lite. You may say that there are cheaper sushi lunch options out there and you'd be correct, but I challenge you to find a sushi meal that's as satisfying and with fish as high quality as this for this price. Each piece of fish is always perfect, the nori is always fresh, and the rice is heavenly. The servers will recommend which pieces to use soy sauce and which to eat on their own, and they encourage you to eat the hand rolls immediately so it doesn't get soggy. 

Every server I've had there has been informative and friendly, and they seem to have their timing down pat, so even if you got one size meal and your dining companion got a different one, you'll be eating at a similar pace. 

This is not the place to go if you're into one of those weird mutant rolls piled high with tempura or mayo. They're all about doing the classics well, and it's always the same menu except for a special catch that they tell you about that day. 

It's a clean, healthy, flavorful, and indulgent meal at a reasonable price in a sleek environment. Worth the early meal time, I'd say!
Was contacted by a regional manager which I appreciated it. Will update again should I make it back to this location.

Sugarfish- where have you been all my life! 

I've heard about this place in LA so when I heard there was one in NY, I had to try it out. Came here around 5pm- and got seated right away. 

Ordered the trust me lite and food comes out one at a time. Let me tell you... the rice is warm and the fish is fresh and buttery! I didn't have a favorite of the bunch but all ways very good. 

I can't believe I waited this long to try this place out. Modern atmosphere, dim lighting and friendly staff. No doubt I will be back!!!

Tired of spending hundreds of dollars on "you think you know your fish and how fresh it really is sushi" Then this place is for you. For $40 lunch you get a tuna app, 10-12 pcs of sushi & 2 hand rolls to finish, it's got to be the best deal in NYC. For dinner $50. And NO TIP NEEDED. Melt in your mouth warm vinegar rice is the Their signature here then topped with fresh fish already sauced up. Pop it in your mouth like you just don't care. Only downside is the wait & the boring pics that you will soon take.

I have been to sugarfish in LA uncountable times. 
Its so amazing and so good....it is seriously  a godsend to all sushi lovers from LA. 

This is the only place I can eat and love sushi next to Japan. isnt that sad? yet its good now that sugarfish is in NYC

Hypes:
- Best bang for your buck for an omokase in nyc
- fresh fish with the perfect blend of flavors that you dont need any soy sauce for the flavors unless they tell you. 
- get the "Trust me" - I always get that. Its the perfect amount of sushi without feeling over full or sick. 
- love how some rice is cold and some is warm. mmmMMMMMmmm

i have nothing else to say except that you need to go there.

Went for a weekday lunch at 11:45 and got seated right away at the counter. Service was excellent, food was even better. Ordered Trust Me menu and it was the right amount of food for lunch, and everything came out perfectly timed. Fresh sushi, great presentation, amazing taste.

Interesting sushi place. First of all be aware this is not a regular sushi place. Even unique amongst high end sushi places. There's no avocado. There's no spicy mayo. It's basically based on 3 tasting menu options where you eat what they feel like giving you lol. That said, the sushi was amazing! High quality fish of course, but the most unique part in my opinion was the soft sushi rice. It literally falls apart if you aren't careful when dipping it in soy sauce. While impractical, it was delicious! So soft the rice was and tasty, highly enjoyed the meal. Price was not outrageous at under $50 for a full 6 course tasting menu. Worth the detour to check this place out, I went during the week for lunch and there was no wait.
Excellent sushi, excellent price point. Whether you are sitting at the sushi bar or taking it to go for lunch, Sugarfish is always a solid choice. There is usually a wait but it goes fast!

It's 100% true - there's too much vinegar in the rice!  It overpowers and masks the underlying flavor of the fish.  

I went to Sugarfish for lunch this week.  My advice is to go early on a weekday.  The lunch menu offers a "Trust Me" selection at reasonable prices (tip included). The staff is well trained & professional. They give you sushi eating tips - "eat the handrolls immediately, so the seaweed is crisp."  That's nice but it kind of reveals who their audience is.  The restaurant is a dimly lit cavernous space. The sushi is ok but I wouldn't wait two hours for it.  A pleasant surprise - an open waiting area upstairs is very comfortable and well-lit. 

The bathrooms are spacious, gender-neutral and provide a choice of scented or unscented soap.  Unfortunately, the bathrooms are also too dark & it's a set up for disaster (some patrons missed the target - wet unappetizing floor).  

Bottom line: If you love innovative food at decent prices (like me), you'll love Sugarfish.  If you're into traditional/exceptional sushi, suggest heading uptown to Hatsuhana or Masa where you'll probably pay a lot more.
