The food was so fresh and delicious the only bad thing is that we had to wait 3 1/2 hours to get it. The wait was way to long , I wish they had other stores on the east coast, but  the food was still great

I've been back at least four times over the summer and the food is spectacular . Once you have sushi here you can't have it anywhere else. The least busy hours are usually between 2:30-5  Monday through Thursday. So you can just walk in and be seated .

This spot holds a special place in my heart. Forgive me, but I'm inevitably going to compare this to the ones I've had in LA.

I've been to the one by Union Square several times and each time has been very consistent. I always get The Nozawa set menu (plus a few extra pieces to fully embrace the eventual mercury poisoning I will have down the line). The most recent time here (a few days ago), I did the same. You can look up what that includes, but the ones that were memorable were the first tuna sashimi marinated in soy, albacore, salmon, yellowtail, snapper, sea bass, toro hand roll, blue crab handroll, and the daily special (scallop sushi)....so all of them. i also usually get a couple extra, and in this case, i got my go-to. Unagi (eel sushi). My girlfriend who also has oralgasms from sugarfish, usually orders an extra uni. Unfortunately, for the past 2 times, they haven't had any uni, which to say the least is disappointing. We asked the server why and they told us that if the chef doesn't like the uni they try in the morning, they won't buy it for the day. For that I forgive them, but i will never forget them robbing us of the buttery joy that is uni.

The first thing that most people notice is the sweet savory warm rice. Purists will say it's blasphemous, but any sushi lover will say it's bliss. The one in LA was my first glimpse, my portal, into the world of what quality fish tastes like. For most, it is the perfect segue into more advanced sushi experiences.

However, I do feel like the one by Union Square is not quite up to par with the ones in LA. While my normal everyday memory is poor, my tastebud's memory is keen. It may be that I only enjoyed LA's Sugarfish more because one never forgets their first love. Still, I highly recommend it. 

p.s. wait time can be long during peak hours, I suggest going around 3pm on a weekday.

Hands down the best sushi delivery I've ever had in NYC. I ordered via Postmates and had the best experience. The order arrived before the expected delivery time which was a bonus. I enjoyed the To-Go Lite. It was the perfect portion size and so incredibly fresh! My favorite roll was the blue crab cut. I loved how the sauce was separate on the side and that they provide pairing instructions. Seriously obsessed. Can't wait to order again!

Would I wait in line for this? No. That's madness. This is decently priced, dumbed down sushi and it definitely hits the spot when you are craving sushi but it definitely isn't the real thing. The rice fall apart all the time, there is no miso soup and there really is no point of waiting to eat mediocre sushi. Go to LA, there are 20 of these shops.

Okay. I'm going to keep this short because all you need to know about this place is TWO things: 

1. It's possibly the best sushi that I've ever had that hasn't and won't break the bank. 
2. You NEED to come here and try this because it's life changing. 

I had it in LA for the first time while I was there visiting and it was so good I thought I was dreaming. I've been looking forward to eating it in NY and it's just as amazing. 

Look no further, this is your sushi spot.

Not bad quality for the price and no-tipping policy. Rice kept coming apart when you pick it up though and that's usually one of the first things true sushi chefs learn to master. 

Only come for lunch to beat the volume of foot traffic. We favored the blue crab roll the most! Sweet shrimp was very good, too.

Amazing.

Just Amazing.

This place is beyond great.  At first glance it may seem like there is not much to offer since the menu is rather small. However, the quality of the food is out of this world.

I got the "trust me" dish. At first I was hesitant due to the price ($39), but it exceeded all my expectations. The fish was so fresh that I don't think I will ever look at any other sushi dish the same.  In fact, some of the sushi pieces were so fresh that you don't even need to use any soy sauce with the dish

Go. Here...now or tonight if you're reading this on your morning commute

Rounding up from 2.5 stars. 

Finally was able to snag a seat with no wait! Granted, it was at the bar in the back at little before 12pm on a Saturday. 

I opted for the Trust Me ($33 for lunch). Everything came out timely and not once I felt rushed to finish my plate before the next one came. 

Overall, the fish was very fresh! The only thing I did not enjoy was the rice. The sushi chef smothered each sushi with sauce. I like a little seasoning on the fish, but please respect the rice. The rice was drenched with the sauce that the chef put on it. It made it hard to pick up each piece. The sauce also took away the sweetness of the rice - it was overwhelming. I'm not a sushi connoisseur by any means, but aren't sushi chefs taught to respect the rice and isn't one of Sushi 101/etiquette to not dump the rice part in soy? Why would the chef purposely destroy the rice?

Like I said, the fish was very fresh. If I find myself in the area during lunch time with no wait at all, I may Dine here again - but only if the chefs will honor my request to lightly sauce the fish only.

90 min wait on a Wednesday night. Worth it but wouldn't wait again. This is quite an experience everything's fresh and buttery. I had The Nozawa Trust Me for $51. it was enough but wasn't full. One thing I didn't like was how hectic it was in there, I mean for a place that serves sushi plate by plate, small portion at a time it was hectic. I felt a lot of anxiety in there with all the waiters running around. Regarding the rice, to me it wasn't too vinegary I thought it was loose/easily breaks apart but other than that I actually really enjoyed the rice. Also I didn't really have the need to dip my sushi into soy sauce. A lot of the sashimi has a bit of ponzu or something lighter. My favorite for sure is the albacore,salmon,and the big scallops those were like butter especially the albacore I could eat it alllll day. 

Anyways I would be back but I wouldn't wait another 90 mins.

Holy mother of god this place was delicious! I ordered The Nozawa TRust me and all I can say is that it was one of the best meals I've ever had. Unfortunately I didn't take pics (sorry) but how it works is they give you each piece or roll as its freshly made so that you can enjoy it while the rice is warm. All the pieces had either lemon or ginger rubbed on it or some kind of house made sauce. The fish just melts right in your mouth. I will come back again for more. The wait wasn't too terrible on a Thursday night .. about a hour to a hour and a half. But for all the sushi lover out there, stop in here and prepare to go to sushi heaven!!!

Wait was about 1 hour after putting names down at 5:30PM for a party of 4. The ambiance was romantic-ish with dim lighting and candles. I personally prefer more lighting so I can see my sushi. The rice was warm which didn't strike as something bad to me, but I felt like it had too much vinegar taste. Everything started to taste the same after the first few pieces because the vinegar/ponzu/yuzu was overpowering the fish pieces. I actually started to split the rice and the fish apart to eat. The rice was too wet which I assume from the soy sauce they put on the bottom which actually caused some breakage of the rice. I think it would be better if the chef brushed the sauce on top of the fish instead. The sweet shrimp a la carte wasn't very good. Again the rice overpowered the shrimp so all I taste was vinegar and yuzu. For the Santa Barbara UNI, it wasn't super fresh but wasn't terrible. I felt that they should've brush a tad of wasabi and soy sauce to mask the slightly bitter taste to it. Lastly, the shape of the sushi was more like a square. It actually makes it more difficult to put the whole piece in my mouth and I just found that there were too much rice with fish. For the price it's not bad. Anyways my opinions!

Over priced for what it is or really isn't !
They tell you what to eat and overcharge for it!
Example what they call two pieces of yellow tail for 7.25 is really one piece of yellow tail cut in half and served to you as two small sushi order!
No matter what one orders one is getting taken for a ride and you leave the restaurant hungry and feel you were robbed!
I will never go here again!
An order of Tuna each order is two pieces which is really one piece of sushi cut in half and counted as two pieces!! Order of yellow tail order of Eel and one green tea with two order of salmon and one order of Tuna which my wife ordered Eighty dollars!
Normally in any regular sushi restaurant would cost forty to fifty dollars max! I do not recommend this place you do not get value for your money they refuse to give you any sauces!!! Would not go back!

Wow!!! The sushi is the bomb! I just ordered a lunch take out. Super super great tasting sushi and sashimi!! 
Only thing I don't like is the wait time for the take out .. next time I'm placing the order on the website first

Finally had the opportunity to try this LA transplant. They only serve nigiri style sushi and hand rolls other than a small tuna sashimi appetizer. Most people get the Trust Me $39, trust me lite $29, or Nozowa $52? Which are presets. My bf and I shared a Nozowa and trust me and added on uni and sweet shrimp. Some of the sushi is presauced on purpose. I personally found the rice a little too sweet. I found the service excellent. We sat at the counter. Stand outs were the scallop, sweet shrimp, and toro hand roll. It's a NO TIPPING restaurant. Sake is reasonably priced. I live in the neighborhood so I went at 5:20 to put my name down and it was only 30 min wait so I had to wait around until the wait was longer  I wanted to eat around 7:30. I put my name down around 5:45 on a Friday quoted 1.5 to 2 hours but was texted to return in an hour. When I got there the table was ready right away. They told me that the wait time goes from 30 min to 3 hours around 5:45 to 6:45. For the quality of the fish I found this meal very reasonably priced. They also have a take out counter in the back right that you can order online on chowhound or delivered through a third party. Pricing is a little different on take out.

I have long anticipated sugarfish ever since the opening, but I have heard of the horrendous wait times. 

My friends have finally decided to venture out and to arrive early at 5:30 to beat the hours long wait. We were given an estimate 1-1.5 hour wait time on a Friday evening at 5:30! The wait time turned out to be only 1 hour though. The good thing, they have a very spacious comfy lounge upstairs (also where the restrooms are). 

Since it's a great location, you can head to a wine bar and sip wine while you wait, go to eataly or shop around. Bed bath beyond, west elm & the container store are all nearby! Also you're in the flatiron district with many retail shopping options. 

Our group of four settled for "THE NOZAWA TRUST ME" since the special of the day was scallops. We also added on orders of sea urchin from Santa Barbara and sweet shrimp. 

I enjoyed the tuna sashimi appetizer very much, as well as the salmon, scallop and blue crab hand roll. Those were the most notable pieces. Everything else was nothing special and quite average IMO. It was a big disappointment for all of us as we kept eating. I really disliked the sweet shrimp, it didn't taste fresh at all.  The Santa Barbara uni was also a disappointment to me. 

So there was a big issue with the "warm rice" and the amounts of ponzu and yuzu sauce that was drenched onto each piece of fish which the rice soaked up on. I loveeeeee ponzu/yuzu and even have it with my shabu shabu/hot pot. But to have ponzu overpower every single piece was way too dramatic. 

This establishment was certainly worth a try however it is completely overhyped. The quality of the fish does not justify a long wait time of 1-3 hours.

Sugarfish is responsible for my disdain for most every other sushi restaurant I've gone to after my first experience here. The freshness of the fish is AMAZING and the quality is second to none. Seems to always be a wait unless you go around 11pm, but it's well worth it to put your name down. 

I tend to lean towards the Nozawa Trust Me and am never let down. I eat fish here that I don't eat elsewhere because I'm sensitive to overly fishy smells and tastes. The flavors are light and subtle, basically perfect if you're not looking for a heavy meal.

The tuna sashimi, salmon sushi, unagi sushi, large scallop sushi, blue crab hand roll, and toro hand roll are my faves. 

Sugarfish is a non tipping restaurant and the service is very attentive. One time, the server stated the wrong daily special as being large scallop sushi when it was actually unagi for that night--and we ended up getting both on the house.

I love it here!

Flavorful sushi.
Tip is already included in the price.
Long wait time.

Very good sushi at a great price. The freshness, the quality of the ingredients and the way the rice is cooked makes this a great experience. I recommend going in the afternoon if you are not to keen on waiting for hours. I went on a Saturday afternoon at 3 pm and got seated right away. Plus, no tipping is always good!

Really really fresh fish. Melt into my mouth.
My Favorite part is it is probably only restaurant serve Sushi with warm rice...Love it. Last time I had it was when I want sushi for breakfast and they had to make it in a hurry with freshly cooked rice Which impressed me so much... any how, bit expensive for me. Spent $50 still have to eat few cookies to fill up...seriously...

I visited Sugarfish two weeks ago, and have reminisced about how great this sushi was more times than I'd like to admit. 

My wait time was about 90 seconds (I came for a solo lunch), and sat at the back bar. Upon sitting down, I received a good overview of the menu and decided to go with the "Trust Me." Each course was extremely fresh. I was really bummed when everything was over even though I was full. I will be back and highly recommend this place if you're a sushi lover or an $11.50 2-roll special kind of person. You will be pleased.

Ordered 'trust me' lunch, after half hour wait.  Quality/taste of sushi & hand rolls excellent.  However, portions were miniscule, service was pretentious, and overly 'precious'.  This is not the place, if you're really hungry; curiosity now satisfied after reading 'rave' reviews.

Got here at 430 on a weekday and the restaurant was mostly empty and no wait. Got the "Trust Me" which was $39 with a significant amount of sushi. Everything was fine and efficient but I can't say it's the best sushi I've ever had. Some pieces are covered with a strong citrus drizzle which provides a sharp refreshing flavor but overpowers the fish. The fish was also just fine; decently fresh but not melt in your mouth quality. The rice also isn't sushi rice with vinegar. The service was fine; sit by the bar as is tradition and your food will come to you more quickly (and fresher).

Having heard amazing things about sugarfish but also reading not so amazing things about sugarfish's delivery service (mainly that they can cancel your order after it's placed if they get too busy with in restaurant customers)---it took me a while to finally get my butt down to this blazingly hot sushi spot on a day & time where the wait was not long.  We went on a friday at 4pm --having heard that waits can be 2-3 hours at peak lunch / dinner time--our wait was 30 minutes--totally reasonable.  On the bonus side--sugarfish takes ur phone # & texts u when table is near ready--therefore if u have a long projected wait time you could theoretically go home or go to the park or shopping at the nearby flying tiger copenhagen store or like us we had happy hour snacks at beechers' handmade cheese shop across the street.  Either way it beats restaurants with loooong wait times that force you to linger outside the restaurant for old fashioned low tech name call!!

Now onto the food: sugarfish is known for its really really fresh fish--best showcased in simple hand rolls, sushi & sashimi--they don't sell the crazy 15 ingredient special rolls that often are on menu at lesser & common sushi joints.  The easiest way to order is to get one of the three Trust Me (trust me, trust me lite, nozawa trust me) set menus.  I got the basic trust me & my husband got the nozawa.  I also added on the uni sushi ($15 with 2 pieces) a la carte because I'm such a huge sea urchin fanatic.  

My favorites include: the salmon sushi with sesame seeds, uni sushi & the blue crab hand roll. 

Kid friendly? Not really, we went with a really small infant in carrier who just slept during our whole meal but I don't think sugarfish is great for older infants/toddlers as restaurant tables are small & no kids menu & no room for strollers.

This is an extremely overrated restaurant to the point that it's sad. I want to start off with the food - The fish is fresh. But that's all there is to it.

Our wait time was a few minutes shy of one hour for lunch on a Friday around 2PM which wasn't too bad. I did a bit of shopping and arrived back to the restaurant after receiving a text from Sugarfish. I ordered the "Trust Me" at $33 and my boyfriend had "The Nozawa Trust Me" at $45 for lunch. This is NOT a bargain because the food served here is nothing special and everything is drenched in yuzu or ponzu sauce.  Also, am I the only put off with how the fish is cut here? Everything looks like an amateur cut it and some pieces are cut way thicker than others. The rice here has a good vinegary taste to it, but is packed horribly. Every single piece is packed so loosely that everything breaks apart once the sushi is lifted off the plate. I had to carefully grip each sushi with all 5 fingers just so the rice would stay somewhat intact. And I want to emphasize on the flavorings - Yuzu, Ponzu, whatever. Almost everything was covered in these kinds of sauces. Why ruin a good piece of fish with excessive flavoring? I just don't get it. Toro handroll which is essentially unwanted toro pieces mashed up rolled into a handroll tasted like nothing, and the blue crab handroll was equally as disappointing. It had no crab taste that I honestly would've been better off eating kani. 

To top it off -  what's sad is I think I know why Sugarfish has such great praises and reviews that they are not deserving of. People don't know good sushi, don't know good fish, and don't know that the way rice is cooked and packed can make or break a piece of sushi. These two chicks next to me were raving that sugarfish was so amazing and the best they ever had. I wanted to LOL, but a random lunch on a Friday wasn't the best time to be rude to people with low standards. Yes, so Sugarfish is great for those with low to no standards, and also great to people who don't know what is good sushi.

I think Sugarfish is the only sushi I would ever order to-go. I ordered the Nozawa Trust Me, which is one of their takeout options. The sushi is presented in a container specific to the restaurant and specific to transporting your sushi without it getting squished. The lid of the container has images of your sushi and instructions on what to dip or add to the nigiri, all included. Included in the box was a ponzu sauce, soy sauce, yuzu ponzu, lemon wedge, wasabi, and ginger. It wasn't anywhere near the best sushi I've had in NYC, but it was still good.  I enjoyed the blue crab cut roll. If I was going to get sushi on the go, I'd get it from here--just for the fun and unique experience.

I have been to the LA location before and so I was so excited to learn that there was a spot in New York. Amazing quality sushi, creative presentation, wonderful tastes and flavors. This is my favorite place to get sushi because each time I walk away so pleased and so satisfied. I have never had anything on the menu that disappointed me. 

Yes, it is expensive and yes you will likely have to wait a while but I think it is worth it. The last time I was there I walked right in and sat down with no wait time. Some of that just depends on luck and of course the time of day you are going. Another time I have been there, I had to wait an hour.. so it really just depends. 

 Every time I have been, the service has been extremely quick.. so once you sit down- it shouldn't take too long to get sushi going. They bring it in rounds and in my experience I have never had a long wait in between rounds.

Can't go wrong here, just did the chef's tasting menu sushi tastes wicked fresh and is very good.

The wait is easiest served at a different spot, several little pubs around that can serve as a nice waiting room to get you ready
Great spot.  Amazing sushi.  It a fancy presentation but probably the best hand cut roll you will find

Since this a no tipping establishment, it showed in their lack of customer service. With the extremely long lines throughout the day, their focus is to turn tables as quickly as possible. I was quoted a 1 hr wait and was given the option to wait there or around the area. They'll text you when your table is ready. We chose this route but when we returned after receiving our text, they said we didn't return in time.  We were back at the restaurant within 8 min of receiving our text.  They made us wait another 30 min to be seated with no sincere apology on their part. 

The entire dining experience was so rushed. As soon as we finished one course, the next one was immediately dropped off at our table. 20 minutes after being seated, the omakase was over and we only went through half our bottle of sake. 

Overall the quality and value of the sushi is great but not worth the long wait or the service.
Nozawa Trust Me was great.  Fish extremely fresh.  Hand rolls were really tasty!  Came on a Saturday afternoon at 3pm and sat at the bar - no wait.

Came here Friday night with friends. The wait was very long but expected. The fish was phenomenal - so fresh and paired impeccably with sauces. Everything I had was delicious. The food comes out for the kitchen whenever it is ready and is meant to be eaten as soon as it comes out. I wish the rice stayed in formation a bit better but overall slam dunk and will definitely be back!

I honestly think this place is over-rated and hyped up way too much. Came here on a Friday around 5:45, so virtually no wait time. Ordered the Taste Menu with a friend. The quality of the fish was great, but my biggest gripe is that there was too much lemon sauce on a lot of the pieces such that the taste of the fish was overpowered. The tartare at the beginning was delicious, however. Also due to the massive lines, the food was brought out way too quickly. The waitress luckily noticed this and slowed it down, but we had already finished half of our meal.
I think best high quality value for the money sushi restaurant in Manhattan.

The rice literally melts in your mouth. You don't even need soy sauce because the fish is so fresh and delicious. Perfect portions and regardless of how busy they are the staff is amazing. I will be going often. I don't think I can ever have sushi anywhere else.
Going into this restaurant will definitely be a wrong turn. Extremely long wait times, over seasoned fish, lackluster omakase, and spotty service are what define this restaurant. Booooooooo.

Stopped by for lunch today and with a friend and ordered the Nozakawa Trust Me. Highlights were the scallop, albacore, and the blue crab handroll. Our waiter was very attentive which was great but my friend and I did not receive our plates at the same time. The servers that dropped them off at our table murmured what the fish was and quickly ran away. Cons were the sushi rice was HOT and fell apart really easily. Prices were decent and the fish was good. I had higher expectations for Sugarfish but I would go back a second time.

I missed my opportunity to try Sugarfish in LA and was super excited to hear that they opened a location in Flatiron. The wait for my friend and I was about 30-40 minutes during lunch time. We shopped around the area until we got a text from the hostess that our table is ready. My friend and I got The Nozawa Trust Me. For $45, you get: edamame, tuna sashimi, 2 pieces of albacore sushi, 2 pieces of salmon sushi, 2 pieces of yellowtail sushi, 1 piece of snapper sushi, 1 piece of sea bass sushi, a toro hand roll, a blue crab hand roll, and 2 pieces of a daily special (I forgot what my daily special was the day that I went). I thought everything was fresh and delicious. But the yellowtail and blue crab hand roll definitely stood out the most for me.

Although this is a no tipping establishment, their customer service is nonetheless exceptional. Our water and ginger were constantly refilled. Our waiter came over a few times throughout our lunch duration to ask us how our meal was or if there was anything that could be improved. Will definitely come back when I'm around the area next time!
Best Sushi in NYC! So fresh, best flavor! My friends  and I can get enough of this place. The sushi melts in your mouth and the cut rolls are just DEVINE!!! Love this place!!!
Get the Trust Me - everything was good, and I could eat the blue crab roll all day. Nice bar seating space too if you're there alone or with just one other person.

Buttery... mmmm that's the best description to describe how fresh and delicious their sushi. Their salmon is the best I've ever had. It has ruined me for mediocre sushi, which is 80% of the sushi on the market.

Sugarfish never disappoints! I would go all the time when I lived in LA - so consistent which the quality of fish and service. Always get the "trust me" it is very tasty and filling! My boyfriend said he was still full afterwards and could eat a little more (but he always gets a lot) I was very satisfied and very full! 

Note: they do not accept reservations, if you get there around 7pm for dinner, the wait time is typically about 2 hours.... and they mean it. Try to get there early, put your name down, and go for a drink a somewhere near by (or go home and get ready hahaha) there is also a great "drinking/waiting" area upstairs that not a lot of people were utilizing... you can order with the hostess and sit up there until your name is called as well :)

This is quite possibly the most aggressive table clearing I have witnessed (ever)...and I eat at plenty of "hurry up and free up the table" places in Chinatown. But as my friend took the first bite of her sushi, the server immediately came by and snatched the plate away. There was definitely an air of "please hurry up, there's a ton of people waiting" that became increasingly annoying as we progressed through our meal. After we received our check, and the server said "take your time", she literally spun around not 2 minutes later to see if we had paid (I was just pulling out my wallet from my bag). 

Honestly, I may be alone here, but while the food quality is as good as they say, I thought the service was ridiculous. I also think it's nuts that you have to get there close to 5pm to even GET a table (to start) because they close their waitlist quickly.

I read the reviews and decided to try this place with the many sushi options in NYC.  We went early around 6 on Sunday but still had to wait about an hour.  It did not help that they forget to check me back in after texting me to come back.  So it started off on a bad foot but quickly changed once the food came into play. I got the special tasting menu. Loved the handrolls that came with the dinner (toro and blue crab), definitely enhanced with the crispy seaweed.  All the sushi was fresh and nicely complimented with sesame seeds and touch of sauce/spice (salmon, snapper, sea bass, albacore, yellowtail and special scallops). The real show stopper was the extra albacore belly ordered.   I liked the gratuity (good service) and tax included in prices on menu.  In summary, wait was well worth it for delicious and fairly priced sushi.

I've been hearing about Sugarfish for years but don't go to LA often and wasn't willing to wait for hours when it first opened in NY. Now that the dust has settled and I've had the opportunity to dine in their handroll bar KazuNori (it's amazing!) it was time to make a strategy for Sugarfish. It turned out to be easier than I had thought. The restaurant is not far from my office so I walked over shortly after they opened (around 11:45) and put my name down for a table for 5 and walked back to my office. Thirty minutes later I received a text that a table would be ready shortly, rounded up my coworkers and returned to the restaurant which was pretty busy by then. We were seated after a few more minutes. It was as smooth as this kind of transaction can be.

Now on to the meal. I really love the concept. Sushi doesn't have to be complicated or ridiculously expensive. Rice should be warm. Sending things out one at a time fills you up and you don't need to order 10 rolls. The no tip thing did not affect our service. The waiter was prompt and easy to flag down. 

I have to say the Trust Me omakase menu is probably the cheapest omakase meal you can get. At $33 (with tip!) it's a steal! I also appreciate the instructions with every dish, ie this comes in a ponzu sauce, therefore you don't need to add soy sauce. 

The fish itself was amazing. I know the term melt in your mouth gets overused a lot but it really felt like it was melting in my mouth. It was just so so good!

My one star off is for edamame. I'm particular about my edamame, especially at high end sushi places and for some reason that is often their weak point. The edamame came out cold and flavorless. 

There's also no soup option which I kind of missed. 

Overall, I would love to return here for another meal and try their dinner menu next time. I felt very very full after this meal but my coworkers and I couldn't stop talking about how delicious everything was.

I heart sugarfish. Especially because it's some of the only affordable, good sushi ive had in NYC. I will say the ones in LA are better buttttttttt I'm still obsessed and would choose it over most places here in the city. I love the sho chicku bei nigori (sake) and always feel impelled to get it because it compliments the meal perfectly :)

For the price and quality, it is very good. There are plenty of places in NYC with poor quality with higher prices. Problem of omakase might be that it is pricey and you are still hungry. Sugarfish did it just right. It is not too omakase or fancy but I didnt mind at all.

SUGARFISH, NYC has been waiting for you for a long, long time.  

Everything about our experience here was fantastic.  My husband was able to put our name down for our party of 4 ahead of time and was quoted about a 30-40 minute wait at 6 PM on a weekday.  

Menu options were pretty simple.  All of 4 of us opted for the Nozawa Trust Me, which was incredibly filling in my opinion.   The servers tell you which pieces don't require soy sauce - most of them didn't - and the flavors and quality of fish was just out of this world.  The standouts were definitely the albacore tuna (OMG), salmon with the sesame seeds, and the special of the day which for us were the scallops (another OMG).  I was so full after the 2 plates of sushi that I felt like I couldn't really enjoy the hand rolls, but they were fantastic as well.  

I could eat the albacore tuna all day erryday.

I will say, quality and service are top notch here. Everything is quick (hellooooo they have a million people to serve and a line that goes out the door!) but not rushed. They want you to enjoy your experience but are diligent at getting courses pumped out and bellies happy.

Lunch: Trust Me. 

I was stuffed after eating 9 pieces, three of which were hand rolls. My only critique is that the rice was so much of the meal, which isn't to say they skimped out on the fish.. there was just a ton of rice and the lemon was more noticeable than other experiences. Some places like to serve their rice slightly warm. I was not a fan (or fàn 飯 in chinese)

Ive been to yasuda and seki a few times also sushi on jones. I give sugar fish 3 stars for failing to balance the flavors for the tasting menu trust me which also they increased 5$. The first plate with the salmon, albacore and red snapper the rice were a bit too much on sugar therefore sushi mostly tasted sweet. 2nd plate was scallops, yellowtail and bass which tasted  too much of not sure if it was lemon or vinegar. Nothing compare to cheaper sushi on jones omakase. Although their uni which i would go back for lives up to yasuda quality though cheaper than yasuda price. Also the crab roll is good. Conclusion wouldnt do the tasting menu again rather if im to go back ill order uni and crab roll. Also the toro roll is good too

Fresh is an understatement - dayum! Worth the wait - make sure you're whole party is there prior to putting your name down. That set us back 45 minutes! Get the prefix for $33, if you get the smaller portion you'll most likely order more. Can't wait to go back!

Honestly was a little weary of the hype but this place IS AMAZING! The fish is SO fresh and SO GOOD. 

My friend and I came around 3PM on a Friday, which we thought was a pretty off time to grab lunch. However, the place was still PACKED. Fortunately, there were a few tables available and there was no wait. 

Both my friend and I ordered the trust me. And WOW, I was blown away. All the sushi is EXTREMELY fresh. I have a very sensitive stomach, but I was able to enjoy the entire meal without feeling any sort of uncomfortableness. 

The hand rolls were what surprised me the most. I honestly thought they added the hand rolls in as a sort of last minute decisions to give the overall meal some more substance. However, the hand rolls were DELICIOUS. Unexpectedly so good yet so simple, perhaps one of my favorite parts of the meal. 

I also ordered a Sauvignon blanc, which I didn't find to be anything special. The amount they give you is pretty small for $9. However, besides this, the meal was absolutely spectacular.

The best part is that the tip is included. At first I thought my meal would come out a bit pricey, however at 45$, the quality and the amount of food was absolutely worth it. Will 100% be returning to this restaurant.
Very average, dull almost, extremely crowded for no reason. Limited menu and options. The rice on nigiri was bland and tasteless. A dozen other better spots in NYC. Once was enough..

It's supposed to be room temperature fish with mouth temperature rice. Yet all the fish comes straight out of the refrigerator and ruins everything that makes sugarfish great. Please, fly someone over from LA once a month to check on things.

Yelp really needs to give us the ability to give half stars. This place is definitely better than 3 stars but I just can't see myself giving it 4 stars.
I was told to come here ok recommendations from a few friends. The wait here is crazy. You have to come either really early, like before 5, or really late, like after 9 because the wait here can be upwards of an hour and a half. Also they are kinda confusing when they explain to you about the wait. So they tel you the wait time and they allow you to leave and come back because they'll text you when it's time to come back and to just check in when you're back. However what they don't tell you is that if you decide to stay and wait that you must also check back in even if you haven't left. I made the mistake of just waiting before realizing that I needed to come back and ended up waiting an extra 20 minutes. 

Now as for the food, I was a little underwhelmed. I was told by many friends to order the "Trust Me" and that it would be a culinary experience like no other. However I didn't have quite that experience. The edamame was cold which was different from the traditionally warm edamame serve at other sushi restaurants, but still tasted good. The tuna tar tar was good as well with hints of sweet, sour and spiciness to it. Then came the sushi. The salmon was phenomenal, it melted in my mouth like it was butter. However the other fishes that came out were so great. The sauces they put on the fishes overpowered the fish itself and took away from the flavor and freshness of the fish. The meal ended with 2 hand rolls, a toro hand roll and a blue crab hand roll. The hand rolls themselves looked a little sloppy as rice was kinda falling out of them and they were in the shape of a cylinder, almost like an uncut sushi roll, unlike in the cone shape that I've seen in so many other sushi restaurants. The toro hand roll tasted pretty good but I thought the blue crab hand roll was a little dry. 

The service however was great as we finished or meal in 45 minutes and didn't have to wait more than 2 minutes in between each plate. 

I can't see myself coming back here to wait over an hour as there are other places with sushi just as good.

I just don't get the hype with this place. Good marketing I'd guess. If there wasn't a wait, sure, I'd come here. Fish was all very fresh and sliced with care. But nothing was especially memorable & the wait is c r a z y. The service also felt super formulaic and like a race to the next plate. There are tons of great sushi spots in NYC. Probably won't return because the wait is just impractical

We were hooked on sugar fish ever since being exposed to it in LA. The albacore nigiri with ponzu sauce is addictive. Now the east coast has access to this sushi restaurant and damn are we lucky for it.

The wait times vary, but peak lunch and dinner wait times get up to 3 hours. The space is small. The purpose is to allow sushi to be made and delivered instantly so the rice is still warm and melts in your mouth. 

We were seated at the bar counter at the back of the restaurant, we both order the trust me. This includes edamame, tuna sashimi in a ponzu like sauce, 2 pc. Yellow tail tuna, albacore, salmon. 1 pc. Seabass, 1 pc. Snapper, 1 toro hand roll and 1 blue crab hand roll. This is all for just 39 dollars, which is an unbeatable value for quality.

Everything was so fresh and the rice was perfectly warm and vinegary. The hand rolls are excellent and encouraged to be eaten within 20 seconds of being made. This is definitely were I will get my fish fix in on the east coast.

For this specific price point sugarfish is now an unmovable presence in the New York sushi scene. Hurry up and have a meal at sugar fish, trust me. 
B
Atmosphere: 5/5
Food/drink: 5/5
Cost: 5/5
Service: 5/5
Overall: 5/5
When i was there restaurant was full. Sushi was good but I wanted to make order to go and waited a lot of time.

I love SUGARFISH!! Trust Me ;) or Trust Me Lite! Go with these choices and add on what you like. My secret is to get here before the evening rush, or on a holiday, and or late evening...9pm can be the sweet spot if you don't mind eating late. No TIP policy and service is to the point. Can't get enough of this place.

Decent sushi and nice/attentive/efficient staff. I ate at the bar alone and was served quickly, able to get my green tea refilled (added hot water) 3x. I ordered the "trust me", which includes a tuna appetizer, 6 pieces of sushi (2x albacore, 2x salmon, 1x yellowtail, and 1x, and two handrolls (toro and crab). Overall, good experience but not because sushi itself was amazing (more combo of good staff and affordability). It's on par with domodomo in my opinion, which takes reservations so you don't have to wait a ton of time. I will note though that this place will take your name and text you (so no need to sit there to hold your spot)- which is something...

I got here super early on a Monday night and had no problem getting a table for 2 at 5:15.  I've heard the wait can get crazy long, but if you want some of the best sushi you've ever tasted than I say put your name in and grab a cocktail somewhere.

I went with the Trust Me menu option. I surprisingly enjoyed the cold edamame. The tuna sashimi was SO flavorful with the light ponzu sauce and beautiful presentation.

The salmon with the sesame seed garnish on top was so simple, but legit melts in your mouth. It was SO good.  All of the fish was so fresh and I loved the warm Sushi rice and course by course presentation. I was really able to enjoy each piece of fish since it didn't all come out at once for me to shovel in my mouth.

At the end I had asked for a bay scallops roll instead of the blue crab. I only did this bc I love me some scallops.  DAMN. So tasty.  It was just enough food to feel absolutely satisfied, but not overly full.

Can't wait to go back. And also kind of loved eating super early on a Monday night. Totally worth it!

The service was also excellent!

This place is absolutely amazing! Between the food and the service, it was so on point. The wait was over an hour but they kept you updated on the time and it turned out that the wait was sooo worth it! I would recommend this to anyone who would like to open up their taste buds to sushi. I will definitely be back!!

Best sushi I ever had in my life. Definitely worth the wait. There are some bars in the area while you wait so it's not so bad. There was not a single item on the menu that I didn't love! These guys know what they are doing. This is a must for sushi lovers!

Sugarfish first became well known in the LA sushi scene for offering affordable and fast omakase that was surprisingly good quality for the price. 

This location pretty well does its OG LA location justice. I will say that the fish is still fresher in LA, but that's in general. Trying to find fresh sashimi in NYC usually ends in a travesty or a three figure bill. Sugarfish successfully brings tasty and affordable sashimi to NYC, for which I am grateful.

Just be ready for a super long wait, unless you come at an odd hour!
Finally got to try this place. Waited about an hour. Overrated, expensive but sushi was good. Not sure if i will return. Only if there is no line or long wait time.

******customers beware******** this is the worst sushi place i have ever been too... the staff is very rude and the food is not even all of that for the price i paid i had way better!!!!!! i would say walmart sushi is better but that would be a lie . if i was you reading this post i would not think twice i would think 3 times about going to this place.. i also talked to the "so called regional manager who wouldnt give me his name for this compliant. and he was a piece of work . i will never go back to this place .. and all caps is needed for this post cause i fell like i wasted my time and money and want to get my point across 
thank you for your time

Love sugarfish! It's such a staple for me when I'm in LA and now NYC can enjoy the deliciousness!! And never once had I have a bad experience in the 27 times I've been!

When you walk into sugarfish, the decor is just simple and clean and you can tell that the food is going to be just exactly that. 

What I love most about sugarfish is the simplicity. Things that come sauces doesn't not require additional soy and things that aren't, are welcomed to be dipped in soy. 
I love that you can taste each sushi pieces own characteristics. 

My go to are either the trust me or the nozawa (usually share with a dining companion). Both super filling and it doesn't break the bank. 

Where there's a sugarfish, there will be me!!!
Excellent. Simple ingredients and all about them flavors. Blue crab, yellowtail, salmon - all favorites.

Definitely worth getting the Trust Me Lite or The Nozawa Trust Me option! The fish is really fresh and melts in your mouth.  The rice in the nigiri sushi tends to fall apart really easily, but the flavor is great.  

it's good to note that Sugarfish has a no tipping policy because hospitality is already included in the prices. Also, it's worth noting they have a birthday program.  If you come twice a year, and sign up using their online website, you will get a free meal on your birthday! There are some technicalities to the birthday gift so it's worth reading their policy closely.

You have got to go. I recommend going a little before 12 o'clock to get a table this place packs out fast! Fish is fresh and be adventurous and try the chiefs table. I've sat at both the sushi bar and a table and service is great as well they really know there stuff.
Overall Great experience! Amazing quality Sushi, especially for such a reasonable price. Menu is limited, but everything I tried has been delicious. Attentive Service.

I haven't had a chance to set foot into the restaurant itself since my review is for their takeout but every time I walk pass the store, there are people on line past the doorway. 

For my coworkers birthday we decided to order their takeout boxes and we were blown away but the quality and overall presentation of these boxes! 

I shared the Nozawa Trust Me which consisted of: 
Organic Edamame
Tuna Sashimi
Albacore Sushi (2-pc)
Salmon Sushi (2-pc)
Yellowtail Sushi (2-pc)
Snapper* Sushi (2-pc)
"Daily Special" (2-pc) (for that day it was scallop) 
Toro Cut Roll (4-pc)
Blue Crab Cut Roll (4-pc)

First of all, the box is really nice..(maybe cause im a graphic designer?) but that really stood out to me. The sugarfish logo was centered and embossed with this shiny blue foil while the box was just smooth white.Once opened, the instructions for eating was on the backside of the lid. Very cute. All the sauces were labeled and clearly instructed for what usage. Anyway, back to the contents of the package. The fish tasted fresh and for the price, it's totally worth it. The blue crab roll was a bit on the saltier side but fine if you don't dip into the sauce. 

When Nozawa said he wanted to make quality sushi more affordable, he made that happen. I am no sushi expert but for today I finished my lunch with a happy and full stomach.

I've been wanting to try Sugarfish for the longest time! I'm a little sad to say it didn't live up to my expectations. The two most important things to me while eating Omakase is the fish and the rice. A lot of people complained that the rice had too much vinegar. I guess I'm one of the few who didn't mind it.  Chef Jiro uses A LOT more vinegar in his rice. My problem was that the rice broke apart too easily. The everytime I used my chopsticks, the rice fell through. This was a constant thing throughout my meal which made my dining experience unenjoyable. The fish itself was alright. Our waiter was super informative and welcoming. The wait was a little insane. A table for 2 took 40 minutes. Everyone waiting for a table was crowding the host. New people coming in didn't know where to go, lots of confusion.

Sugarfish exceeded my expectations in taste, quality and service! All were excellent for a reasonable price!

We were hearing about Sugarfish since it opened, December 2016. We heard about the great prices, delicious sushi and Very long waits. Just the rumor of the 4 hours wait for dinner was enough to deter us.

But we finally tried Sugarfish for lunch, I was very pleasantly surprised! The fish pieces are unconventionally large and not artistic, but beautiful clean and delicious. 

We ordered the Trust Me (9 piece menu with some pieces being duplicates). Starter was a tuna sashimi. It was coated in soy sauce and shredded scallions. The tuna was lean, not stringy and tasted like smooth tuna.

The albacore and salmon sushi were delicious. The albacore was meaty, smooth and so fresh! The salmon was fatty, and sweet. It was so fatty it tasted of the consistency of o-toro. I was so surprised! 

The yellowtail and sea bass were fresh and very good. The yellowtail had a little too much wasabi and yuzu sauce so it masked the fish flavor but still the fish was fresh and firm.

The toro hand-roll hand crispy nori and good amount of macerated toro. The blue crab hand roll was amazing! The blue crab was so fresh, meaty and had the perfect amount of sauce. It was even better than the Hand Roll I wanted another.

So the Trust Me was a little too light for both of us, so we ordered Nozawa style shrimp and unagi. The unagi was fluffy and topped with sweet soy sauce. This was very good. The food amount was perfect. 

If I were to return, I would definitely order the Nozawa trust me (13 pieces).

If you're looking for the three most condescending men in New York City, look no further! Upon asking for a table, Sugarfish hosts and manager will immediately infantilize you by explaining their non-reservation policy before telling you to wait in their confined lobby area for up to two hours for a meal that will last no more than 35 minutes. This is New York attitude at its finest, and I urge all patrons in the area to go see this Oscar-worthy performance of three men who don't blink as they kindly show you the way to their middle fingers.

Went here once and had the menu I think it was $65 very good food and good value, we also had a small flask of sake that was good and some unusual Japanese beer, I have been back but was told there was a 3 hour wait. I am not sure how one deals with this find another resto you like, send a TaskRabbit to get you a table, I would be happy to give a cc # but ....
This system of not being able to book sucks city wide

I first heard about west coast sushi and the better balance of price and quality than NYC four years ago and always wanted to see for myself.  Sugarfish really gave me a great sampling of what is possible.  Gone are the pretensions of super high price sushi tables (which is still a real treat sometimes).  Sugarfish reached a quality and consistency that really astounded me.  The fish were incredible quality, very fresh with just the right marinade and flavoring.  The cutting is not very delicate but the pieces are huge and the rice is perfectly flavor vinegar and a bouncy-ness that makes every bite refreshing.  The nori for handrolls were toasted for a nice warm chewy bite.

Sugarfish sushi is delicious in every way, the service was fantastic, the flavor is authentic and as good to every bite to some of the highest quality sushi I've had.  It's a real treat.

Get yourself to Sugarfish, whether you're a seasoned sushi eater or a first timer, Sugarfish is a great experience all around.

I finally understand why everyone's been raving about SUGARFISH. The food, service, ambiance: everything was better than expected. 

My friend and I decided to come on a weekday night to avoid the dreaded wait time. We arrived around 5:30 PM to drop off our names and was informed a 45 - 60 minute wait. You're sent a text confirmation and when you're at the top of the list they send you another text so you could start heading back. 

My friend and I both ordered the TRUST ME set, with an additional order of the bay scallops sushi (2 pcs per order). TRUST ME is a nine course set: starting with edamame and tuna sashimi, following with sushi, and ending with hand rolls. We were devouring plate after plate of sushi. Everything we had was just so fresh, and the rice to sushi proportions were perfect. 
I loved that service was so attentive and informative - perfect for first timers like me. They advised us to eat the hand rolls as soon as it arrived, to ensure the nori would still be crispy when you bit into it. The servers also recommend that you only use soy sauce for the pieces that don't already have sauce. 

Some of the best sushi I've ever had for only $39? I'm already planning my next visit.

I've been to Sugarfish lots of times in LA, but this was my first experience at the location in New York. Came in for a late lunch on a Saturday at about 3 p.m. Wait was about 15 minutes. 

Everyone was very nice and the sushi was almost identical in taste to what you get in LA, which was surprising.

Is it the best sushi on Earth? Maybe not. In New York, there are tons of amazing sushi restaurants. But it's quite good and worth trying out.

The experience started out bad when they won't even let you put your name down until the full party has arrived. It's like a game of chess just to be able to wait for a table. Lines start forming around 5 pm, so hopefully no one in your party works a normal schedule. There's hype around this place, but if you're able to go visit the CA locations don't bother going here. Quality in NY is good, but CA is way better. We had the trust me option and yes, prices are also more expensive here than in CA.

Worth the hype and the wait. I put my name down for a two hour wait. They texted 20 minutes prior. We did the Trust Me and ordered an extra eel. Everything was delicious and melt in your mouth. I would highly recommend to any fish lovers.

Great quality, melt-in-your-mouth sushi at an affordable price. I got the nozawa omakase and the special of the day was scallops. My favorite pieces were the salmon, tuna sashimi, and the crab roll. Wasn't into the red snapper, yellowtail, scallop, and toro roll pieces. My friend got the trust me omakase and the difference was only 4 pieces. I would get the trust me next time especially if I'm not that hungry. 

Service was superb as the waitress explained all the pieces and how to eat them as they arrived and was very attentive. 

Overall had a great time and would come again.
Service was great and very inexpensive for fresh fish sushi. Sweet fish was my fave, though I wasn't really blown away.

love SUGARFISH so happy they opened one in nyc I first had SUGARFISH in la and I was hooked! I came by on a weekday night for dinner and there was a long wait so I took it to go and it was still just as good. Always get the trust me by the chef! favorite piece is salmon ugh craving it as I write this review. Best part is I don't find them to be so expensive and still great quality. Never disappoints

Sugarfish was well worth the hype. I arrived at 5:45 to put my name on the list for dinner for 2, received a "top of list" text at 6, and was seated by 6:30. I was a bit annoyed that it took 30 minutes from the text, but at least they have a system so for longer waits you can leave and enjoy the neighborhood while waiting. 

Despite the wait, the sushi was truly incredible! I would recommended getting one of the 3 tasting options to get a good sample of their best fish. I got the trust me which begins with edamame which were cold and not spiced - a simple and bland start to the meal. However, the meal was redeemed by the fish. The tuna and salmon course comes next and was the best sushi I've had outside of Japan. The fish tasted and felt like butter that melted smoothly in your mouth. Next was a course of yellowtail, bass and snapper - also perfect. Then the meal ends with hand rolls - toro and blue crab. These weren't traditional cone shaped hand rolls but rather uncut sushi rolls. The fish on all rolls was the best quality and the rice was warm and packed with flavor. 

Another great part about Sugarfish - tip is included in the prices! So my $38 sushi menu didn't come out to that much more, which really isn't that bad for a high quality meal!

I came here for the lunch course.  We ended up getting the 45$ sampler, though I was suggested to get the "trust me" sampler by a devoted friend.  The decor was very Japanese-esque with a very woody nature aesthetic to the spot. 

1. The place was busy (as always) we waited about 40 minutes, we gave our phone number and buzzed around the area and they texted us when our spot was nearing.

2. The service was excellent though warning the dishes come out one at a time, they don't just bring everything out, it's a bit choreographed so it in a way goes with the speed of the chef, the people dining, and they get a sense of where you are so this isnt a spot to come if you're uber hungry.  Exect each dish, to come, slow, with some space in between.  (we waited extra long and they said the chef is 'perfecting the rice' whatever that means).

3. the quality of the sushi was superb, i suspect the wasabi was real wasabi not the cheap immitation so eat with caution.

4.  The fish had a refined quality to it, though I had salmon and tuna they didn't taste 'fishy' they were creamy and buttery in texture so definitely this is a step up form your average sushi spot.

5. Personal favorite was the scallop roll, it was amazing. 

6. Can be very very busy and quite noisy, and you do sit very close to people next to you so its not as spacious for those who enjoy space.

I would definitely come again.

Turned up here with another couple on a Thursday night at 10pm. Told i would be a 45 min wait. 

We got the call inside 30 mins, immediately seated. We took the Nozawa menu - which was about $55 or so maybe $60.

Was the best japanese i have had in the city so far, and for certain you won't find better against the price. For us to maybe be their last customer of the night and the strength  and freshness of the food - wow.

Loved the Tuna sashimi starter was excellent and then it is basically a runway of assorted sushi post that. High quality, decent serving size - fantastic.

Will definitely go back and be a little more experimental with the menu so can comment further but for 60 dollars (Including tax and tip - this is amazing btw), I doubt you will do better.

Service - 5
Food - 5
Ambiance- 5

After visiting a few of the California locations while out there on business, I was delighted when they opened a Sugarfish in New York City. While this location isn't quite as good as its LA counterparts in terms of service, the quality of the food does not disappoint. 

You can't go wrong with a Nozawa or Trust Me meal; the sushi and sashimi is much better than other NYC restaurants at the same price point. The rice is consisently good and the fish melts in your mouth. The tuna sashimi appetizer in the house ponzu is one of the most delicious cold appetizers I've ever had. 

Pair a Nozawa meal with a nice bottle of Nigori and you're walking out of there for under $80 with a full stomach. Sugarfish is definitely worth the wait.
I think God herself must be one of the sushi chefs there. Best fish and rice I have ever had. Worth the 3 hour wait.

I was swayed by the hype of some reviewers. When I called, they said "no reservations"
However they also said that if w are only 2 ppl. the wait is around 45 minutes. We immediately took a $20.00 cab ride. When we arrived, they said 2.5 hours. Really? No "sorry" or "can we help you with a future ..." NOTHING
I have choices and I will use them.

Believe the hype. It's REALLY good. I don't even mind the wait since they call. Just go to a bar nearby and hang out! 

The rice is so tasty and at the perfect temperature, and the fish melts in your mouth. Frankly, I would say it's as good as the sushi I had in Tsukiji Fish Market in Tokyo (I did not go to Dai or Daiwa, though). Service is polite and efficient.

I was excited for this but it did not live up to its hype. Had to grab a second dinner at CATCH where I was finally satisfied. All the pieces taste pretty similar, the toro has no taste and the rice is too heavy. The crab hand roll was disgusting. Also the rice shouldn't be warm; it ruins the taste of the fish itself.  This is definitely a small Omakase for those who can't afford the higher end stuff and don't know their fish. I wouldn't come back.

Very good experience. Being a traditional sushi diner, this is a welcome treatment of a contemporary Japanese dining experience. The fishes are excellent and the excellent sushi rice has an acceptable sesame taste to it. It was lacking though in sake choices of the premium quality.

The hype is worth it! Fresh fresh fish. Hands down the best sushi I've ever had.  I now understand why people wait over an hour to be seated and will definitely happily wait that long the next time I'm craving sushi. I got the trust me lite and it was a good amount of food. I left just full, not overly stuffed or hungry.

My all time favorite sushi place ever. 
They know us by name haha. 
Get the trust me and add an albacore belly (make sure to ask at the start of your meal). 

Its so so so good. 

Also make sure you come at lunch if you want to save a couple bucks as it's cheaper for the same food at that time.

This restaurant is really good for its pricing, fish options, and speedy service. Obviously the lines are too long but its a high class problem. Everything was good, especially the sweet shrimp. My only complaint is the salmon sashimi was too cold.

When they say the fish melts in your mouth, they're not lying. I've never had such flavorful sushi before and was savoring every bite! We got the Trust Me, which was just enough food to leave us full. 

We went on a Saturday afternoon and waited around an hour for a table for six, as expected. The service was excellent and very quick even though the restaurant was full and we were a large table. I loved every minute of our lunch and can't wait to try the Nozawa Trust Me!

Amazing as always!  I eat at the one in Marina Del Rey, CA weekly and in town visiting family and had to try the NYC location... did not disappoint!

The meal was just as delicious and the staff was just as nice!  

Went on a Monday at noon and was sat right away... table of 3.

Yes the rice is warm and the fish cold but that is part of the Sugarfish charm!  Anybody who complains about that should go elsewhere :)

Sugarfish is supposedly a great place for affordable omakase. I've heard a lot about this restaurant and was really excited to hear that there was one in NY. There was an hour (and some) wait for 3 people, though they have a nice waiting area upstairs. The entire restaurant itself is rather dark and candle lit, which I wasn't quite expecting.

Our group of 3 each ordered the $39 Trust Me omakase. 
-ORGANIC EDAMAME: They give you quite a large amount of this. Pretty standard.
+TUNA SASHIMI: I think there were different cuts of tuna in this, as they had varying textures. I enjoyed this one! 
-ALBACORE SUSHI: Tasty but again, standard.
-SALMON SUSHI: I love salmon so I've had a lot of it; again, this was standard.
+YELLOWTAIL SUSHI: I enjoyed this one! Yellowtail or hamachi usually doesn't stand out to me but this one did! 
+SEA BASS SUSHI: This one is unique! I've never had this and appreciated that it was in the omakase.
-SNAPPER SUSHI: Again, standard.
-TORO HAND ROLL: This was super fatty tuna in a hand roll! Just be aware that it's a fattier fish. I love toro but wish this one stood out more.
+BLUE CRAB HAND ROLL: This was also unique and quite good!

Overall, the meal was a good amount of food but nothing too mindblowing. I do have to say that it's the cheapest omakase that I've had, though my omakase experiences have been much different (sushi counter instead of a dining room). The food comes out a little too fast, and we occasionally got dishes while we were still eating the dish before. Though I understand that this might be the reason that the omakase is affordable as they're trying to get you to eat and go. 

It's interesting to me that the sushi comes out much rounder than the nigiris I'm used to, but I didn't find this to be problematic at all. All in all, pretty decent omakase. It seems like a place I would take someone having sushi for the first time since it's a good introduction.

3.5 stars. My friends and I came here after work around 530pm. We waited close to an hour before getting seated. For such a large establishment, I feel like they should have a better way of seating their guests. Why they dont take reservations.. blows my mind. 

My friends and I got the Nozawa Trust me Omakase special which was 51.00 during dinner time. Essentially about 16 pieces/items for 51 dollars is  a great deal/ The fish wasnt exactly the best quality but the flavor was amazing in almost every piece. I did not expect to enjoy the albacore but that was the highlight for me. Most of the pieces melt in your mouth and the rice tasted like it had more vinegar than needed.  I expected so much more from the blue crab but that was sub par for me.

Overall, the experience felt rushed, and the food was average for me.

Really wonderful experience! We were accommodated by the hosts just between that weird after work time and the dinner rush. My idea to go here with friends was very spur-of-the-moment. I had a craving for sushi, was going to go alone, invited them to come with me, and it was such a good decision. We all sprung for the Trust Me because why not just go for an experience?! And quite the experience it was! I loved almost everything! Seriously, the best sushi I've ever had and I'm pretty sure my friends agreed. So many pieces that melted in our mouths, the rice was the perfect temperature, the hand rolls were a great mix of textures, the list goes on. We didn't get to try the Toro because it wan't up to their standards that evening, so they replaced the roll with salmon. Still delicious! My least favorite dish was the blue crab hand roll. It reminded me of canned tuna, but it was the last course, and everything else had been so good that I didn't care. I love that they don't allow you to tip here. As someone who has a good amount of restaurant experience, it's nice to know that they are paying their staff what they deserve, if not very close to it! And the staff from the Hosts to the our servers to the runners/bussers were extremely nice.  So happy to have come to sugarfish and I can't wait to return and try more off of the menu!

Gave this place a try since I loved KazuNori however SUGARFISH was only alright for me. The concept seemed okay but the execution is terrible for omakase. 

The fish quality was decent - I've had better but for the price point it's not bad. The service was impeccable. The servers were extremely nice and took their time to answer any questions and to explain the menu. 

Some users would describe their experience as rushed but I felt that the serving style was the reason for it. Unlike KazuNori, the sushi wasn't served at a steady paced, which gave the meal an awkward feeling. I enjoyed my meal, but didn't love it as I hoped.

First of all, the wait is very long. Waited over 1.5 hours for a Friday lunch with my husband (we were quoted a 1 hour wait when we arrived at 230pm). Unfortunately, by the time we were seated, the menu had switched over to the dinner menu, so both of our orders ended up costing more. aka COME FOR THE LUNCH! 

Solid sushi, but NOT the best I've had. I tried the "Trust Me". My husband had the "trust me nozawa", which cost $12 more but only had 2-4 more pieces, didn't seem worth it. We were sat at the bar. Service was friendly and efficient, and being so close to the kitchen made the wait for food very short. It's evident the sushi and rolls are freshly prepared. 

There was one piece of fish that truly melted in my mouth. I think it was the albacore. The hand rolls were also delicious, nice and crispy. However, I wouldn't return if the wait was more than 30 minutes. I think this place is hyped up.

So bummed that they raised the price! I used to say this place is THE cheapest nigiri you can get in Manhattan for the quality. But I'd still say it is pretty cheap albeit less. You can easily pay double to have the same quality sushi in Flatiron. Anyhow, I did notice that some pieces had what tasted like a wasabi water (?) garnished on them that was a bit too much. Otherwise I still love this place and would definitely come back. For two people looking to get some sake, I'd highly recommend getting one bottle of Nigori.

Delicious sushi for a great price! 

I came here on a weeknight with 3 people, and waited about 30 mins to get seated. We all ordered the $57 omakase. We started with the edamame which was pretty standard. Next was the tuna sashimi. It was flavorful and the sashimi was delicious. Next had the albacore, which was one of my favorites. It literally melts in your mouth. Some of the other sushi that I enjoyed was the scallops. The toro hand roll was good but the blue crab hand roll was so delicious. I ordered another one after the meal. My friends and I also ordered the toro and let me say $15 for two pieces was not worth it for the quality of the toro we got. Definitely have had better elsewhere. 

Anyway, the $57 omakase is extremely filling and definitely worth it. Service is good and the waiters are very attentive. I wasn't a fan of the interior. It was extremely dark and loud inside. However, I would definitely come back when craving sushi next time!

The first time I had Sugarfish was in LA and I definitely think LAs was more delicious but this place was good too! We got lucky, came here on a Sunday for lunch and there was no wait. The service was super nice and attentive. The restaurant looked clean, simple, modern.

As for the sushi, we got the Trust Me and everything tasted great. The fish tasted fresh, the rice had good taste. Everything was well prepared with good seasoning on the light ponzu sauces. The hand rolls came out fresh with the delicious seaweed aroma. 

Overall, definitely worth a try, especially if you never had the one in LA. It's worth it for the price and quality of the meal.

I was very glad that SUGARFISH opened its NYC location. We came here for celebrating my birthday. I ordered the trust me lite, which included organic edamame, tuna sashimi, albacore sushi (1-pc), salmon sushi (1-pc), Nozawa-style shrimp sushi (1-pc) and toro Hand Roll. The amount was just right. I wanted to save the space for dessert. My husband ordered the Nozawa trust me, which came with organic edamame, tuna sashimi, albacore sushi (2-pc), salmon sushi (2-pc), yellowtail sushi (2-pc), snapper* sushi (1-pc), sea bass sushi (1-pc), toro hand roll, blue crab hand roll and sweet shrimp sushi (2-pc). He also ordered a side of toro. Everything was super fresh and tasty. No wonder the wait was long at all its locations.

I had the "Trust Me" and it was absolutely incredible. Best sushi I have ever had in my entire life. I will make a point to come here every time I visit NYC in the future. Service was great as well. Wait was long--about two hours--but would have waited six if it meant I could eat this sushi.
Super fresh and delicious! Very basic but high quality. Great service! Passionate team. A little pricey but worth it.

There's rules to this game so I don't get why people are surprised.  But hey folks it's nyc you want to eat at a new hot spot you are waiting its not that serious.  We usually put our name down and go to cosme and have dessert first.   Or go between 3 and 5 I have never waited at that time.   I have never waited longer than they quoted and everyone there is so friendly.   Food is awesome but that was not even a question- they have a stellar rep for a reason.

Love this place. They have really fresh sushi and it's very well priced. The wait is super long, but you can get lucky sometimes and get seated in just a few minutes. The usual wait here is 1-2 hours. Sounds crazy, but if you like sushi, it would be well worth the wait.

Can't believe it took me this long to finally try Sugarfish. Tried to come for lunch twice and both times had like a 2 hour wait. Finally my manager went to 1145AM and we got seated immediately. 

The "Omakase" options are the following
1. TRUST ME Lite : $23 
2. TRUST ME : $33 
3. THE NOZAWA - Trust Me  : 45

The fact that Sugarfish is a no tipping establishment makes these prices wayyy cheap for Omakase. I went with the Nozawa of course and ordered additional sweet shrimp and uni. Those were around $10-$15 for 2 pieces, not cheap at all. 

My feelings going in was that it would be alright, just alright. True Omakase is a daily changing tasting menu with the freshest fish of that day being showcased by the chef. This constant tasting menu being offered in bulk orders just didn't show potential to me of being anything special. I was wrong to think that about this place. Some how it works and I'm a fan.

The fish were amazingly fresh and some pieces were prepared with some sauce, so don't go using wasabi on everything now. The best thing on the tasting menu was the Albacore, followed by the very close 2nd runner up scallop sushi. Then comes the tuna sashimi and salmon sushi. Oh and the toro handroll too! The rice was a little too warm and soft though, and fell apart way too easily. 

Overall really loved the sushi here and would come again. Food came out quickly but not too fast to make us feel rushed in any way. For this type of "Omakase", it's great for what it is and I absolutely enjoyed every bite.

First time I went to Sugarfish was in LA, and I was majorly disappointed in that fact that New York's didn't open yet.  I know my review is a little late since Sugarfish has been opened for a while but better late than never. 

The overall decor is amazing.. I love that it feels private but yet you are seating one foot away from the next table. 

I also go with the trust me menu!! I make sure I come super hungry so I can eat everything on it. 
It starts off with Organic Edamame-- Perfection. Tuna Sashimi also amazing. You get 2 pieces of the following: albacore, salmon, yellowtail sushi and 1 piece of the sea bass and snapper sushi. They are all beyond what you have eaten in NY thus far. This is the real reversion of Sushi and the proper way to eat fish. The waiter also says do not use and additional sauces since everything they serve is to be eaten within 2 mins and nothing else should be added. 

By far my favorite items of the trust me menu is the Toro Hand Roll and the Blue Crab Hand roll. It comes inside a seaweed wrap and it's so flaky and crispy. They say start eating so you can get the full taste of the seaweed. Mouth watering just writing the review. 

MUST Go-- eat enjoy and be happy!!!

I just left the restaurant with a very disappointing experience.   Asked to be seated at the bar for a party of 1. 

I was told that the wait would be an hour and a half, even though there were empty seats at the bar.

When I asked why, I was told that regardless of the size of my party, everyone is seated in order of arrival.

This sounds ridiculous and I have not experienced this type of service at the restaurant before.

I was seated at the bar on numerous occasions even though there were no available tables.

customer service is awful and needs revamping.

By far the best sushi I've eaten in New York, both in terms of flavour and value. This is supported by the difficulty one has trying to get a table at this fantastic restaurant. I've stopped by on a Sunday at 4:30pm only to be told that the wait is 3+ hours! With that in mind, my tip is to arrive close to when the restaurant opens, a little before 12pm to be safe. 

Onto the food, it's a no brainer to order one of the trust me variations depending on how hungry you are. Both the salmon and tuna sashimi are unbelievably good. I'm not a big tuna guy, but the immaculate preparation and fresh flavour impressed me. To the pieces of sushi, my favourites were the large scallop which had some sort of ponzu dressing, and the salmon nigiri, a classic. I want to make particular mention of the rice at sugarfish - the perfect level of seasoning, vinegary and warm in your mouth, it is undoubtedly the finest I've eaten. To finish up, hand rolls are brought out, so freshly made that the seaweed is slightly crunchy. 

The size of the meal, along with the price (tip included) are perfect - be sure to stop by!

For someone who doesn't really like eating raw fish, this place wins in my book! Definitely a must try if you are a sushi lover! This place sets the standard for quality sushi! 

I had heard of this place from youtubers and thought, eh what is so special but from the looks of the instagram posts and youtube videos, I was like OK, I will try this sushi because I feel for the hype and it looked really good. Glad I went to try it out. The first time I went a few months back was after work around 6pm, it had a 4 hour wait so we were like forget it. This time we came on a Thursday around 4pm and it was only a 15 min. Yes, we were going to finally try this place out! 

I got the Trust me and trust me it was good! At first, I was going to get sushi a la carte but glad I went with what I got because it was amazing!! 

My favorites are definitely the tuna sashimi, salmon, and seabass. All the sushi went down like butter so smooth and delicious. No additional soy sauce is needed and if you really want wasabi on it, you could put a lil pea size but otherwise, it is perfection without the extra condiments. The ponzu sauce for the tuna sashimi and the kick in the seabass make me drool and want to go back ASAP. All the sushi here definitely melts in your mouth. Can't wait to go back for another round!

Delicious 

I went with the middle selection at $33 dollar.  Next time I will happily try the larger selection for $45.00.  They are very reasonable and allow some substitutions.  It was very very well paced and delicious.  My favorites were the tuna in ponzu, and the toro had roll.

So the sushi here is fabulous! Very inventive. Strongly suggest the "Trust" tasting options. So, why only 3 stars? That's for the arrogant, diva-like, disrespectful, bow-tied maitre d.. "Are all 4 of you here? Raise your hands and smile". When you fire him, let me know and I'll change this to 5 stars. Or let me know what night he is off, so I'll know when to come back.

Okay so to be fair I ordered SUGARFISH on DoorDash instead of waiting in line. I'm not sure if there's anything better than eating SUGARFISH in bed so.... 

It was great. I ordered the Trust Me. The rice was still warm and everything. You can tell that the fish is high quality and super fresh. I also love how it comes with a plethora of condiments and tells you how to pair every piece of sushi. My personal favorite was the salmon and blue crab roll. Highly recommend treating yourself to this if you're feeling some kind of way. But you probably won't catch me waiting in line for 3+ hours at the flatiron location.

Sugarfish most definitely lives up to the hype. I have been twice now, once for lunch, once for dinner and both were enjoyable experiences. My recommendation would be to come around 11:45 for lunch and you most likely will not have a week, at least during the week. We were promptly seated and the courses started coming out one by one. You may think it doesn't seem like a whole lot of food, but since you eat in courses, it makes you fuller. I got the Trust Me for lunch and it was perfect. I would recommended the larger one, however, for dinner. All in all an amazing experience and even better fish and rice. So happy it is close to my office!

Deliciously fresh fresh sushi. I came here for lunch and left STUFFED. The only negative aspect of this place is there will always be a wait. I waited for about 30-40 minutes while sipping wine upstairs so, not super terrible. Try not to come for a quick grab & go lunch! Regardless, the food is so fresh and enjoyable. I love sushi & this is the highest quality sushi I've had in my life. I ordered the Nozawa -- Trust Me and I was so happy I did because all the food was DELICIOUS. I will definitely be coming back!

Great atmosphere, cool vibes. Really good sushi for the price. Gets super crowded fast. I went there at 4:45 for dinner (totally random), and by 5:15 there were a ton of people waiting for tables.
