The fish is really fresh. It's an omakase, but not served piece by piece as everyone is seated at tables; it's more so served in courses. The portions are really generous and the service is really friendly. 

Unagi and uni were so good!

Everything here gets 5 stars - the service, food, and ambiance. No hyperbole at all. It was THAT good. 

The concept of this restaurant is amazing. Fresh and simple sushi. This isn't your typical sushi restaurant. The fish takes center stage instead of tons of extra toppings and sugary sauces at your local sushi spot.

They also have an awesome rewards program. If you check in three times a year, you'll get a free meal on your birthday! Wish I lived closer to take advantage of this!

I had a wonderful experience at Sugarfish! They have very great service. They also have wonderful food. The trust me omakase is amazing and each piece they give you is a burst of flavor! Would highly recommend.

I wish we had more branches of Sugarfish in NYC because then I wouldn't have to get there either ridiculously early or make alternate plans because of the super long waiting time for a table! 
The only time I have managed to eat here was when two of us came for  a weekday lunch and we arrived at 11.40. We were fortunate enough to get a table straight away. Luckily I don't eat breakfast so I'm happy to eat an early lunch. 
Anyway the atmosphere was nice, minimal decor, subdued lighting and our waiter was good, perhaps a little impersonal, but nice enough and very efficient. 
We both had the large Trust Me tasting menu and everything was fantastic. The fish was fresh and the correct temperature (not chilled), the rice was perfect, fish to rice ratio good etc etc. I can't fault it. I particularly enjoyed the tuna tartare and the blue crab hand roll. One of the sashimi items was scallop which I can't eat but they swapped it out for yellowfin which I appreciated. I enjoyed the food immensely, it was great value for money considering the quality and drinks were also good and reasonably priced. Tip is included in menu price.
I would give Sugarfish five stars but the silly wait times and the fact that the meal felt a little rushed knock a star off.

sugarfish is probably my favorite quick omakase spots in New York. I love the different options you have depending on how hungry you are and you can always add on items as you go or at the end. service is spectacular, my server Jeff was amazing and took care of us. always look forward to dining at sugarfish because I know I will get great service and great quality sushi!

Loved it! The service, food and atmosphere were all amazing and I think this would be a perfect spot for a date. The best sushi I have had in a long time - Make Reservations though! The restaurant fills up fast.

Sugarfish has a great atmosphere and I loved how they served each of the courses explaining what each item was and what sauce it was best to eat it with and when. I felt like I was at a high-end restaurant but without the high prices. My friend and I each got the "Trust Me" (I actually wished I had ordered the "Trust Me Lite" because it was a little bit too much food for me) and it was a great sampling of everything they have. 

I love love love that the tax and tip are included in the price. It was very affordable for a Sushi dinner in New York. Thank you SUGARFISH, I will definitely be back!

First off, there is no question the food is excellent and the staff quite pleasant and professional.

The question, however,  is whether the dining experience is worth the typical 2 to 2-1/2 hour wait.  

Management's policy of not taking reservations and requiring people to show up in person to be placed on a 2 to 2-1/2 hour waiting list is poorly conceived, borderline obnoxious, and unquestionably Inconsiderate.

Wanting to see what all the fuss was about this place, I showed up, left my name, and then patiently waited to see if the food was worth the wait and hype. 2-1/2 hours later I returned and ordered the top-tier omikase. $54 for a tuna appetizer, 12 pieces of sushi, and three hand rolls-unquestionably an excellent buy, one of the best and least expensive omikases in town.

That said, there was nothing particularly creative about the omikase.  It was delicious, fresh, and expertly prepared with the requisite cut and bevel to maximize the flavor and texture.  However, there was nothing particularly creative about the combination of ingredients, presentation, or culinary choices.  There is also not much selection ordering outside of the omikase.  The drink selection is extremely sparce.  And there are no desserts.  Wait, really??

During the 2-1/2 hour wait I could have caught a taxi and gone to any of a number of sushi places in Manhattan and had an equally good if not better omikase.  But I would not have gotten the same good deal at $54.

In summary, come here if you want the best possible fish at the lowest possible price--as long as you are able to coordinate your trip here with a movie or errands during the inordinate wait.  Leaving your name and then catching a movie around the corner would make a wonderful evening.  You'll spend nearly as much money on the movie, popcorn, soda and Sweet Tarts as you will on the omikase afterward.

Best sushi we have ever had in our entire lives. We have heard amazing things about the LA locations, and we weren't sure what to expect. Hands down most incredible service and overall experience. The wait was about two hours on a Saturday afternoon, but we were able to explore the nearby area because they texted us when our table was ready. Servers were fast and efficient. Definitely will be back!

They should call this restaurant PONZUFISH instead, because they LOVE putting ponzu sauce on everything, for no reason.

I'm just not understanding the hype behind SUGARFISH. Prior to dining here, I had only heard great things about this place. It originated in the West Coast, and made its way east and opened a location in Flatiron. The only bad thing I heard was that they don't accept reservations and the wait times were long, which is why I put off going.

I finally got the chance to try it one December evening. For our party of four, our wait was about 20 minutes. The trick is to show up before 6 and put your names down, since it's not prime dinner time yet.

Most of us ordered the 'Trust Me' ($33), which comes with edamame, tuna sashimi, two pieces of albacore sushi, two pieces of salmon sushi,  one piece of yellowtail sushi, one piece of sea bass sushi, a toro hand roll, and a blue crab hand roll. All of the pieces (with the exception of the hand rolls) had ponzu in them. Don't get me wrong - I like ponzu as much as the next girl, but it's unnecessary to overuse it. I wonder how many vats of that stuff they go through per day. If it weren't for that, the meal would have been pretty good. The fish tasted fresh - apparently, they use the same fish vendor as their LA restaurants. I didn't really enjoy the blue crab hand roll. I'm not even sure if it was crab. It tasted more like canned tuna.

Bottom line - don't buy into the hype. There are plenty of better sushi restaurants in NYC for the same (if not lower) price point, where you won't be drinking ponzu.

Solid 3.5. Wait time: 1 hour or more. Time it took for us to eat: 5 minutes total. Verdict? NOT worth it. 

Interior: Really neat. Upon entering you can see the modernized decor. There is additional waiting space upstairs by the bathroom. The bathrooms are unisex, spacious and very clean. They had two soaps: scented for after eating and unscented for before eating. Interesting..

We ordered: The Trust Me (which I highly reccomend coming during lunch time since the sets are cheaper) 

We started with edamame and then the tuna sashimi. Not memorable whatsoever. 

Then we had the albacore and salmon sushi. Now these were phenomenal! The fish melts in your mouth. Delicious. Good seasoning. Wish I had 3 more servings. 

Following we received the yellowtail and sea bass sushi. This was a let down. They OVER seasoned the rice and they really did not need that ponzu sauce. Just to let you know I usually have my sushi without any soy sauce. You can see (in my pic) that the sauce was all over my plate....as if the chef carelessly prepared it. The sauce also left the rice falling apart. 

We ended with a toro and blue crab hand roll. Very good. The rice was sweet and warm which paired nicely with the fish and crunchy nori. 

The meal left us extremely thirsty. Not a good sign. I would've enjoyed it more if they didn't over season the rice which unfortunately over powered the fish. I won't be returning. It's overpriced and not worth the hype.

Wait was 1.5 hours, another 30 minutes after we got the text that our table was ready; 2 hours in total... It was a Wednesday night. 

2 stars because the staff was friendly.

The food was mediocre, we were a party of 5 and 4 of us got the Nozawa $51. 
Starting with the edamame and then the tuna sashimi mixed with a whole lot of ponzu. The tuna did not seem too fresh, which started me on my journey of doubts. Then most of the sushi came presauced, it was so overwhelmingly sauced that I could not taste the fish. Halfway through the meal I started to feel nauseous. I'm not sure if it was due to the fish or the rice or the sauces or if it was because it was paired with ice cold water. I was so nauseous that I could not finish my meal. Two others in my party started feeling nauseous as well, so we ordered hot tea to try to feel better. We were never offered more hot water for our teabags once our cups ran dry. 

Would I come back?
No

Would I recommend?
No
Amazing sushi. Had the tasting menu and did not disappoint! I'm definitely coming back. The highlights are the sashimi and crispy rolls so basically everything

Just like all of their locations in Los Angeles, this place is slammed constantly. It's understandable: they serve some of the best sushi around. Super fresh, melt-in-your mouth fish at not astronomical prices. The warm rice gets me every time. They don't take reservations so go, put your name in, and catch a movie down the street (you'll have time).

We got lucky and was seated right away. We arrived around 4 pm if that haps anyone. The fish was very fresh and the trust me course was perfect if you aren't starving. It was very unique and different how the rice was warm whereas the fish was cold, interesting combo. I've heard of people waiting hours to try and although it was highly worth it when looking at how much the course was per person, I don't think it justifies waiting hours for. I would say it is definitely a must try though.

Seriously just amazing. Nothing else to really say. If you haven't tried it you must go. I love the environment. Everything tastes so fresh. Service is on point. Foods on point. Will be going here more often.

THE BEST sushi in all of manhattan, and at a reasonable price! Their specialty is serving sushi with warm rice, which sounds odd at first but is so delicious! They also make a house ponzu sauce that comes with the Toro order, which I get every time. Their hand rolls are also to die for, I get the crab and lobster hand rolls every time. Service is always excellent and each dish comes out right after items prepared. For two people it's typically around $90 or so without drinks, and also depending on what you order. They don't take reservations, so if you go during the week try to get there before 6 PM otherwise there is a wait!

The SUGARFISH location in NYC does not compare to the one in Downtown LA. Period.

I came here on a Friday evening at around 6:30 with 3 other friends for dinner. We were so excited to have one of our sushi connoisseur friends try SUGARFISH, especially since my experience in the Downtown LA location was so amazing. I will admit that the ambiance in the NYC location was better - dimly lit and had good music playing - but the service and food here did not compare.

For those who remember their first SUGARFISH experience, you know this isn't a typical local sushi spot. Ordering is different and how you are supposed to consume the dishes is different. You're not really supposed to add your own soy sauce or wasabi but this wasn't explained to the first timers by our server. My friend and I who have eaten here before had to tell the others about this and make suggestions on what to order. 3 out of 4 of us went with the Trust Me Lite, and unfortunately, it did disappoint a bit. The fish was COLD, and obviously I don't want lukewarm sushi but this was bordering ICY... near brain freeze icy. Also, everything was just DRENCHED in ponzu. The Sushi connoisseur in our group jokingly (or not jokingly because it's kind of true) called it PONZUFISH because the chef that night had a ponzu sauce party with our dishes. I did get to try the uni there for the first time though and it did not disappoint - it was fresh, buttery, and delicious. Worth the extra charge from our main dishes for sure.

When we got our check, which was divided up evenly by 4, there was a mistake on it so the charges had to be voided and charged again. It happens and I totally understand. Not the biggest deal, just a minor inconvenience for us.

Point of the story - the LA location has won my heart. The next time I go to SUGARFISH, it'll certainly be in Cali.

Really more like a 2.5 star review.  Let me first start by saying that a meal at Sugarfish can be fairly enjoyable.  I've somewhat enjoyed the three times I've eaten here, but I always have the same feeling as I leave: sure it all tasted alright, but there were just so many weird quirks that I can't ignore.  

Sugarfish is probably the most overrated sushi restaurant in the city.  People praise the overall "value" of items on the menu such as the "Trust Me" options, but if you actually strip down what you're getting, its really just an overall mediocre value.

To start, the wait for this place can be ridiculous.  Other solid sushi spots take reservations, and its hard to fathom why you're waiting 1.5 hours when there are other options. 

A good thing about Sugarfish is that the fish tastes relatively fresh overall.  I never really had any complaints about the fish itself, so that's at least a  solid start.  But take a look at any of the pictures, and you can tell that whoever cut the pieces really was only concerned about getting the pieces out the kitchen as quick as possible.  The slices are oddly shaped and looks simply placed on the rice instead of molded into one piece.  The technique from even any delivery sushi place that you get on Seamless produces better pieces than Sugarfish.  Also, its very evident by the fact that there isn't a sushi bar that they're drawing the focus away from the fact that the pieces are probably assembled by inexperienced chefs.

I've seen this in other reviews as well, but they tend to put too much sauce, whether it soy, or ponzu, or whatever.  And they really love their ponzu sauce.  Way too much of it at times.  Subtly is not really a thing here.  Which is a shame, considering the flavor that really stands out most of the time here is not the fish.  

So this is one of those things where it seems good on paper, but the execution just isn't there.  They hype is what probably makes this worse.  But really, invest about ten more dollars and go do a proper omakase at a place like Sushi on Jones or Sushi by Bou.  Or go to a place like Hatsuhana and pay less for a far more crafted product.

YUM! I tried this in California and enjoyed it. I finally got around to going in NY. I had the Trust Me Combo and it was so fresh and delicious. I am not daring with Sushi especially since it's so expensive and could be kinda risky if you end up not liking what you order. I trusted them (get it) since everything on the combo sounded good. I was thrilled with each plate they put in front of me.

My only complaints are there are no reservations so you get stuck waiting and also, the drinks menu us VERY limited. But honestly, it's worth a visit...or many visits actually. I'll definitely be going back (but with a snack to eat while I wait).
Consistently my favorite late night sushi spot. The service is always great as is the food.

I'm a fan of the Sugarfish restaurants in LA so I wasn't surprised by how yummy everything tasted. What I was surprised by was how much the quality of service surpassed its west coast counterparts.

The first night was super busy Bc it was stupid Valentine's Day, but we still received amazing service by the servers and the hosts/hostesses. I wish I had gotten our original server's name--he went above and beyond to make sure we were happy. When his shift was over, an equally amazing server (Michael) finished off our night. In fact, we loved our experience so much that we returned the next night and received great service again--especially by Michael and Taylor (hostess) who remembered me from the night before. :)

This isn't a restaurant, it's an incredible dining experience. Like nothing I've had before. What am amazing meal. Trust me, you want to order the "Trust Me." And if you don't like this cuisine, you don't know what you're missing.

Not too much to say here, there probably isn't a better quality to price ratio anywhere in the country. This place is only one notch below Nakazawa and Azabu in deliciousness, but several notches below in price. Worth it every time.

I would give it 5 stars if it wasn't for the wait getting a table . 
The food is light, it comes out at an acceptable interval. Very simple, fresh and to the point in a way. I mean no frills. That's a good thing.
They serve sake, wine and beer.
They won't give you any sauces, no punzo, no spicy mayo etc... they don't serve any cooked fish and no deserts either. You cannot leave a tip as it is included in the price of the food. The waiters all look happy and they all smile  it's an experience ! The toro is excellent but my favorite is the yellowtail no contest.
Loved it!  Went and got The Nozawa to take back to the hotel.  Perfect. Fresh. Delicious.  It's a box of sunshine for any days.
Great sushi and great value!  The fish is amazingly fresh, melt in my mouth.  Be prepare to wait, they don't take reservation but it's worth the wait if you have the time.

I've been here a few times so far and it's become my go-to sushi spot to recommend to people. The sushi is amazing and fresh and I think the set menus are worth it. 

I will say this though - if you're looking to have a slow dinner with lots of conversation etc, that's probably not going to happen here. At least if you get the set menu (can't speak for the a la carte because I've never gotten ordered from that part of the menu). They keep things moving pretty quickly and since you're supposed to eat the sushi relatively quickly when it comes out, you'll probs be done in about an hour. I have zero problems with this because I start to get antsy if conversations start dragging anyway. 

No reservations. They only seat you once everyone arrives. I've only ever gone with someone else so it's never been an issue, but I'm guessing a larger party would be a problem, especially during the busy lunch/dinner hours. 

Only part that makes me sad is that they never have uni when I'm there  :(

I cannot wait to come back to this place. Holy mackerel, it was good. I got there towards the end of lunch service one day and ordered the trust me lite. The guy next to me ordered the trust me and an extra blue crab roll, saying it was just that good, so I ended up ordering one for myself. The edamame was pretty standard, but the tuna sashimi, sushi and hand rolls were incredible. Even the rice that they use is top notch and flavored perfectly. And my dining  neighbor was right, the blue crab roll was definitely worth an extra order.

Ashley was taking my to go order and SHE IS AMAZING. My office sent me (the intern) to order lunch for the office and she was so helpful. She made sure that the order was correct for each person and she made sure the whole process went smoothly. Thank you Ashley! 

The lunch itself was amazing. I got the salmon cutroll and it was fresh, filling, and delicious. I will be coming back for date night for sure.

My stars are not accurate because I rounded up. I would rate it a 3.5. However, I gave it 4 stars because I'm afraid I had high expectations walking into this establishment. My friends hyped this up for me. I also I read up extensively about their process.

I ordered the obvious Nozawa Trust Me. However, I don't know if I can trust them in the future. My main complaints include: rice was too loose without much flavor, sushi appeared to be factory cut because it was very boxy looking, and wasabi appeared to originate from a tube. An Edo style sushi chef should provide the wasabi and soy on the sushi piece with a delicate balance so none of the flavors are overpowered. Note to high end sushi restaurants: please don't trust me to place the right amount of wasabi and soy on my sushi piece. I did not attend culinary school to know the proper proportions.

I had two pieces I really enjoyed: the albacore sushi and the blue crab hand roll. I might only order that next time.

I still haven't decided if this is a overpriced sushi conveyor belt establishment or an affordable fancy one. I'll give it another chance and maybe update my rating and review.

Horrible time just getting a table. Why don't they offer online reservations? The sushi is good, portions large and pretty reasonable price. No desserts on the menu whatsoever is also disappointing. Overall was nice to try Sugarfish once but not really worth the headaches.
I love their sushi!  I have been 2x and sat at the bar both times.   The wait is annoying, but just go grab a drink nearby.  It is worth it in my opinion.

Sushi is simply so fresh and amazing at a great value! There was a little confusion on our wait time but the General manager took care of it with a friendly attitude and our waiter was well attentive & informative! Both guys are amazing!

Came here with a friend on a Sunday afternoon around noon and did not have to wait, although the place was pretty packed and I did spot folks having to wait after we were seated at the bar for a bit.

Went with the Trust Me and overall a pretty solid and lovely experience. By far my favorite were the salmon and albacore. The combination of the warm rice and cold fish was to die for. Quality of the fish was incredibly fresh! I really didn't care too much for the hand rolls. If I ever go back I would definitely not opt for the Trust Me and go for individual pieces. Overall though I thought it was a good value.

Huge shoutout to the service. Incredibly friendly and attentive, made the experience so much better. It's a no tip restaurant but would have loved to tip those sweeties big!

Was here recently during lunch with a few friends and I was very happy with my meal. It's a set omakase menu and the food was decently fresh. Upon walking if we were greeted by the hostess and she took our name and phone Number for the waiting list. I immediately got a text on my phone stating I was now on the waiting list and how long it will be until I got a table. They had a small seating/waiting area right by the entrance but it can get quite cold sitting there in the winter, everytime the door opened the cold breeze was brutal. Upstairs they had a dedicated waiting area along with the bathroom. We waited roughly about 30 mins which wasn't too bad. 
The menu is pretty much a set omakase meal so there isn't much to choose from really. Every piece of sushi that was brought to our table was explained in detailed so that was very good. Only thing I did realize was that the rice of the sushi fell apart easily so that made the dining process sometimes a little frustrating. The servers were always close by to refill our drinks and male sure we have everything we need. This place is good for indecisive people as the minimalist menu can be a great help to that.

I came after hearing it about this place last year and after doing some research I learned about what makes SUGARFIAH different from the rest of the 100s of sushi spots NYC has to offer. 

The wait was only 5 minutes (because we put our names down earlier in the day) otherwise there would have been a 2-hour wait. We went for the Trust me and the Trust me, Lite. Both were meals were delicious and the food came fast!

I would highly recommend this place and will be back again soon.

This is officially my FAVORITE sushi restaurant of all time. My husband came here and both ordered the "Trust Me" which is an assortment of pieces selected for you. It did not disappoint. The customer service is phenomenal!!! This will be a regular spot for me and my husband.

Officially in love with sashimi, thanks to this place. I used to be terrified of eating raw food esp. sushi and I'm sure you know why. But this restaurant serves some fresh and delicious seafood. There was a wait on Saturday evening ~40 minutes, but it's easy to kill time in Union Square. 

Trust Me ($33)-5/5 This comes with with organic edamame, tuna sashimi and 2 pc albacore, 2 pc salmon, and 1 pc yellowtail, 1 pc sea bass, and a toro and blue crab hand roll. The edamame was unexpectedly cold  but still great. I substituted the salmon for a Nozawa-style shrimp, which was of course delicious. EVERYTHING was well seasoned, tasty, and not chewy. The sushi melts in your mouth! 

Hot Green Tea ($3)- You obviously need green tea when you eat sushi. :)

We came here Sunday about 1:20pm and there was no wait. We asked for seats at the bar, but unfortunately eating at the bar here isn't any fresher than eating at a table since all the sushi comes from the kitchen. Our meal started at 1:30 and lasted 45 minutes. After another 10 or 15 min settling our bill, we were out the door. 

// Atmosphere 
This restaurant kind of feels like an upscale fast food restaurant. It's not the same as omakase since it's not made by a sushi chef in front of you. Also, the customer doesn't really surrender much "trust" given that the Trust Me lists everything you'll be getting - more like a set menu. The ginger, wasabi and edamame and were pre-prepared on dishes so the waiter just pulled out a couple and took the saran-wrap off and served them to us. The tuna sashimi seemed like it had been sitting pre-made in a fridge for a while too. It still has a nice modern vibe - all the servers wear black, there's low lighting, and soothing decor with lots of wood and neutral colors.

// Food
We ordered the Nozawa Trust Me, $45 for lunch. The dinner version comes with 2 more sushi and is $6 more. 
Edamame - I'm not a big fan in general but these were pretty salty
Tuna sashimi - very bright red color, but seemed like it had been pre-made given the slices stuck to each other, had varying colors based on where they stuck together, and was very cold
Albacore - with scallion and ponzu yuzu, delicious, one of the best of the meal
Salmon - with sesame seeds on top, delicious, my 3rd fav
Yellowtail - creamy, delicious, simple with citrus salt, one of my favorites
Snapper - with citrus salt, didn't stand out to me, kind of tasteless 
Sea Bass - way too much ponzu!
Daily special of large scallops - way too much ponzu!
Toro Hand Roll - the toro is chopped up which seems like a waste since good toro has a melt-in-your-mouth texture. Also when the waiter set it down, the whole thing unraveled, so he brought it back to the kitchen so they could roll it back together
Blue Crab Hand Roll - very tasty

I prefer the classic cone-shaped hand rolls since the filling fell out when eating these. They did a good job at crisping the seaweed though. 

The rice is really good, always comes warm, and the fish is fresh. Sugarfish will never compare to a real omakase like Gari or Nakazawa, but it's a fraction of the price, so incredibly good value for what it is! They do a great job of streamlining their sushi experience to keep costs down and make good sushi accessible to more people. I'll definitely return!

This was hands down the best sushi I've ever had! I decided to order a la Carte, instead of getting one of the the set menus. I got edamame, salmon sushi, yellowtail, and a crab hand roll. The salmon sushi was the highlight of the meal and hands down the best salmon I've ever had. The sushi just melts in your mouth. 10/10 will definitely be going back! Also the staff were all very friendly and knowledgeable.

It is what it is. Great name, great hype, okay sushi. It's definitely fresh and a good experience but it's not the best and not worth waiting hours for. So, since I did not have to wait on a Saturday around 1230p for 2 people, I'd say not bad! The salmon was melty but the yellowtail was a bit more tough. The value is definitely spot on but in the end i got a-la-Carte so i can pick my favorite. 

Good service, they're very polite and explain things well. The hand rolls were tasty but definitely in the chop-fish realm. 

I'll come back if i know I won't wait ;)

I went to the LA branch twice years ago and had fond memories (minus the wait). There always seem to be a line out the door. I tried getting in the nyc branch but was confronted with a 3 hour wait. I made another attempt on a Monday at 3pm, no wait!

I sat at the bar and ordered the lunch: trust me set menu which came with edamame, tuna sashimi chopped in a sauce, 2 piece salmon, 2 piece tuna, 2 piece yellowtail, 1 tuna roll and 1 crab roll for about $35. High quality fish and so fresh! Love the warm sushi rice and how they come out in courses so that the sushi is eaten at the right temperature. Good service and delicious meal and without the crowd! Will try to come back for a late lunch :)

I was really excited to try this after hearing great things and waiting almost an hour an a half to be seated. 

The fish itself was amazing! Great quality and fresh. But the rice had way too much vinegar, which made it soggy and crumbly. Not to mention the acidity threw off the mouthfeel and taste altogether. 

Another thing I noticed was the temperature of the fish against the rice. The fish was way too cold and the rice was too hot. I was really disappointed because the potential was all there!

Sadly, I won't be returning :(

Absolutely amazing sushi, best location in NYC for omakase. The fish literally melts in your mouth (salmon and albacore belly are like butter), and the rice is perfectly warm. Service is always great - and it's a no tipping restaurant which makes the whole experience very seamless. Worth the wait - ALWAYS.

The sushi here was so top notch that it's life changing. Never again will I be able to have mediocre sushi. The fish was so fresh and it melts in your mouth. The attention to detail was perfect. You eat the sushi right as it comes out - so so fresh and fantastic. My favorites were: tuna, tuna sashimi, albacore, salmon and yellowtail.

Only downside - the wait is absurd. I put our names down at 6 and we ate around 9. Just be sure to plan on waiting, so grab drinks at one of the nearby bars. 

Still, it deserves 5 stars because the food is such good quality.
Great meal for a lower price point than most restaurants serving the same good quality- at least for this city/location.

Heard nothing but rave reviews about this place in Los Angeles so decided to see if the New York location was up to par.

Yes, in my opinion it really was. If Sushi (not rolls) is your thing, come here.

The fish is really fresh, the rice is delicious and served warm, and the prices are great. 

About $3-4 a piece for most of the non-specialty sushi varieties. Was about to snag about 12 pieces of really high quality stuff for $50.

Is it Sushi Yasuda? No, but its half the price for most of the quality.

Describe simple perfection & you have Sugarfish. Sushi is served without glitz & sauces & goo. Simply raw fish served either in sushi over rice or in a cut roll. Fresh - fantastic - easy menu to survey. They brought LA sushi to NY now I need them to expand to So FL & my life would be complete.

This place is always packed. I got there around 6:00 pm for dinner and still had to wait to be seated. You won't find a traditional omakase here at SUGARFISH. Instead, every piece of chef selection has a bit of a modern touch, which makes it super interesting as you would always wonder what's coming next. Food is very high quality. Casual ambience makes this place cute and lively. Reasonable price for omakase and they offer three different options. My friend and I had the "trust me"  set ($39) and we were super satisfied.

Keeping with the Japanese tradition, this restaurant is a no-tipping restaurant. Definitely worth a visit and five stars!

Listen.  You'll probably have to wait for 1-2hrs to get a table here, but you need to do it because it is SO WORTH IT.  They'll collect your number and text you when the table is ready, so go grab a drink somewhere for a bit!  (The cellar next door is cool).  Okay, on to the review.

Trust your chef... trust the process... order the Trust Me for your entree.  You waited all this time, just order this it's phenomenal!!  The slices of fish are so fresh and perfectly seasoned, I used 0 soy sauce.  And the RICE that it's on top of is so flavorful, the perfect crunch/texture to pair in your mouth.  You'll get pairs of fresh rolls brought out 2 and 4 at a time in courses, around 5-6 courses total including a few large rolls to finish it off!!  You'll get salmon, sea bass, tuna, yellowtail, crab and all sorts of stuff.. each bite is insanely good.  Well worth the $40!  Pair it up with some sake and you are good to go!!
This place was delicious and my waiter was very pleasant! Fish tasted very fresh. It gets pretty crowded and there could be a wait.

Sugarfish doesn't take reservations so be prepared to wait. I highly recommend the SugarFish Prix Fixe omakase. The sushi is really delicious, the rice they serve the fish on is a little on the warmer side but the hand crab roll is the highlight of the meal. Definitely a bargain for the food. 

-@EricHoRaw

Really good sushi. They don't take rezzies so expect to wait awhile (an hour) but they will text you when your table is ready.

Most people seem to order 1 of 3 pre set 'trust me' choices. You get edamame, tuna, salmon, yellow fish etc sushi. We each got trust me lite for $39 and ordered some side rolls. Overall pretty good price but my two complaints were cold edamame and they only have beer, white wine and sake. The white wine was disgustingly sweet but at least it was chilled. Maybe they keep it with the edamame

Sugarfish has the most amazing sushi I have ever tried. The rice is warm, the seaweed is super crispy, and the fish melts in your mouth. I've had the blue crab, salmon, lobster, yellowtail, and albacore belly. You really can't go wrong with anything, but the albacore belly is out of this world.

Love fueled by value.  For a pretty affordable price, you can get a decent selection of above average fish.  A few starting disappoints but overall a worthwhile sushi journey. 

The first pass through my wait was 3 hours and so I Ieft for the handroll joint 8 blocks north.  My second pass was early afternoon and luckily I quickly scored a seat by the bar.  Service is attentive at the bar (compared to 3 servers among a million people at the KazuNori bar) and since it was early in the day, the ambience was much more calm and the restaurant was much brighter.  I'm not a fan of this whole modern dim dining experience at night, especially for a sushi bar.  

First disappoint - didn't know limited availability meant REALLY limited availability to the point they only had 2 specials available.  No uni to try :`(

Second disappoint - wow the edamame is like stale and old. 

Third disappoint - the "daily special" was just a randomly selected 2-piece from the list of sushis.  It wasn't like, anything actually special.

I went ahead and trusted, regular. 

The ginger was good, and the first few pieces surprisingly melted in my mouth.  Does melt-in-mouth signify glorious sushi? You know, I always thought so.  The sushi was reaaaally fresh, but I found it a bit lacking in flavor, like the true flavor of the fish (particularly the salmon, which is my favorite).  Maybe that's why it's downed with ponzu sauce?  I didn't find too much love for sea bass either.  

I think I'd come back to try the unagi and scallops.  I think I'd bring folks who like sushi and haven't had an omakase experience, as this is a really worthy affordable one imo.  I wouldn't wait over 30 minutes for it though.

We came on a Saturday around 10pm and was told the wait was 2 hrs...We expected that so we waited and it def was worth the wait. The sushi was super tasty. Just a warning it is a bit pricey. Def reccomend coming here at least once.

i think this is my favorite sushi of all time in the states.  I got the TRUST ME dinner menu (organic edamame, tuna sashimi, albacore sushi, salmon sushi, yellow tail sushi, sea bass sushi, snapper sushi, toro hand roll, and blue crab hand roll). LIKE CMONNNN how is this place SO DELICIOUS. ive had their sister restaurant in LA at kazu nori for hand rolls, but just come here to get both sushi AND hand rolls. i will dream of this sushi every day no joke.

the sushi rice is warm and MELTS in your mouth. each bite of sushi, whatever fish it is, just MELTS and isn't chewy, stringy, or fishy at all oh my gosh. its like butter, where you just bite through and it required 0 effort. i got like maybe a super tiny crab shell in my blue crab roll (i mean thats inevitable because crab is so hard to deshell, and maybe a small bone in one of the fish but thats okay. like 2 bones/shells in one meal? cmon..but i forgive cuz its so good).

i HIGHLY recommend getting the tuna sashimi and albacore sushi. I think it was the most delicious dish ever out of all the dishes that came out for my dinner. i really cant explain each piece, and someone definitely wrote a better review than me that you would be interested, but JUST GET IT ALLLLL ITS SO GOOD. if you don't like sushi, this place will convert you. you really don't need to dip your sushi or rolls in soy sauce. and EAT IT AS SOON AS IT COMES OUT when its warm!!

the wait sucked, came on a saturday night (duh the best time ever) at 5:00pm thinking we would beat the dinner rush but nope, got there when every one sat down, so we waited almost 1.5-2 hours, and got to sit at the bar. BUT ITS SO WORTH IT. if you don't like the wait, you should order take out. also, keep in mind that it is a no tipping restaurant!! which is awesome because everywhere else in the world does not tip except for america, and they give even better service.

and to the staff and management - EVERYONE IS SO FRIENDLY. i love you all.  just be my friend please~ ill be your best friend.

Friends visiting from out of town who wanted to check out this place recommended it. They don't take reservations, so the earlier you come or the more flexible you can be, the better. We showed up at 4:30 PM on a Saturday afternoon. That gave us a little time to enjoy the nice weather and explore the surrounding Gramercy/Flatiron area a bit more. 

We were seated in the middle of a full restaurant, but the building is clearly designed to absorbed sound well and attracts a sophisticated crowd that is not too loud. We had an incredible waiter who not only knew the menu inside and out, but could give very good recommendations and descriptions of menu items and their tastes. 

Four of us ordered the "Trust Me" and the other ordered a la carte. It is great to have this optionality. The only complaint that I had about our meal was that the plates came out too quickly in succession, which almost seemed as if they were trying to hurry us out of the restaurant. 

All the fish was incredibly fresh, and it was great that all of the rolls were pre-seasoned with the appropriate sauces. This was probably the best sushi I've ever had. They also have a wine list from which three of us ordered white wine and one ordered sake. 

Though not cheap, its great that taxes and fees are embedded in the menu price to avoid the annoyance of tipping at the end of the meal. Hope to come back soon.

Am a fan! Now get the hype about this place. Got the Trust Me for lunch and the wait for one wasn't bad - 5 mins on a busy Friday. Seafood super fresh and melts in your mouth. Rice is nicely seasoned and served a tad warm. Mmmm! Sat at the bar and they bring each dish as soon as prepared. Personal faves were the tuna sashimi served with a citrusy light sauce and the toro hand roll - accidentally made a surprised noise of pleasure after the first bite ;)
Staff very friendly and nice space! Highly recommend and this place likely ruined run of the mill sushi spots for me. I will be back!

Horrible waiting time every evening, but other than that - best sushi you can get for that price in NYC.  Really something special.  Very delicate (and unapologetic) flavors.  Emphasis on freshness and quality.

The quality of the fish here is excellent. Sushi was simply lovely. Combined with the reasonable price, and you can justify spending $100-150 here for two. Including a bottle of wine. The rolls are not very good, but this seems intentional. Didn't have a hand roll, but I would expect they are excellent. The $40 bottle of wine is drinkable at best, but it's hard to convince me to buy a bottle of Chardonnay for over $50 and the $40 Sauv Blanc was the only non-Chard option (they only have 3 wines, white only, $40, $60, $80). Overall service was top-notch, very friendly and professional and the sushi was very delicious. Will definitely be back!

I have been wanting to try out this sushi spot for a while, we finally got to go during lunch time. They do not take reservation, which makes it a bit difficult, especially since this is a popular spot. We got there after the lunch rush, so we didn't have to wait too long before we got a table.

We got there after the lunch rush, it was still very busy! Most of the tables were occupied, we were very lucky to get a table quickly. 

As for food, we were interested in their Omakase menu. They have three kinds of Omakase, and we went with the middle one called "Trust Me". This one is eight-course meal, most of them sushi pieces. It comes with Organic Edamame, Tuna Sashimi, Albacore Sushi, Salmon Sushi, Yellowtail Sushi, Sea Bass Sushi, Toro Hand Roll and Blue Crab Hand Roll. The portion is rather small, but this place is definitely quality over quantity. And we do value quality more than the quantity for sure. Each item was well crafted, high quality, tasty and most of them just melt in your mouth! 

The service was really great, polite and friendly. They gave us good information on the menu and dishes with a warm smile. And what is most surprising, they have NO tipping policy! The hospitality is included in the price, and yet, the service level is great. We had a really nice lunch here, my expectation was high and they did not disappoint.

Best Sushi I've had in the last couple of years!! Went in at 8 and had 50 people on a waiting list ahead of me. I gave them my phone number I went to a bar until I got a text saying I was close to the top of the line and to head back. The service was great! My favorite was either the tuna Shashimi or the 2 pc of Eel. For a Sushi joint this place had a very good price and the quality of sushi was amazing. If your looking to Eat here I would recommend checking in at the restaurant atleast 2 hours earlier

The staff here are so friendly and kind. Their takeout trust me sushi box is an absolute favourite that I would definitely recommend! The fish is really fresh and the various sauces and toppings elevate the takeout sushi experience.

This restaurant somehow always full.i tried to eat there on Saturday night and the waiting was 2 hours. so I came today on monday, the waiting list was thirty minutes. it's Monday night and its full!! 
there are 3 set menu which recommended by the waitress and it's much better to choose the set menu then Ala cart because the ala carte is kind of Expensive. one sushi roll is $11, so me and my boyfriend order two different menu and a bottle of sake. The price is already including tax and tip so no tip needed.
The thing is, for that kind of price, around $40 per person and the portion like that, both of us didn't feel full at all. we don't think it's worth it. The sushi I have to admit is fresh, the rice is different, Definitely different than sushi runned by Chinese. but for the price and the portion like that I don't think I wanna come back any soon.

delicious fresh fish ~

get the nozawa to split for two persons and then order extra sushi and rolls! i was pleasantly surprised by the bay scallops - definitely recommend trying it to supplement a set menu

tried this place in LA before and was excited they opened one in nyc! however the wait can get pretty long - waited almost 45 minutes on a monday night at 6pm. they don't take reservations and the restaurant is kinda dark

but service is pretty good and the fish is delicious - definitely a good spot if you're looking for good quality sushi for decent prices

it's also a no-tipping restaurant :)

So I came back yesterday at about 9pm and was told there was a 45 minute wait for a party of two. After 10 minutes, my friend and I received a text that said we were at the top of the list.

For some reason, my opinion of this place has completely changed from my first time here. I ordered the Taste Me along with sweet shrimp under the limited availability. Absolutely amazing!! Everything, especially the albacore sushi and the blue crab hand roll! The last time I was here, I stuck to ordering from a la Carte and many of them were absolutely drenched in ponzu sauce. This time around, there was just a perfect amount. 

I am DEFINITELY hooked now that my experience yesterday finally matches up with all of my friends' experience here.
10/10 fresh and tasty sushi. cousin of kazu nori (which is also good). get the largest sushi set!

Great food, and a lovely place. Though sometimes hard to get a seat at, SUGARFISH's three "Trust Me" menus are worth the wait. With three sizes depending on your level of hunger (and a willingness to allow substations for preference or allergies), these prix fixe menus are a good showcase into the quality and variety of food served here.

Where SUGARFISH really shines is in the quality of ingredients that it uses in its dishes. All of your senses (except hearing) tell you that the fish is of higher quality than it is at competing sushi restaurants. The sushi rice is also absolutely delicious. 

As for any bad parts of the experience? Well, the waitstaff seemed fairly indifferent to the patrons, both at our table and around us. Also, even though it's primarily a sushi menu, I felt the menu lacked creativity. While it did have a decent selection of fish and allowed you to have them as sushi, or hand rolls or whatever, I felt it could have offered more options. Overall, a very good place that id recommend if you're in the area and willing to spend for a "Trust Me" menu.

Best fucking sushi ive ever had. The fish was fresh, the sake was sweet and the ambience was everything 

I went with a group of co workers to celebrate a recent event success and im definitely coming for a date night!

I'm not going to lie, the only reason made an effort to try Sugarfish is because of its heavy endorsement from social media influencers like Kylie Jenner and her crew of socialites. Aside from its insta worthy take-out boxes, I really had no idea why this LA based chain was so popular or even fully offered. 


Arriving on a Friday night at around 10PM with no reservations, we were told the wait would be around 45 minutes to 1hr. Fortunately for us, the hostess was able to find a table for our party of 5 within 15 minutes after confirming other groups had skipped out on their reservation. After being seated, we were provided menus and given a full run-down of the offerings by a very enigmatic and passionate waiter. To take the guessing out of ordering (and perhaps for novice sushi eaters), SF provides 3 main offerings as a packaged meal set. 4 of us opted for the Trust Me ($39) option which included albacore, Salmon, yellow tail, sea bass and snapper sushi as well as edamame, toro and blue crab hand cone; the fifth person did a la carte with an assortment of tuna and salmon tartare and sushi. Each item is brought out in order as listed on the menu and the servers advise which items require additional soy sauce/wasabi and which should be enjoyed as is. As someone who typically can't eat anything besides tuna (food poisoning flashbacks), I was astounded by just how fresh and tasty each piece of fish was. My friend who recently came back from Japan and had fresh sushi almost daily from the fish markets noted she hadn't tasted anything similar until Sugarfish. 


For the quality of food, fantastic service and great ambiance, $39 was a very reasonable price. We shared a large sake, had a few beers and it ended up being about $50 or $60/person. Definitely worth it. We actually wanted to come back multiple times!

Hmmm...
1) Not a single Japanese person in the restaurant
2) We were seated at the counter to bear witness to the kitchen, which looked like a pizza place: Lots of stacked, pre-folded to-go boxes being filled and shuffled out to Postmates delivery peeps
3) Rushed (but cordial) service 
4) two hour wait (on a good day)

So why 5 stars? 
1) Because everything tastes amazing (especially the albacore and the salmon), 
2) the price is right (even on the small bottles of dry sake), and
3) the 'omakase' combined with the no-tipping policy means very little brain power/decision making necessary
I was impressed by the funny lunch combo name - "Trust Me".. and the place earned my Trust after going through the lunch course...

For the price, ambience, and taste - this place is definitely worth trying! 
I loved everything that we ordered off the sampler "Trust Me" menu and the lobster roll. I was not a fan of the salmon eggs at all but everything else was fresh tasting and delicious. 
The ambience is dark and romantic and this place is very unpretentious. There's no fancy decorations on any of the dishes, no tipping for service since it's included in the price, and no pushing from the wait staff to order more food than you want or need. I appreciated that! 
The only downside is the wait time - they don't take reservations and it was a 2.5 hour wait (via text alert). This worked out since we just hung around a bar, but be mindful of planning to come here early if you want to eat dinner on time

It sucks. This place is small, crowded, noisy and expensive. The waiting time is about 1 1/2 hours... for what? Sorry, it is not worth it 
This is a place for wannabes

I didn't have the the chance to eat because the place packed. I had a two glasses of wine that for me it was a little bit pricey. I paid $36 for only two glasses plus the tip. They make you wait upstairs while you wait for your table but since we were so hungry we couldn't wait and left. It's a crowded and  noisy place. We ended up dining at the next door Italian restaurant.

For the price please go to sushi on Jones, your tastebuds & wallet will thank me. The trust me sets are a cute idea for fixed omakase but it worries me that it doesn't seem to change with what's in season. They overdo it on the rice portions, the vinegar and the rice and everything else tasted strongly of ponzu sauce. The salmon sushi was probably the best piece out of all of them. Very busy for a Friday afternoon, not the best there is .

So good and so fresh! I got the "trust me" which came with edamame, tuna sashimi, 2 pieces of salmon sushi, 2 pieces of albacore, 2 yellowtail, 1 snapper, 1 sea bass, one spicy crab hand roll and one toro hand roll. I loved the tuna sashimi as well as all the sushi pieces. I also really liked the toro hand roll. I really didn't like the spicy crab hand roll and they noticed so they ordered to substitute it for another hand roll which was so nice and great customer service. I would definitely come back.

We were very lucky last Saturday afternoon to get seats at the back bar with kitchen view with only a 20 min wait. The menu is curated and they do it extremely well. We had the Nozawa selection and also ordered a la Carte. They do not advise you to add any sauce to already sauced sushi and I was happy to oblige. You could taste the quality and freshness of the fish and appreciate the craft and skill and ingredients in the preparation. I have not had such wonderful sushi in so long and I cannot wait to go back and also try the roll bar that is by the same chef. There is definitely a devoted following for this place. I was surprised to see the 1 star NYTimes review. I think this place is fantastic!

We got the trust me option and I have to say it was really good and much than expected! I thought it'd be like an average sushi chain quality, but exactly like they advertise the rice was warm and fish tender. They also season their rice and fish heavily so it was very flavorful, but some people may not like that. The trust me was the perfect amount to get me decently full and normally I can eat a lot of sushi. I also liked how the price was tip included so the cost was pretty good for nyc.

I'll admit that we had to pre-dinner before this because the wait was 2 hours. But the quality of the fresh was really good for the price  (we did have an incident where one of the fishes wasn't deboned properly though/or there was a hair, don't quite remember what it was) and they gave us some extra pieces of fish to make up for it.

This place was good - I loved their lunch specials were called "Trust Me." I of course got the Nozawa trust me, with the largest array of fish. The tuna sashimi to start was some of the best tuna I've ever had. The sauce and scallions went so well and the tuna was perfect. It fell apart in my mouth. Special of the day was bay scallops and that was the piece of fish I liked the least. The scallops were kind of fishy. The seaweed was awesome! Super crispy and I liked both handrolls. The rice was really good, and the servings of fish were a nice fish. The tuna and yellowtail were super tender and melted in my mouth. Delicious. My reason behind four stars is the fish was too cold, but otherwise I really enjoyed this place. Affordable and nice staff, too.

Although the wait is long, I'd say that it's worth it for the price. We went to grab a small bite to eat not far just to calm our hangriness. 

As it was our first time, we chose the Nozawa Trust me to try everything. Let me begin with the quality of the fish. I don't normally like tuna sashimi, but this first item was phenomenal. Not only was the tuna fatty, the sauce paired with it complimented the flavour. All of their fish is fresh, and the salmon was so good it melted in my mouth. 

My only complaint is that there was too much vinegar in the rice that was falling apart. They could definitely game up on their rice, as it makes up for 70% of the flavour of the sushi. The service was fast and lovely.

My fav were the tuna sashimi, salmon sushi, crab handroll and tuna handroll.

I was very excited to finally try Sugarfish after hearing so many positive things about it both on the east and west coast. Unfortunately, this location failed to deliver. 

The price is quite nice for the amount of food you get, however there are better establishments that give you an equally great value, better service, and a better overall experience. 

My entire party, excluding 1, ordered the same omakase menu and we all ordered the same a la carte item. The lighting is very dim and the omakase service was awful. We had 6 people in our party and our omakase orders were messed up multiple times. 

The experience was made even more uncomfortable and confusing because waitresses would literally run to our table, drop off serving portions for only 1-2 people at the table, disappear, then 3 minutes later a different waitress would come and drop off a couple more servings for 2 other people in our group. This would continue until everyone in our party had the same plate. It made for an awkward dining experience because everyone in the group would have to wait around 7-10 minutes for everyone to be served before we could enjoy the sushi. At that point, the sushi was soggy. Moreover, the waitresses would mumble what the offerings were and abruptly run away or even worse, genuinely say they were not certain which pieces were what type of fish. I was shocked that at a sushi restaurant, they weren't familiar with their omakase offerings. 

As for the actual food, it was okay. Nothing spectacular and the experience was certainly very underwhelming. 

TLDR: based on this experience, I would not return and I would not recommend.

Hands down one of my favorite sushi restaurants in NYC. Stellar service, atmosphere, and INCREDIBLE FOOD. 

Came around 5:30pm on a Saturday with a friend and we didn't have to wait long at all. We both ordered the Trust Me and TRUST ME, the sushi chefs know what's up! Our server was nice and helpful and even let me make substitutions which I did not expect. They even gave me an extra blue crab hand roll on the house because they brought this hand roll out before the toro hand roll. All the fish tasted super fresh and delicate! I usually take pictures of my food before I eat but everything looked amazing and I just couldn't wait to eat haha. 

SUGARFISH definitely lives up to the hype! Will definitely come back in the future and the server even suggested to try Kazu Nori nearby!!

Been dying to come here! I wanted to stop by Fish's Eddy so we came here first to get our name on the waiting list for lunch. 50 minute wait which was perfect for us to pick up gifts at my favorite store! Great way to kill some time! 

We ate at the bar and the staff is fantastic here! Everyone is having fun and the food is beautiful! I think it was my husbands favorite meal in New York. We both got the set menus but my husband got the bigger one. Everything comes out so cute!!!! Totally enough food but we happily ordered more because we couldn't get enough! I noticed other couples also getting more food after their set menu had completed. 

Super trendy spot. You might even see a celebrity while dining here!

Very good value sushi - great prices for fresh sushi and good portions. Not the best sushi ive had, but again, great meal for the price! Usually has a long wait, which can be 1hr plus, so recommend going early ~5pm or so to get seated right away.

Good sushi at a high price point. There's hundreds of other more affordable sushi spots in the area (sushi para 88's unlimited $26 sushi for one), but if you're feeling like a treat this is a place to try. 

The wait was an hour, and the hostess accidentally gave up our spot without acknowledging it. Despite this, the meal was pretty good when we were finally seated, so won't reflect that in the review and allow the food to do the talking.

I came here for my birthday dinner. I was pretty disappointed with my experience here. Each piece of omakase was drench with their signature sauce which completely overwhelmed your tastebuds. The sauce is supposed to compliment the freshness and taste of the fish, not the opposite. I get that it's some what of a mass produce chain of service but the quality shouldn't be compromised. The only reason I'm giving a 3 star review is cause of the pieces, my dinner companion and I ordered separately from the omakase set was actually good.

I've never had omakase before coming here so I was really excited. I can honestly say that it was a good experience though. 

The servers were great because they described each thing that was on our plate and was always good at refilling our cups. 

We got the Trust Me which was the perfect portion for my friend and I. The sushi was really good because it was really fresh and they gave a good portion of the fish. I know sugarfish specializes in their warm rice but I felt like the sushi rice had too much vinegar. It often overpowered the fish. With that in mind, the rest of the experience was pretty good. After this visit I've gone to better omakases that made me come to the conclusion that I did. 

The ambiance of this place is really intimate and relaxed so I recommend this place for date nights. It is a pretty good spot but there's even better omakase spots. So this place is more of a 3.7 rather than just a 3.

Awe, we were so excited to order Sugarfish, but it turned out to be a let down and made us naush. We put a lot of trust into their trust me box, but ended up feeling betrayed. 
Despite all the hype, sugarfish is not our type.

Bomb sushi, reasonable pricing

Great atmosphere..very cozy, prepare to wait. No reservations here.

2.5 hour wait on a Monday but totally worth it! Came here with friends already anticipating a wait, but didn't think it would be this long for a Monday but no big deal...we put our name on the list, they gave an estimate wait of 2 hours so we went to a bar nearby. At the conclusion of the 2 hour mark, we returned and received a follow up text that we would be seated shortly which we were. By the time we were seated we knew exactly what we wanted. We had built up quite an appetite with the wait so the 3 of us went for the Nozawa trust me which includes a daily special which for us it was large scallops. As a sushi fanatic, this place has definitely raise my standards. Every bite was so fresh and tasty that leaves you wanting more. The Nozawa was def more than enough food if you come hungry. Service was great, the waves in how each set of sushi or roll comes out was a perfect pace. Loved this place and can't wait to be back!

Stopped in for lunch with 3 others yesterday at 12:30. Was told it would be a 20-30 min wait. We decided to wait, but the wait was more like 45 + min.  Then they crammed us into a corner table for 3!! 
I've been to the Beverly Hills Sugarfish, nothing special. But my friends wanted to go here for lunch.  It was underwhelming at best, the hostess and host were unapologetic and the service was slow.  The sushi was basic, which I can appreciate (I'm not a proponent of adulterated sushi with mayo and sauces that disguise the actual taste of the fish). So why did it take so long to turn out sashimi and a few hand rolls?  Yes they were busy, but this lunch dragged on & on. And not friendly at all and I left hungry.  $120+ later. Not worth it and I'd never go back.  There are way better places that have better service, sushi and atmosphere.

Great sushi, one of the best I have been to. I have been here about three times now for lunch, I usually pick on of the tasting menus and octagonally add one of the specials (the albacore belly and the nigiri are both delicious). The service has always been great as well. One warning, they do not take reservations, I suggest coming before 5 on a weekday if you want to get seated in a reasonable amount of time (usually around 30 minutes). I have never attempted to come for dinner but have heard about wait time exceeding 3 hours. Great sushi and very inexpensive for what they offer. I defiantly recommend it.

Best I've had ever in the city. Hands down, or up. I've been in the city for over a decade, so that says a lot, or nothing at all...I'll go with the former.  The service is impeccable and the ambiance is second to none.
Delicious. Quality is on point! The warm rice and the cold fish makes an interesting contrast but it's good! Personal faves: tuna and albacore.

I've heard and read so much about this place and the chef it was named after that I dragged the bf here on a hot hot hot Saturday afternoon for lunch. There was only about a 15-20 minute wait which wasn't bad. Once we got a table, we both ordered the Trust Me set and while some pieces of fish tasted really fresh and good. The whole meal, process, and presentation were a bit disappointing. They brought dishes in little intervals and sometimes it took a while between each plate. I mean, it's two pieces of sushi on a plate. It doesn't take that long. It certainly didn't help that we were both hungry. The other disappointing thing was that the rice didn't hold up well and crumbled when I picked it up. I find that surprising for a supposedly respectable sushi chef named restaurant.

Somewhere between a 3 and a 4 for me, though the uneven pacing and the no-reservation/wait time skews closer to 3. 

Here are the positives: 
Everything was supremely fresh.
I could have eaten five more rounds of the tuna sashimi in ponzu served at the beginning. 
Prices were reasonable, given that tax and gratuities are already included (though I will note that they mentioned this fact to the couple next to us at the bar but not to us). 

Here is what threw me: 
The 2-2.5 hour wait. We're all savvy people with too little time in the day to just sit around and blankly wait (but Sugarfish does offer a little seating area on the first floor and a bigger area on the second floor to do just that) so my friend and I killed the time by grabbing a drink nearby. But in a city of really good food and OpenTable, it's hard to convince me that anything is truly worth waiting over an hour for. 

The inconsistent timing of when food was brought out. So my friend ordered the Trust Me and I got the Trust Me Lite + a scallops hand roll. Our food, except for the edamame and sashimi at the beginning, rarely synced up. She'd be eating or I'd be eating. I've been to omakase in the past where there'd be intervals between food and it never really bothered me but this time, I would have preferred to eat with my friend. I will say, though, that if you have a smaller appetite, the Trust Me Lite and 1-2 more handrolls were the perfect amount of food. 

Like many reviewers pointed out, the rice is pretty vinegary, so much so that I couldn't really taste the fish. 

Overall, good for one visit but not sure I'd come back for a repeat.

WORTH THE WAIT! Came Monday night with a couple of friends. I ran over right after work and put our name on the list. The host was very helpful when I was trying to strategize when to put our name down because of the timing of people arriving. We went to a bar nearby and waited a little over than 1.5 hours. So expect to wait but just be patient, they are very good at seating people promptly and efficiently and will text you when you're near the top of the list. 

Now to the food! We each got the trust me. It was a lot of food and we all left very full. I think if I had done the level above I would have been way way too full. Definitely go with one of them though because you get a taste of everything. I loved the toro hand roll and the yellowtail. Also the tuna sashimi was very very good. Also tip is included! So it only ended up being about $50 per person including the drinks we got. 100% worth it and some of the best sushi I have ever had.
Excellent place for sushi. Fish is great, service is great. Good sake options. Recommend the "trust me" sample menu. Can't go wrong here.
Some of the best sushi I've had. The sushi was so fresh it almost melted in my mouth. Would love to go back again one day.

Tl;dr definitely worth the wait for some melt in your mouth sashimi 
----
The two times I came here (dinner and lunch) have been nothing but positive experiences for me. For someone who eats a lot, the Nozawa trust me platter is enough to fill me up! Both times, the daily special has been unagi, which has a good crisp to it, and wow, no bones !!

The servers are very nice and friendly and consistently reminds you to not dip the fish that already have sauce in them! 

There is a nice little waiting area upstairs as well if you don't want to walk around the area while you wait for the text message.

I heard about sugarfish a little while ago and was in New York so I went there for lunch. First impression when we walked in the smell was pretty fishy but it didn't bother me. It was very nice, modern, and clean wasn't to busy we got to sit down right away. We sat at a table rather than the sushi bar so we could have a booth but I liked how they gave you the option. When we sat down the server Tim was very polite, attentive, helpful, and on top of everything such as empty plates more drinks etc. I went to wash my hands and the bathrooms are upstairs which I thought was nice so there was more room downstairs for seating there we also elevators so it was handicap accessible. There was two different soaps one for before and one for after eating I loved that especially since I am constantly washing my hands. When it came to the food I was very very impressed it was so delicious. There was two of us and we got two Trust me lite and salmon sashimi. The trust me came with edamame, tuna sashimi, albacore tuna, salmon, shrimp, and the last thing a Toro hand roll. Everything was so flavorful and most didn't need soy sauce because it already had a sauce. I got a hot green tea and my grandpa got a beer. The tea was the real stuff not the fake stuff! Overall I had such a good time and a fantastic lunch I will definitely be going back. One other thing you don't need to tip hospitality is included! You will definitely enjoy if you love sushi!

I've been trying various sushi places near work for lunch and sugarfish was on my list.  I was seated at the sushi bar in 5 minutes which was nice becuase it looked like they had a line for a table.  The place was dim, casual, japanese style.  No music I could hear, just the sound of people chatting over lunch. Different servers will interact with you and I was greeted quickly after sitting down.  This place is opinionated to say the least.  They know best and have several options the steer you toward.  I'm on a low carb diet so I was pretty screwed.  They had 2 sashimi plates in the a la carte and tons of carbs in all the suggested meals.  I asked if they could serve any of the sushi as sashimi and they acted discussed I'd even suggest it.   Ergo I didn't just order the sushi and leave the rice on the plate for fear of being booted.  they also have these rules like don't use sauce if the dish has sauce... Is wasabe considered sauce?   Anyway the sashimi I ordered was good but not over the top.  The sauce was some type of special soy that tasted good too.  Portion was on the smaller size for the price.  Another thing, no tipping allowed.  I probably won't go back.  I like traditional Japanese sushi and I don't mind a place with opinions but not enough variety for a low carb eater.

Good sushi at reasonable prices. The downside: long wait, very dim, and they bring the food in trickles. It was awkward to eat with friends. I'll come back here for late lunch so I can see what I'm eating, and probably not too busy. Hopefully we get the dishes that we order at the same time.

My friend took me here for the first time and I loved everything about it. We went late (11pm) so we were seated right away. I would definitely recommend doing one of the three combination options. Everything was fresh, delicious and I thought it was reasonably priced. There is no tipping at this restaurant and I found the service to be top notch.

On the Friday after the 4th I finally had the chance to try this place after what felt like forever having it bookmarked and hearing rave reviews from my friends. Was it the best sushi I've ever had before in my life? No, but the bar is high. Do I wish this place took reservations so I wasn't stuck waiting 45 minutes to sit (and that's on the shorter side, I've heard)? Yes, definitely. But was it still an absolute steal for really solid omakase? Yes, and that's exactly what I was hoping to find.

They recommend trying one of three omakase options - I opted for the "Trust Me" or the middle of the three. It's slightly abridged compared to the Nozawa trust me, which also includes a daily special (it was scallop when I went) but I don't feel like I missed out on much.

We started with edamame (a generous portion, no less) and tuna sashimi, which was wonderfully flavored and super fresh. The two friends I went with also really enjoyed it and heralded it as one of their favorite bites during the meal.

Next, a long line of sushi - albacore, salmon, yellowtail, and sea bass. The yellowtail was one of my favorites, although my friends preferred the albacore. All were phenomenal. The complaint I've heard from many that the rice is too vinegary was not echoed among my group; although it was heavy on the vinegar compared to other nice-ish sushi spots, I actually think I preferred it. 

Then, two hand rolls - toro and blue crab. The toro was actually a little disappointing although I can't put my finger on exactly why. It's obviously one of the most expensive types of fish you can get and it's generally my favorite, but this roll didn't do much for me and I actually highly preferred the blue crab, which was incredible.

The pacing of dishes was much better than expected given some comments in other reviews - despite one member of my group getting the Nozawa trust me, everything came out in a timely manner and was well-coordinated. 

Service was nothing to note and I wish they had explained some of the fish better, but hey, it's a no-tipping joint so it's tough to complain. The place itself is really chic on the inside and the bathrooms upstairs have both unscented and scented hand soap for before and after eating, respectively.

All in all, hands down some of the best sushi you can get for $50 ish per person. In terms of quality I'd put it at Sushi on Jones or Tomoe but with a much nicer dining experience.

Came here for lunch on a Friday and it was packed. There were originally 13 parties ahead of me when I got there but I was able to get seated after half an hour. The servers were very friendly and explained how the menu worked and what each piece of sushi was when it came to our table. I ordered the Nozawa Trust Me which was a decent amount of food. If you're a big eater you can order separate sushi as well. All of the food was fresh and of high quality. I especially liked the toro and blue crab hand rolls. They are also a no tipping restaurant so the prices you see on the menu are basically what you pay for. Would definitely come back again.

Finally decided to try this place on a Sunday night with my friend. We arrived around 6:00pm, and it was still a 1 hour and 45 min -2 hour wait for a party of 2 :/ You are allowed to put your name down without the whole party arrived, and they will text you when your table will be ready soon. Next time, I'd definitely stop by earlier just to go ahead and get my name on the list. My friend and I went to the nearby Cellar for happy hour wine and a cheese board while we waited so it wasn't too bad. 

We ended up not getting seated until right around the hour 45 mark, so the wait estimate was accurate. The menu has 3 main tasting options and then a la carte sushi, but I believe the vast majority of diners choose one of the 3 main options. We both opted for the Trust Me ($39) and hot green tea. The Trust Me Lite ($27) I think would've been slightly too little food. The Nozawa largest tasting ($51) would've been a lot, but I will probably want come back to try at some point.  

Our sushi tasted incredibly fresh and flavorful. The only dish we didn't love was the blue crab hand roll because it was mushed kind of like spreadable canned tuna. Otherwise we really really enjoyed everything else. The service was friendly but definitely a bit rushed. They would bring out the next course immediately after we finished the last bite of our sushi, so the meal moved quickly despite the multi courses. Each course was explained, but we kind of wished the last course would've been announced. It wasn't and then the meal was just over very abruptly with the waitress asking if we wanted to order anything else. 

Overall worth the hype for the price and quality. The atmosphere is also nicer than I expected but still casual. Def will come back but with the understanding of stopping by at least an hour earlier to go ahead and get a spot on the waitlist.

Came here on a Saturday night with my two friends. We put our name down around 6:15 PM and were able to sit down by 8ish. Two of us ordered the Trust me set menu ($39) and my other friend ordered the trust me lite ($27) and then added scallops to her meal. 

I thought for the amount of food and the quality of the restaurant, the prices weren't bad at all! Tip was included in the $39, so we just had to pay for tip, which made the meal around $42. 

My opinion may be a little skewed, because prior to eating here last night, I had poke the last two days in a row, so I was kind of sick of eating raw fish. But I will say that the quality of the fish here was amazing. The salmon was probably my favorite...it was so buttery and just kind of melted in your mouth. The fish was really cold and the rice was nice and warm and flavorful as well. 

I had never tried a hand roll before, so I was very pleasantly surprised. The seaweed on the outside was crispy and flavorful and the rice was warm, with again a cold layer of fish inside. I really enjoyed these--I will probably check out Kazu nori, which is the brand's hand roll bar in the future. 

Overall, I thought that the food was really great and of high quality for the low price point. The manager was on point, he was the one that came around and refilled our waters, but I thought that our waitress wasn't the greatest. She kept giving our other friend, who ordered the trust me lite my food....and it was really confusing, because when she brought the dishes out, she didn't take time to explain which fishes she had brought out and who the order was for. It was kind of frustrating and stressful because she kept giving my food to the other person and we weren't sure who the food belonged to?? We also didn't know which fish we were eating, because she didn't tell us. I would probably give this place 3.5 stars, just because of the subpar service.

This review is not on the food. That gets a 5/5. This is for service/space. So the place is always small and always packed. Came here at 4:30 on a Sunday and there's already 5 parties ahead of me and their sushi bar seats like 6 people. As a party for one it's so disappointing to see the small space for such high demand. You have to squeeze by people to get to the bar/order out (which I ended up doing after being told it "could be a thirty minute wait") and watched as one girl at the take out counter struggled to put together 20 meals. Everyone did their best with a smile but I doubt I'll be dining in again. I also have a splint on my foot and it is not accessible in any way. UPDATE: I nearly waited 45 minutes on a carry out order when I was told no more than 20.

Like everyone else says it is worth the wait. Got here on a Thursday around 6:30, it was a two hour wait, waited across the street at a Mexican place that has a very good tequila/ mezcal bar. We ordered two of the Trust Mes and it was very good quality sushi and was fairly priced for an omakase style dinner. The service was good and quick. Overall had a great experience. Would definitely recommend.

Normally im very apprehensive about trying new sushi places, but today decided to try Sugarfish for the first time and i have to say WOW! 
About 30 minute wait at 3:30ish PM. great friendly service and even more amazing sushi.
Will visit again and definitely recommend
