Sooooo worth the wait!! The hospitality and customer service is what MAKES this place. The kindness of the staff to go above and beyond their required job is admirable! I came here for my birthday dinner, and they kept us updated with timing and accurate information about seating us. This place has an extremely long wait if you come later at night, and they even have a second floor dedicated for people to wait. I had a luggage I was carrying because I came here straight from the Port Authority bus station, and they kindly put my luggage in a closet for me! 

As for the sushi... I was so shocked with every bite! Freshest fish I've ever tasted, and I didn't even need use soy sauce because it was so good! 

I'm no sushi expert, but the customer service and service itself was the outstanding part. The waiter kindly explained all the different options of the night and answered all questions. Service was speedy, but they also never rushed you while eating. The waiter just knew the right moments to come over and serve the next plate without making the experience seem too rushed. 

Overall, the sushi experience was great and it was lovely to enjoy a nice atmosphere with good sushi.

Fish is fresh, price is fair for where it is and what it is but there were some key failures in my dining experience which would prevent me from re-visiting Sugarfish.

What went well:
- pricing of the omakase menu was in-line for the neighborhood this place was in, making one feel good value as gratuity was included in their pricing model
- fish was fresh
- lineups and waiting system was a fair one and aligned to expectations

What didn't go so well:
- sushi rice was warm/borderline hot, suggesting that the chefs did not cool the rice down to room temperature quickly enough.  hot rice with raw fish?.  There is no coming back from this error.  game over.

-rice was on the overcooked side of the spectrum.  there's only 4 components in nigiri.  Fish, sushi rice, Wasabi, and soy.  fish and rice take the lions share in concentration of importance.  you fail the rice, you fail the sushi.

That pretty much sums it up, spent 118 USD for two people for a failure to make proper sushi rice.  Meanwhile you have other patrons in the restaurant happily smiling away like nothing is wrong, enjoying a what they think is a fantastic meal, none the wiser.

Finally got to try this place the second time around. Tried to come here about a month ago but walked and settled on kazu nori instead due to the wait here. I arrived around 6pm on a Tuesday night and the wait was still around an hour and a half (eeek) it was totally worth it though! Me and my girlfriend were debating on getting just hand rolls but decided we should do one of the set courses instead. At first we were going to settle on the trust me lite and add another hand roll but decided it's best if we did the regular trust me course. So glad we decided on that one because we both are huge eaters and it still wasn't enough food for us! My girlfriend even ordered an additional roll on top of the trust me course. 

The wait is very long but I strongly feel it's worth it. There's additional waiting area upstairs that people are not aware of. You can also order drinks while waiting which is a plus. Everything was tasty and delicious. Customer service was superb and I'll definitely bring my bf next time!

Another one of my absolute favorite restaurants, and IDEC that it's a chain. I've been here at LEAST 6 times in NYC and twice in LA. The sushi is simple and delicious: fresh, flavorful fish; warm, vinegary sushi rice (the warm rice really makes it next level), and that's it. The toro is a special (I believe you can usually get it on weekends) and is literally the best toro I've EVER had, and I've been to some of the bougiest sushi restaurants in NYC (looking at you, Sushi Nakazawa). The albacore belly, large scallop, and eel are all amazing a la carte additions to the "Trust Me" menus as well. The ONE downside is obviously the long wait - but it is SO worth it! I've definitely thugged out a 3 hour wait with no regrets.

I'll let you in on a little secret: The Emperor has no clothes. Seriously. For the price the place is fine. But a two hour wait on a rainy week night for OK sushi in a city that is literally packed with hundreds of far superior restaurants is incomprehensible. Except for the fact that that people love an Instagram moment, a brag-able wait time or the hype of an LA to NY chain there is nothing about this place that explains it's crazy popularity. It is certainly not the sushi, which again, is fine.

Honestly the restaurant is very nice. The service was polite and efficient. I enjoy that the tip is included and I felt well fed for the price of my Trust Me menu considering how hungry I was by the time I sat down at 9:30. 

If this place was in my neighborhood and I could pop in for dinner I would probably return and overlook the overly sweet sushi rice or the fact that for an "trust me" menu it is always the same with a few small exceptions.

For me, though,I would rather spend a little more, wait a little less and have a real omasaki.

Disappointing - that was my experience with Sugarfish summed up in a word. Consider yourself warned.

I was planning to grab brunch at nearby Union Square Cafe, but my friend suggested sushi instead and I am not known to turn down an opportunity for raw fish. As a result, despite my prior hesitations to try out this hyped-up LA export, I went in.

We were seated after about 20-30 minutes for a late Saturday lunch, and both quickly settled on getting the Nozawa Trust Me ($45). The tuna sashimi with ponzu to start off was encouraging, but the next dish and everything to follow confirmed the worst of my fears. 

The main issue was the rice: mushy and overseasoned with both vinegar and possibly sugar! As a result, every piece immediately coated my tongue with sharp acidity and a weird sweetness that completely drowned out the fish on top. The handrolls also were overfilled so that it was impossible to devour it without spilling rice and fish all over your hand. The daily special of large scallops were probably the only above-average piece.

The attractive price point that Sugarfish boasts draws crowds that can lead to wait times greater than 2 hours on an average night. Those people can enjoy their wait while I enjoy decent sushi at a similar price tag at Sushi Yasaka or Sushi by Bou*.

*Sushi by Bou has sadly closed since I originally wrote this review.

For the price that you pay, and overall quality and amount of food you get,   it is a pretty good deal. However, I came as a party of 4 at 5:30 pm on a Friday, and I waited over 2.5 hours for a table. At around the 1.5 hour mark, they already told me two tables of 4 are about to leave, and I still wasn't seated until over an hour later. The sushi rice was very warm, kind of felt hot, and the rice fell apart in my hand. I mean I understand that you get what you pay for, but that's still a bit disappointing for a sushi restaurant like this one.

Dined at one of the LA locations before. Was not disappointed by the NYC location.

This is great quality casual sushi. There's three sets: Trust Me Lite ($27) , Trust Me ($39) and Trust Me Nozawa ($51).

Having got the higher priced set before I opted for the middle "Trust Me" set. It was just the right amount of food and the best value.

As with Japanese custom this is a true no-tipping restaurant so gratuity is included in the prices of the food. Service was excellent from everyone we interacted with.

We loved our experience at the bar. The place was packed yet the staff was friendly and worked well--you couldn't tell they were slammed by their faces, so kudos. We also thought the food was delicious. Finely calibrated flavours and portions. We would totally return!

This is another sushi spot that doesn't require tipping which I love. Even though there's no tipping, the servers were still very friendly. I love the fishes because they were so fresh and so good for the price you're paying. I like that they serve a lot of drinks including wine. The wait is usually very long, so I was lucky to be seated right away.

Took about 40 minutes for a party of 2 to be seated... the hostess was nice but the waiter didn't offer much information about what was popular. We ordered off the Trust Me menu which was recommended on yelp. It had a few bite sized pieces of sushi with decent flavor. The places were spaced out and wasn't worth the money or wait. We were not only disappointed but left hungry. Not sure what the hype is about but wouldn't recommend this place to anyone I know.

We went in at 9pm (Saturday night) and put down my name for a party of 2. The guy at the front told us there were 38 parties in front us. I misheard him and thought he said minutes. We ended up waiting for 2 hours and there were still 12 parties in front us. It was already after 11pm, and they close at 12pm. I'm not sure how they were going to seat everyone on the list because a lot of people came after us. We were so sick of waiting we ended up getting takeout, which was cheaper and way cuter. I regret not getting takeout sooner. To order for takeout, you have to walk all the way to end and on the right corner that was the takeout corner. 

The sushi: it was good. It was better than the average sushi, but not as good as those fancy omakase places. But I don't think the wait justifies the sushi. I recommend getting takeout and walk over to the Madison Sq Park and eat there. It's scenic and romantic (unless it's night time, then beware of little NYC creatures roaming around). If I ever get it again, I would do takeout.

This is seriously the best sushi I have every had. Everything was extremely fresh and delicious. It's a decent price for the amount of food and quality of fish that you get. Will definitely be back!! It gets really busy for lunch and dinner so I would recommend going around 3

Finally got to try this LA hit transplant. It delivers on food (4/5), service (5/5), atmosphere (4/5) and value (5/5) - $40-50 for a good variety and amount of sushi/rolls that is hard to beat in NYC.  You won't get exotic or imported fish from Japan or fanciful rolls or complex flavors, but you get fresh fish that is well prepared and lightly seasoned.  The rice was a bit more on the loose side but manageable if you have half decent chopstick skills.  It was a bit more on the vinegar/sugar side but not overwhelming so like some viewers pointed out so it didn't detract from tasting the fish or crabmeat.  Perhaps it depends on who prepared it that day.  The only area where it falls short is the lack of ability to make reservations and the 2hr or so wait to get a table during peak hours.  If you are a smart diner then plan to put your number down and go get a drink and small bite elsewhere.  When your table is ready they will text you. That is what we did.  They don't have a bar but there is some seating upstairs where you can wait but it isn't really a lounge.  Once you sit down at the table the dishes come out fairly quickly one after another.  Will definitely be back.

My first experience with SugarFish was in Santa Monica and thought it was amazing. Everything was really fresh and even though it was super busy, every order came out at a even pace. Unfortunately, the one here in the city did not meet my expectations. I've been meaning to come here for awhile since it opened in 2016 but because it was super hyped, the seats were hard to get unless you come at odd hours or by yourself. So I came by myself last night at 5:30pm and got seated right away at the "sushi bar". It's not really a sushi bar when there's no sushi chef making sushi in front of you. It's literally just a bar seating and it's right next to a semi-open kitchen. 
 At SugarFish, there are three pre-fixe options you can get: Trust Me, Trust Me Lite, and Trust me Nozawa. Or you can do a la carte. I decided to order the Trust Me Lite since I wasn't feeling that hungry. It came with edamame, tuna sashimi, 4 pieces of sushi which included albacore, salmon, yellowtail, and shrimp, and a toro hand roll. I also ended up ordering a blue crab hand roll in the end. However, I was disappointed that a lot of the sushi pieces kind of came apart. It was fresh for sure but not as a fresh as the one I had in Santa Monica.  I was also sitting near the kitchen so I could see what was happening behind the scenes. These guys are not sushi chefs. Saw one guy making a hand roll and didn't even wrap the seaweed all around it and was ready to serve it. My waiter gave him a side-eye so clearly something's up. And I don't think Nozawa even has control ownership of how things run at this chain anymore so don't expect a high quality omakase experience here.

Overall, delicious!  We've eaten at his other restaurant, KazuNori, before, so we knew what quality to expect.  My husband and I each ordered the Trust Me Nozawa (largest) pre-fix menu.  Very filling.. I would almost say it was too much food.  The regular set might be a better way to go.  A disclaimer though, they had accidentally given me a double of a dish (which I alerted them too, but after realizing their mistake, just told us to enjoy it for free!) so I was fuller than most probably would be.

They don't do reservations here, so make sure you have the time to wait, or get there early.  We went as soon as they opened at 11:30 am and were lucky to get one of the last empty tables.  This place fills up fast and it doesn't stop until they close.

Prices are a bit high, but it's no-tip and worth the price (for the most part).  The rice is perfect - warm, loosely packed, and melt-in-your-mouth.  Everything is prepared fresh and given to you right away, so you can enjoy it at it's best.  Loved nearly all of the dishes, but there was one plate towards the end that really threw both of us off - it was the one with the scallops and it just had a weird tangy taste that didn't quite go with the rest of the food.  I would have been very happy just without that dish.  That's the only reason I didn't give this place 5 stars.

Google Maps has a misleading wait time because everyone puts down their name, leaves, and then actually waits at the location for up to 15 minutes. Any night after 4-5PM is 2-3 hour wait. 

With that said I went on a Thursday night at 7:00PM and the wait was 2.5 hours, even just for 1 person. Ordered out and got the To Go Trust Me $40. My favorite pieces was the blue crab cut roll and then tuna sashimi. To go orders don't offer hand rolls due to quality control and SUGARFISH's desire to provide the best sushi for immediate consumption so everything to go is either nigiri or a cut roll. 

I also ordered scallop nigiri $7 and felt that the rice in all the nigiri pieces wasnt that good because it was over seasoned and unbalanced with the thin piece of fish on top where as the cut rolls were perfectly balanced in flavor. 

SUGARFISH really mastered the art of to go with such an informational box on how to eat any of the popular pieces with the provided soy sauce, yuzu ponzu, scallions, and lemon wedge. The to go boxes also have salted edamame, wet napkin to wipe your hands, chopsticks, and a regular napkin. 

I highly recommend walking to Madison Square Park with all the plethora of seating to have your meal. This definitely isn't worth a 2-3 hour wait but okay to go and you might want to try Kazunori instead for their terrific hand rolls and pricing.

If you're serious about sushi this place is undoubtedly one of the best sushi spots globally. I've travelled the world and eaten at some of the top sushi spots. This place is on par! Excellent, fresh melt in your mouth. Only problem is no reservations and the wait can time put you off.

Our waiter was amazing and honestly was able to keep my excited about my food throughout the meal, but I left feeling underwhelmed by Sugarfish due to all of the hype that came with it. One good thing about the restaurant is that pays its workers fair wages (I hope), which contributes to this being a no-tipping restaurant. Overall, the quality of the food definitely wasn't worth the 3hr+ wait we had before being seated. I'd say try it out, but you're better off going to its sister restaurant, KazuNori, on 28th and Bway.

What a curious experience. 

Armed with everyone's reviews about the wait time, I arrived on purpose during the afternoon lull around 3pm. We were seated immediately at the bar. The ambiance is chic, but you already feel the sense of fast pace exuding in the atmosphere as you walk in. It does sort of feel like fast casual. I ordered a new menu, "Don't think, Just Eat"- they mentioned it is their anniversary menu. 

For $63, tip included, I got a well-paced meal with a variety of hand rolls, nigiri pieces, and sashimi bowls (already in sauce). The bathrooms have a nice detail- unscented soap for "before" eating and scented soap for "after" - so that you don't impact your taste buds before eating. The random casual upstairs lounge area is actually spacious and feels like a nice repose from downstairs. Lighting at the bar is well-adjusted for your perfect Instagram shots, if you care. 

There were some lovely scallop pieces. The albacore tuna was a standout as well. The controversy about the rice is interesting- the famous Pete Wells claims that "the rice is not only warm. It's seasoned with so much vinegar that it's almost pickled. This makes it appealingly energetic, a quality that sets it apart from the rest of the food."

I agree that most of the fish tasted neutral, and that I didn't find that the salmon or tuna exhibited the usual tender heft that I expect from high quality fish. 

The service was pretty good considering the objectives of the restaurant. I never felt like I was waiting around too long for anything. Overall my interactions with the servers were low touch, high volume and therefore came off rather robotic. 

I don't think it's good enough for me to want to wait more than 10 minutes for a table here. The price point is decent enough for the volume of food, and it satisfied my craving for semi-affordable omakase-style eating. I added on two uni pieces for $15 at the end as my personal dessert, and that was fantastic.

The edamame is perfectly salted and evenly done so. The tuna tartar is lemony and fresh. Very crisp. The rice here is 100% the best sushi rice I've ever had. 

The sushi is excellent. Service was great. Price is decent for what you get, leaning on the slightly overpriced side, but somewhat justifiable considering tax and gratuity are factored into the meal. 

Will absolutely be back. 
4.5 stars.

I had an incredible meal here. The pieces were incredibly fresh and the hand rolls were crispy and perfect. Very limited menu but everything tastes perfectly done. Best eel I've ever had. Great sake! I'll be back soon!

fantastic service! seating is very close to each other so you do unfortunately hear the people next to you. 

my friends and i had the prix fixe and thought the fish was great. i didn't enjoy any of the sauces that were used for the items, and that is what knocks down this review from a 5 star. the sauces are overpowering and not complimentary to the freshness and delicate flavor sushi should have. I did mention this to the waitstaff and they were very kind and tried to redo the item for us. the quality was superb, but again, the sauce is what kills the items.  

you do get a great value from the prix fixe and i again, loved all the items that did not have a sauce.

Decent curated sushi at its price point. Echoing much of the other reviews here, the ponzu is too overpowering on many of the courses, though the fish itself seems good quality. 

Sleek and spacious interior. Came on a Saturday afternoon around 3pm and had no wait.

Excellent quality sushi, especially for the price.

Doesn't take reservations but I've had success arriving weekdays around 11:30-11:45.  There is no wait at these times.  If you arrive at 12:30, you may wait an hour.

This is the best sushi I've ever had. Not only is everything incredibly fresh, but the sauce used on the actual sashimi or nigiri is so unique. My friends and I kept guessing what the acidity was behind each sauce, which was quite nerdy of us but so so fun. I'm probably ordering takeout from here all the time.

Hands down some of the best sushi I've ever had.

We tried the Trust Me special and each and every bite was amazing. The staff also time it really when when they bring out the next dish, so you aren't too full all at once. 

The good thing about Sugarfish was both the sushi and the experience. Super fun, and highly recommend to anyone and everyone in New York!!!

As someone who occasionally splurges on fancy omakases, I will say that the best part of an omakase meal is typically the first piece of nigiri - the little bundle of warm rice gently coaxed into a cuddle that hugs your tongue when you eat it. (Subsequent pieces eventually becomes room temperature, since the bamboo basket that holds the cooked rice does allow the heat to slowly dissipate.)

Sugarfish gets it right with its consistently warm rice, so that every piece feels like that first glorious piece of an omakase that is twice or thrice the price of a meal here. The fish was pretty good too - thick, succulent slices of fish that were meltingly tender and rich. (The opening tuna sashimi was cold and frosty, but everything else was solid.)

I came around 3 pm on a Saturday afternoon and had to wait about 15-20 minutes. You can get a drink and hang out in the upstairs seating though.

Service here is kinda wonky though. Even though me and my boyfriend both got the Trust Me set, our dishes came at separate times. The rolls also come BETWEEN nigiri pieces, and not at the end, so it was a little disorienting to get the tuna roll after our first course and were like "whuut just happened".

I'd most certainly come back if I was hankering for sushi.
Good sushi. Loooong wait. I like the rice. Sometimes it's better than other times. Make sure to put your name in... no reservation

The best sushi in NYC for this price point. 

Reasons why I love Sugarfish:
1. Warm sushi rice is a luxury I never knew I needed
2. They have iced matcha green tea with free refills (you can also take your tea to-go)
3. There is no thinking required. They offer set menus & tip is already included in prices
4. Service is always friendly

Tips for your Sugarfish experience:
1. It gets crowded, they don't take reservations, and won't seat you until everyone is there. Plan accordingly. I find coming for a late lunch helps with wait time
2. Make sure to participate in the birthday deal! Fill out the card insert you get with your bill on two separate visits to get a free Trust Me meal set on your birthday

I came to New York with few intentions:

Vacation away from Home
Drink whiskey at speakeasy bars 
Eat delicious foods

When I met up with one of my best friends Cat, her friend was also in town and he suggested this place which had a 2 hour wait. It sounded like it would worth it since my friends were edifying the crap out this plaice. Apparently you get their omakase  the busy try's are the albacore belly and tuna. The fish MELTS in your mouth. And the flavor is so great that you don't need soy sauce to eat with most of it. There signature is that they use warm rice.

After dinner I've concluded that these statements are all TRUE. I've had good sushi in the Bay at a fair price. SUGARFISH is on another level though. You wouldn't think so since Japan is closer to west coast, but sometimes thats not always the case. 

The chefs probably are that legit. 

It was a great spot, slightly pricey but you're get what you pay for. 

Definitely coming back again as well as Bohemian. They both are my top two Japanese go to spots in NY. 

Great place for dates.

I think Sugarfish is a great VALUE for the price and amount/quality of fish! 
Even though it opened last year, there is still quite a bit of a wait.

We went around 6:30pm on a Sunday and still had to wait about 1.5 hours. We didn't know, but there's an upstairs waiting area with nice seating! 
They'll text you when your table is ready, so go ahead and walk around the area or grab a drink.

They have 4 different sushi set options. Trust Me Lite, Trust Me, Nozawa, and one that's not on the menu but they said it's the biggest option.

The Nozawa seemed like quite a bit of fish for me, so I went with the Trust Me, which was more than enough! The bf got the Nozawa and was pretty full as well.

Every set comes with edamame and tuna sashimi to start. The waiters are attentive, clearing out plates when you're done so you're ready for the next plate. 
The only thing that bothered me was timing. Even though we got different sets, I think they could've coordinated a little better. But i do understand that their sushi is meant to be eaten right away since we don't have the luxury of being served at the bar. But there were times when either of us were eating alone.. 

Aside from that, quality of fish was great! Some pieces were definitely melt in your mouth. There have been lots of complaints about over-seasoned rice, but I actually didn't mind it. 

Overall, it's a great deal for what you get. And I'd definitely come back

**They have a birthday program, where you write your email on the card provided with your receipt. If you visit twice before your bday, your birthday is free!

Great sushi but the service wasn't great. They had mixed up my order with my friends several times. I wish they would've figured that out. And luckily my friend and I didn't start eating right away because they didn't realize until about 5 minutes later. 

The bathroom was pretty filthy unfortunately.

Food "A"
Super yummy. Definitely One of the best sushi places in New York City. It's almost impossible to eat this high quality sushi with this price. 

Price "A"
Again, it's even cheap for this quality. 

Service "A"
Staff are nice and friendly. 

Cleanness "A"
Nice atmosphere, clean bathroom.

You will have to wait for 2-3 hours(some times more) so get there early and put your name down and go somewhere else and kill time. Go get some drink. they will text you when your table is almost ready. There are too many fake Japanese sushi places in New York that says it's hard to enjoy authentic sushi with good price, but here, it's perfect.

The idea of affordable sushi in New York seems like an impossible concept but Sugar Fish makes it work minus the ridiculous wait time due to the small size of the restaurant and demand. Definitely go and put your name on the waitlist at 5pm if you can and you'll still wait a couple hours before getting seated. We put or name for a party of 2 down at 7pm and waited until 930pm. 

The food: Definitely not the best sushi I've ever had, but really good for the price. We got the "don't think, just eat" which is perfect for people that don't want to think about their order and just want a tasty variety meal. If you're picky about certain types of fish, you should order from the ala carte menu. I liked this option though because it filled us up for under $70 (tax and tip included) and gave us a variety of fish including tuna, salmon, scallop, crab and lobster... they ran out of uni though, so we weren't able to try that.

I would absolutely come back here, but hopefully find some way to get around the long wait time. Maybe put your name down and go watch a movie or something. 

Bottom line - don't expect out-of-this-world quality, but expect fresh, delicious fish for a price that won't break the bank.

Sugarfish is an absolute must have!!! I have always loved visiting while on the west coast, so very excited to have a location in NYC now. I always order the "Trust me." Great sushi and a couple glasses of wine only takes you to around $50. I would easily pay more than that for the quality too. The hand rolls are to die for, served warm with crisp Seaweed. But hands down my favorite is the albacore belly. Melt in your mouth tuna! And they mean it when they tell you soy sauce isn't necessary. The only downside here is the wait. Even for lunch we had to wait around 30 minutes. Hope some more locations open up to combat the popularity!

It pains me so much to write this, but my most recent Sugarfish experience was a solid 2 stars. I've been here three times before, and I couldn't imagine a better free birthday meal than Sugarfish, even if I had to wait 2 hours. They actually now even have an integrated system with Yelp so you can check your status in line when you look at your Yelp app! So cool. After 40 minutes of waiting, I saw that I had 25 parties ahead of me. Who waits 2 hours for dinner on a weeknight? @_@ 

In any case, I was super excited to finally get to eat here; I've only eaten here on Saturdays at noon because I usually line up a few minutes before Sugarfish opens. It's been spectacular every single time (as I've said in my last review). The edamame started out fine. The tuna appetizer was pretty good. And then the sashimi came.

Nothing was disgusting or rotten, but I was hugely disappointed by everything I ate after that (except for the crab roll, scallop, unagi and sweet shrimp. Will get to that later). The rice was incredibly inconsistent, either wet and falling apart or dry, bland and cold. Where was the consistent, perfect, sweet, warm, vinegary, energetic rice I've eaten the past three times? I held Sugarfish's sashimi rice to be my standard, and this was absolutely shattered. 

The fish didn't taste particularly fresh, and I noticed more than before the use of the sauces to brighten up the fish. The citrus sauces were stronger than before, which I didn't mind, but bothered Raymond. Nothing tasted like what I had eaten before. The toro roll was especially sad; the toro was so cold that it felt like it had come out of the freezer 30 minutes ago. (The rice there and the seaweed were good, though).

My meal was a free Trust Me, which did not include the scallops. Raymond got the Trust Me Nozawa, which did; the scallop was actually really good (like it is usually). We ordered sweet shrimp and unagi à la carte, and they were both really great - a total contrast to everything else we ate. It really makes me wonder if Sugarfish sacrificed quality for quantity/getting Trust Mes out ASAP on weeknight dinners because this was such a drastic departure from what I've eaten in the past. Why were the à la carte items so much better made? The crab roll, which is one of my favorite pieces, thankfully, was solid. 

Overall, I'm still willing to give Sugarfish a chance - but on weekend lunches only. I was completely willing to wait 2 hours for a free birthday meal, but I would not be willing to even wait 5 minutes to eat on a weeknight again if it's going to be this bad.

I'm such a fan. Although the hype of their grand opening is long over, you're still faced with a several hour wait time. I've found a trick though, come 15 mins after they open weekdays and you'll get sat immediately ;)

I always order the Trust Me. Fresh fresh fresh. And affordable as all hell. 

I'm obsessed with how all their items are pre-sauced. And the salmon with it's aromatic sesame seed touch is always delightful. Also Yuzu sauce on the yellow tail. AND SWEET SHRIMP is what we always order a-la-carte as an addition to the Trust Me. My god. Lay those all over my body please. 

Last but not least, gratuity is included. Just come here please thanks xoxo

Sorry but waiting and waiting and waiting and waiting to be seated will never ever compensate for how good the food could be. Even after waiting and waiting and waiting and waiting they said we were next and then we proceeded to wait and wait and wait and wait. If I don't see a fishbowl on my table and a master sushi chef performing miracles this is a one and done.

This was our third time going and it was definitely a different experience. The hand rolls were so cold the fish was actually icy (my fiancé called it acai fish).

The service was mixed, some friendly staff and some that barely explained the rolls. Some of the pieces were cut very poorly, and had holes or tears. There were a few good pieces, scallops being one, but overall the experience was rushed, crowded and underwhelming. 

We won't be back for a 4th visit, it's sad to see that it's gone so down hill after our first visit.
Best sushi in the world. I have been to many places and I can safely say the quality of the sushi here is impossible to top. AMAZING!

I'm convinced this place is purely thriving on hype.  Maybe it's because I just waited 3 hours for just 1 person but the sushi doesn't taste as good as I'd expected for a place that would have this long of a wait. I've been to their location in LA which I am pretty sure is better (then again, in LA I didn't have to wait, I was seated right away during an off hour weekday afternoon).  

The staff is very nice about it, upbeat but apologetic about the wait.   But maybe they have to be because I'm sure a riot would breakout if they weren't so pleasant about it.

Not to be racist but also noticed that front of the house is all Asian but no one making the sushi is remotely Asian... is that weird for a sushi joint or is it just me?

Some of the sushi come with a sauce but it's not indicated on the menu.  I would have made my choices differently if I knew.

Anyway, after 3 hours of anticipation I really expected more.  Yes, it's better than your average Taiwanese-owned sushi joint but in my opinion not worth the wait.  

Maybe next time I'll try the take out (which actually comes at a cheaper price than eat in)

Having heard of Sugarfish initially by word of mouth and then seeing the massive waits each time we attempted to go, I was a bit skeptical at first if this place was even worth the hype - a quick check on Yelp would also reveal mixed reviews throughout. However, after popping by at an awkward time between lunch and dinner, we finally managed to get a seat. After sampling Sugarfish's offerings, I am beginning to see why it attracts the crowds day in and day out.

To start off, the simple, non-cluttered menu makes ordering easy. As a party of two who wanted to try everything, we got the "Nozawa Trust Me," which essentially is a pre-fixe or omakase selection of fish and hand rolls paired up to be perfect for a group of two. And coming in at only $51 for the premium options (NO TIPPING EITHER), you are looking at slightly over $25 dollars for two people to enjoy fresh, delicious sushi.

Our selection that day consisted of pre-marinated tuna sashimi, salmon, toro (fatty tuna), yellowtail, sea bass, scallops, fluke, sweet shrimp, AND a blue crab hand roll. Once again, let me reiterate, ALL of that cost only $25 a person with no tip needed. Even at this price point, the fish themselves were non-compromising in flavor. The staff also encourage you eat right away as the rice is warmed and seaweed crisp (so take those pictures right away!). The next time I am in NY, I will be sure to come at the same time again to ensure a spot at Sugarfish's table!

I have been to Sugarfish in LA a bunch of times and loved it. It's always consistent - fresh fish and very fairly priced for the quality of sushi. I was excited when Sugarfish finally opened here in NY, but the wait time is just ridiculous. I've gone 3 times and have waited at least 2 hours or more. When you finally sit down the service is so rushed it's kind of hard to enjoy your meal. The sushi is good but not worth the long wait and crowded room.

I previously posted a negative review for the restaurant. We gave it another chance and I'm going to a 5+ star with strong recommendation.
We spoke to the manager Daniel and sorted out the issues we had from prior visit. He dealt with it amazingly well and we got past prior issues.
Service was awesome.
Food, as I had previously said too, is awesome.
Put it on your list as a must visit restaurant

I've been wanting to go to this place for months but it's not the easiest to get in during prime dinner hours. They don't take reservations so you have to come and but your name down. We put our name down at 6pm on a Friday, they texted us at about 7:45pm but then we had to wait another half hour after we got there for a table. It lost a star for that process but the food itself was excellent. It definitely met expectations. We got the Trust Me and it was a nice amount of food, and everything that came out was incredibly fresh and well prepared. The price ($39pp) was not cheap but definitely worth it for the quality, good service and overall experience.

I have not done many omakases but I will say I've tried many different kinds of fish, cooked and raw.  I love seafood in general and especially appreciate freshness.  My gf highly recommended sugarfish since she had it in LA so we went to this one in NYC to try it out.  I appreciated the menu selection but went with the "don't care, just try" option for $63.  My gf went with the "Trust me" set.  We essentially got the same items with the exception of 5 things.  I had scallops, she had sea bass, etc.  Breaking it down into three parts, rich, fish, prep.  First, rice was good.  Warm, well sized and clumped for optimal chew resistance.  The fish and seafood quality had great textures but lacked a bit in fishiness.  Salmon was overpowered by sesame but still tasted really good.  Albacore was good quality bit much on the soy sauce.  The toro was buttery but not fishy enough.  Scallops were fresh but again, the scallop flavor was lost.  There was only one where the fish stood out and transported me to a taste of the sea but I unfortunately did not catch which fish it was.  Picture available.  The preparation overall was good though.  Good serving size, good sauces, good presentation.  This is definitely mid tier sushi for mid tier prices.  Great atmosphere with great service so if you want basic sushi that won't disappoint, it's a good spot.

Incredible sushi experience!! Amazing food, we got the "Trust Me" and "Nozawa Trust Me". Our favorite was their signature Albacore Tuna highly recommend this place, everything was really good and everyone was very friendly!

Sugarfish originated from L.A., which was also where I first had it, however the NYC one is by far better.

I've attempted multiple times to try out the NYC Sugarfish, but couldn't put myself to line up for 2+ hours. When I came back from LA, I decided I had to, just to compare the original and the one here. I ordered the Nozawa Trust Me which was $51 before tax (this is a no tip restaurant). Although the price is a bit hefty for the amount you get, it was well worth it. Now is it something that I'd have every week? Probably not, but the sushi here is not your standard sushi. It is comparable to the restaurants that you'd have to line up for in Japan. 

The sushi is served a few pieces at a time, and the reason for this is so that the temperature of the rice and fish is controlled. Some of the sushi pieces do not require the use of soy sauce, but this is something your server will inform you of. To be honest, you'd probably want to use it sparingly anyways. The fish is literally melt in your mouth. I did not have any piece where I disliked it. 

The hand rolls came at the end. I was super excited for the crab hand-roll since I had it at their sister restaurant, Kazunori (it was AMAZING)! I have to say though that kazunori made it better. The only downside to this review is: 1) I waited two hours for a 35 minute dinner 2) I wasn't full.

This place has a long wait time but the sushi is seriously high quality. I would ,however, not wait more than an hour for this place. I got the trust me omakase and for that price, it's hard to fault them for anything. The only thing I can nitpick on was one of the sushi had too much sauce and the rice was falling apart before it got on my plate. The sushi was still delicious. You should definitely come during lunch time and try this place. I felt that it met the hype it generated and deserves better than the four star it has. Sorry for no pictures but you should eat the sushi as soon as it comes out.
This is my favorite sushi restaurant ever!!! I've had it in LA & New York. SUGARFISH never disappoints. I truly wish there was a location in Texas. The rice is amazing!!

What is with the hype about this restaurant? It's similar to other local sushi restaurants but other places you don't have to wait. You cant compare this place to traditional omakase places. Apple to oranges. Nigiri wasn't properly formed. Loosely balled overly vinegared rice topped with a slice of fish. Rice was chalk-like. We both ordered the Nozawa. After the first 6 pieces, for the first time in  my life I wished the meal was over... sorry. I really tried to like it especially for the price point. 

Not sure but probably all the hype and the wait time caused the disappointment. Won't be returning.
Great dining experience and even better food. I recommend eating there vs take out. That being said, take out uses to take over an hour but now only take 20-30 min at most.

This was my third time here. The wait is unbelievable, but that just shows you that this place is high in demand. Honestly, I would just do take out but that really defeats the purpose of Omakase, since you need to eat those right away. I would recommend coming here as soon as they open for lunch or come in an hour or hour and a half before they close, so you can get seated right away. Staff there are amazing and friendly, which is a huge plus. The sushi...man...one of the best I've had during the 2.5 yrs I've been in NYC. Definitely suited for its price point and the fish is so fresh. Basically melts in your mouth. Recommend this place 200%!

Just as good as the ones in LA!
Very good quality fish at very reasonable price.  I appreciate the simplicity of the menu and the Trust Me option at $33 is my default and is just the right portion for lunch.  What I especially love is their perfectly seasoned warm sushi rice. The nori is also fresh and crisp.  

I dare say it's even better than my other favorite, sushi Yasuda.
It's a no tipping restaurant, service is cordial and swift.
I only wish they have a reservation system.  Wait for weekday lunch is 30-45minutes.  So build in wait time and get ready for some fresh taste of the sea.

Oh, do sign up for a free bday meal once you ate there twice.

I rarely eat sushi so I'm no sushi expert. But I rarely eat it bc I usually don't like the texture or taste (maybe the sushi I ate wasn't fresh enough). However I came here bc one of my friends really wanted to go. We arrived at around 7:15 on a Friday night. We were given a 2.5-3 hour wait. We had some drinks in the cellar at the beechers place nearby. At about 9:45 we were seated. 

It's not the super best sushi ever. But for the price it was pretty amazing. The waiters were nice and helpful. Initially I thought the restaurant was too dark but surprisingly I could still see what I was eating. As I'm writing this review I'm craving the sushi and planning when I would return. 

Overall, despite the wait I would go back bc the price is pretty sweet for all of the yummy sushi

3.5 stars. Is this place all hype? Not exactly. My friends and I came here to celebrate a birthday. We were all there at 6pm on a weeknight and expected that there would be a wait, maybe an hour? 2 hours later, we were open to sitting a little bit closer together at a table meant for 6. It's a very cozy space regardless, seating is only on the 1st floor as the second floor is more of a lounge area with bathrooms toward the middle/back; it's probably more comfortable to wait upstairs. Since we had so much time, we pretty much knew what we were ordering the moment we sat down: Trust Me, Nozawa and the Don't Think, Just Eat (anniversary menu).

In terms of quality, the fish was fresh. Although, I felt some of the pairings in terms of sauces or toppings took away from the sushi itself. I personally like salmon the most, but here it is served with sesame sprinkled on top, which can be overpowering. The sushi rice was also falling apart constantly, even the ones w/out sauce. The hand rolls were pretty good, but I wasn't a fan of the crab one, just too creamy? My favorite was probably the tuna sashimi, just perfect. They do a to-go option, which might just be a better option if you don't want the long wait. This place is good considering its price point, but I'd say it's worth a 45 min. wait, tops.

Side note: We ordered iced green tea all around and they were different shades of green, from dark to almost clear (like water). We brought it to our waiter's attention and he thought it was water at first, but was quick to swap them out to have some consistency in tea/color. The staff here is very quick and efficient!

This place opened nearly two years ago! The hostess and manager are incredibly rude and condescending. 

This place is a chain restaurant and there's no reason to treat it and customers like it's the hottest spot in manhattan. 

Suggest the manager and the wait girl lose the attitude and learn what hospitality means. 


Fish is sub par at best. 

Suggest they lose the attitude.

very disappointed. some pieces are drenched in soy sauce. rice is too sweet. rice falls apart too easily. save your money. this restaurant is for rich white yuppies who don't know what real sushi is. absolute f'ing shitshow

Came here with a friend on a Sunday night. Waited about 40 mins for a table. Ordered a Trust Me and a Nozawa Trust Me. Everything was very fresh and tasty. The only complaint is the sauce overpowered the fish in a couple of sushi.  But it was a great price for the quality and quantity.

The fish was decent quality, but the rice was mushy, hot, and too vinegar-y. I was pretty surprised at how that made it out of the kitchen, given what I've heard about their standard of quality. The service was quick and very friendly.
Great sushi and love their menu. Rice is well seasoned and dish melts in your mouth. Highly recommends.

I know I know, the LA location is better.... 

On this occasion, no!! We had an amazing meal and opted for the "don't think, just eat" -- and thankfully the menu title lived up to its name!! 

The hand rolls were some of the best and the sushi was incredible!! The fatty tuna was the star as it literally melted in my mouth! Service is top notch!! Service is included in the price with tipping made impossible. 

As with all trendy places, the line was horrible! We debated if we should stay but fortunately the two bottles of sake we ingested made that our wait time fly.... ok not true, but numbed our senses.... 

Overall, I'm a fan -- I will be back but maybe on a Monday when the wait could be shorter??!

The first time I experienced Sugarfish was in LA when I was 16 or 17. I've been dreaming about it ever since. When this NY location opened, I was a little wary because I didn't think it'd be as fresh and because, in true New Yorker fashion, I despise waiting. I've been a handful of times now and I wish I could say that it isn't worth the wait so that less of y'all would try to go!! I definitely try to time my visits to keep the wait under an hour and it's worked thus far, but honestly I'd wait for hours--just bring a little snack and good conversation. Must(!!) have: blue crab roll and luckily it comes with all of the "trust me" options. Yeah yeah we all have trust issues but truly, TRUST ME on this one!! In the words of my younger sibling (15) who has extremely discerning tastebuds, "this is it, chief."

Melt in your mouth sushi, which respects tradition, while adding a unique, modern twist. 
They have set menus for every occasion - We went for the "Don't Think Just Eat" one, which was really impressive, and only slightly more expensive than the "The Nozawa Trust Me" set menu. Definitely recommend the upgrade!
We had edamame as a starter, tuna and salmon sashimi marinated in citrus soy sauce, 2 sushi pieces of salmon, albacore, sea bass, Shrimp, yellowtail tuna and scallop each (each piece cooked/prepared in a different way), toro and lobster hand-rolls (same or better quality than Kazu Nori).
Overall the perfect sushi experience!

My favorite sushi spot in New York. They have great deals for omakase, although I recommend the Trust Me ($39). It comes with edamame, tuna sashimi, albacore sushi (2 pc), salmon sushi (2 pc), yellowtail sushi (2 piece, sea bass sushi (1 pc), sea break sushi (1 pc), toro hand roll, and crab hand roll. My favorites are the hand rolls, the salmon sushi, and the yellowtail. All the fish is so delicious and fresh. Food also comes very quickly, one dish after another, which is a plus. My only warning: line every time I have come has always been about a 2 hour wait and the restaurant does not take reservation. Service and staff is great. I have become a regular

Cucumber roll lacked flavor. Didn't order anything else :/ 

I waited for over an hour and the menu lacked vegetable options.


Disclaimer: I do not eat fish

Sugarfish - yes please. The sushi here is some of the best I've ever had - in my top 2. So super fresh. There's no reservations, be prepared to wait and have your whole party there when it's time to sit. Not a very big place, so it can be kind of loud and it contributes to wait times, but it's worth the wait. I've sat here a couple of times and have done take out quite a few times. It's been consistently good every time. If you're a sushi fan, you have to try this place.

This was, by far, the worst sushi experience we've ever had. I still can't believe how this place is this popular and have this much stars here! 

I'll tell you the whole experience.

We went there on a Saturday at 15:00 (they don't take reservations and we knew that before) the place was packed and we waited for 1,30 hrs to be seated.
When we seated a nice waiter came and told us that she'll be serving us tonight and then she left and never came back! Another waiter came and took orders, we ordered diet coke which tasted like water with sugar and our dishes started to come.

We started with edamame, seriously there was 10 pieces of edamame on the plate(I've been going to Asian restaurants since so many years and they bring edamame in huge bowls because it is the cheapest thing they sell!!!!!!) anyway, then the only good thing came; tuna sashimi, nothing special but not bad.
Then the sashimi and cut pieced sushis came. They smelled like kitchen counter and basically it was nothing special that you can make it at home!!!!! Just 2 ingredients; raw fish and steamed rice together! The food was seriously that bad that we went to dinner at Eataly right after there!

The other bad thing we experienced was that at our next table there were 2 couple having dinner, they were talking about how amazing the food are so they liked the place very much. while they were in the middle of dinner their 1 friend joined them and he was just talking to them while they were having food, not sharing their food or anything just sitting there. The manager came to their table and told them they can not expect such a thing and he should leave the table or he has to drink or eat something immediately. He was in such a rude manner we were shocked how unhospitable he was! They changed their mind about the place because of his attitude! 
Oh and one more thing!!!!!
By the time we were seated, suprisingly menu switched from lunch to dinner menu but they mistalenly give my husband the dinner menu and to me the lunch menu which led us finding out that they charge more money for the same dishes!

Seriously, I would recommend everyone and this place's chef to go to Zuma and have sushi there to learn about sushi and manners! The prices are similar! 

Worst sushi experience!

My favorite sushi restaurant in the city! The food is always on point whenever I go there to eat. The fish is always fresh and even if theres soy sauce on the table, I dont think you need it! It still tastes good on its own! Everyone at sugarfish are so nice and friendly! They always make you feel welcomed, and they check up on you to make sure everythings ok. Whenever my family or friends come to visit, I like to take them here and everyone loves it! I 100% recommend sugarfish to anyone who loves to eat sushi~

I got here at 9 on a Sunday night and had to wait almost an hour to get seated. Be sure that the entirety of your party is there or else you will not get seated. 

The atmosphere of this place was candlelit. Maybe they're trying to save costs on electricity or something. I ordered the cut crab roll, eel and salmon nigiri, and the toro hand roll. 

The cut crab roll was by far my favorite - it was very flavorful and deliciously made. 

Next up I enjoyed the salmon nigiri, presentation was beautiful. I will say the rice was a little hard to my memory. Not sure what the deal with that is. 

The eel roll didn't impress me that much and I generally don't have high expectations for eel. So I was surprised this didn't hold up to a much cheaper place. 

Not sure if I tasted anything in the toro roll. It was all just textury to me, like eating something that definitely melted into my mouth but had no taste. 

Another note I will make is that each individual dish comes out on its own. They didn't place two dishes on the table even once. And sometimes the dishes would come out in 20 minute intervals which was kind of annoying. My friend only ordered one dish and I preferred 4 so it was kinda awkward when one of us would be eating and the other would just be sitting there. But I guess it may be due to the fact that this is a no tip establishment.

The wait is bonkers but worth it! Sugarfish does not take reservations, so I recommend lunch or wait listing yourself 2-3 hours before you're ready for dinner. I personally enjoyed the wine bar across the street while waiting for availability. 

Rice is warm and fish is super fresh, just melts in your mouth. Crispy seaweed on the handrolls. Great value - fair price for high quality sushi. Expect to spend around $30-50 per person.

The ambiance is dark and trendy with great background music. I enjoy sitting at the sushi bar because I find the experience to be more intimate - great date spot. I also like to see the food that come out of the kitchen and add on to my order based on what looks most appetizing.  

Service is extremely efficient. Very friendly. Restaurant does not accept tips. 

Highly recommend! Also check out the sister restaurant for handroll sets, KazuNori. Wait time is typically not as long.

So I took a trip down from Virginia and heard so many things about SUGARFISH, that it being very popular in New York and California- so why not try it to see what the hype's about? Firstly the atmosphere was very modern as oppose to other sushi restaurants, not a bad thing but just interesting. Now onto the sushi, we decided to trust the chef and try the omakase. Our waitress was very informative in explaining the difference about SUGARFISH- that in which they pay special attention to the rice. The warm rice with the fresh fish gave the sushi such a melt in your mouth feel. Honestly just reading the other review, I was doubtful how sushi can be that good- but trust that SUGARFISH does that for you. Even the ginger slices and wasabi were of top quality! 

Dont let the price scare you away, trust that this is probably the best sushi Ive eaten my whole lifetime- and for sure on my list when I travel back to New York.

Sugarfish was decent but perhaps not worth the hype imo. They have about 3-4 preset omakase menu to choose from, each vary little from one another. We had the $45 omakase that consisted of  10 pieces of sushi and 2 hand rolls.

Of everything served, I personally enjoyed the two hand rolls the most. One was toro and the other was crab. While the sushi pieces were good, they did not always stay intact, and sometimes the sauce can be a bit much. 

The service was good, and I definitely liked the professionalism and the organization of the place. However if there is one thing that can be improved, I'd hope that the same dish at the same table could be served at the same time. My plates were always served before my friends and at first we weren't sure if they were just putting it on the same plate (first sushi dish had two of the same fish), or if his will be coming out soon. All throughout the 7 plate course meal was like this, where my food will come out before his. 

Overall though I'd say this place still deserves a 4 star for many of the reasons such as being delicious, relatively affordable for omakse, organized service, clean dining area etc. Although probably not too often, I do think Sugarfish is worth visiting with a fellow friend or date.

Without question, the best Sushi Omikase for the price in Manhattan. Don't waste $200-300 per person at Nakazawa, Shuko, Yasuda, Masa, Gari, O Ya, Kanoyama, Ginza Onodera, Amane, Zo, Uchu, 15 East and a few other great places. Sugarfish is as good or better than any of these Omikase superstars.

The difference is that it is 1/4 to 1/3 the price. In addition, the timing of your meal is a lot better at Sugarfish. The most amazing thing about Sugarfish is that there are no Japanese Sushi chefs. Have you watched some of these documentaries about Sushi chefs in Japan taking 30 years to learn their trade? Well. the Sushi chefs at Sugarfish are all Mexican, Black or White guys/girls off the streets of NYC. 

Sugarfish has taken away the secret mystique of how to become a "great" sushi chef. The answer is obviously the ingredients, the rice preparation, the rice temperature, the fish preparation, and some other Nozawa secrets. Try Sugarfish and you will never waste your money again at some of these other somewhat ripoff sushi joints.

Beautiful space 
We had lunch there & if you value the great quality I won't recommend nor I won't go back there 
They name it beautifully with Japanese but it is just another franchise with fancy deco but mediocre sushi

Excellent place to have lunch on a weekday! Been here twice, and both times have excellent! 

This is basically a streamlined omakase place.

Haven't been here for dinner.... well, cuz... everyone says the wait times are ridiculous! 

My wife and I had the "trust me" course, I had a cola.  All included was $75, which is dirt cheap for what you get.
This place is UNREAL. Tuna literally melted in my mouth. Crab roll was phenomenal. Honestly, one of the best food experiences I've had.

Melt in your mouth, delicious sushi. The stars were the yellowtail, albacore, and salmon. I've been to Nobu, Tanoshi, and Sushi of Gari...and I think Sugarfish exceeded all 3 in terms of lower price point for extremely high quality fish. One star less because of the 2+ hour wait and no reservations, but part of me appreciates it because it gives everyone a fair chance to check this place out and to be honest, worth the wait (especially if you grab drinks).

Where to begin. I went at 2pm on a holiday weekend Saturday, so there was barely a wait, which was nice. I went to the bathroom upstairs, where there was a cloud of smoke - the whole second floor smelled very strongly of marijuana. This should have been the first indication that something was up with this place. 

After about 15 minutes I was seated at the counter. I ordered the "Trust Me" (regular size set) and the large scallop special. The server seemed very conscientious about food allergies. So far so good...and then the food started to arrive.

My two issues with the food were 1) the rice is really sweet, soggy and mushy and 2) the fish, while fresh, was inconsistently either room temperature (as it should be) or ice cold (uh, no).

When I asked why the rice was soggy, I was told that it's the chef's stylistic choice to use "warm and loose rice". A manager (I think) came by to investigate and explain the chef's style, which was nice. But when I commented again about the soggy rice (see pic - note that the albacore tuna comes with sauce on it already and I did not add any of my own soy sauce) I was told "that's not soggy". Nice try, but kind of rude? The manager said that most people use their hands to scoop up each piece, but I didn't really feel like getting sticky sauce all over my hands...the pics I have posted speak for themselves.

The meat on the salmon and scallop sushi tasted very good - room temperature. The rice is way too sweet for my taste. The rest (albacore, sea bass, yellowtail, tuna and salmon hand rolls) were fresh and beautiful to look at but so cold that I couldn't taste anything through my brain freeze.

I am not sure what the hype is about this place but as "cheap" as my lunch was at $45, I'd rather eat sushi elsewhere. At least the hot green tea was good.

By far the best sushi place I've ever been to in Manhattan! If you haven't tried it I highly recommend the Nozawa Trust Me Lite. There's plenty of different options and the food is well prepared and so tasty. It is a bit pricy with little food but it is definitely worth it! The employees are extremely nice and be sure to warn you about the food and possible allergies before you eat.
I mean, REALLY?! Just the best sushi I have had anywhere on the planet. It defies the taste buds. GO! as often as you can.

The wait is real. Not sure what the key is to dining at an optimal time.. 

We weren't too hungry so we got the trust me and I was actually really full by the end of the meal. The salmon was sooo good. I would have ordered it a la carte if I had any more space in me. However, the tuna and the yellowtail was actually pretty fishy, which was quite ironic considering their little blurb on the side of the menu. Still, we enjoyed our meal. 

If there's one thing that I would have changed would be the timing. I think the reason why I was so full was because they kept on bringing the next dish out too fast! Especially when they recommend eating the handrolls immediately.

Fancy, upscale place to have lunch! I was visiting NYC and came here with a friend about 10-15 minutes after opening on a Friday and was seated right away. However, pretty much right after we got seated, lots of people came in, so make sure to come right at opening, or else be prepared to wait.

I got the Trust Me, and my friend got the Nozawa Trust Me. So if you don't know and haven't seen the other reviews, they serve it one dish at a time. It was cool, since even though the Nozawa had more items, they made it so that they doubled up some stuff for my friend's dish so I wouldn't have to awkwardly sit and stare at him eat without anything myself. 

All of the sushi and fish were fresh and had great flavor. I enjoyed the salmon sushi and hand rolls the most. Only downside is that it's quite pricy for the portion. We were both still pretty hungry after the meal. Don't expect to be full, but come here to enjoy a nice meal in a classy atmosphere.

There can be a serious wait, but that is a good thing as it means the food is good.  It is simple enough to order from the Trust Mes.  I ordered the Trust me and my friend ordered Nozawa.  The standout rolls to me were spicy shrimp and seabream.  I wasnt that thrilled with the crabmeat hand roll.  It was just ok. I actually think the prices are really good compared to some other places I have been that do not have such a variety of maki, sushi, and sashimi in a platter.  This place offers a good variety for one price.

Love this place! I always go on a weekday so there's never a long wait! The sushi is always so fresh and the warm rice just melts in your mouth. My favorite is the crab and toro hand rolls. Simple but tasty. I usually order the Trust me for $33 during lunch which includes the two rolls and a few sushi pcs of the day. It's just the right amount of food. I enjoy sitting at the bar. They bring the sushi and hand rolls straight from the kitchen. Service is always quick and servers are attentive and friendly. Tip is already included in the menu prices. This is definitely a good spot for quick delicious quality sushi.

Really great place! The food was amazing and the service was even better. We went with the Trust Me option and  everything was delicious and brought out in a timely manner. Definitely recommend to anyone that loves sushi.

It's such a shame that the management at SUGARFISH: Flatiron was so incompetent, as my food was absolutely stunning.

However, not warning guests of a problem with your giftcard retrieval system before they sit down, then saying there is nothing you can do, and then fighting kicking and screaming to even discount $15 off a check is the worst service I have ever received in an nyc restaurant. 

After offering to leave my gift card and cc information for any remaining charges they refused and truly treated us with disrespect and hostility. 

The management team should be ashamed of themselves as EVERY other part of our experience was lovely. However, I will never be recommending or frequenting this place again.

If I could I'd give this place no stars. They went from having someone who could not wait to come back, to someone who never wants to set foot on their property ever again.

Great experience. Def worth the wait. The place is really cool and laid back. Highly
recommended.

This is one of the best deals for omakase in New York City! The most expensive tasting (The Nozawa Trust Me) is only $45!! The trade off is you cannot make reservations in advance and the wait times tend to be 1.5+ hours long...That being said, they do take your cell number so you can put your name down and go to a nearby bar or coffeeshop.

The quality of the fish here is excellent. It is also a relatively wide selection of different types for the price. My only complaint is that the rice is a little too wet, so the sushi tends to fall apart in your hand if you don't eat it immediately. 

The sake is also great! We took a recommendation from our waiter and had the one in the pretty blue bottle (don't remember the name).

The ambiance is buzzy and dark. Great for any occasion - can be upscale or casual but I would say it is more on the casual side.

I've been here a few times and will definitely be coming again!

well pour some sugarfish on me, cause this place is worth the hype! 

as you may already know they don't take reservations, so i came in around 5:30 on a saturday hoping to beat the rush. the waiting area was empty and i went right up to the desk and gave my name and number to the sweet hostess. I was quoted about an hour wait for 2 people, and as i was leaving sure enough there was a line forming out the door. i guess i recommend coming in early if you can! 

the wait ended up being only 45 minutes (you can check your place in line from your phone and they text you when you're close to the top of the waitlist) 

i got the trust me and my bf got the nozawa trust me (i'm not a fan of raw scallop which was the daily special that comes with the nozawa version) and we also got an order each of the unagi roll and sweet shrimp roll. sadly for the bf they were out of the uni. 

we were so impressed! i thought the fish quality compares with some of the best omakases in the city. and i loved the sushi rice, i don't know why i noticed it so much but it was warm and complemented the fish perfectly. 

hard to pick a favorite dish, because we loved them all, but the toro hand roll, albacore, and unagi rolls were the highlights for me. i definitely recommend ordering one of the sets, rather than a la carte. 

hostesses and waiters were super nice too, they never made us feel rushed even with growing mob at the front of the restaurant. can't wait to come back!

I would say the best way to describe this place is it is the Japanese of dung Tai Fung where the quality isn't omg top notch but for the price you pay on how they can be consistent at ANY location it's pretty impressive.

I got the middle pre set which was about $33 before tax you get 2 hand rolls and 6 sushi pieces total of 9 pieces with edamame to start off with then tuna in house made ponzu sauce.

Bathroom is clean 2 of them single stall uni sex 

We can exactly when they open and there is a wait already so I say come early and try to avoid lunch rush.
Great place for sushi. They had three preselected sushi menus based on how much you wanted to eat. I like the atmosphere its great for lunch. Will go again.

After putting our name down on Friday at 7 pm, there was an estimated wait for 3 hours. Hungry, we walked to Big Daddy's around the corner. We leisurely shared a shake, burger and tots while watching our spot in line at SUGARFISH advance on No Wait. We figured that was the appropriate amount of food to digest before omakase.
When we returned to SUGARFISH, we were curious but not starved. In this new state, we were more critical. In contrast to other sushi places, this place is dimly lit and there is little fan fair. No little warm towels, tea, or sushi chefs on display. The fish is, indeed, fresh.  The portions generous with each fish coming in pairs. We found the rice and ponzu sweeter. 

The service is very friendly. One waitress brought a plate of sushi which was already brought. Though I wanted it sent back (being full after a prior shake and burger), I was told that it's ours once it hit the table.

The hype is real. We came on MLK Monday (1/21/19) at 1:30pm and was told we were second on the wait list with a 30 minute wait time. It was also 9 degrees out that day. I debated on the rating for a long time and decided to go with 3 stars...

Positives -
Reasonable prices for omakase, incredibly fresh quality, quick service and cozy ambiance. My favorites are the salmon and scallop (even with hair/fuzz on it, see photo)

Negatives -
The wait time is ridiculous, no sushi is worth the usual 2-3 hours wait. The inconsistent timing of when food was brought out bothered me, my friend and I both ordered The Nozawa Trust Me and either she had to wait or I waited. A few of the pieces were dosed in sauce which took away the freshness of the fish, some of the rice also fell apart even without sauce. Here comes to the good part.. there was a piece of mystery hair or fuzz on my scallop!!! I had to send it back for a new plate, the waitress simply apologized and moved on with her day.
Waited 2 hours to get basic service and basic sushi. For all the hype, i promise you it's not worth it, way better sushi spots in New York.

Get the Trust Me or Nozawa! And recently new on their menu, if you're hungry "Don't Think, Just Eat" is worth every dime.

Worth the wait for this amazing sushi. Like nothing you've had before. Very transparent, no tipping, and very courteous staff. The manager, Daniel, always goes out of his way to be welcoming and making suggestions. Leave your name a few hours before you want to dine.

Even though I generally prefer red wines, the white wine selection is superb. One of the best sushi spots in NYC. Excited for a new location to open up!
I've been here twice and had a great experience with chef's selection. Amazing sushi bar, If you have patience to wait 3 hours on the line.

I've been wanting to try Sugarfish forever and I'm glad I finally got the chance to. I thought it was a little overhyped but still so amazing. I don't think this deserves any less than 5 stars. 

We got the Trust Me and the Nozawa Trust Me. They are served Omakase style. They had the same amount of plates but the Nozawa (approx. $20 more than Trust Me) had I believe 4 more pieces of Nigiri. The Nozawa special was 2 pieces of scallop (another standout). 

Absolutely amazing flavors! Honestly the added sauces didn't overpower any of the fish for me. I could just appreciate and taste the simple, fresh flavor of fish. 

Edamame, Tuna ponzu dish, 2 plates of nigiri, and 2 hand rolls. Everything was good. Both the toro and the blue crab hand roll, oh my goodness were out of this world amazing. I would go back just for the hand rolls. Nigiri is amazing of course, but it wasn't too special to me becauset they were on par with many other good sushi restaurants.

This place has warm loosely packed rice, so it does fall apart easily! But it's really good so worth it. They say don't dip the fish already sauced into soy sauce. 

We came around 4:40pm and there was already a huge line. You have to be present when they call you for your turn. We waited upstairs in the waiting area but it wasn't too bad. Once we were seated, the plates came pretty quickly and we finished in less than an hour. There is a short wait between each plate. 

Overall, experience amazing and a must try. Pretty good price for omakase-style sushi in NYC. Not every piece will blow your mind, but overall the whole meal is incredible. (Also they print on to receipt not to tip because it's likely already included).
If you come prepared to wait it's well worth it. The fish is super fresh and the rice delicious. The value is great (tip included).

Absolutely amazing! Have been here a few times now and it is consistently delicious. I would highly recommend one of the prefix choices rather than a la carte. Both the Trust Me and the Nozawa's are a perfect amount of food and definitely satisfying. All of the fish is incredibly fresh and melts in your mouth. The sushi pieces are simple yet powerful in flavor. My favorite's are the salmon sushi and the crab hand roll. 
Service is great, pretty fast considering how full it usually is inside. They don't take reservations so I would recommend trying to get there earlier for dinner if possible/be prepared to have to wait a bit. Overall, an amazing place to go to and I will be back!

Giving Sugarfish four stars because sometimes I absolutely love it and sometimes I'm more eh on the experience (and takeout/delivery is more of a three-star situation). Because I live three blocks away, I'm a frequent visitor and sometimes a little bored by the standard Trust Me that I usually order. Fast forward to this Sunday when I decided to change it up with the mysteriously named "Don't Ask. Just Eat." I couldn't help myself though and had to ask what I was in for. It consists of edamame, 12 pieces of nigiri, two sashimis and two handrolls for a VERY reasonable $63. I thought I could handle anything (and fancy myself an amateur Adam Richman of Man v. Food) but about 2/3 of the way through I was struggling to find room in my tummy. Luckily the fish was so delicious, consisting of all your favorites with varying preparations, that I was able to power through. Though I had to literally ROLL (haha, sushi pun) myself out the door, I will definitely be back for this treat the next time I'm feeling ravenous.

SugarFish By Sushi Nozawa is one of the best places to try affordable omakase with the quality on par to many 4-5 star Japanese restaurants. Sugarfish is an LA-based restaurant with several locations throughout California, and this NYC location is the only location outside of LA. Each serving is brought out individually. We were told to eat each sampling quickly and not to dip any plates that come with sauce into the soy sauce -- definitely, the most favorite place to get non-sushi roll place Japanese food. My GF got the Trust Me, and I got the Nozawa Trust Me. Tbh, my food does not justify the $12 premium since the only difference between mine and her were the NZ Sea Beam sushi and the raw scallops. The scallops were really delicious. I also like the Crab Handroll. There is no reservation, so it is a first come first serve restaurant. No, you cannot leave your telephone number. You can wait upstairs and order a drink while one of the servers downstairs calls your name. Lastly, you do not need to tip, so feel free to order as much food as you want -- great service, nice interior, and very delicious tasting that you will not regret.

Are you 14 and want work?   Do you talk to loud and can't communicate?  Is your perception of time and space totally incoherent?  We have a job for you at SUGARFISH!  You can greet our valued customers on the way in, and thank them in the way out.  It may be helpful to hire hosts at the front desk that can at least fake professionalism.  #theexperiencestartsonthewayin

Simply fantastic. Can not go wrong with the Trust Me. Always reliable for an amazing experience. Takeout quality is also fantastic. Be sure to put name in advance since they don't take reservations and it fills up fast.

The best sushi ever! We don't have any of these in SF, so every time I visit LA or NYC I have to get my fix. Last visit to NYC we stopped by and the wait was over 2 hours, so we had to give it a miss. Made sure to get there around opening time on Saturday and were seated straight away. We had the trust me and as usual it was amazing and great value for money. Only wish I could go here more often.

Sugarfish prides itself on fresh fish that is never fishy. Preparation is simple and the quality of the fish is the focal point here. I have eaten Omakase all over the city and some of the most expensive places around and I can confidently say that the quality of fish at Sugarfish is as good as anywhere, for a fraction of the price. They are beyond consistent and I have never had a bad meal there. The pieces of fish are soft, buttery, never fishy and just everything you could want from simple pieces of sushi. It's worth the wait and always A+

Bravo!

Minus one star because of the reservation situation, but if you can put in your name and come back, this is one of the best Japanese tasting menus in the city. The fish is always beyond fresh. I always go with the Trust Me menu so I get the Crab Hand Roll, which is one of the best courses. The tuna sashimi is always up there in terms of best dishes, although they're all great. My tricks for getting in is going for lunch and by myself so I can get seated quicker. They also give you a free Trust Me meal on your birthday if you eat there two times during the year and fill out the card after your dinner. Good luck!

It's really not worth the 2.5 to 3hrs wait. The food ain't that good. Everytime I come here the wait was 2.5 to 3hrs and everyone else were willing to wait so I thought this must be good! Well, it was not. 

I first came here on 1/30/19, a Wednesday at 7pm. I was told that the wait would be 2.5 to 3hrs. I put my name in because most places are actually faster than the time they give you. Well, I got a text notification 2.5hrs later. Canceled and came back on 2/1/19, a friday at 6:30pm. This time I actually waited the 2.5 to 3hrs.

Pros:
1) Its cheap. $52 for 12pcs of sushi, 2 handrolls, an edamame, and a tuna sashimi. 
2) Better seaweed than what Kazunori | The original Handroll Bar has to offer. Easier to bite and chew. 
3) Scallops were creamy! I could eat 10 of these at once. 

Cons: 
1) The albacore sushi was drenched in super sour sauce, I don't know what the sauce was but it was super sour. 
2) The rice fell apart when I picked up the piece of sushi with my fingers.
3) The rice was still warm. Good sushi rice is not supposed to be warm. 
4) The right way to eat sushi is to actually flip it upside down, fish facing bottom, and eat it in one bite. I can't do that with the sushi at Sugarfish because the fish would've dropped. 
5) Too much sauce on the Sea Bass sushi. 
6) Basically too much sauce on every piece of sushi that they decided to put sauce on. The rice were drown in sauce!
7) 2.5 to 3hrs wait 
8) Everything was pre-made. They just put it on a plate and give it to us. 

I wish I didn't order the Nozawa Trust Me menu and just order a la cartes instead. The food was not worth the wait, and Sugarfish is not a place I would be proud to tell my sushi enthusiast friends about, as they would always ask me where I went for sushi.
