Also, there was not a single Asian chef in their kitchen.

Have been here a number of times. As the restaurant has become more popular, it has become increasingly poorly run. For example last night my party of four put our names down on the waitlist at 5:57pm for a dinner table. We were told it'd be a 2 hour wait - which was fine since this is a normal wait time on a Friday night for a non reservation restaurant. So we left and returned to the restaurant at 8pm. We weren't seated until 10pm!!! Which means we spent 2 hours waiting in their bare upstairs waiting area. We ordered (expensive!) wine and beer at the suggestion of the receptionists but they would not serve any food outside of the main dining area. So we ended up very buzzed and were starving! I was flabbergasted - a four hour wait for a table!!! It was awful - by the time we were seated we were ravenous and miserable. Would not recommend! We'd have been better off going anyplace else. The appeal of sugar fish to me until now has been value - quality at a low price. But I'd rather just pay more for better service and less of a wait. Horrible. Won't be back.

I'm not someone who likes to wait a long time for food, especially when there are so many other options available, but Sugarfish was worth the wait.  The food is absolutely amazing!  If it were possible to make a reservation and avoid waiting a couple hours, I would go more often.

High quality sushi and good prices! The wait is long but they do a great carry out that easy and quick. Takeout comes in lovely boxes, with all the sauces marked and great instructions. Overall if you love good, fresh sushi you will love SUGARFISH!
Very nice & generous portion. Always a great sushi spot that won't break the bank. The albacore is to die for as always & great to go packaging
If you want a unique taste of sushi this is your place to go. Ambience is kind of dark and cozy and sushi is delicious. If you're craving sushi this is the place to go

So much hype around SUGARFISH and it just didn't live up to it for me. I think that it is great that the fish is fresh and the chef is picky in terms of what they are serving their guests. It makes so much sense, but I was super bummed out to wait (just an hour because we came here at 4 PM on a Saturday) and there was no uni on the menu. I literally craved for unit that very day and decided to give SUGARFISH a try since it was an awkward hour. 

I will applaud the restaurant on the ponzu sauce that they create which is a perfect blend and really enhances the taste of the fish that it is paired with. I will also say though, that it is overpowering when there was too much thrown on the sushi so the chef should really watch their hands on that pour. 

The set menus are the perfect share for everyone to have a piece of sushi of each fish and adding on two rolls will give you an equal split of every item. The price is affordable compared to omakase, but I'll stick to omakase and Kazunori (the sister bar for handrolls) because the handroll was the only thing that really had me excited here.

I have gone to Sugarfish 3 times now, and it is always very solid! I usually get the Trust Me ($40 for dinner, $33 for lunch). Everything is extremely fresh. The wait during the evening can be up to 2 hours, and up to an hour during lunch. Service can seem very rushed since it gets busy; they sometimes bring out the next plate before I'm done eating.
It's was such a great experience. The service, the food was just perfect. We came at 2:20pm on a weekday and had to wait about 15 min to be seated. At 3pm there was no wait at all

Okay, let's start off by acknowledging​ that the hubby and I are sushi​ snobs. 

S-U-S-H-I   S-N-O-B-S. Sushi snobs.

Now that we got that out of the way, Sugarfish is a nice value for the price. If you want fresh sushi that sticks its small toe into the world of Sushi of Gari with sauce pairings​ you will be quite happy here. 

From what I understand, there can be an extremely long line. We were lucky and didn't have to wait as we were outside at 11:10 am for lunch.

They immediately put a cold plate with edamame in front of you when you sit down. We ordered the Nozawa Trust Me menu for $45 per person. 

What surprised me was that they didn't have any uni on the menu or sake by the glass. Also, what surprised me is that they didn't employ any real sushi chefs. The kitchen staff was a lovely bunch of young men and women who were working very hard. 

They were not sushi chefs. Not even a little bit. 

That being said, they did a good job of preparing good sushi. The ponzu sauce was very good and the sushi rice was tasty but the nigiri fell apart when you ate it. The rice wasn't tightly packed and completely fell away from the fish no matter how you tried to eat it. A real sushi chef would have been horrified.

Before you come for me, we have eaten at Sushi Nakazawa, Sushi of Gari and Masa (3 times if you count our visit to Bar Masa). It is safe to say that the hubby and I are sushi connoisseurs (aka snobs).

The fish was very fresh and tasty, the service was good if a bit too speedy. In the end, we had a lovely lunch. 

That being said, if you have had the privilege​ of dining at one of the establishments mentioned above, this place is only worthy of lunch, not dinner.

NO WHERE COMPARES. POINT BLANK. Best sushi I've ever had in my life !! I've been to the location in California many times before coming to this one and I'm so happy there is one in NY where I live. I commute from Long Island just to eat here. Warm rice with fresh fish It is indescribable!! It just melts. Definitely get the trust me, sweet shrimp, bay scallops and lobster cut roll! A MUST go!

I've been here on multiple occasions, and I have to say that it's very inconsistent, i.e. very hit or miss. The fish is without a doubt very fresh every time. The last few times I've come here the rice is undercooked and the servers were rushing my party out as we were finishing our last set.

Willing to give it another try, but going to try a couple other spots before doubling back
Best sushi ive ever had! The "Trust Me" special was amazing and fairly priced for NYC. 5 stars highly recommend

The long wait isn't worth it.

They over-season the sushi rice leaving a tangy pungent flavor that can overwhelm mild fish rather than compliment it.  Fish quality, though, is really good.  They have the regulars, but also the premium fish only the better sushi restaurants can get (and with a name like nozawa attached, of course you can expect high quality).

I came here many times when it first opened because it is good value for what types of fish you get, but you are better off going to the new $50 omakase spots that are popping up all over.

Make sure to put your name down to get credit for your birthday meal! You need to visit twice to qualify for a free meal on your birthday (though I'm not sure I personally would want to spend my birthday here, you never know).

I get delivery from Sugarfish all the time and it NEVER disappoints! Everything on the menu is amazing. My usual order is a split roll of yellowtail and crab, each of which are absolutely delicious. Once you've had Sugarfish (or their sister restaurant, Kazunori), you'll never want to eat anybody else's sushi ever again. Seriously!

Decent sushi but not worth having to deal with the pathetic host. Told us the wait was 1 hour. we waited 1:45 and we still could not get a table. Dozens of other guests where seated before us. Plenty of better sushi with great service in NY.

Came for a company lunch. Wait for four people was about 30 minutes on a Wednesday a little after noon. We all ordered the Omakase. I got the Trust Me. The food was absolutely phenomenal, and I'm very particular about my sushi. This fish is melt in your mouth good. The service was just okay. The courses are brought out one by one, and at one point, they brought me another table's next course. They let me keep the food because it was their mistake and they didn't charge us for that, but just a hiccup in the experience as I felt I had to eat something I didn't order very quickly to make room on the table for my actual food. Once the courses had been dropped off, no one really followed up with us to see if we needed anything or how the food was. Again, not a huge deal but not an amazing experience service wise. The food was very good for the price, I think $35 for my 4 course Omakase, and tip is included.

This is one of the more affordable places if you want good omakase. They have three types at three different prices that correspond to different amounts of food. They also have menu items a la carte if you prefer that instead. I got the Nozawa Trust Me during lunch, which was the most expensive at $45. This is a no tipping restaurant so you don't have to worry about that. I thought that the food was pretty good, especially the hand rolls, which were my favorite. The Nozawa had two hand rolls: toro and crab. The sushi and sashimi were very fresh and good too, though the rice was sometimes hard to pick up because it was very soft, especially if there was a sauce. The atmosphere and lighting of the restaurant is good, though it can get a bit loud with everyone talking. It also took longer than I expected for the food to come out, though that is also likely due to the amount of people inside. If you eat here, prepare to spend at least $25-$30 and at least an hour. This place is also first come first serve for full parties so come ready.

When we arrived, I made eye contact with one of the servers at the counter and she ignored me and proceeded to talk to her co-workers and work on the computer. That's fine because she had something to do but when we walked up to the counter, none of the other 2 people even acknowledged us. The first girl noticed and then helped us get seated. 

We ordered the trust me for $40. The sashimi tuna was alright but the sauce was overwhelming. The other pieces of sushi has cold fish which I've never experienced at other omakase restaurants. The rice would fall apart. Each piece seemed to be drowned in sauce so much so that the taste of the fish wasn't there. The crab handroll tasted like crab meat with mayo which wasn't what I was hoping for. Another thing that I thought was weird was that towards the middle of the course, I was served my plate of sushi first and then a few minutes later, my boyfriend got his plate. We both got our plates at the same time in the beginning of service so that as strange. 

I wouldn't recommend Sugarfish for omakase because there are other places that do a decent omakase for $50. If you're really willing to splurge on the experience, sushi nakazawa is the best omakase I've ever had and is worth everything.

Co-worker highly recommended this place. Had 'Trust Me' at a bar table. 

Taste: Great
Portion: Ok
Service: So so
Location: Great
Price: Ok

As a sushi lover, taste was Great. However it was too loud to enjoy my food. Whole time I couldn't hear what my friend was saying even though he was seating right next to me. Music was too loud, making people to talk louder. Unless its the concept, bit quiet music will be better? I'm hoping to try again at the table instead of the bar.

UPDATE : they were very active in contacting me about this and have apologized. Great customer service and assured me they would make sure to let the kitchen know. 

Have been here and ordered delivery multiple times. While the wait is annoying the food is always relatively good so worth it. Not anymore. I ordered delivery off of postmates today and found a dark corse hair intertwined in my rice (normally I give benefit of the doubt, but clearly not mine). Sorry but for sushi at this price this is not what I expect to find. Truly grossed out and now I guess I'm eating Pringle's for lunch.

After hearing so many good things about Sugarfish, I decided to stop by and try the Trust Me. I came here at an odd time (4 PM or so) alone on a weekday, so I did not have to wait for a seat by the bar.

I just don't get the hype around this restaurant. I don't know if it was just this day/time or other circumstances, but I wasn't impressed by the food here. Yes, the food was all fresh (as to be expected with sushi...), but the taste was just okay. There wasn't anything memorable about the Trust Me.

If you don't have much experience with (nicer) sushi, then this place might be a good place to eat for you. The food here isn't bad. It's just that I could get similar-quality sushi for less or better-quality sushi for the same price. Otherwise, I'd go with one of the many, many other sushi options in the city.
The food is GREAT, but we found a bone in our sushi and they didn't even discount our bill... at this price, that shouldn't happen.

Sugarfish undeniably offers one of the best omakase options in NYC. Not only do you get great value/quality for the price you pay, gratuity is also included in the price advertised on the menu. 

There are 4 different omakase options ranging from $33-$63. I personally think the $45 Nokzawa is the perfect amount and selection. Each plate is served as soon as it's prepared and the rice that's served on the sushi is always loosely packed and always served warm. I believe all these little things paired with fair prices is what makes SUGARFISH very popular.  With that said, reservations are not an option and wait times cant be up to 2 hours long. I highly advise to come during off hours. (Bet lunch and dinner).

Beer, sake, and wine are available. I highly recommend the nigori (unfiltered sake) for those that enjoy sweet/chilled milky sake. Cheers!

EXTRA EXTRA:
*Free street parking available after 7pm. 
*Servers politely decline any requests for additional sauces, rice, or salt.
Food was average and service is pretty bad I got to say...don't understand what the hype for this restaurant is?? There's better sushi in EV than this place.

Let me start off with saying that the freshness of the sushi and rolls were BOMB. They were great. The crunchy seaweed paper and warm rice really does make a difference. The fish cuts tasted fresh, and it's clearly very different from other sushi joints.

HOWEVER. $10 for two small pieces of sweet shrimp (literally one piece for me, the other for the bf) was just... not really worth it for me. Was it good? Yes. Was that worth $10? No, sorry. I could have gotten a shrimp tempura roll with the tail still at the end at the sushi place 3 blocks away.

The edamame was disappointing. It was $10 for what looked like 10 pieces, and it was cold. I've never had cold edamame... it's always hot at any place I go to. Maybe it's just their thing? Dont know. But I wont complain too much about it.

The spicy salmon tasted better than the spicy fatty tuna, in my opinion. It did melt in my mouth, but I felt like sauce was needed on the side. The menu states (and the waiter, too) that they dont serve sauce with your rolls or sushi. ...ok, fine. I guess the chefs want you to experience sushi/maki the way it's supposed to. BUT if after that first or second bite of whatever roll I got just isnt doing it for me, I feel like sauce should be an option available. I personally would have loved more spicy mayo or eel sauce on the side. But I'm sure if I begged for any sauce, it would have been like $5 extra. So I didnt bother trying.

The waiter did do a good job at explaining whatever we had questions about. But honestly, I wouldn't come back unless it's a special date night & if I dont mind spending a few extra bucks for that crunchy seaweed bite. The place felt like somewhere you take a date you're really into, or a place for an expensive girls night out, or maybe even a quick bite to eat if you got money to spend like that.

I'm a panko-sprinkled, -imitation crab, -chopped up spicy mayo with tuna, -shrimp tempura tail left on the roll, -warm edamame- type of person.

If you scrolled to the bottom to find out what's the end point:

Yeah they're good, if you dont mind spending. But no, I wouldnt wanna be a regular here just because it is pricey.

Probably one of the best sushi experiences I have ever had in my life. It's a pain to be able to book a spot to eat here because they don't take reservations and you literally have to go to the restaurant and put yourself on the waiting list which will take a minimum of 90 minutes on a weekend. Holidays could take up to 3 hours and even more depending on what kind of holiday it is. But it's definitely worth the hassle.

I came here on a Sunday with 5 other friends around 2pm and the wait was about an hour so we just walked around Union Square to kill time until we got a text notification that we were about to be up in the queue. We were seated promptly after checking in with the hostess and the great experience begun.

I got the Nozawa Trust Me combo where I got to have a slew of sushi, rolls, and sashimi. They are all prepared as fresh as they can be, each bite with such amazing flavor and taste. You can tell the quality is not to be messed around. You get one sashimi plate, five various sushi rolls, and two hand rolls along with a plate of edamame. Each is served as soon as they are made so you'll get served six different plates before you're fully done with the experience. All of this costed 49$ including tax and tip.

The service is exceptional. They break down how they roll, all of the options on the menu, and clarify menu options such as the difference between the select combo options. It is printed on the menu that there is no tipping as it's priced into the menu already which I like. Overall, it's a very wonderful experience and will be back in the future when I find the waiting time not too long or just plan ahead that day.

I cannot believe I waited 90 minutes for just a spot for myself on a Tuesday from 6:15-7:15 and they still wanted me to wait another hour. I've eaten at SUGARFISH in LA so I know the food was good but holy shit, nothing is good enough to wait that long.

I wish they had given me any sort of update or estimate when I checked in. She definitely led me to believe it would be quick because I was alone.

Came here with my girlfriend for Valentine's Day, got there around 6pm there were no wait at all. We got to our tables and the servers explained to us the whole menu. The food here was one of the best sushi I've eaten around here. The rice comes out warm and perfect match for the fish. We have accidentally blow of the candles place in the middle of our tables, the servers took no time at all to light it back up. Over all the servers amazing. All the dishes comes out one at at time whenever you finish the dish before it.

Totally ridiculous: tried to order from them online -- they categorically refuse to take orders by phone -- and website just kept insisting 'this merchant is not available for pickup or delivery at this time.'  Don't waste time browsing their delicious-sounding menu because they don't actually want to sell you food!

This has been a regular spot for me since it hit the NYC scene. I go here every few months. Why? Let's start with affordable fresh fish. For $6 and some change you get fresh albacore that's brushed with the slightest of tangy yuzu. Sure, you can go ahead and get a $12 bento lunch special elsewhere, but once you taste fresh fish you wouldn't want to do that to yourself!

Their bay scallops are little pops of heaven in your mouth. And the crab handroll makes you feel as though you went crabbing for it yourself. 

I've also noticed how attentive they are in terms of customer service. One woman said she didn't have sesame seeds on her salmon and boom two fresh pieces out no questions. Another instance, I just had a conversation with my waiter and asked about his day, he saw I waited a bit for my 2 pieces...boom, comped! There's a reason why this place is making waves in the NYC restaurant scene where competition is stiff. I hope they venture to have warm dishes on their menu one day.

As for wait times, I am strategic. I either hit the times before or after the rush. And I've never had to wait more than 10 mins.

Great sushi!
I got the Nozawa trust me..
Start with tuna with ponzu sauce which i really enjoy.
The fish is very fresh. The rice is warm and tasty.
The best part is the special 2 pieces sushi which I got large scallop and also I like the crab handroll.
Overall is great food and the price is reasonable.
We will be back!

Highly recommend trying this place if you're a fan of sushi. We got here at 7pm on Tues night and waited 1.5 hours, but the second the actual sushi came around, I knew it was worth it. The warm rice, the sweet and tasty fish, the extreme attention to detail was greatly appreciated. Salmon with sesame seeds was unlike any other I've had. Super top quality fish. 

The $40 "trust me" omakase is definitely the way to go. Perfect amount of food, it comes with several sashimi dishes and some hand rolls, and gives you a taste of everything. We paired it with two bottles of $11 sake and had a great night. 

Only weird thing was that the edammame and some of the seafood within the hand rolls was cold. Other than that, everything (including service) was grade A perfect. I think they are a "tip included" establishment which is nice.

Both of my experiences at Sugarfish were off the charts foodwise. You should go to this restaurant with someone you know well and catch up before and/or after, because during this experience you'll want to focus on savoring each and every beautiful bite they present. I always sign up for the trust fall options and it's been worth it both times. They allow you to customize a bit--I wasn't crazy about the crab so I was able to switch it out for salmon. 
Cons: You'll always wait at least a little bit and the tables are super tight. I considered not even noting these two because, well, it's NYC and what do you expect, right?

The fact that the sushi rice is warm is such a game changer! Just elevated sushi to a whole new level! Loved the fact that a menu was already set in place and I did not need to think. Course after course my group was pleased with the deliciousness we received.

Came here today to celebrate my husband bday with our dear friend. We got the "trust me" and "don't think just eat" dinner set. Everything came out as they make it. Very different from other sushi restaurants where everything comes out all at once. At sugar fish every plate come out as they prepare it and it's super fresh. The rice was still warm! And the sushi just melts in your mouth. I would definitely go back again. It wasn't that bad of a wait but there's still a wait. Our wait time was close to 40 minutes but we were catching up and talking so the time went by pretty fast. Might be better to go on a weekday instead of a weekend. Especially on a holiday weekend.
Food was more than excellent. Service was decent. I wish they had more drink options. You definitely have to order a lot to get full though but it's worth it.

At first I thought this place was just a hype and a trend but after trying their sushi, I now understand why everyone is so obsessed. Their sushi is the best I've ever had. It's super fresh and made right there at the bar and served as soon as it is made. Everything is SO good and melts in your mouth! 
I would definitely recommend that you try this place at least once if you are a sushi lover (and love Raw fish, not California rolls)
I got their Trust Me which came with 8 different kinds of sushi. 100% would recommend! They did not disappoint at all. Their crab roll was also EXCELLENT

Wow. This was amazing sushi. Really fresh tasting. No fishy aftertaste. Clean buttery melt in your mouth fish. Opted for the trust me option for lunch at 33$ it was a steal. Great value just right amount of food. Tasty selection of sushi. The hand rolls are amazing. Fresh fish with warm rice and a crispy seaweed. Highly recommend.

Very rude staff. I've been a few times, food is fine - though they didn't honor my food allergy and I had to send my food back. But the experience the last few times has been bad given the waiter & host's attitude to me and my friends.

AVOID!! Got extremely sick eating here, you get what you pay for sometimes I guess. Poor quality fish and extremely rude staff.  This place has gone downhill. Plenty of better options around town. Overhyped.

I've heard so many great things about SUGARFISH and was very excited to try it for myself. 

Wait: I knew this place didn't take reservations but the wait was insane for a Tuesday evening. We arrived at 6:20PM and weren't seated until 7:30PM. We went to do happy hour at another restaurant in the interim. They have a digital wait list and will text you when they're almost reading to seat you but we still waited 20 minutes after receiving the text.

Ambiance: It's super duper dark in there. Not great for food pics but okay for overall ambiance. I guess the darkness gives the place a classy feel. The upstairs is much brighter.

Food: We ordered the "Trust Me" special and it was delicious. You really get what you're paying for. You can clearly taste the quality of the fish and it does not disappoint.

Service: Service was just okay. Nothing special here. Food didn't come out particularly fast and our waitress wasn't particularly nice but it was okay overall.

Would come back solely for the quality of the food. It's pricey but well worth it.

Wow! This place is awesome. Been awhile since I had some very good sushi. Note they do not take reservations.  We were table of 4 on a Monday night and the wait was about 30 mins. Food and service was fast and friendly. Got some sake and opted for the $42 trust me omakase. Really good and fresh. Must try!
SugarFish is amazing every single time I go. Never lets me down. If you have not tried it before you don't know what you are missing! Check it out!

I personally think sugarfish is some of the best sushi you can get in NYC without emptying your pockets at a place like Nobu. My girlfriend and I both did the preset tasting. The hand rolls were awesome and I loved the sushi being served over warm rice! Highly recommended Sugarfish for affordable, high quality sushi in the city

Hmmm, pretty good food at an attractive price point. Service was attentive and ambience was pretty nice. For the food, Albacore was delightful, as well as the crab roll, which was light and juicy. Most other pieces were good but not exceptional. Toro hand roll was disappointing; not bad per se but didn't have too much flavor; don't believe it had negi in it. Sushi rice was definitely on the warm side compared to other sushi places but was fairly good. Felt like the acidity was a bit heavier than I'm used to and could be a bit sweeter. The lack of wasabi for all nigiri was also a bit surprising but certainly acceptable at the price point. Overall, I would certainly recommend trying out Sugarfish.

At first I was thrown off by the lack of diversity in the sushi rolls offered. Although I proceeded to order and could not have been happier with the decision to do so. The fish is so fresh and high quality it just melts in your mouth. Service was also amazing as they don't rush you and bring things out one at a time so the table is never crowded. Amazing and will be going back.

Surprised there wasn't a wait, but it was probably because it was a rainy Sunday afternoon. We got seated immediately. I got the Nozawa trust me ($45) and my boyfriend got the Don't think just eat omakase ($63).
- The Nozawa Trust Me 
All the fish were fresh and delicious. The rice however had a bit too much vinegar to a point where it overpowered the taste of the fish. The rice to fish ratio had a bit too much rice. 
- Don't think. Just eat. 
Pieces were pretty similar to the Nozawa except for a few. The waitress said it include some of their limited availability items. The pieces we liked the most were the scallop pieces! For the price of $63 I think I'd rather go to Sushi on Jones ($58 w/o tax Nd tip)

This is a no tipping establishment! Which is rare in NYC.

Fish of excellent quality. Definitely one my favorite sushi restaurants in the world.
Highly recommended.
They don't take reservations, so you should expect to wait a bit.

I went here on a Monday evening solo and it was nice and easy to get a seat (so I guess I didn't have a proper Sugarfish experience.) The wait staff here was nice and the foot was good though as my omakase suggests, very "lite." Staff at the bar section was excellent.

Short answer- order rolls or don't come here

I ordered the omakase lite though I probably should have ordered the normal size. As with everyone else, they start the meal with edamame as well as some sad looking wasabi and ginger for your fish though I generally do not add either. The edamame was good as expected and I prefer it cold like this so it's refreshing.

Their appetizer of the day was tuna in ponzu. This was delicious and I'd recommend ordering a plate if they have it as a separate appetizer.

The sushi was one piece each as said in the lite description. This consisted of albacore in a similar ponzu sauce, salmon, yellowtail, and shrimp. All of the sushi pieces had pretty warm rice which stuck to the fingers a bit.

Albacore: Good texture though it fell apart really easily especially with the semi-warm rice. The ponzu is unneeded also

Salmon: Good

Yellowtail: Fine

Shrimp: Good texture though not super sweet

After these four pieces, I got the last piece which was a toro hand roll. This was much better then the sushi with good seaweed and a good amount of nice buttery fish. The rice was also the proper temperature (perhaps someone else made this one.)

I ordered a crab hand roll as extra at the beginning and this was easily the best thing I had. The crab was sweet and there was much more of this then anything found in the lite menu.

The food here was fine but not worth the price or what I see is the usual wait (I've walked by this place with a line out the door on occasion.) 2.3 or so. Almost a 3 with the crab hand roll and the appetizer but I can't help but feel I got ripped off for the price I paid even with there being no tip. The staff here were excellent though and there were a few good dishes.

I had a great experience here. Ordered the "Trust Me" option, which started with the Tuna Sashimi in ponzu sauce and scallions. This was one of my fav parts from the set; smooth, bright and satisfying. I also loved the albacore nigiri, and the yellowtail. Each nigiri/hand roll placed in front of you is specifically crafted with utmost care, vinegary, sweet, warm, cool based on the fish you are served.   
Also, the iced green tea is a great accompaniment!

Service was excellent when I went. The place runs like a well-oiled machine, yet everyone is still personable and friendly.
The omakasa is to die for. Aside from the over 1 he wait, such a great experience. Highly recommend.

Love the fish here.
Seating was quick, despite the popularity. Took about 15 minutes in a busy Thursday lunch time. We ordered the nOzawa trust me sushi which I highly recommend, and the limited availability toro and albacore. - our top picks were the limited albacore belly -So buttery and creamy, melts in your mouth, and the tuna sashimi - similarly soft. I must say, the yellow tail sashimi (part of the NOzawa special) was really underwhelming though chewy with an aftertaste, and that is perhaps because the rest of the pieces were so outstanding. And the other not so great piece was the crab roll, we did not even finish the tiny roll. Tasted a bit like tuna salad w Mayo. For sush an outstanding restaurant with high quality food, I felt underwhelmed By the yellowtail and crab roll.

Otherwise- FANTASTIC!

Only reason why this restaurant is rated so highly is because NYC sushi scene lacks quality mid-tier pricing options.  Quality of fish is just so so, but service was horrible.  Almost 2 hours for lunch, our food was brought out in completely random order, one order at a time, 10-15 minutes in between each one.  Not everyone was served at the same time too, one person would get one order while everyone else sat around waiting for the next 10 minutes.  I was missing one last order when the waitress asked if we were all done.  I told them I was still waiting for one more order, she went back to check, then the hostess came over and told me that they indeed had already served me all my orders.  My group and I all were all confused and I told her I didn't receive everything. She immediately gave me attitude and when she later brought my food over, she might as well have thrown the food down in front of me, no acknowledgement, no eye contact.  

Absolutely shit service.

This is the best quality to price I have had in NYC. We really enjoy the food, but I am debating if it should be 4 or 3 stars when I consider the entire experience. If I was just rating the food then it would be 5 stars. Where I had some issues is that they don't take reservations and we had to wait 2 1/2 hours to eat, they do have a system that allows you to check your place in the waiting queue but I don't think is accurate because even though we knew upfront we had 25 people ahead of us, the first 18 were seated within 45 minutes so I said to my family it should not take that long for the other 7, but that took another hour an a half, and they don't give you any explanation. So for a meal planned for 7:30 ( yes I know hard to get a table at that time but I was ok to be seated at 9 ) we ended up sitting at 10 PM, so to begin they did not have the omakase we wanted, they could have told me that an hour ago and I would have not waited, so we order another omakase, as I said food was excellent to we wanted to repeat one specific type of nigiri and we were told that this was their best seller and they needed to save it for people waiting. To me the same way I was told there were out of the omakase I wanted, they could tell other people they were out of that nigiri. I don't think they should treat that way a customer that waited 2 1/1 hours to eat.

My wife and I went for dinner on a Friday and ended up waiting 3 1/2 hours before being seated. We obviously went around the city and went to a couple of different bars before coming back to the restaurant to be seated, so it was no problem for us. 

We ordered the "Don't think. Just Eat." which consisted of everything in "THE NOZAWA Trust Me" came with but I think a couple more pieces of sushi, one more handroll, and some scallops. 

The fish was great we absolutely enjoyed every bite of it. Although, it was a little weird the way they would bring things out in random order. We decided to share everything so we didn't just sit there while the other was eating. The Ponzu sauce the Tuna Sashimi came in was so good my wife said she wanted to drink it. I told her I wouldn't be embarrassed if she did!

The Handrolls were my favorite part of the meal because they actually felt filling while eating them and had a crunch I really enjoyed because of the seaweed. A lot of times handrolls sit too long and the seaweed gets a little too moist before being served. They bring it out to you immediately and recommend you eat it right away. 

The couple of things I that were a bit offputting for me was how close you are to everyone else. I do enjoy a little personal space and I get distracted very easily (something my wife doesn't appreciate) and when I can hear everyone else's conversations it takes away from the experience for me. The servers were really nice but one of the waitresses was extremely robotic.. You have to imagine she says the same thing over and over again hundreds of times a day. These are just little pet peeves that really don't matter to most so all in all I definitely would recommend this place to friends and family.

Sugarfish NY, i am not sure why more expensive Sugarfish than LA has inferior fish!
The fish quality does not equal the amazing fish in Los Angeles!  
Service was so bad an inferior compared to Los Angeles!! ( update on Los Angeles) Los Angeles  Sugarfish was horrible in ApriL 2019.  Beyond depressing how my favorite restaurants (SugarFish) went down hill.  

There was a waiter with bleached blonde hair that should be fired.
My waiter was kind. We ordered. Edamame came, i ran 
upstairs to bathroom which takes a bit!  By the time i came back the nice waiter brought sashimi which I literally hadn't taken 1 bite of edamame .
So i asked waiter to please slow down food.  I like to eat my edamame first.  So he offered to take sashimi away and i said thank you.  So as he took our sashimi's away! Enter the bleached blonde rude guy! Who takes the sashimi from the nice waiters hands snd says coldly  and rude to us, you have to eat this!!! With an attitude he walked away!basically shoved it in our faves with his high and mighty attitude!!
So at that point the whole vibe was weird and than i guess the manager came over and asked what happened?? I politely told him! He apologised and asked what he could do?? 
I said we were OK.
However every time i looked up the bleached blonde waiter was staring evil eye at us.  Totally uncomfortable!
The fish was mediocre.  Yellowtail did not taste fresh!
Black sea bass from montauk was best bite of the day.
Albacore belly was chewy not sweet and did not melt.
So disappointed ~ 
Also my guest ordered a green tea and we never got it???
Had to ask fir extra wasabi twice.
Hmmmm
What is wrong with this place???
Prices, quality, and rude service!!

I ate at Sugarfish at least 10 times over 3 week period when i was in Los Angeles last month!! Amazing!
Delish & fresh!
I tried sugarfish NY shortly after it opened and had a bad experience with food! 
I basically would not of come back but my friend wanted to go as she had never been!  So embarrassing 
Silly expensive for the bites you get of mediocre fish
And to top it off the rudest waiter i have ever encountered at any Sugarfish or Kazu Nori ~
I promise i will not ever be back to this location, i would be scared of that waiter and the high cost of the restaurant makes no sense! Plenty of other great sushi places in NY.
The manager should of taken the 17 percent gratuity off bill or brought us something! Nothing was done!
I should of refused automatic gratuity ~ but just wanted t

Underwhelming experience overall. There was a lot of hype about this place so my friend and I decided to check it out. We were told there was about a 45 minute wait on a weeknight, which ended up being closer to an hour and even then we were seated at the bar. The sushi was average....nothing to rave about in my opinion especially considering it was also overpriced.

Fresh, fantastic service and pricing.
Nothing to complain about and looking forward to going back!

I came in by myself while in town for a business trip. The hostess was friendly and inviting and said that the wait was about one hour. I went to a nearby restaurant for a drink and only waited only 30-45 minutes, presumably because I was a party of 1. 

I really enjoyed the concept Sugarfish presents: limited drink selections, prix fixe menus, and no gratuity. It's like all of the hard decisions of dining  are already made for you!  I decided to go with the Trust Me menu. At first, I feared it would be too much food, but it was really the perfect amount. 

Each part of the meal is brought out separately and from what I can tell, the order of the dishes is intentional. The fish was impeccable; high quality, fresh fish, in large portions. The pieces would melt in my mouth. 

The service was also great. I did not feel rushed at any point in my meal, nor were there any awkward pauses in between plates. Coming from Denver, it's easy to say that this was some of the best sushi I've ever had. For the price, I really don't know if this can be beat. I would absolutely return next time I am in NYC. Thank you, Sugarfish!

Oh, yes, this place is awesome---and is as good as everyone says! The sushi (and everything else) it's so tasty and fresh! 

Like a lot if people reviewing here, I got one of the Trust Me lunch special (I got the largest one - $45).  I was a little worried that it was not going to be enough food to fill me up. But, I was wrong! Succulent and delicious.

A work colleague had recommended this place for taking an intern out to lunch whose last day was upcoming. I was totally glad for this recommendation because it was spot on! We were all thrilled and delighted how good. I would definitely go back here for a special occasion any time

Both my partner and I ate here recently and it was some of the best sushi we ever had. We both ordered iced green tea's and the don't think just eat. Personally, I thought it was the perfect amount of food. I was full, but not completely stuffed. The tuna hand roll was simply the best roll I have ever had. I also enjoyed the scallop very much. Both sashimi's were excellent as well. I didn't much care for the sea bream, but I think that was just my personal taste. 
My only minor complaint is that the restaurant was absolutely freezing!
Besides that, the experience was incredible and I fully recommend this to any sushi fans looking to a special meal.

Was very much looking forward to trying this place. It is quite good. Very fresh. Not as good as kazuroll I thought. But there were no lines which was very nice. Very similar experience to the rolls at Kazu. Very fresh sushi and love the wrap.

came in solo on a Monday night around 9:45 and there was still quite a wait. opted for takeout and I'm so glad I did! it was a really quick process, I probably only waited about 10-15 mins for my food then I was on my way. great quality fish and I love the ponzu combinations, too!

Great sushi restaurant. Real sushi tastes nothing like what you've had before. The service and manager was very good and the special way the recommended dish was presented was exceptional. Once I get a sushi craving I will be coming here once again.

Really really underwhelming experience, from the atmosphere to the quality of the food. Since this place is SO highly praised, I was extremely excited to taste their omakase menu.  Needless to say, the 2 hour dinner wait on a Tuesday night (as they don't take reservations) was not worth it whatsoever. Let's start with the restaurant itself- VERY dimly lit, very black and moody interior, but without any redeeming decor. I tried their "trust me" menu and each of the pieces was brought out to my table one at a time. Let's talk about the rice; it was hot, which was a stark contrast to the cold fish, and very sticky, dry, and very tasteless. A huge component of good sushi is the rice, and frankly this rice tasted worse than that of the $11.99 lunch special sushi I've had in the past. What's more, all the fish served throughout the night all tasted the same; bland, and extremely overpowered by the orange and lemony flavors they put on the rice. There was no wasabi added to any of the sushi rice and the hand rolls just fell apart instantly (not to mention, the hot rice again amidst the cold nori and cold fish was just an odd combination). 

Here I thought, perhaps because we got seated at 10 pm and the restaurant closes at 11, they were rushed, perhaps they wanted to get people out and did not put their best work forward. So I gave it another shot, on a Thursday lunch. Nope, same bland food, same overpowering lemon and orange flavors, same hot, sticky, crappy rice. Never again. Don't buy into the hype of this place. Want to try real great omakase in the city that won't cost you an arm and a leg? Try Sushi by Bou- now that's truly a great food experience.

Incredible experience! Well worth the wait. 

First, let me start that you will most likely have to wait if you come there for dinner. But the wait is definitely worth it. Their nigiri is out of this world, the rice is warm and fluffy and sashimi is practically melting in your mouth. 

We ended up with sharing Nozawa menu with additional Toro and Crab hand rolls. Towards the end we also tried the Albacore Belly Tuna roll which was unbelievable. 

The ambiance is excellent, it's low light and quiet, perfect for a dinner date or a after work dinner. Service is very fast, you don't really have to wait for long but at the same time they are not rushing you.

As for the food, the tuna sashimi was very good, fresh tuna with sauce that was full of flavor. All the hand rolls were amazing, the seaweed wrap is crunchy and not chewy (like what you typically get with hand roll), the rice still feels warm(!) and the sashimi is super fresh. 

If you have some room after all the items from Nozawa/Trust Me I highly recommend trying out Albacore Belly special. Tuna felt super fatty and full of flavor, it was a perfect way to end our meal. 

Overall I would say this place is one of the best sushi restaurants when it comes to Nigiri. This is basically Omakase, but way cheaper than what you pay at Nobu or Nakazawa and the quality is superb. Highly recommended!

Sugarfish was our favorite restaurant back in LA and we were excited to see there were two sugarfish locations in NYC. We visited the one in SoHo last week and were disappointed with the service and quality of fish/rice. It was nothing like back home. However we came to the flatiron location yesterday and it was way better. The fish tasted more fresh and had better texture. Also the service was way friendlier. I was happy overall and will definitely return
The best sushi and service I've ever had! Ambiance is great... low lighting and truly a 5 star experience.

After spending a great deal of time searching around for a sushi spot in NYC of which there are probably hundreds of good options I decided to give SugarFish a try.  

Pros: 
Amazing quality sushi
Simple and unique menu 
Great Space 
Awesome Waitstaff
Really moderate price for the quality in NYC 
(No Tipping is an added + as well) 

Cons: 
No Reservations
Very Long waits (was told 2.5 hours and waited 1.5)
Hostess was a bit snide when it came to telling us the wait almost as if to say "you thought you could eat dinner at this time?!"


Overall, great experience if you need a cool spot and are wanting a night out that will most likely include going to a nearby bar after putting your name down for a table. If you are looking for a quick bite or a new frequent place to grab something like a California or Spicy Tuna roll (both not on menu) you may have better luck elsewhere.

Sugarfish is a an essential experience for Sushi enthusiast in NYC.  The fish is incredibly fresh and the sushi is delicately seasoned not to change the flavor, but simply to enhance it.  Wasabi and ginger are provide but the true delight comes from trusting the inspirations of the chef.

Ingredients are fresh, visit this place only if you like to eat nigiri with warm rice which warmed your fish on top at the same time, how efficient!! 
The rice is very soft so you can enjoy your nigiri like fried rice, the rice fell apart when you pick up the nigiri. 
The warm rice also made the lobster hand roll seaweed so sticky and easily stuck to your oral cavity. 
I ordered the 63 dollar no brain set, at the end I got the salmon sashimi as cold as my ice water glass. It woke up my tongue and my brain wondering why I have never tried my sashimi so cold...what an experience and I think I will not go back for a long while. It is unforgettable. 

This place breaks the rule of proper temperature of fish, rice, and plates in JP dining.

I came here at 6pm on Sunday with a friend. It took me 40 minutes to get a table. 

I ordered Trust me ($40).
The service is awesome. The dishes are awesome with high quality. Nice ginger and vinegar. My only suggestions is that the rice could be warmer. 

Overall, my favorite sushi place in NYC. Recommend to come again

Fish was really good, but rice was terrible! The sushi rice was horrendous, soggy, and unappetizing. It fell apart before you even picked it up. A serious sushi restaurant would have a good rice game instead of a newbie making their rice. Owners need to be more stringent about quality control instead of letting terrible soggy rice leave the kitchen.

We had been to the California outposts several times but hadn't visited in our own backyard before. I am happy to say the quality and service have traveled well. The sushi is always very good - from the freshness of the fish, the perfectly prepared rice that is still warm to the delicate sauces that enhance the fish flavor but never overwhelm it. The waitstaff are very attentive and seem to always be nearby even in such a popular and crowded restaurant. Bottom line is that it is worth the wait that seems like it could be solved if they allowed reservations but the wait proves they are doing it right.

Sushi quality is quite good, as is the service. Don't expect a super quick meal though- orders are served piecemeal as they are ready. For lunch I usually go for the trust me lite with an add on or two. For dinner the trust me usually fills me up. My fav things on the menu are the tuna with ponzu, the tuna and salmon sashimi, and the toro and yellowtail handrolls. Sweet shrimp add on is good too.

No tip policy makes a meal pretty reasonable (especially for lunch if having no drinks). 

One star deduction is for the fact that solo diners are only allowed to sit at the counter, not at tables. My preference is actually the counter, but what bothers me is that parties of 2-3 also get slotted into the counter, so as a solo diner you are most likely going to be waiting to be seated AFTER groups that put their names down after you, as they get options of both counter and table. This has happened to me every time I've put my name down, pretty frustrating and sort of discriminatory. The AC at the counter is also BLASTING so bring a sweater if you plan to dine alone. 

Overall a decent experience but I only plan to go back when there's no line.

We each did the "Trust Me" dinner course. The fish was fresh but nearly every sushi creation was doused in a sauce that was often sour. The rice used was fluffy but fell apart whenever we tried pick up the sushi. Presentation of each dish was poor with no effort to dress or arrange the sushi to make the plates look less empty.

Recently returned to try the "Don't Think, Just Eat" at Sugarfish. The "Don't Think, Just Eat" menu is very similar to the Nozawa menu:

You start off completely the same with edamame and tuna sashimi. 

The second plate comes with 2 pc of Snapper, 2 pc of Salmon, and 2 pc of Sea Bream. "Don't Think, Just Eat" brings another element of preparation to the fishes to showcase different flavor pairings. For example, you get one standard piece of the salmon with sesame seeds and another comes with a thin piece of kombu or kelp As for the sea bream, you get one with a shiso leaf and for the snapper, you can one piece prepared with soy and ginger.

Then, you get a toro handroll, which they tell you to eat right away before the seaweed gets soggy. (in both menus)

In the "Don't Think, Just Eat", you get salmon sashimi in a ponzu sauce and topped with sesame seeds, very similar to the tuna sashimi. Too similar to the tuna sashimi, so this was kind of a miss for me. 

The next plate comes with 2 pc of Albacore, 2 pc of Shrimp, and  2 pc of Scallop (only in "Don't Think, Just Eat"). The shrimp was prepared in two different ways - one which is quickly parboiled topped with sesame and second is the Nozawa-style, which was my favorite piece of the night because of the sweetness of the shrimp. The scallop was also prepared in two ways - one was the standard scallop piece and the second was the large bay scallops with mayo. The large bay scallops piece was also a miss for me, just average.

In the Nozawa menu, you get a crab handroll and the last piece of the menu is a daily special (2pc). 

The last piece of the "Don't Think, Just Eat" is a lobster handroll. 

So all in all, you really only get one extra plate of sashimi. 

After just been at Sushi Nao, I prefer the different flavor profiles at Sushi Nao. However, Sugarfish gave a valiant effort. Some of the pieces were a hit or miss for me, but still a very interesting menu from the Nozawa or Trust Me Menu.
The best sushi for the best price can't beat! Me and a friend go every time she comes to visit. Depending on the day and time never waited more than 30min

Came in on a late Tuesday night with a friend and luckily did not have to wait to be seated. From what I hear the wait can be hours! We each ordered the Nozawa special and sake. The sushi was very fresh. I felt the price was reasonable for the location, attention to customer service, and food quality.
Super simple and delicious sushi. Wait time is doable and totally worth it. Chill ambiance. Albacore belly is a must!!!!

Sugarfish is one of my favorite sushi places. I would say I think the sushi was much better at the LA locations I've been to though. 

Anyway, there was a bit of a wait but was expected so we had some drinks at the bar across the street and then more sake at the counter when we walked back in. 

The fish here is so buttery! And the sushi rice has some sweetness to it, in a good way. I usually get the middle menu since it's not too little not too much, just right amount of food. Unless you're super hungry then get the biggest one.

Best sushi in New York. If you're looking very a California roll or miso soup, this is not the place for you. SUGARFISH's believes in the most simplistic form of sushi. The fish is extremely fresh and delicious. I will say that there are a couple downsides to this restaurant... They do not take reservations and are always packed! If you come any later than 5:30 for dinner you will be waiting at least 50 minutes for a table. If you are impatient, I recommend doing their takeout menu because it is just as good and comes in a very aesthetically pleasing box. Another downside is the lighting. I would not bring a first date here because you will barely be able to see their face across from you. Although you can be waiting to get a seat here for a while, the food is definitely worth it.

Tried The "Nozawa trust me" from the menu amazing quality seafood and rice! The only downside for me is its a bit salty from the rice and the vinegar is a little  bit too much. All in all really good food. Worth the $$$.

A good mid range option for a quickie but quality sushi meal. Went at 12:30pm on a Friday for two and the wait was minimal, the front desk will make it out as if the wait will be very long, "8 parties ahead of you..." but we were seated in 5 minutes.  We opted for the most expensive omakase and the food came immediately. The only complaint I have is that the food came at different times for me and my friend even though we ordered the same thing and at the same time. 

Sushi was very good, fresh and tasty. The hand rolls were a bit too hot and the nori would get soggy immediately. Otherwise, a solid choice.
More like a 3.5. Service was unenthusiastic and the restaurant felt tired, however, the quality of the fish was high and the price point excellent for this city. I'd eat here again in a pinch.

By far the best sushi on the East Coast! Once I had Sugarfish, it ruined any other sushi restaurants for me. 
They do not take reservations, but you can order a drink (wine/beer/sake only) and sit upstairs in their lounge. Usually, we will put our name in and go down the street to a bar. When you are nearing the top of the list, the restaurant will text you so you know when to head back over. On a Saturday night, be prepared to wait 1-2 hours for your table- BUT do not let that turn you away...it's worth the wait! 
I typically order the trust me lite, and it's more than enough food for me. My husband usually orders a la carte. The chef recommends you to eat the food as soon as it comes out - especially anything with seaweed. My favorites on the trust me lite menu, are the albacore sushi and the toro hand roll. Usually my husband and I will order an extra toro roll to split, because it is that amazing and fresh. 
We are big sushi fans, and this is actually our favorite restaurant. The sushi is prepared perfectly and is extremely fresh.
If you are wanting to try this restaurant but not willing to do the wait, one of the slowest times that I have seen is a Sunday afternoon during football season. We have gotten in several times with minimal wait (maybe 15 mins). Just to note- they will not seat you until your entire party has arrived.

The freshest sushi you will ever eat without contest. You have the option of doing one of their tasting menus or get sushi a la carte. Unlike many sushi places they don't do all the specialty rolls packed with veggies and spicy mayo, just top quality sushi, sashimi, hand and cut rolls. I'm new to the sushi game in the last few years and am I big fan of those speciality rolls and never cared much for just straight up raw fish, until now - melt in your mouth delicious. The Toro is to die for and the crab hand roll was the best I've ever had. 

The food is 5 stars for sure, but our waitress, unfortunately, made the experience just under 5 stars. We had to ask her to stay the 2nd time she came around so we could order. Only after she rudely came by and couldn't be bothered to just excuse herself to take our order the first time and then just stormed off. Needless to say she was far from attentive, but the food makes up for it and we will most certainly be back!
Can't stop craving the Trust Me. Wish the wait was not so long and I'd love them to open up more locations. Could eat the albacore belly and crab handrolls every day.
Good food but the place is too loud to be enjoyable. If they could turn the volume down on the crowd, it might be worth going back.

I really liked this place which is shocking because I honestly can usually only relate to the negative reviews. This place might be more of a 4-4.5 stars but since I so strongly disagree with the negative reviews, I feel compelled to round up.

The wait was 2 hours on a Tuesday night which is excessive but my friend and I were expecting that so it wasn't a problem. The host was honest and helpful and let us know that we would have 5 minutes to return to the restaurant once we received a text letting us know that our table would be ready so we were able to go elsewhere for a drink while we waited.

We ordered one trust me menu and a few other items from the a la carte section. The rice was soooo good (it did have a BIT too much vinegar because it fell apart on one or two pieces but still so good) and warm and flavorful. The sushi was also pretty good. It was not the freshest fish in Manhattan but significantly better than just acceptable. One of the pieces (I forget which) had a little too much lemon/citrus for my liking but the rest were really well prepared even though none had wasabi. 

The courses were served from light to heavy and were timed perfectly.

I'll definitely return again and again.

Is there even anyone who eats at sugar fish and does not immediately have this restaurant top their list of favorites? We've been to kazunori a handful of times for their handrolls and decided it was time to commit fully and try the restaurant. All I can say is, wow. We waited about 45 minutes at 10pm on a Saturday, we were quoted about 1.5 hours. We put our names down and walked half a mile for some beer and ran half a mile back because the wait ended up being much shorter. We picked the nazawa trust me and split it between the two of us because we were actually pretty stuffed from a full day of eating. Each plate they brought to us was a new experience. Each piece melted into our mouths and flavors danced on our palates. The fish is out of this world soft. The rice is perfect. The combinations and complexity of flavors really shows how thoughtful each artfully crafted piece is. We were sad when it was all over and the final pieces were eaten. We almost wanted to order more but knew that our bellies were filled to the top.

My only gripe with this spot is that I wish it wasn't so dark. I know a lot of restaurants are dimly lit especially for dinner service but I do love to eat with my eyes as well. Despite that, I can't wait for my next visit here.

TLDR: Best Sushi hands down in NYC.

I ordered the Nozawa Trust Me, and the fish and the handrolls that they serve is the softest fish I've ever had. I usually shy away from japanese food places because the regulsr take out 3 rolls for $12 lunch specials weren't always worth it to me when chipotle is only $9 (I also tend to eat a lot and look at volume of food vs price). But trying this place got me hooked on very good japanese fish!

Wait
Waited 40 minutes at around 9:30pm on a Saturday night.

Would definitely go again.

If you're a creature of comfort, the Trust Me meal is consistently high-quality, delicious, and paced well. I've enjoyed it in both LA and NYC. Service is impeccable. Prices are reasonable. Around prime dinner time, expect to wait 45-90 minutes.

We have been waiting 2.5-3 hours for our reservations and it is now 9:03pm. The wait timing was way off. We got the text message to go to our table and it was an extra 30 min wait. I am currently  waiting in line hearing the manager say the exact same excuse why people are waiting. "The text message to indicate your table is ready does not mean your reservation is ready, but it means you are close to the end of the wait line". This was not communicated. All I want is please don't underestimate the time of the reservation if you don't understand the parties involved and how long they may take. What is interesting is there was no apology to me or my family. This is poor quality and it deceives the customer. 
Food was good, but definitely not worth the waste of time of my night. I would not recommend this restaurants especially for people who value their time. To my fellow yelpers! I am not one to write reviews but damn...Please pick someplace where you can get a good meal and also have your night to enjoy. SUGARFISH is not the place to go.
Stellar quality of fish and great atmosphere! The wait was quite long (1.5 hours after we put our names in) but the experience was great once we were seated. The tasting menu is 100% worth it!

Only deducted 1 start because of their absurdly long wait and no reservation policy.  Other than that this place is amazing!  It has quickly become my favorite place for sushi and I love that the tip is worked into the price of the meal already so that makes life easier.  The fish is always super fresh and delicious and the service is wonderful.  Pro tip, if you don't want to wait, they do have take away and they pack it in the chicest bento box packaging I've ever seen.  Also they deliver!  I will keep coming back though...the wait sucks but its worth it!

Everything on the menu melts in your mouth!!! I've been to their location in LA and this is just as good. Really long wait - over an hour around 3pm on the weekend so plan accordingly! But worth it! You can't go wrong with the menu

I didn't think I can have an orgasm in my mouth.

But holy moly, sugar fish is where it is at, man. I thought I had the best sushi ever but nah. This is a whole new league and honestly, the best I ever had.

The rice is warm...? Which is new to me and didn't expect that at all, but it melted with the albacore in my mouth. I had to pace myself because the food was delicious. The way the restaurant's menu is basically prefix menus. I ordered one of their trust menus and you're supposed to eat as they're served. So throw out social etiquette out the damn window. The food also comes in 2-4 pieces which encourages you to dine slowly and interact with your guest(s). It makes the food and experience more enjoyable btw. Versus inhaling our food like animals lol.

Also, the they're are seasoned and there is no need for the soy sauce per se. and the wasabi? Fresh. High quality. It's amazing how little you can use and you're dripping from your nose lol.

Staff is attentive. Wait is very long. They don't do reservations. You may wait up to like 2 hours.... which we did...
I can't say enough good about sugarfish. It's the best I've had. The warm rice cold fish served immediately as its made is a model more places should embrace.
Great service. Fast. High quality. Delicious. Very high value for the dollar. I haven't found sushi of this quality (at this price) in New York outside of the sugarfish franchise.

3.5/5. Came on a Monday evening and there was a long wait. My friend and I waited for 90 minutes to get seated. I had high expectations for this but honestly, I was not impressed. The salmon and shrimp sushi were good, but the tuna sashimi and albacore sushi were not fresh... The other thing that really bothered me is that rice fall apart whenever we tried pick up the sushi.The rice was soggy and too loosely packed. Definitely does not worth the hype or the wait. (Or maybe I just came in when the food quality was inconsistent)

Love that the tip is worked into the price of the meal though, it really made everything easier.

This is a very authentic feeling sushi restaurant. The fish is FRESHHHH and delicious. Also, the pricing is fantastic. What a great value! I left feeling like I got my money's worth which, unfortunately, doesn't always happen at a sushi restaurant in NYC.

This is one of those "tip is already included" set ups. I LOVE IT! The servers worked as a team to help us and I felt like we were never waiting around for a long time.

I recommend coming here for a date or catch up session with a close friend. It's not too loud so you can actually hear each other talk and it feels very intimate.

With regards to value. This place has the best fish you can get for the price. My girlfriend and I love this place and come often. However the only down side is that you can't make reservations. Its walk in only.

Amazing every time. The sushi is the best I have ever tasted in my life!!!! I usually don't like hand rolls but the ones at SUGARFISH are amazing- the seaweed is fresh and crispy, the rice inside is warm and the fish is always the best quality. The servers are always extremely professional and friendly and the restaurant itself is always clean.

Hard to fathom how someone could not rate this place 5-stars - Absolutely exceptional experience in every way!

Sushi was amazing, service was impeccable - we had our young child and were having trouble keeping him calm, but the wait staff was super cooperative and understanding the entire time and made sure to bring plates out when that person was present and ready for it.  

This caused us to take up the table for a longer time than normal, but was very much appreciated.  

Can't say enough about SUGARFISH!!!
This place is way overrated. Waited an hour and a half because of the hype. The sushi was no better than some of the less expensive options in the neighborhood.
The sushi is pretty good for the price point but they don't take reservations and it is typically a 3 hour plus wait and can be very variable.
Best sushi I've had among the incredibly expensive options New York has to offer. Go go go! I grew up eating at the Sugarfish in Santa Monica, CA, and it's equally as fantastic at either locations.

The sashimi melts in your mouth. The rice comes out warm and the fish is so fresh and tasty. Timing and service is impecable. The sushi rolls were also excellent. The food was so good that it didn't need any soy sauce. I'd recommend this place for anyone looking for authentic Japanese sushi. The only thing I didn't like was that the bathroom was pretty dirty, even though we arrived on a Sunday at noon, which is when the restaurant opens. 

Overall, fantastic!

Came here on Friday right when it opened at around 11:20 I was surprised to see a small line but by 11:30 the line definitely doubled which was quite surprising since it's been a while since they opened! 

The service was quick and fantastic. Whenever we were done a plate was cleared and our server explained everything to us quickly and efficiently. 

We got the most expensive lunch set which was $49 because their daily special was scallops and I love scallops!! It was quite filling and for lunch it's a great deal -- all the sushi melted in my mouth! 

With that being said I don't think I would come here for dinner. I heard the lines were super long, this sushi is good but good enough to wait ~3 hours for. But if you're in the area for lunch -- definitely worth checking out!!! 

The bill was so easy because tip is already included :)

I am sorry to say I have had a terrible experience with the restaurant, but after awaiting for 2 hours for the waiting time. We are still not seated. It is just poor disappointment form my perspective. I wish they have better service.

Awesome meal. The highest quality fish, slightly warm rice and slightly crispy seaweed. No frills, just really great sushi. Some of the sushi and sashimi come with its own sauce. We got tuna and salmon sashimi and they were both great. The scallops were great, had two different kinds. Everything we had was top notch. We went at an off time so we had almost no wait in late afternoon. They do not take reservations so I'm not sure how long the weights would be during lunch or dinner. I assume there would be quite a wait.

I will definitely be going back and highly recommend.

Finally made it to dinner at SUGARFISH! Is it just me or is this the most pretentious restaurant to ever exist? Yes the sushi is good and fresh. The fish melts in your mouth. But everything about going to eat here is extremely inconvenient. 6 pm on a Sunday there was a waitlist of 17 groups ahead of us, no problem went to grab a drink nearby. 30 min later the wait dropped to 12 groups. Ordered second drink, of course immediately get text that our table is ready. Tried to call them and say we will be there shortly, they have no phone lol. But whatever we finished our drinks then went and our table was ready. They don't have too many drink options, it's literally a few white wines, Sapporo, or sake. I got the trust me for food, it was delicious! My husband got the one level higher, called the nizawa or something. Special was sweet shrimp which was our least fav. It is kind of annoying though that they tell you 10 times how to eat their food. Every time they bring you a hand roll they're telling you BEST ENJOYED IMMEDIATELY.

Overall: The restaurant is unique, a traditional Japanese with a modern twist. The place has the perfect darker atmosphere for a date or a small group of friends. It is important to mention that Sugarfish does not take reservations, therefore be ready to wait at least 20-30 minutes to be seated during the weekend. Nevertheless, the waiting is worth it!

Food: The menu is simple to navigate, and the service is quick and straight to the point. When choosing what to eat, do not hesitate in asking the waiter/waitress for advice! For the best experience, I'd recommend going with one of their tasting menus. There are limited options when it comes to alcohol (wine, beer, and sake only).

Not my favorite sushi place for omakase. Yes the price is much more agreeable at $33 for the lunch menu Trust me selection, but the sushi was nothing remarkable. It wasn't a melt in your mouth kinda sushi. The sushi rice also broke apart very easily.... pretty sure that's not what was supposed to happen. Service was great and the waiters were attentive. But I think I'd just prefer to pay more money for better quality sushi.
My favorite sushi place in the city, definitely the wait can be long but worth it. Go with the Trust Me option for the taste test.

Absolutely incredible food. The fish was unlike anything I had ever tasted before. At times, I felt like I could barely enjoy it because it was so soft that it melted in my mouth so quickly. But I loved every second that I spent eating the fantastic sushi pieces here.
I think the $40 deal is best if going for dinner. It was just enough to fill me up. On top of that, I had the nigiri sake. It was sweet and very delicious.
The only reason I'm giving this place 4 stars is because of the wait. It's absolutely ridiculous. Like insane. Arrived at 7:30 and was number 42 on the list. Didn't get seated until 9:30 and this was a Tues! Two bloody hours...nah that's too damn much.

You really can't beat the omakase deal here. Quality is good, service is quick, and prices are reasonable. Definitely try to come at an off hour or else you'll be waiting for a few hours.

I got the Nozawa trust me version for $45. It came with a good mixture of sashimi, nigiri, and hand rolls. All the ingredients were very fresh. They didn't overpack the nigiri and hand rolls with rice.

Went Friday night for dinner. We put our names down around 615. We luckily live around the corner and waited out the waitlist (45 people) at home with a few bottles of wine. 8 o'clock we got out notification to come back, and we did. Unfortunately, we got seated an hour after that. At 9. Frustrating but made up to us by the manager with a on the house lobster roll.

We really loved and enjoyed our tasting menu meals. Have been to many expensive omakase in NYC, and this is right up there. Definitely recommended. 
But These guys have to use Resy or open table!! Would lead to many more happy customers.

Closer to 3.75 stars, but not 4.  Fish was poppin' phresh and the decor/service was fine.  Buuuut...I have been craving a sushi tasting since my most excellent experience at Sushi By Bou and sadly, this wasn't it. I felt the rice to fish ratio was too much in favor of rice and most of the offerings were in the "it's just raw fish onto of rice" category rather than me closing my eyes and savoring a new adventure with each bite.  It was almost too clean.  There were four courses that were nearly identical, tuna and salmon with a soyesque sauce as well as the sweet shrimp and pink lobster which was an $11 dollar add on.  With that said, the shrimp and lobster were my favorites of the meal.  Relative to price, I did enjoy it overall, but would likely not return as there are many other adventures to be had in this great city of ours.
I was less than impressed...the service was mediocre and they aren't very accommodating when it comes to food allergies.  They don't seem to care too much about the customers experience.

Amazing sushi and sashimi. Super cool ambiance. I'd recommend sitting at the sushi bar. The service is great and the food comes out fast. Definitely go with the prix fixe menu - perfect choices and enough food.

Food was extremely great but the service sucks. We were two and the wait was almost two hours on a Saturday night. There were a party of three after us on the waitlist but apparently the party complained they were very hungry and the manager sat them immediately, I went to the manager right away and told him they were after me and asked if I complained like they did would he sit us right away??? He then apologized and we got a table right there. It's no fair for the rest of the patrons who leave their number and wait, we came inside to wait when Sugarfish had 12 parties ahead of us and got sat when we were #8. Our waiter was way too busy helping many tables at the same time,  he was never around when we wanted to order more drinks or appetizers, looked like they were short handed that night. Again the food was amazing but staff and management sucks!
Best sushi ever!  The rice was perfectly seasoned and warm, and the fish super fresh!
Amazing. Literally the best sashimi, handroll, and service. Great idea to have choices of menus and simplify deciding and what goes together. Delicious sake as well. Can not recommend more highly.

Sugarfish is our favorite place to have sushi, but be warned, if you order takeout, there is a mandatory 16% fee they tack on with no explanation, but they do mention it is also taxed. So your $38 Nozawa Trust Me is actually $48 after taxes and fees. This place is fun but pricey!

Loved it, came for lunch and the wait was much shorter. Sushi was fresh and the whole experience was awesome! I would recommend coming for lunch because I came for dinner on a Saturday night (prime time)and there were 86 parties ahead of me, waited until midnight and gave up on it.

What a fantastic experience! I highly recommend if you love good sushi. We picked the 6 course menu, and also ordered saki. The fish was so fresh and delicious. I loved the food and the experience. There was a little bit of a wait, but not too bad.

Finally tried SUGARFISH by sushi nozawa after passing by locations ten thousand times. And it was my kind of restaurant. Why? Because half the name is capitalized, while they other half is completely lowercase. Just kidding. 

I went here with my girlfriend before seeing a concert in midtown. It was a crazy good value. We both ordered the "Nozawa - trust me." Which was only $52/each INCLUDING tip. In Manhattan. 

All the fish we got tasted fresh. The food came out quickly. The service was fine. I definitely recommend coming here at least once if you like sushi. 

Note - we got there at 5pm on a Monday so there was no wait. The reason I haven't tried this place sooner is because it doesn't accept reservations. I can imagine there would be a longer wait later in the evening/on a weekday. Plan accordingly.
Sushi was spectacular. We went to lunch and had the large treat me items. Again, sushi was awesome and place has good ambiance. Get there when open for lunch as wait when we left.

Came in with a group of friends. My friend who has soy and fish allergies ordered a cucumber roll. She brought mayonnaise packets with her so that her rolls aren't plain. The manager came over and said to us that no outside condiments are allowed and that is "not what the chef intended". We explained that she has soy allergies and he took the mayonnaise away and threw it out. The rest of the experience was really rude. They gave us no customer service. Did not take any of the plates away until the end. Did not refill our waters. Did not tell us to have a nice day. I don't recommend this location and much prefer the other soho location. I felt like I was ostracized and targeted, like I had a red flag sticking out of my head. When I received my check, they didn't say anything. I would LOVE to know why there was ZERO customer service at all. They could have at least FAKED it. They really took advantage of the "tips included" policy because I had such a sour experience.

I took my wife and brother-in-law here. I had been to the one on Spring so I was already expecting something good. But...you know when you're the person saying 'we should go here, you'll love it' and then you're like 'oh man...I'm feeling some pressure now'. That's how I was feeling.  I was dumb.

So...don't be dumb. Go here. Go the one on Spring. Go. Tell your friends its amazing and don't worry about it. Also, order the 'just eat' or 'just feed me' or 'i don't care how fucking fat I get just keep it coming' option. It was cute. I forget the name but it was the most expensive and treat yourself. 

So. 

Don't be dumb.
Go there.
Eat lots.

Say nice things about me behind my back.

Absolutely delicious nigiri and sashimi sushi. My sister and I wandered into this gem after a day of shopping and were absolutely delighted. The staff is attentive and helpful and the food was simply out of this world. Some of the best sushi I have ever eaten!

Is it bad that I eat sugarfish at least once a week? I shamelessly order two nozawa trust me for lunch and eat it all in one sitting. The blue crab roll is my favorite, followed by the uni when available, and the unagi roll.

One of, if not my favorite sushi spot in NYC.
